title:100 METERS: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title:100,000年後の安全: Once the waste reaches a certain level, the facility will be sealed, never to be opened again. But who can guarantee that? Is there a way to reliably warn the people living there 100,000 years from now of the danger? They might mistake it for ruins or tombs of our era, or a place where treasures are hidden. Will those people of the future even understand
title:1975年のケルン・コンサート: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title:2045 FILMS WORKSHOP vol.1:
This short film omnibus marks the first independent project from "2045," a label comprised of next-generation creators from BABEL LABEL—a content studio behind numerous films and dramas. The collection features three works directed by young filmmakers belonging to the label.

"24 Frames of Nonsense" (directed by Ren Akiba) is a fantasy love story that weaves together fiction and non-fiction to depict a film director struggling with the script for their commercial feature debut while confronting their own past and present. "For My Grief" (directed by Hitomi Tatsumura) is an ensemble drama that follows four couples who love in their own ways and choose to part for their own reasons, portraying the act of cherishing the people and the time that were undeniably there. "Yomosugara" (directed by Mikumo Yoshimura) is a human drama about a young person who, despite turning their passion into a career, is driven to the brink by the gap between ideal and reality, chronicling a single night they spend in a mysterious cafe they happen to stumble upon.

The directors include Ren Akiba, who made his feature debut with "Tokyo Escape"; Hitomi Tatsumura, who is also an actor known for her lead role in "Angels"; and Mikumo Yoshimura, a prolific creator of short films and music videos who gained recognition for her Nihon University College of Art graduation project "The Last Train." title:2046: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
title:20th Century Women: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title:20センチュリー・ウーマン: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title:2部／3部)濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, now in their late 30s, believed they were close friends who could share anything—until they discovered Jun's secret. Born from a citizen-participation improvisational acting workshop in Kobe, this three-part film features mostly first-time actors and was created through unprecedented methods. It won the Best Actress award at the 68th Locarno Film Festival.
title:361 White and Black: Director Koichiro Oyama, who received high praise for his 2020 feature debut "The Murders of Oiso," directs this human drama centered on the game of Go. Masato Kamijo, living in a port town, happens to see a press conference on television where the world Go champion, Park Han-myeong, declares, "I have a rival in Japan." While everyone assumes the rival is Sara Yonehara, 7th dan, expectations soar for a direct showdown between Park and his rival at an upcoming tournament in Japan with a total prize pool of 100 million yen. Meanwhile, Masaki Kosaka, a production director for the tournament's broadcast, meets Masato during his research and discovers that he is a childhood friend of both Park and Sara. title:361 – White and Black –: Masato Kamijo (Ryota Nagano), living in a port town, happens to see a press conference on television where the world Go champion, Park Han-myeong (Park Yu-chun), declares, "I have a rival in Japan." While everyone assumes the rival is Sara Yonehara, 7th dan (Nao Hoshino), anticipation grows as Park enters a tournament in Japan with a total prize pool of 100 million yen, sparking hope for a direct showdown with this mysterious rival. Meanwhile, Masaki Kosaka (Koudai Matsuoka), a director for the tournament’s television coverage, meets Masato during his research and discovers that Masato is a childhood friend of both Park and Sara. Upon learning that Masato is an online Go champion, Masaki encourages him to enter the tournament, only to find that Masato is traumatized by a past event that makes him unable to play Go face-to-face. Through Masaki’s unconventional plan, Masato eventually enters the competition and faces off against formidable opponents. What was the tragic event that occurred between Masato, Park, and Sara in the past? What is the secret hidden within the tournament? Through his matches, Masato arrives at a single truth...
title:365DAYs＋2彷徨う大人たち:
In the documentary "365DAYs+," director Hiroyuki Kitaura chronicled the year leading up to his retirement. This sequel serves as a personal record of his daily life and inner struggles starting from his second year after leaving the workforce. After 36 years as a corporate "salaryman," Kitaura transitioned into life as a househusband and documentary filmmaker. His first year of retirement was a whirlwind of activity, from visiting the public employment office to enrolling in graduate school.

By his second year, as the initial dust settled, Kitaura had finally attained the "free and unconstrained life" he had dreamed of during his corporate days. Yet, he noticed a faint, lingering sense of unease beginning to stir deep within him. To uncover the source of this feeling, he once again began filming with his smartphone. Through his graduate studies, travels across Japan and Asia, and interviews with friends and former colleagues, he searches for the true nature of this restlessness. During a month-and-a-half stay in Manila to obtain a Philippine retirement visa, Kitaura spent his time reflecting while staring at his hotel ceiling, eventually arriving at a conclusion he presents as "My Personal Formula for Happiness."

Like its predecessor, the film is constructed from a vast archive of footage captured daily on a smartphone. It offers a raw look at the reality of life for a retiree while exploring the fundamental meaning of "working" and "continuing to work" through candid interviews.
title:404 Still Remain: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title:47系統: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:5時から7時までのクレオ: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
title:90 Meters: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title:90メートル: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title:A Comedy in Front of the Station:: The 15th installment of the 'Ekimaé Series,' which produced 24 films starring Frankie, Morishige, and Bando. Riding the unprecedented manga boom, this film features Frankie as a manga artist and is a legendary oddity, with appearances by 'Obake no Q-taro' and 'Osomatsu-kun' within the story.
title:A DOCUMENTARY FILM OF LOSTAGE -ひかり:
What is life? What does it mean to make a living through music? What, exactly, is a rock band?

LOSTAGE is a three-piece rock band based in Nara that continues to tour live houses across Japan. Their work is never reflected in the hit charts—they deliberately chose a path outside of major distribution and sales channels. Yet, every one of their releases has sold over 5,500 copies, and their back catalog continues to be repressed, with sales figures steadily climbing to this day.

Now in their 40s, they are a rare active band with a devoted following that transcends age and gender, recently completing a sold-out 47-prefecture tour and a successful solo performance at the Hibiya Open-Air Concert Hall. Now in their 25th year, the three members have each built families in Nara and run community-based businesses, continuing their musical activities as a direct extension of their daily lives.

Once expected to "make it big" as a rock band, they even experienced a major label debut. However, with 2011 serving as a turning point, they have navigated a path of twists and turns, buffeted by the whims of reality.

While "deified" by countless fellow musicians, the three members remain firmly grounded in their daily lives. This intimate documentary explores the mystery and allure of LOSTAGE in their truest form—a band that continues to pursue a dream-like existence while remaining rooted in the reality of home and family.
title:A DOCUMENTARY FILM OF LOSTAGE ひかりの: A documentary exploring the enigma and allure of the alternative rock band LOSTAGE as they mark their 25th anniversary. Formed in 2001 and based in Nara, the three-piece band continues to perform at live houses across Japan. Despite choosing a path that avoids major distribution and the hit charts, every one of their releases has sold over 5,500 copies, with sales of their back catalog continuing to grow. Now in their 40s, the three members have built families in Nara and run community-based businesses, maintaining a musical career that is inextricably linked to their daily lives. Once burdened by the expectation to "make it big" and having experienced a major label debut, they reached a turning point in 2011, navigating a winding path through the shifting realities of life ever since. Directed by filmmaker MINORxU, who shares a 20-year history with the band, the film depicts the trajectory of three men who are revered by fellow musicians yet live grounded lives as everyday people.
title:A Foggy Tale: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title:A Missing Part: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title:A Missing Part また君に会えるまで: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title:A Naughty Angel: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.
title:A New Dawn: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title:A New Love in Tokyo: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title:A Sun-Tribe Myth from the Bakumats: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title:A Useful Ghost: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title:A pátý jezdec je Strach: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:Adam's Sake: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title:Affeksjonsverdi: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title:After Life: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
title:After the Storm: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title:Afternoon Breezes: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title:Agatha and the Limitless Readings: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title:Agatha et les lectures illimitées: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title:Ah Special Attack Corps: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
title:Aikatsu Stars! The Movie: The theatrical film of the TV anime 'Aikatsu Stars!', which began airing in April 2016 as a new series following the popular idol anime 'Aikatsu!'. It depicts the struggles of girls, including the protagonist Yume Nijino, who enrolls at Yotsusei Gakuen aiming to become the top idol. In this first theatrical film of 'Aikatsu Stars!', the story is set on a southern island where the characters come for an event. It revolves around the rumored 'Legendary Dress' said to be sleeping on the island, and depicts the friendship between Yume and Laura Sakuraba, as well as the school's top four-idol unit 'S4' taking the stage together. The short film 'Aikatsu! The Targeted Magical Aikatsu! Card' is shown simultaneously.
title:Air Doll: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title:Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
title:All of a Sudden: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title:Alpine Fire: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title:Amélie et la métaphysique des tube: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Another Home: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
title:Arabian Nights: The Adventures of: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
title:Asako I & II: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title:At the Triangle Intersection: A documentary observing a 99-year-old woman and her son and daughter-in-law, who were affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster and live in disaster recovery public housing, over a three-year period from 2018 to 2021. Seven years after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, a family forced to evacuate from Namie Town, Fukushima, wavers between returning to their hometown and choosing a new life. Having closed their long-running printing business due to the disaster and living in disaster recovery public housing in Iwaki City, the roles and relationships within the family quietly change. Tetsu, the 99-year-old mother, clings to memories of her birthplace, Okuma Town, even as her memory fades. Her taciturn son Takemasa respects his mother but leaves most of her care to his wife Shigeko. Shigeko, who has continued to bear this role, begins to reexamine her taken-for-granted position within the family and her own way of living. Through the family's daily life in flux, the film questions what "home" is and what "I" is. Directed by Toru Yamada, who has continued making films in Fukushima since the Great East Japan Earthquake.
title:Au Hasard Balthazar: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:Au hasard Balthazar: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. title:Au pan coupé: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title:BE:the ONE START BEYOND DREAMS:
The third installment in the "BE:the ONE" documentary series follows the popular dance and vocal group BE:FIRST on their first-ever world tour, held from April to July 2025.

Spanning 12 cities across Asia, Europe, and North America, the "BE:FIRST World Tour 2025 Who is -BE:FIRST?-" transcended language and culture to captivate audiences worldwide. This film features not only their stunning live performances but also the moments of inspiration the members found in various cities and their brief moments of downtime. Furthermore, because the members themselves took turns behind the camera, the film offers an even more authentic, true-to-life look at the group.

The documentary also focuses on RYOKI, who went on hiatus (and subsequently left the group) following the Singapore performance on July 5. It portrays the feelings of each member and their experiences on the ground, capturing their final performance as a seven-member group and their interactions backstage. Additionally, the film includes brand-new interviews capturing the raw emotions of the members after returning home, delving deep into where they stand today.
title:BRING HER BACK: After their father dies, brother Andy and his visually impaired sister Piper come to live with foster mother Laura. Also living there is a boy named Oliver who does not speak. Andy feels uneasy about Laura's seemingly excessive affection, but a new life for the siblings begins under her care. From a certain day onward, unsettling events begin to occur one after another in the house. Furthermore, there are mysterious circular motifs scattered around the house, and the presence of Oliver. When these seemingly unrelated elements all connect, Laura's hidden 'terrifying wish' is revealed.
title:BURN: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title:Beyond the Fire: The Life of Japan: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title:Blue Moon: From director Richard Linklater, known for the 'Before' trilogy beginning with 'Before Sunrise' and the six-time Oscar-nominated 'Boyhood,' this conversation piece stars his longtime collaborator Ethan Hawke and depicts a night spent at a party attended by legendary Broadway lyricist Lorenz Hart. On the evening of March 31, 1943, the night of the premiere of the musical 'Oklahoma!,' created by his longtime composing partner Richard Rodgers with a new collaborator, Lorenz Hart—the lyricist behind hits like 'The Lady Is a Tramp' and 'My Funny Valentine'—was invited to a party at the Broadway restaurant Sardi's. Over the course of that night, Hart confronts his own swirling emotions of love, jealousy, anxiety, and longing. Ethan Hawke plays Lorenz Hart, alongside Margaret Qualley as Elizabeth, the woman Hart pines for; Andrew Scott as his former partner Richard Rodgers; and Bobby Cannavale as Eddie, the bartender Hart trusts as a confidant. The film was screened in the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, where Andrew Scott won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Actor. It was nominated for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor (Ethan Hawke) at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Bonne Chance: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
title:Boy Meets Girl: The feature debut of French maverick Leos Carax, released in 1983. It depicts the encounter of two lonely souls wandering through the Paris night in beautiful black-and-white imagery, winning the Youth Prize at the 37th Cannes Film Festival and generating buzz at festivals worldwide. Alex, a young man whose best friend stole his girlfriend, has a fateful encounter with Mireille, a woman who just fought with her lover. Alex falls in love with Mireille at first sight, but they soon meet with an unexpected tragedy. The roles of Alex and Mireille were played by then-newcomers Denis Lavant and Mireille Perrier. The protagonist Alex, played by Lavant, later reappeared in transformed forms in 'Bad Blood' and 'The Lovers on the Bridge', forming what is known as the 'Alex Trilogy' along with this film. Jean-Yves Escoffier handled the cinematography and continued as cinematographer for the subsequent two films. In Japan, it was first theatrically released in July 1988, following the release of 'Bad Blood' in February of the same year. A 4K restored version was re-released in January 2026.
title:Boyfriends and Girlfriends: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title:Brand New Landscape: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.

title:Broker: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title:Bugonia: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
title:By the Stream: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:B面の夏: A man whose lover was stolen by his best friend (Kazama), a woman who loved a man for whom she felt no affection (Henmi), and a woman who longs to be alone but cannot (Ishibashi). The lives of these three individuals, each standing at a crossroads, gently intersect in a town by the sea. Because the original source material is a haiku collection by Madoka Mayuzumi, the connecting screenplay was developed entirely from scratch. Despite the unique nature of its production and release—created as a promotional video for Meiji Life Insurance to be distributed to its customers—the film boasts a cast and crew on par with any major theatrical feature.
title:CROSSING 心の交差点: Lia, a retired teacher living in Georgia, sets out for Istanbul, Turkey, alongside Achi, a young man who claims to know her missing transgender niece, Tekla. However, finding Tekla, who has vanished without a trace, proves more difficult than they ever imagined. Eventually, Lia crosses paths with Evrim, a lawyer fighting for transgender rights, and enlists her help. Why did Tekla leave Georgia? Set in Istanbul—a city where East and West converge in an evocative cultural tapestry—the journey to find Tekla becomes a path that slowly brings Lia, Achi, and Evrim closer together.

The latest film from Levan Akin, director of *And Then We Danced*.
A journey of the heart connecting past and future, woven in Istanbul—a city where encounters and farewells intertwine.
title:CURE: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title:Call Me Dragon: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title:CatVideoFest（キャットビデオフェスト）:
CatVideoFest is a globally beloved festival held annually since 2016, now screened in over 350 theaters worldwide, including the United States, Canada, and Europe. The festival features a carefully curated selection of the latest and greatest cat videos from across the globe. Cute, hilarious, and sometimes deeply moving—you can experience the full charm of these feline stars all at once on the big cinema screen!

As a theater-exclusive event, the festival has become a massive hit in the U.S., with attendance growing every year. Last year, it surpassed $1 million at the box office, proving that the unique experience of "watching cat videos together" continues to draw crowds to the cinema. These 73 minutes, filled with smiles and comfort, are truly a "dream come true for cat lovers."

Furthermore, the festival is built on a foundation of compassion: the act of watching the films directly supports cats in need. A portion of ticket proceeds is donated to animal welfare organizations. Since 2019, screenings around the world have raised over $150,000, saving the lives of countless cats. For the screenings in Japan, a portion of the proceeds will also be donated to local rescue groups to fund medical care, foster programs, and other essential support for cats in need.

Help cats just by watching. CatVideoFest is a celebration of feline wonder filled with kindness. Welcome to a "Kitty World" that fills the entire screen! This winter, treat yourself to the ultimate heartwarming cat video experience.
title:Catching the Stars of This Summer: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title:Chaser Game W: A Match Made in Hea: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
title:Chuckle Chuckle: A fusion of individuality from promising young creators. Directed by Yuka Nishida, a graduate of Kyoto University of the Arts, who now belongs to STARDUST CREATORS as a screenwriter. This film is her graduation project, made when she was 22. It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
title:Citizen Kane: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title:Climbing for Life: This drama marks Sayuri Yoshinaga's 124th film appearance and is modeled after Junko Tabei, the first woman to successfully summit the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. It portrays a female mountaineer who staked her entire life on reaching the 'top.' In 1975, as deputy leader and climbing captain of the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, Junko Tabe became the first woman in the world to summit Everest. Her achievement astonished the world and brought light to herself, her friends, and her family, but it also cast a deep shadow. Her challenges as a mountaineer continued, and in her later years, even while battling illness and after being given a terminal diagnosis, Junko continued to smile, involve those around her, and climb mountains. The cast includes Yoshinaga as Junko Tabe, a character based on Junko Tabei; Koichi Sato as her husband Masaaki; Yuki Amami as Etsuko Kitayama, Junko's ally and Everest climbing partner; and Non as the young Junko. The film is directed by Junji Sakamoto, who previously directed Yoshinaga in 'The Light of the North' and reunites with her after 13 years.
title:Close to the Bone: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
title:Cléo de 5 à 7: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.

title:Cranko: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.
title:Cruising: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
title:Cry Out: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
title:Cure: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title:Cyborg 009 and the Monster Wars: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title:DANS LA VILLE DE SYLVIA: This film follows a young aspiring painter wandering through places of memory, searching for traces of Sylvia, a woman he loved six years ago. It constructs an obsessive love story reminiscent of Alfred Hitchcock's 'Vertigo' (1958) with meticulously calculated sound and imagery, resulting in a groundbreaking work unlike anything seen before. The film was shot entirely on location in Strasbourg, France, an ancient city where medieval streetscapes and cutting-edge railways coexist without dissonance, creating a stateless atmosphere. The masterful sound design, which orchestrates the city's noises—the murmur of people, the passing of trams—like a symphony, and the beautiful, luminous chain of images captured through glass reflections and tram windows, transport the viewer into an unknown, otherworldly space.
title:DEAD OR ZOMBIE:
Set in a city overrun by zombies, this unconventional drama depicts the quiet survival of individuals struggling with the burdens of life. Originally released as the 2022 short film *DEAD OR ZOMBIE: Even if Zombies Appear, We Won't Change Our Self-Esteem*, the project was expanded with prequels and sequels to form a single feature-length film consisting of four episodes.

A zombification phenomenon breaks out in a regional Japanese city. Saki, a high school girl who had been a shut-in in her room, remains in the quarantine zone to care for her zombified family, carving out a life of survival (Episode 1: "Even if Zombies Appear, We Won't Change Our Self-Esteem").

An ancient virus is discovered in samples collected from an asteroid by a Japanese unmanned space probe, and analysis begins at the National Space Research Institute... (Episode 0: "The Origin of Life").

With the Japanese government’s response lagging, the U.S. Forces Japan take control of the quarantine zone. Meanwhile, China sends in a research institution to investigate the zombies (Episode 2: "The Will of the Universe").

title:DIE MY LOVE: Director Lynne Ramsay ("We Need to Talk About Kevin," "You Were Never Really Here") presents a psychological drama starring Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Pattinson, depicting a couple torn between love and madness. It was screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. Grace, a writer who moves to a countryside town with her husband Jackson, begins a new life. Peaceful days are shattered after childbirth: her writing stalls, and the pressure and loneliness of childcare, along with fragmentary hallucinations, gradually distort her reality. As the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs, Grace's mind quietly but surely collapses. Jennifer Lawrence, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook," plays Grace and also serves as a producer, drawing on her own childbirth experience to embody the loneliness and anxiety of a postpartum woman. Robert Pattinson ("The Batman") plays Jackson. The film is based on the novel "Die, My Love" by Ariana Harwicz, with Martin Scorsese as a producer.

title:DISTANCE: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.

title:DOPPEL:
Director Kenji Tani, known for *Reminiscence Journey Reenact*, helms this drama depicting the life of a young rookie actor set within a popular theater troupe. Troupe Byakuya, which enjoys a cult following, shifts its creative direction to cater to a new fan base after a stage adaptation of a manga becomes a massive hit. Noboru Mitsui, a newcomer to the troupe, feels frustrated and anxious that the current style is preventing him from honing his craft. With the support of the troupe’s star actor, Miyabayashi, Noboru appeals to the leader, Terada, expressing his desire to perform the kind of edgy plays they once did, and is subsequently cast as the lead in their next production. Tasked with playing an "emotionless killer," Noboru undergoes extreme character preparation as Terada’s demands during rehearsals grow increasingly severe. Eventually, Noboru begins to feel a growing anger toward himself for being unable to discard the very desire to "act."

Daisuke Morisaki, formerly of the global boy group BLANK2Y, makes his film debut as the lead, Noboru Mitsui. He is joined by Shohei Hashimoto, a veteran of numerous "2.5D" stage plays, as the troupe’s star Yosuke Miyabayashi; Yusuke Hino from the tokusatsu drama *Kamen Rider Gavv* as Tomoyuki Sotodate, a former member who holds the key to the story; voice actor and actor Shintaro Asanuma, also an active playwright and director, as the troupe leader Nao Terada; and Taro Hasegawa, the film’s screenwriter and an actor/director himself, as theater writer Harumitsu Fujimaki.
