title:Immediate Family: A music documentary tracing the journeys and bonds of four session musicians who supported the American West Coast sound. In the early 1970s, musicians Danny Kortchmar (guitar), Waddy Wachtel (guitar), Leland Sklar (bass), and Russ Kunkel (drums) participated in recordings for artists like Carole King, James Taylor, Jackson Browne, and Linda Ronstadt, who lived around Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles. Later called the supergroup "The Immediate Family," their solid playing and musical understanding contributed to the birth of many classic songs, continually supporting the artists' expressions. Through interviews with the four musicians themselves and the renowned artists they made music with, the film reveals moments of creation in the studio's closed space and the deep bonds between musicians. It also explores projects each participated in solo, depicting their rise to becoming popular musicians. Directed by Denny Tedesco, who also directed the music documentary "The Wrecking Crew" about the session musicians who supported the American music scene of the 1960s and 70s.
title:In Our Day: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:In Praise of Love: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title:In die Sonne schauen: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title:In the Mood for Love: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
title:Inside Llewyn Davis: The Coen brothers, directors of "No Country for Old Men" and "True Grit," won the Grand Prix at the 66th Cannes Film Festival in 2013 with this film. Loosely based on the life of Dave Van Ronk, a musician who represented the 1960s folk scene, it humorously depicts a week in the life of a struggling young folk singer. In the winter of 1960s New York, singer-songwriter Llewyn keeps performing at live houses but can't seem to make it big. On the verge of giving up on making a living through music, he still manages to get by with the help of his friends. Oscar Isaac, who appeared in "Robin Hood" and "Drive," plays Llewyn and also performs the songs. The music is by T Bone Burnett of "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" and "Crazy Heart."
title:Into the Belly of the Beast: A crime suspense film depicting a man consumed by a desire for cannibalism as he descends into the abyss of ruin. It won the Grand Prize at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, a first for a suspense film in the festival's history. Satō, a young man working as a host at a cabaret club, harbors a secret desire to eat people. One day, he finds a smartphone at work, which leads to him being threatened by a mysterious duo and forced into a dark side job as a courier. After making a large sum of money from the illegal but lucrative work, Satō begins to use his earnings to satisfy his hidden desires. Shun Tohari stars in his film debut as Satō. The film will be screened theatrically as part of the 'Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026.'
title:Is This Thing On?: A couple whose smooth-sailing life takes a turn and their marriage falls apart. The disheartened husband, Alex, finds a new purpose in life by turning their marital woes into comedy at a comedy club.
title:Ishibumi: A theatrical release version re-edited from a special 70th post-war anniversary program broadcast on Hiroshima TV in August 2015. It reveals the portraits of 321 first-year students of the former Hiroshima Prefectural Hiroshima Second Middle School, who lost their lives in the atomic bombing and for whom a memorial stone was erected along the Motokawa River, based on the writings of their bereaved families. While building on a reading drama broadcast on the same station in 1969, composed by Matsuyama Zenzo, it adds original elements such as projection performances using wooden boxes and interview footage by Ikezawa Akira.
title:It Was Just an Accident: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.
title:JAWAN/ジャワーン: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:JAWAN／ジャワーン: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:JOTARO: Novelist Jotaro Izumi (Sojiro Yoshimura) made a spectacular debut after winning the Bungei Prize. However, his success was short-lived; now, he spends his days in depravity, borrowing money from his editor, Eiji Matsumura (Kohshu Hirano), on the condition that he write. Pursued relentlessly by photographer Ranko Kijima (Aika Yukihira), he drifts into a relationship and moves into her home, yet the twisted desires writhing within him remain unfulfilled. It is then that Matsumura introduces him to a research subject: Anna Unabara (Suika Yamasaki), a woman once dubbed the "Beautiful Criminal" for swindling 30 million yen through sugar dating. Beneath her quiet and submissive facade lurks an inexplicable strangeness—and Jotaro begins to feel that she may be the one who can finally satisfy his desires.
title:JUST ANOTHER: A documentary following the punk band "the Genbaku Onanies" as they reached their 38th anniversary in 2020. Formed in Nagoya in 1982, the group centered on EDDIE, formerly of THE STAR CLUB, and TAYLOW, known locally as the "Punk Doctor." Through numerous lineup changes, the band is also known for having included members such as Tatsuya Nakamura (who later joined BLANKEY JET CITY) and Ken Yokoyama of Hi-STANDARD. Remaining committed to their home base in Aichi, they have held steady jobs rather than aiming for professional status, and continue to play punk rock today even after turning 60. In this film—the first documentary of their career—the members themselves reveal internal truths about the band that have never been told before. It is directed by Michiko Oishi, the filmmaker who created "MOTHER FUCKER," a documentary about the music label "Less Than TV."
title:Jack and the Witch: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
title:Jawan: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title:Jeanne Dielman, 23, quai du Commer: A masterpiece drama by Belgian female director Chantal Akerman, who left many works earnestly examining women's lives in society and daily life, carefully capturing a housewife's frustrations and details while tracing how cracks emerge in ordinary routine. Jeanne lives alone with her adolescent son in a Brussels apartment. Boiling water, peeling potatoes, going shopping—she leads an "ordinary" life, but... Starring Delphine Seyrig, known for "Last Year at Marienbad" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." Screened at the "Chantal Akerman Film Festival" (April 29 - May 12, 2022, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya).
title:Jeunes mères: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
title:Johatsu - Die sich in Luft auflöse: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). In Japan, approximately 80,000 people go missing each year, with thousands vanishing completely. Known as "evaporated people," their reasons range from relationship troubles and debt to yakuza threats. Some, with the help of so-called "night escape artists," abandon all ties and start new lives elsewhere. "Evaporation," intersecting deep loss and the hope of starting over, has been a motif in literature and film. This work uses immersive imagery to delve into the unknown work of "night escape artists" and the emotional conflicts and paths to reconciliation for both the disappeared and those left behind. It garnered attention at film festivals worldwide, winning Best Documentary at the 39th Munich International Documentary Film Festival.
title:Johatsu - Into Thin Air: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). title:John Cranko: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.
title:Jules: A human drama starring the acclaimed actor Ben Kingsley, humorously depicting a lonely elderly man who, after getting caught up in a bizarre commotion with his neighbors, rediscovers the joy of life. Milton, a 79-year-old man living in a small town in western Pennsylvania, continues to live alone despite his daughter Denise worrying about his early symptoms of dementia. One night, an unidentified flying object from the sky crashes into Milton's yard, shaking his peaceful daily life. When no one around him takes him seriously, Milton shares the secret of the flying object with his neighbors Sandy and Joyce, who are around his age and also witnessed it. The three, each carrying their own loneliness, rediscover the forgotten joys of life and face their futures. Harriet Sansom Harris ("The Bodybuilder") plays Sandy, Jane Curtin ("Coneheads") plays Joyce, and Zoe Winters (series "Succession") plays Milton's daughter Denise. The director is Mark Turtletaub, known as a producer for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Loving."
title:KEEPER キーパー: A horror film directed by Osgood Perkins of "Longlegs" fame, depicting extreme terror closing in on a woman brought to a mountain lodge by her lover, rendered in a mysterious, nightmarish world. Liz, an artist living in the city, is invited to a mountain lodge owned by her boyfriend Malcolm. Malcolm is a wealthy but somewhat enigmatic doctor, and for Liz, who wants to confirm his true feelings, this weekend trip to mark their first anniversary is supposed to be special. The lodge, reached by car driven by Malcolm, is in a remote area surrounded by dense forest. Nearby is another lodge owned by Malcolm's cousin Darren, who visits with his young lover Minka, but Liz feels repulsed by Darren's crude and intrusive manner. Encouraged by Malcolm, Liz eats a chocolate cake said to be a gift from the caretaker, and is plagued by strange nightmares and hallucinations. The next day, Malcolm is called away to the hospital for an emergency, leaving Liz alone at the lodge. Gripped by a vague unease, Liz is beset by one abnormal event after another, losing the boundary between reality and nightmare, and is threatened by the presence of something unknown stirring within the lodge. Tatiana Maslany, who also appeared in Perkins' previous film "The Monkey," plays the protagonist Liz, and Rossif Sutherland from "Orphan: First Kill" plays her boyfriend Malcolm.

title:KUBO AND THE TWO STRINGS: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
title:KUBO／クボ 二本の弦の秘密: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
Kamen Rider Decade, aka Kadoya Tsukasa, arrives in a "certain world." In this world, for some reason, the photos Tsukasa takes do not distort the image. Suddenly, a certain Western-style mansion comes to mind. Following faint memories, Tsukasa reaches the mansion, where he meets a girl who calls herself his sister, Kadoya Sayo. Tsukasa becomes convinced this is his own world. However, even in this world, the "collapse of worlds" is progressing. Sayo's servant, Tsukikage Nobuhiko, claims that the cause of the world's collapse lies in the Riders born in each world, and declares that to stop it, they must decide on a single "strongest Rider."
title:Kamen Rider Hibiki The Movie: Hibi: In present-day Japan, the giant demonic monster Orochi appears on a coast. Hibiki and Asumu rush to fight it, but Hibiki is defeated by Orochi and falls into a coma. Asumu seeks clues to save Hibiki in the Takeshi's ancient documents describing Orochi, but there he finds the name "Asumu," the same as his own, along with the stories of Oni... The ancient document tells of a village in the Sengoku period. There, Orochi demanded a human sacrifice every year. When Asumu's acquaintance Hitoe is chosen as the sacrifice, Asumu consults Tobei Tachibana to find a way to save her. Following the idea of asking an Oni for help, Asumu and the others set out to search for an Oni.
title:Kamome Diner: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
title:Kaneko Fumiko: This biographical drama centers on Fumiko Kaneko, a nihilist and anarchist who fiercely resisted Japan's state power about 100 years ago, depicting the 121 days from her death sentence to her suicide in prison. Directed by female filmmaker Sachi Hamano (known for "Yukiko-san no Ashioto"), the film draws on tanka poems that convey Kaneko's own voice to portray her solitary struggle. Born in 1903, Kaneko grew up as a "non-registered person" because her father never filed her birth registration. At age nine, she was sent to live with her grandmother and aunt in Korea, where she suffered abuse akin to slavery from a family that exploited the colonized Korean villagers. In 1919, she witnessed the March First Independence Movement in Korea. Sent back to her mother's home in Yamanashi at 16, she later struggled through poverty in Tokyo, moving ideologically from Christianity to socialism, anarchism, and finally nihilism. She eventually met Park Yeol, a Korean independence activist who had fled to Japan. Becoming comrades and lovers, they campaigned against Japanese imperialism and colonialism, but were arrested during the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake and sentenced to death. After her sentence was commuted to life imprisonment through amnesty, Kaneko was sent to Tochigi Women's Prison, where she continued her solitary fight behind bars. Nanana stars as Kaneko, embodying the soulful cry of a woman who defied state power to the end. Katsuya Kobayashi plays Park Yeol, with supporting performances by Masaki Miura, Yoko Horaguchi, and Kazuko Yoshiyuki.
title:Kantara: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.
title:Keeper: A horror film directed by Osgood Perkins of "Longlegs" fame, depicting extreme terror closing in on a woman brought to a mountain lodge by her lover, rendered in a mysterious, nightmarish world. Liz, an artist living in the city, is invited to a mountain lodge owned by her boyfriend Malcolm. Malcolm is a wealthy but somewhat enigmatic doctor, and for Liz, who wants to confirm his true feelings, this weekend trip to mark their first anniversary is supposed to be special. The lodge, reached by car driven by Malcolm, is in a remote area surrounded by dense forest. Nearby is another lodge owned by Malcolm's cousin Darren, who visits with his young lover Minka, but Liz feels repulsed by Darren's crude and intrusive manner. Encouraged by Malcolm, Liz eats a chocolate cake said to be a gift from the caretaker, and is plagued by strange nightmares and hallucinations. The next day, Malcolm is called away to the hospital for an emergency, leaving Liz alone at the lodge. Gripped by a vague unease, Liz is beset by one abnormal event after another, losing the boundary between reality and nightmare, and is threatened by the presence of something unknown stirring within the lodge. Tatiana Maslany, who also appeared in Perkins' previous film "The Monkey," plays the protagonist Liz, and Rossif Sutherland from "Orphan: First Kill" plays her boyfriend Malcolm.
title:Killer of Sheep: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:Kin-dza-dza!: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
title:Kind Hearts and Coronets: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).

title:Kokuho: A human drama depicting the tumultuous life of a man born into a yakuza family who dedicates his life to the path of art as a Kabuki actor. A talked-about sensation that has taken the Japanese film world by storm, finally screening!
title:Kraft der Utopie – Leben mit Le Co: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title:Kubo and the Two Strings: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
title:Kung Fu: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title:Kyoto Hippocrates: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title:Kék Pelikan: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title:Köln 75: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title:L'Ami de mon amie: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title:L'Argent: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:L'Avventura: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title:L'Intérêt d'Adam: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title:L'avventura: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title:LADY JANE 終幕式「破の刻」 Final Stage:
A documentary capturing the four-night final event held after the closure of LADY JANE, a venerable Shimokitazawa jazz bar that brought the curtain down on its 50-year history in April 2025.

Since its founding in 1975, LADY JANE served as a cornerstone of Shimokitazawa’s cultural scene. Visited by a multitude of artists and intellectuals—including Seitaro Kuroda, Ryuichi Sakamoto, Yusaku Matsuda, Kotaro Sawaki, and Miyuki Nakajima—the bar was a crucible where encounters between diverse talents sparked countless cultural and artistic movements. The live performances held every weekend transcended genres and career levels, serving as a beacon for aspiring artists and a space for new connections and creativity for veterans.

Though the bar closed to much regret on April 13, 2025, a final event titled "LADY JANE 50th Anniversary: 'Ha no Toki' Closing Ceremony" began just a few days later on April 17 at Shimokitazawa The Suzunari. The theater featured a recreation of the bar's interior, and the stage brought together a stellar lineup of performers connected to the establishment, including a twin-drum set by Takeo Moriyama and Tatsuya Nakamura, as well as Yoshihide Otomo, Akira Sakata, Eiko Ishibashi, Jim O'Rourke, Mariko Hamada, and actors Tomoko Nakajima and Kyoko Koizumi. From the audience, leading figures in theater, film, music, and literature, along with many supporters and associates, looked on. This film captures the essence of those four nights and brings them to the silver screen.
title:LADY JANE 終幕式破の刻〜 Final Stage:
LADY JANE: the legendary Shimokitazawa jazz bar that stood for 50 years. This documentary captures the four nights of final live performances held following its closure.

Founded in 1975, LADY JANE was a legendary establishment loved by actor Yusaku Matsuda and immortalized in song by Miyuki Nakajima. A cultural crossroads where music, film, literature, and theater intersected
title:LIVE IN THEATER「BATTLE OF TOKYO-うつ:

*No discounts applicable. Complimentary tickets and free passes are not accepted.

This theatrical release fuses animation with footage from massive live music events that embody the world of LDH JAPAN’s next-generation comprehensive entertainment project, "BATTLE OF TOKYO."

Set in the fictional future city of "Super Tokyo," "BATTLE OF TOKYO" reimagines real-life LDH artists as virtual characters, weaving a narrative that traverses both real and virtual worlds. Large-scale live events held in 2019, 2022, 2023, and 2024—featuring GENERATIONS, THE RAMPAGE, FANTASTICS, BALLISTIK BOYZ, and PSYCHIC FEVER (2023/2024 only)—have drawn a cumulative total of 500,000 attendees.

This film presents a specially edited mix of selected live performances and music videos, with audio remastered in 5.1ch surround sound. The animated segments vividly and dramatically capture the final chapter of the story based on Soki Tsukishima’s original novel, portraying the battles and bonds of five teams of young people endowed with special skills.
title:LOST LAND ロストランド: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." It depicts a young refugee brother and sister, driven from their homeland, risking their lives to cross borders in search of their family. Blending unrelenting reality with fantastical imagery, the film portrays the harrowing journey of refugees smuggling themselves across borders from a child's perspective. Five-year-old Shafi and his nine-year-old sister Somiir, living in a refugee camp, set out with their aunt for distant Malaysia, hoping to reunite with their family. Unable to obtain passports, they are led by smugglers onto a fishing boat, and despite facing the fury of nature, pursuit by security forces, and the threat of human trafficking, they desperately overcome the grueling journey. The cast includes over 200 Rohingya people, led by the siblings Somiir and Shafi in the lead roles. Their voices and gazes, as people who have themselves been driven from their homeland, lend the film a powerful realism despite their lack of acting experience. The film received high praise at film festivals worldwide, including winning the Special Jury Prize in the Orizzonti section at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025, the first time a Japanese director has won this award.
title:LOST LAND／ロストランド: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." title:La Vérité: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title:La fiebre de los ricos: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title:Lady Vengeance: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title:Late Shift: A social human drama that depicts the relentless hard work and unexpected troubles constantly falling on nurses in an understaffed, full hospital ward, which became a huge hit in Switzerland. Directed by Swiss screenwriter and filmmaker Petra Volpe, it realistically and thrillingly portrays the urgent, universal problem of hospital realities. Florie, a dedicated and highly professional nurse working in a state hospital, faces an even busier late shift than usual because a colleague is out sick. The ward is full, and she also has to train nursing students. Despite the situation, Florie treats patients with anxiety and loneliness sincerely, but she falls into an unmanageable situation and eventually faces a major trial. Leonie Benesch, known for 'The Teachers' Lounge' and 'September 5,' stars.
title:Le Bonheur: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Le Rayon vert: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title:Le quattro volte: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title:Leave the Cat Alone: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title:Legend of the Eight Samurai: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
title:Les Rendez-vous de Paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title:Like Father, Like Son: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
title:Little Amélie or the Character of: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Little Remi and Famous Dog Capi: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
title:Local Reporter: A pollution issue arises in a town in the Tohoku region, and the media war heats up... An excellent film in which Frankie plays a newspaper reporter, depicting the struggles of journalists who, while grappling with the difficulties of maneuvering in a rural setting, burn with passion for producing community-focused articles.
title:Lost Land: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." It depicts a young refugee brother and sister, driven from their homeland, risking their lives to cross borders in search of their family. Blending unrelenting reality with fantastical imagery, the film portrays the harrowing journey of refugees smuggling themselves across borders from a child's perspective. Five-year-old Shafi and his nine-year-old sister Somiir, living in a refugee camp, set out with their aunt for distant Malaysia, hoping to reunite with their family. Unable to obtain passports, they are led by smugglers onto a fishing boat, and despite facing the fury of nature, pursuit by security forces, and the threat of human trafficking, they desperately overcome the grueling journey. The cast includes over 200 Rohingya people, led by the siblings Somiir and Shafi in the lead roles. Their voices and gazes, as people who have themselves been driven from their homeland, lend the film a powerful realism despite their lack of acting experience. The film received high praise at film festivals worldwide, including winning the Special Jury Prize in the Orizzonti section at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025, the first time a Japanese director has won this award.
title:MAMMON:
A crime suspense drama centered on the theme of "yami baito" (illegal part-time jobs)—a growing social issue in recent years—depicting ordinary young people who, despite harboring dreams and ideals, struggle with the gap between their aspirations and reality, falling into an irreversible descent into darkness triggered by seemingly trivial choices.

Reiji, an aspiring photographer working part-time in Tokyo, hears that his old friend Yuya has found a job, and the two meet up with another friend, Mocchan. Reunited after a long time, they celebrate Yuya’s employment. However, in contrast to Reiji and Yuya, who are on the verge of grasping their hopes, Mocchan has already turned to a life of crime. Six months later, Yuya is laid off due to the COVID-19 pandemic and ends up getting his hands dirty in criminal activity alongside Mocchan. Meanwhile, Reiji has a precious girlfriend named Mina, but he is backed into a corner by a certain incident and begins to spiral toward his own ruin.

The film was planned and produced by "Gamushara Club," a creator team consisting of actors Yamato Tokuhiro, Kai Morishita, and Yuto Kawasaki, who have gained attention for their vertical short dramas. Tokuhiro stars as Reiji, Morishita as Mocchan, and Kawasaki as Yuya. Jita Matsunami served as director and screenwriter.
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 R・シュトラウス《アラベッラ:
The third production of the 2025–26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which brings the latest performances from New York’s Metropolitan Opera (MET) to movie theaters. This installment features Richard Strauss’s *Arabella*, an opera set to a libretto by the great Austrian writer Hugo von Hofmannsthal that depicts a tale of love woven into the aristocratic society of 19th-century Vienna (scheduled to be recorded from the performance on November 22, 2025).

Vienna, circa 1860. The family of the retired Count Waldner is on the verge of bankruptcy. Lacking the funds for marriage dowries, they have disguised their younger daughter, Zdenka, as a boy, while pinning their hopes on their eldest daughter, Arabella, to marry into wealth. Arabella, however, remains indifferent to her many suitors, including Zdenka’s friend Matteo. When Arabella finally accepts a proposal from the wealthy landowner Mandryka, a heartbroken Matteo is driven to despair. Zdenka, who is secretly in love with Matteo, grows concerned and hands him the key to her own room, claiming it is the key to her sister’s. Overhearing this, Mandryka becomes convinced he has been betrayed and flies into a jealous rage.
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 ガブリエラ・リーナ・フランク: The eighth installment of the 2025-26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which records and screens the latest opera performances at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. Based on Mexican painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, this production reverses the setting of the classic Italian opera "Orfeo ed Euridice," depicting a deceased wife returning from the underworld to her husband for just one day in "Frida and Diego: The Last Dream" (recording of the performance staged on May 30, 2026). In 1957, on Mexico's Day of the Dead. Diego, who lost his wife Frida three years earlier, is tormented by age and grief, longing to reunite with her. Meanwhile, Frida, freed from suffering in the underworld, is told by La Catrina, the guardian of the dead, that she should accompany Diego at the end of his life, and reluctantly agrees to return to the earthly world for only 24 hours. Diego and Frida have a moving reunion, but Frida is bound by a rule that she must not touch the living.
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 ジョルダーノ《アンドレア・シ:
The fourth production of the 2025–26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which brings the latest performances from New York’s Metropolitan Opera to movie theaters. This installment features "Andrea Chénier," an opera that uses the dynamic music of Verismo (realism) to depict the turmoil between a poet who met his end at the guillotine during the French Revolution, the countess who was his soulmate, and the revolutionary who loved her (scheduled to be recorded from the performance on December 13, 2025).

Paris, on the eve of the French Revolution. At the estate of the Count de Coigny, the servant Gérard harbors a growing resentment toward the establishment while secretly pining for the daughter of the house, Maddalena. At a party one evening, a guest named Andrea Chénier improvises a poem about love, striking a chord with both Maddalena and Gérard. Five years later, Gérard has risen to become a high-ranking official in the revolutionary government, yet he still cannot forget Maddalena. Now fallen from grace, Maddalena is reunited with Chénier, who has been branded an enemy of the revolution. Gérard arrests Chénier and exposes his raw desire for Maddalena, but by the time he realizes the depth of his own folly, Chénier has already been sentenced to death.
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 チャイコフスキー《エフゲニー: The seventh installment of the "MET Live Viewing" 2025-26 season, which captures and screens the latest opera performances from the New York Metropolitan Opera House in cinemas. This recording features Tchaikovsky's opera "Eugene Onegin," a tragedy of love and misunderstanding between a pessimistic young nobleman and an innocent girl, set to lyrical, famous melodies (recording of the performance staged on May 2, 2026). In 1820s Russia, at the estate of a landowner, sisters Tatyana and Olga are visited by Olga's fiancé Lensky, who brings his friend Eugene Onegin. Tatyana falls in love with Onegin at first sight and writes him a letter confessing her feelings, but Onegin gives a cold reply. Months later, at a ball celebrating Tatyana's name day, Onegin dances only with Olga, provoking Lensky to challenge him to a duel, in which Onegin kills him. Years later, returning from his wanderings, Onegin reunites with Tatyana, who has become a duchess.
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 ベッリーニ《清教徒》: The fifth production of the 2025–26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which broadcasts the latest performances from the Metropolitan Opera (MET) in New York to movie theaters. This installment features *I Puritani*, the final work of Bellini, who died at the young age of 33. A pinnacle of bel canto opera, it depicts the course of a romance
title:METライブビューイング2025-26 ワーグナー《トリスタンとイゾ:
The sixth production of the 2025–26 "MET Live Viewing" season, which brings the latest performances from the Metropolitan Opera (MET) in New York to the big screen. This installment features Wagner’s ultimate opera of love—a work overflowing with sensual music—presented through an innovative new production by Yannick Nézet-Séguin and the rapturous vocals of Lise Davidsen (scheduled to be recorded on March 21, 2026).

In the legendary Middle Ages, the Irish princess Isolde sets sail for Cornwall to enter a political marriage with King Marke, traveling on a ship helmed by the King’s nephew and loyal vassal, Tristan. Because Tristan is the slayer of her former fiancé, Isolde harbors a complex mix of love and hate toward him and attempts a double suicide by poison. However, her maid Brangäne gives her a love potion instead, leading the two to fall into a maddening passion. Although Isolde continues her trysts with Tristan even after becoming Queen, King Marke and his courtier Melot eventually return to the site of their secret meeting, where Tristan is gravely wounded by Melot’s sword.
title:MIRRORLIAR FILMS Season8:
Launched in 2020 and produced by Chikara Ito, Shinnosuke Abe, and Takayuki Yamada, "MIRRORLIAR FILMS" is a short film production project featuring a diverse range of creators spanning the gap between major and indie cinema. By Season 7 in 2025, the project will have theatrically released 52 short films directed by everyone from renowned creators to public applicants, including actors, film directors, manga artists, and musicians.

**Winner of the Short Film Special Mention at the 78th Cannes Film Festival**
**Official Selection in the Short Cuts Competition at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival**
Ali is a 15-year-old boy living with his mother in a lakeside mountain village where women are forbidden from singing. To conceal the secret hidden within Ali’s throat, his mother has carefully sewn it shut and keeps it wrapped in cloth. One day, news arrives of a singer audition being held in the village. What is the truth hidden in his throat? This is the story of Ali finding his "true voice."
Director: Adnan Al Rajeev / Cast: Al Amin, Indrani Shoma

Fumiko (Mieko Harada) is a regular at a pachinko parlor, exuding an air of elegance that seems out of place. After she leaves something behind at the shop, she visits a cafe
title:MONGOL: Screened at the 2nd Japan-Mongolia Film Festival (March 14–27, 2026, at K's cinema).

title:MOOSIC LAB2026:

"December Rain" (23 min) ©︎ "December Rain" Film Partners

An inspired film based on the classic song "December Rain," originally released in 1970 on Happy End's self-titled debut album. An "inner world road movie" following Marin, a girl searching for her birthplace, as she travels through her hometown attempting to recover paintings.

Director, Screenplay, Editor: Sawa Kawakami
