title:MOTHERLAND: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title:Maborosi: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title:Magical Secret Tour: A crime drama about three women who have drifted through life, who deepen their bond through gold smuggling and reclaim their respective lives. Director Chihiro Amano ("Mrs. Noisy") was inspired by a real 2017 incident in which housewives were arrested for gold smuggling at Chubu Centrair International Airport. She co-wrote the original script with Madoka Kumagai, with whom she also worked on "Sato-san and Sato-san." Large-scale location shooting was conducted in Singapore, depicting the glamorous yet perilous journey of gold smuggling. Wakako, a mother of two living a peaceful life, learns that her husband has been fired from his company for embezzlement. To pay off her husband's debts, she becomes involved in gold smuggling in Singapore, where she meets Kiyoe, a non-regular researcher struggling with student loan repayments, and Mayu, an unmarried pregnant woman with zero savings. After successfully smuggling gold and getting a taste for it, the three decide to start smuggling on their own. For the first time, they gain money, freedom, and the joy of living authentically, spending a magical time together—but... Kasumi Arimura plays Wakako, the mother of two who learns of her husband's embezzlement; Haru Kuroki plays Kiyoe, the indebted researcher; Sara Minami plays Mayu, the unmarried pregnant woman; Akihisa Shiono plays Wakako's husband Takashi; Yuzu Aoki plays Kiyoe's colleague Shiina; and Takumi Saito plays Takashi's boss Tanoue.
title:Mahjong Horoki: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
title:Mark Antony: This Indian sci-fi action film comically and eccentrically depicts a gangster's son who obtains a phone that allows him to talk to people in the past and tries to rewrite fate. In 1975, mad scientist Chiranjeevi invents a telephone that can call people in the past. Using it, he can avert disasters about to befall his past self or loved ones, or make choices that lead to profit. However, Chiranjeevi gets caught in a gang war at a bar while celebrating, and the phone goes missing. Twenty years later, auto mechanic Mark stumbles upon the phone and learns its special abilities and how to use it. This phone eventually sparks a massive upheaval involving Mark's foster father, gang boss Jackie; Jackie's son Madan; and Mark's deceased father, Antony. In Japan, Vishal plays dual roles as mechanic Mark and his gangster father Antony, while S. J. Surya, known for "Jigarthanda Double X," co-stars as Antony's partner Jackie.
title:Marty Supreme: A drama starring Timothée Chalamet, set in 1950s New York, inspired by the life of real-life table tennis player Marty Reisman. Marty Mauser, who dreams of becoming the world's number one table tennis player in America where the sport has low popularity, works at a relative's shoe store to raise funds to participate in the World Championships. After losing to Japanese player Endo at the World Championships held in London, Marty aims to compete in the next World Championships in Japan. With his mistress Rachel pregnant, his player eligibility revoked by the table tennis association, and his funds running out, Marty tries every possible way to raise money for the trip... Gwyneth Paltrow plays Kay, a retired famous actress; Grammy-winning artist Tyler Okonma, known as Tyler, The Creator, plays Marty's friend; Odessa A'zion plays Marty's girlfriend; Kevin O'Leary plays Milton, Kay's husband and president of an ink company; and Japanese Deaflympics table tennis representative Kōto Kawaguchi plays Japanese player Endo. Directed by Josh Safdie ("Uncut Gems," "Good Time"), the film was nominated for nine Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor.
title:Masters of the Universe: A new live-action film adaptation of the popular "Masters of the Universe" series, based on the action figures created by Mattel in 1981, which have been expanded across comics, animation, and other media, and previously adapted into the 1987 live-action film "Masters of the Universe" starring Dolph Lundgren. Prince Adam of the planet Eternia is sent to Earth as a child to protect him from war, and grows up hiding his identity. Fifteen years later, guided by the legendary Power Sword he accidentally discovers, he returns to his homeworld and learns that Eternia is under the control of his archenemy Skeletor. To save Eternia and its people, Adam transforms into the warrior He-Man and plunges into a deadly battle against the forces of evil. Directed by Travis Knight ("Bumblebee", "Kubo and the Two Strings"), with a screenplay by Chris Butler ("Missing Link"). Nicholas Galitzine, who has gained attention for roles in "Red, White & Royal Blue" and "The Idea of You", plays the lead role of Adam/He-Man. Camila Mendes ("The Revenge Swap", "Upgraded") plays the warrior Teela, who fights alongside He-Man; Jared Leto ("Tron: Ares") plays the villain Skeletor; and Idris Elba plays Man-At-Arms, a father figure to He-Man, in a star-studded cast.
title:Materialists: A love story directed and written by Celine Song of 'Past Lives,' set in the modern marriage market, depicting a love triangle with beautiful imagery. Lucy, a matchmaker at a New York dating agency, is a professional at matching clients' high ideals and detailed conditions, and a materialist who judges love not only by emotion but also by asset value. Leading a busy, work-focused life, she receives a passionate approach from Harry, a wealthy investor she meets at the wedding of a couple she matched. Meanwhile, at the same reception, Lucy reunites with her ex-boyfriend John, who was working as a waiter. They had loved each other, but she couldn't endure the poor life with John, who was drifting between part-time jobs while pursuing his dream of becoming an actor. Lucy begins a relationship with Harry, who is perfect in family background, personality, and education, but her feelings for John, who hasn't given up on his dream, are rekindled. When a client gets involved in an incident, Lucy finds herself at a crossroads in both work and love. Dakota Johnson of the 'Fifty Shades' series plays protagonist Lucy, Chris Evans of the 'Captain America' series plays struggling actor John, and Pedro Pascal of 'Welcome to Eddington' plays investor Harry.
title:Mazinger Z vs The Great Dark Gener: A theatrical version of the TV anime "Mazinger Z," featuring a piloted giant robot as the protagonist. Director Nobutaka Nishizawa heightened the drama by entrusting the robot with the protagonist's worries and pain, depicting the invincible Mazinger Z fighting while battered and broken. The surprise appearance of the successor Great Mazinger, ahead of the TV series, astonished children. "Mazinger Z" achieved strong revenue from merchandise licensing, sparking a trend of incorporating merchandising into projects from the planning stage onward.
title:Memorizu: Starring Tasuku Emoto, this drama explores themes of family memory and records. Yuta, who lives with his wife and daughter in Tokyo, travels to a rural town in Kyushu to care for his father-in-law Makoto, who has broken his leg, until he recovers. While helping out at Makoto's old-fashioned photo studio, Yuta exchanges videos taken on his smartphone with his wife and daughter back in Tokyo. Even without major events, the accumulation of daily trivial records and memories quietly and vividly reveals the long span of a family's life. Moka Kamishiraishi ("Shōgun," "Girl Encounters") plays Yuta's wife Yuki, who continues working and raising their child in Tokyo. Issey Ogata plays Makoto, the taciturn father-in-law, and Yū Kashii plays a character symbolizing precious family memories. Director Miu Sakanishi, who gained attention for short films while at Kyoto University of Art and Design and later worked as an assistant director for Yūya Ishii and a making-of cameraman for Yūichirō Doi, makes her feature-length directorial debut.
title:Merrily We Roll Along: A filmed recording of the Broadway musical 'Merrily We Roll Along,' which won four Tony Awards, screened in theaters. Based on the play of the same name by George S. Kaufman and Moss Hart, this musical, which premiered in 1981, features music by the legendary Stephen Sondheim, creator of numerous masterpieces including 'Sweeney Todd.' The story depicts the tumultuous 30-year relationship between Frank, a successful Hollywood producer; Mary, a former best-selling author; and Charlie, a Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, told in reverse chronological order. This recording captures the 2023–24 Broadway production starring Maria Friedman, which was a huge hit. Jonathan Groff, known for the Netflix series 'Mindhunter' and as the voice of Kristoff in Disney's 'Frozen,' plays producer Frank; Daniel Radcliffe of the 'Harry Potter' series plays playwright Charlie; and Lindsay Mendez, a veteran of numerous Broadway musicals, plays former best-selling author Mary. At the 2024 Tony Awards, the production won Best Revival of a Musical, Best Actor in a Musical (Jonathan Groff), Best Featured Actor in a Musical (Daniel Radcliffe), and Best Orchestrations.
title:Message from Space: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
title:Michael: A biographical film depicting the life of Michael Jackson, the "King of Pop," beloved across eras and borders for his overwhelming vocal ability and innovative dance performances. Directed by Antoine Fuqua of "Training Day" and "The Equalizer" series, it portrays Michael's story—how he transcended music to greatly impact the world—alongside his many hit songs. Michael Jackson, under his ambitious father Joseph's strict training, achieved early success as a member of the Jackson 5. Meeting legendary producer Quincy Jones, he created numerous historic hits as a solo artist and quickly became the darling of his era. But behind the glory lay the loneliness of a precocious genius, the shackles of his authoritarian father, and the struggle between his love for his family and the visions overflowing within him. The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."

The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."
title:Michael／マイケル: A biographical film depicting the life of Michael Jackson, the "King of Pop," beloved across eras and borders for his overwhelming vocal ability and innovative dance performances. Directed by Antoine Fuqua of "Training Day" and "The Equalizer" series, it portrays Michael's story—how he transcended music to greatly impact the world—alongside his many hit songs. Michael Jackson, under his ambitious father Joseph's strict training, achieved early success as a member of the Jackson 5. Meeting legendary producer Quincy Jones, he created numerous historic hits as a solo artist and quickly became the darling of his era. But behind the glory lay the loneliness of a precocious genius, the shackles of his authoritarian father, and the struggle between his love for his family and the visions overflowing within him. The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."

title:Mid-August Commotion: On August 6, 1945, the atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima, and Japan's defeat became all but certain. The Prime Minister's secretary, Nakajima, sounds out senior statesmen about accepting the Potsdam Declaration. But this peace faction's moves provoke the resistance-minded military officers. Unable to persuade the army and out of options, the Prime Minister petitions for an Imperial Conference to be held.
title:Milton Bituca Nascimento: Called the 'Voice of Brazil,' Milton Nascimento, affectionately known as Bituca, led MPB (Brazilian popular music post-bossa nova) alongside contemporaries Gilberto Gil, Caetano Veloso, and Chico Buarque, and collaborated with countless international musicians. This documentary film traces Milton's life and music while following his global farewell concert tour, announced upon turning 80 in 2022. In the first half, Milton's troupe tours Europe and the Americas, receiving ecstatic welcomes. Pat Metheny, Spike Lee, Quincy Jones, and Wayne Shorter speak about Milton, and there are scenes of collaboration with Esperanza Spalding and Herbie Hancock. Milton reflects on his childhood raised as an adopted son, converses with his own adopted child on the road, and shares memories of his benefactor, singer Elis Regina. The second half begins with the landscapes of Minas Gerais, the highland region of inland Brazil that is Milton's home and musical origin. Friends like Chico, Caetano, and Gil, collaborating poets like Márcio Borges and Ronaldo Bastos, and younger musicians who admire Milton, discuss the appeal and depths of his music. Inescapable negative histories, such as racism and Brazil's 20-year military dictatorship starting in 1964, are also revealed. Then, the farewell concert finale approaches: the concert at Mineirão, the football stadium in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. Members of Clube da Esquina (Corner Club), the title of a landmark 1972 album and the name for the family of Minas musicians centered around Milton—Lô Borges, Beto Guedes, Wagner Tiso, and Toninho Horta—share behind-the-scenes stories and perform together.
title:Mobuko's Love: Director Taichi Kazama, known for the TV drama "Silent," adapts manga artist Akari Tamura's comic into a live-action film, a love story about the first crushes of "supporting characters" who have quietly lived on the fringes of society. Shy and reserved college student Nobuko Tanaka identifies with the term "mob," meaning crowd, extra, or non-major character, and has lived her life watching from afar as other protagonists shine. Then, she notices Hiroki Irie, a young man working part-time at the same supermarket. Touched by Irie's natural thoughtfulness, Nobuko gradually becomes drawn to him. Through her encounter with Irie, she begins to struggle to break free from the shell that has bound her, and while sometimes confronted with harsh realities, she perseveres with the support of her coworkers. Meanwhile, Irie also notices Nobuko's quiet kindness and looks straight at her. The accumulation of small, everyday moments eventually gives them both the strength to take a step forward. Hiyori Sakurada ("The Diary of a Substitute Lie") plays Nobuko, aka Mobuko, and Taisei Kido ("Yukite Kaeranu") plays Hiroki Irie, the object of her first love. The cast also includes Ikoi Hayase as Nobuko's junior coworker Abe, Erika Karata as senior coworker Shinozaki, Takuya Kusakawa as fellow part-timer and Irie's friend Kaneko, Tsubasa Araki as new part-timer Ono, and Kanji Furutachi as store manager Orihara.
title:Mononoke the Movie: Chapter III -: The concluding chapter of the theatrical trilogy based on the TV anime "Mononoke," itself a spin-off from the "Bakeneko" segment of the 2006 Fuji TV Noitamina omnibus anime "Ayakashi." It delves into the greatest secret long hidden within the Ooku (the shogun's harem) and depicts the fierce battle between the protagonist, the Medicine Seller, and the most fearsome mononoke of all, the Serpent God, which threatens to shake the Ooku to its foundations. After a deadly struggle with the Medicine Seller, who carries a exorcism sword, and a Tengu umbrella, followed by a decisive battle with the Fire Rat, peace finally seems to have returned to the Ooku. However, the Medicine Seller senses a lingering presence and remains on guard. Around this time, the shogun's official wife, Sachiko, gives birth to a long-awaited son, but the infant soon dies. Sachiko, who had hoped to change her formal marriage to the shogun by bearing an heir, is physically and emotionally exhausted and becomes entangled in a conspiracy that could overturn the Ooku's very existence. Hokuto Mizorogi, the priest of the "Mizusama" faith within the Ooku, watches the events unfold with a solemn expression. At the same time, unnatural earthquakes, as if a giant creature is crawling, occur frequently within the Ooku, and bizarre incidents happen where maids are twisted and crushed to death. Before the Medicine Seller, who rushes to the scene, appears the mononoke Serpent God, taking the form of a giant snake.
title:Monster: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title:Motherland: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title:Mothertongue:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.
title:Mouchette: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title:Mrs. Warren's Profession: One of the National Theatre Live series, which films and screens selected acclaimed stage productions from the UK's Royal National Theatre in cinemas. This recording captures 'Mrs. Warren's Profession', featuring five-time Laurence Olivier Award winner Imelda Staunton performing alongside her real-life daughter Bessie Carter. Vivie Warren is a young woman with progressive ideas. Her mother, however, while upholding the old patriarchal system, has built a fortune by exploiting that very system. But a heavy price lies hidden behind it all. This play by Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw, known for 'Pygmalion' and a Nobel laureate in Literature, is directed by Dominic Cooke, who has also worked on screen productions such as the BBC series 'The Hollow Crown' and the film 'The Memory of Justice'. The cast also includes Kevin Doyle from 'Downton Abbey' and Robert Glenister from 'Into the Sky'.
title:My Brother's Wedding: A director's cut, completed in 2007 through re-editing, of Charles Burnett's second feature film from 1983. Burnett, an influential figure in American independent cinema who consistently depicts the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, presents a tragicomedy of a working-class young man torn between family, friendship, and identity. It quietly reveals class differences within the Black community, psychological gaps between generations, and the frustration of young people left behind by social success, all from the gaps in everyday life. Pierce, a 30-year-old helping his parents run their dry-cleaning shop, drifts aimlessly through his days with no clear future. His childhood friends are either in prison or already dead. When his brother, a lawyer, marries a woman from a wealthy family, Pierce's discomfort and feelings of inferiority grow. Around this time, Pierce reunites with his best friend Soldier, just released from prison, and finds himself caught between his sense of duty to his family and his loyalty to his friend, forced to make a choice. In Japan, this 4K restored version will have its theatrical premiere at the special screening series 'Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues' (from February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:My Mind Is Always Racing: A film themed around the 'quarter-life crisis,' a psychological state common among people in their late twenties to thirties who feel vague anxiety and restlessness about the future, unable to live the life they imagined. Directed by and starring Reimi Miyamori, it won the Actor Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for independent films. Nozomi, a 25-year-old woman who moved to Tokyo to become a novelist, is struggling and going nowhere. In her mind, 18-year-old Nozomi, living a rural high school life, asks her if she has truly followed through on her words and made it big in Tokyo. While resisting a frustrating life where she wants to change but cannot, the 25-year-old Nozomi confronts her 18-year-old self and begins to notice various things she had never faced before. This is the debut feature film of Reimi Miyamori, a graduate of the Nihon University College of Art's Film Department who began making films during the COVID-19 pandemic. She served as director, screenwriter, producer, and lead actress. It was screened in theaters as part of the 'Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024' (May 9 – June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title:NEW GROUP: The second theatrical release from director Yuta Shimotsu, who gained attention for his 2024 commercial film debut "May the Lord Be with You". It comically and seriously explores the underlying psychology of human behavior in group activities, specifically through the lens of group gymnastics, with a unique worldview. High school girl Ai, who has family problems, is shy and unable to assert her own opinions. Transfer student Yu, who has returned from overseas, is the type to speak her mind clearly and struggles to fit into the group-oriented, harmony-focused activities of Japanese schools. Ai is interested in Yu, but Yu grows frustrated with Ai's inability to express herself. One day, a student in the schoolyard freezes on all fours. Soon, other students begin lining up beside him in the same position, forming a massive human pyramid. Strangely, the school encourages participation in the human pyramid as a "good thing," and the stacked students all wear serene expressions. As students gather one after another and obey without a word, Ai herself becomes dazed and nearly joins the pyramid. The situation eventually escalates into a collective supernatural phenomenon engulfing the entire region. Anna Yamada (from the "Golden Kamuy" series) plays the protagonist Ai, and Yuzu Aoki (from "5 Centimeters per Second") plays the transfer student Yu. Pierre Taki delivers a bizarre performance as the principal who leads the group. The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 29th Fantasia International Film Festival in 2025.
title:Nameless: A film adaptation of the psycho-violent manga "Nanashi" by Sato Jiro—who is active not only as an actor but also as a screenwriter and film director—marking his first work based on a manga. Sato stars and wrote the script, with Hideo Shijo of "Bad Summer" directing. A brutal murder occurs at a family restaurant in the afternoon. Security cameras capture a bald middle-aged man who appears to be the culprit, but he holds no weapon. The footage records the bizarre sight of people spurting blood and collapsing just from the man approaching and lightly touching them. Investigating police identify the bald man as "Taro Yamada," who was questioned for shoplifting 11 years earlier. When investigators rush to Yamada's home address, they find a decomposed female corpse. Sato plays the protagonist, serial killer Yamada. Takaya Kamikawa plays Teruo, the patrol officer who becomes the namesake for the nameless orphaned young Yamada. MEGUMI plays Hanako Yamada, who grew up with Yamada in the same children's home and lives with him. Kuroudo Yashima plays Detective Kunieda, who works tirelessly to stop Yamada.
title:National Theatre Live: Hamlet: One of the 'National Theatre Live' productions, where the UK's Royal National Theatre films selected acclaimed stage performances for cinema screenings. This recording features 'Hamlet' starring Sri Lankan-born actor Hiran Abeysekara, who won the Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor for his performance in 'Life of Pi' at the Royal National Theatre. Surrounded by power and privilege, the young Prince Hamlet wavers between duty and doubt. He confronts the ultimate question: 'To be, or not to be.' Directed by Robert Hastie, who became Associate Artistic Director of the Royal National Theatre in January 2025, offering a contemporary perspective on Shakespeare's masterpiece. Co-stars include Alistair Petrie, known for 'The Bank Job' and 'Rush,' Ayesha Dharker, known for 'Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones,' and Francesca Mills, known for the Netflix series 'The Witcher: Blood Origin.'
title:Never Give Up: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.

title:No Other Choice: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title:Nobody Knows: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
title:Nothing But Bones: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title:Notre Musique: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).

title:Nouvelle Vague: From the director of "Boyhood" and the "Before" series, Richard Linklater, comes a film that goes behind the scenes of Jean-Luc Godard's "Breathless"—a landmark work of the French New Wave, the revolutionary film movement that emerged in the late 1950s. It depicts the young people who sparked a revolution in film history, along with their vibrant interactions with the leading filmmakers of French cinema. In 1959, France. Jean-Luc Godard, a 28-year-old critic writing for the film magazine "Cahiers du Cinéma," begins production on his feature directorial debut, "Breathless," starring French up-and-coming actor Jean-Paul Belmondo and American starlet Jean Seberg. Those around him are thrown off by Godard's innovative and freewheeling shooting methods, but the set, fueled by a shared passion for filmmaking, is filled with energy. Following the style of "Breathless," the film is shot in black and white in the Academy ratio (1:1.37), almost entirely in French, and the cast, except for Zoey Deutch as Jean Seberg, is made up of mostly unknown actors. Guillaume Marbeck, who worked as a photographer and model, was cast as the protagonist Godard. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title:O-Bi, O-Ba: The End of Civilizatio: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:O-bi, o-ba. Koniec cywilizacji: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. title:OXANA 裸の革命家・オクサナ:
2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother who devotedly supports him, earning a living for the family by painting icons. However, unable to endure the unfair treatment from the church and the deep-seated misogyny of an irrational society, she flees her home.

In 2008, she forms the feminist activist group "FEMEN" alongside comrades she met during street debates. Their activities expand, beginning with a protest against the death of a female patient due to medical malpractice. In 2009, while campaigning to eradicate sex tourism in the capital city of Kyiv, Oksana strips to the waist to garner attention, arriving at a mode of expression that utilizes the body as "combat gear."

Before long, their activism crosses borders. In 2011, she is detained and tortured for protesting the Alexander Lukashenko regime in Minsk, Belarus, and later sustains serious injuries during a protest against Vladimir Putin in Moscow. As surveillance and suppression of FEMEN intensify, Oksana is forced to make the decision to flee to Paris as a political refugee...
title:OXANA／裸の革命家・オクサナ: 2002, Khmelnytskyi, Western Ukraine. Oksana lives with her alcoholic father and her mother, who devotedly supports him. She helps provide for the family by painting icons, but unable to endure the unfair treatment from the church and the injustices of a deeply patriarchal society, she flees her home. In 2008, alongside comrades she met at street debates, she co-founds the feminist activist group "FEMEN." Their activities expand, beginning with a protest against the death of a female patient caused by medical malpractice. In 2009, while campaigning to eradicate sex tourism in the capital, Kyiv, Oksana strips to the waist to draw attention, arriving at a form of expression that uses the body as "combat gear." Their activism eventually crosses borders. In 2011, she is detained and tortured while protesting the Alexander Lukashenko regime in Minsk, Belarus, and later suffers serious injuries during a protest against Vladimir Putin in Moscow. As surveillance and suppression of FEMEN intensify, Oksana is forced to make the decision to flee to Paris as a political refugee...
title:Oldboy: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title:On Falling: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title:Once We Were Us: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title:One Last Throw: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title:Oslo, 31. august: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).

title:Our Little Sister: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title:PEAK END: A feature film directed, planned, and starring Korean-born filmmaker Shin Chae-rin, created as her graduation project from the Kyoto University of Arts Film Department. Shot with a minimal production setup and incorporating documentary elements, it was screened at various film festivals, including being an invited work at the 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival and selected for the 47th Pia Film Festival. Rin, who came to Kyoto from Seoul, and Sora, who came to Kyoto from Okinawa, meet at university and aspire to make films. They give form to the impulses and desires that arise in their daily lives through the act of 'making a film.' Their relationship, which seeks to know each other through actions like sending jam sandwiches flying into the sky or tracing roots in Okinawa, continues to change. Shin Chae-rin plays Rin, and Sora Itami from Okinawa plays Sora, both also participating in the production. The film was made by a small team of five staff members, including the two actresses.
title:PERFECT BLUE 4Kリマスター版:
[Admission Fee] 1,600 yen flat rate
*No discounts applicable. Complimentary tickets and free passes cannot be used.

The 1998 debut feature of animation director Satoshi Kon, who received high acclaim both in Japan and abroad for works such as "Paprika" and "Millennium Actress." Based on Yoshikazu Takeuchi's novel "Perfect Blue: Complete Metamorphosis," the film depicts the nightmare-like events that befall a woman transitioning from a pop idol to an actress.

Mima Kirigoe leaves her idol group to pursue a career as an actress. While bewildered by a series of provocative jobs that shatter her previous image—including a rape scene in a TV drama and a nude photo book—she steadily gains recognition. Meanwhile, a series of murders targeting those close to her occurs. An individual posing as Mima begins posting detailed diary entries online, and she gradually becomes terrified by the shadow of a stalker.
title:PLAYLIST アジアの才能: An omnibus film collecting works from five young directors from Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Selected from short films screened at the 20th and 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival, these five works showcase next-generation talent, arranged like a music album under the 'PLAYLIST' concept. Though each piece differs in setting and style, they capture universal emotions—love, growth, loss, identity—through the eyes of today's youth. The lineup includes: 'Boxing Day' by China's Zhang Xiaoyi, depicting a nurse who develops feelings for a discharged boxer and is led into a strange dream; 'Suzuki' by South Korea's Ahn Jung-min, following a middle schooler who loves Western music and grows through admiration and unexpected loss after meeting someone in a chat room; 'Rooftop Lempicka' by Vietnam's Nguyen Luong Hang, showing a 10-year-old girl glimpsing the adult world through a Tamara de Lempicka art book found in a bookstore and interactions with a waitress; 'Black Dog' by Taiwan's Yang Lin, exploring family through a girl's attempt to solve the mystery of strange howling from her father's room at night; and 'Melting in the Street' by Japan's Nako Komiyama, depicting queer children who are drawn to each other as they share secrets, along with their struggles and a small escape.
title:PRETTY CRAZY: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title:Paris ni Saku Étoile: Set in early 20th-century Paris, this animated film delicately and vividly portrays the struggles of two Japanese girls pursuing their dreams in a foreign land. In Paris at the turn of the century, two girls who came from Japan live there. One is Fujiko, who dreams of becoming a painter despite being expected to become a good wife supporting her husband. The other is Chizuru, born into a samurai family and a master of the naginata, but drawn to ballet. The two, who met once in Yokohama, reunite after five years when Chizuru helps Fujiko out of trouble. Learning of Chizuru's dream, Fujiko discovers that Olga, the mother of a young man named Ruslan living in the same apartment building, is a former Russian ballerina and arranges lessons for Chizuru. Meanwhile, Fujiko's guardian uncle goes missing. Ami Touma voices the protagonist Fujiko, who dreams of being a painter; Rina Arashi voices Chizuru, who aspires to be a ballerina; and Taichi Saotome voices Ruslan, the young man who meets Fujiko. Directed by Goro Taniguchi of "ONE PIECE FILM RED" and the "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion" series, with original character designs by Katsuya Kondo, who worked on character design and key animation for Studio Ghibli films like "Kiki's Delivery Service." The screenplay is by Reiko Yoshida of "The Colors Within" and "Violet Evergarden."
title:PascaLs しあわせのようなもの: A documentary about the acoustic orchestra band "Pascals," led by Rocket Matsu. Formed in 1995, the group has garnered popularity for their unique, euphoric sound. They have composed numerous scores for films, television dramas, and stage productions—including *The Fish Child* and *Riverside Mukolitta*—and have received high acclaim internationally, particularly in France. While the band had performed with the same lineup for approximately 25 years, cellist Kota Miki passed away suddenly in April 2020. Focusing on memorial concerts held in the spring of 2021 and 2022 during the pandemic, the film captures their music as they grapple with "a presence defined by absence." Directed by Shinichi Ise, the documentary filmmaker behind *Nao-chan* and *Now is Past: My Father, Java & the Phantom Films*.
title:Pastoral: To Die in the Country: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title:Pauline at the Beach: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Pauline à la plage: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title:Pelikan Blue: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title:Petite Maman: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title:Piccola felicità（ピッコラ・フェリチタ） 小さな幸せ: The fourth feature film directed by actor Yutaka Mizutani, familiar from the "Aibou" series. Mizutani also handles planning, script, production, and lead acting, as unpredictable stories intertwine involving three couples in their 60s, 40s, and 30s. Sato, retiring after 25 years at a restaurant, divorced and unable to see his daughter, feels his life is over. A small miracle brings him unexpected joy. Fujio, who runs a painting class, struggles under his painter father's shadow, drowning in alcohol and women daily. Divorce from his estranged wife Miki seems inevitable, but Fujio's final confession changes everything. Reo, working at a hotel, falls in love at first sight with Aoi, whom he meets at a café, and they quickly fall for each other. But Reo learns a secret about Aoi. The human dramas of these three couples are depicted with a theme color set for each story. Alongside Mizutani, the cast includes Nobue Iketani, Nanahana, Gamon Kaiga, Shuri, and Jun Hashimoto. This film marks the first parent-child co-starring role for Mizutani and Shuri. Cinematography is by Masahiro Aida, who also worked on the "Aibou" series, and music by Yoshiki Yamamoto from Mizutani's previous film "Taiyo to Bolero."
title:Pickpocket: Michel, a poor university student, discovers by chance that he has a talent for pickpocketing. Though once caught by a detective, he is released due to lack of evidence and soon targets others' wallets again. Eventually, his methods become organized as he brings in accomplices. In 'A Man Escaped,' Bresson realistically and thrillingly depicted a prison break; here, he turns his focus to pickpocketing, introducing actual techniques while portraying a lonely young man distrustful of others. A gripping masterpiece where the realism born from amateur actors and the suspense created by various pickpocketing scenes blend seamlessly.
title:Playback: A drama captured in beautiful monochrome cinematography, following an actor at a crossroads in life as he moves between the past and present to take a new step forward. The film is the second feature from up-and-coming director Sho Miyake. Haji, an actor on the verge of turning 40, finds himself at a professional standstill, burdened by a mounting series of personal struggles including failing health and a separation from his wife. It is then that Bon, a high school friend he hasn't seen in years, appears and invites him to their hometown for the wedding of another old friend, Yuji. While traveling to his hometown in Bon’s car, Haji drifts off to sleep, only to wake up and find himself transported back to his high school days twenty years ago—yet still in his adult body. Led by Jun Murakami, the film features a talented ensemble cast including Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Masaki Miura, Makiko Watanabe, and Shun Sugata.
title:Point Blank: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
title:Pola X: The fourth feature film by French wunderkind Leos Carax, released eight years after 'The Lovers on the Bridge.' An adaptation of the novel 'Pierre' by 19th-century American author Herman Melville, written the year after his masterpiece 'Moby-Dick.' Shifting the setting to modern-day Paris, it uses emotional imagery and sound to depict the intense, racing love of a man and woman swept up by fate and drawn into despair. Pierre, a young novelist living in a Norman castle, enjoys a wealthy, contented rural life with his mother Marie and fiancée Lucie. One day, Isabelle, a Bosnian refugee claiming to be Pierre's half-sister, appears. Drawn to Isabelle's charm, Pierre abandons everything and heads to Paris with her. Guillaume Depardieu, son of Gérard Depardieu, passionately plays Pierre, and Katerina Golubeva, known for 'Paris at Night,' plays Isabelle. Catherine Deneuve co-stars as Pierre's mother Marie. Cinematography is by Éric Gautier, known for 'My King,' and music is by singer-songwriter Scott Walker. A 4K restored version will be re-released in February 2026.
title:Pretty Crazy: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title:Priest of Darkness: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title:Primavera: A drama based on the true story of composer Vivaldi's appointment as a violin teacher at the Ospedale della Pietà in Venice in the early 18th century, depicting the growth of a lonely girl whose talent blossoms under his guidance, and Vivaldi's inner ambition, craving recognition for his own genius. Venice, 1716, at the Ospedale della Pietà. Cecilia, raised without knowing her mother's presence or love, secretly slips out of bed every night to write letters to her mother with no address. To leave the Pietà and live in the outside world, her mother must come for her, or she must marry a nobleman. Amidst this, Antonio Vivaldi, arriving as a violin teacher, discovers Cecilia's exceptional violin skill and appoints her as the leader of the first violins. Under Vivaldi, Cecilia endures rigorous practice, hones her violin skills, and they gradually grow close. However, the officer the Pietà has chosen as Cecilia's husband returns from war, and an incident soon occurs. Tekla Insolia, noted for the Italian TV drama 'The Art of Joy,' plays Cecilia, and Michele Riondino of 'The Sleeping Beauty' plays Vivaldi. The film is directed and written by Damiano Michieletto, a leading Italian opera director who served as creative director for the opening and closing ceremonies of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics.
title:Project Hail Mary: A film adaptation of the bestselling science fiction novel by Andy Weir, author of "The Martian" (the basis for the Oscar-nominated "The Martian"). It depicts a middle school science teacher entrusted with the fate of Earth on the brink of extinction, who encounters an unknown life form with the same purpose at the edge of the universe, and together they risk their lives to save their home planets. An unexplained anomaly occurs where the sun's energy is being drained. If this continues, Earth will freeze and humanity will perish. It is discovered that the same phenomenon is happening not only to the sun but to countless stars scattered across the universe, and a single intact star is found 11.9 light-years away. Humanity's only remaining option is to travel to that star in a spaceship and solve the mystery to save the sun and humanity. Sent into space for this "Hail Mary" project is Grace, a brilliant scientist who left academia and now works as a humble middle school teacher. Alone in the vastness of space far from Earth, he relies on his scientific knowledge to tackle the mission, where he meets Rocky, an alien also struggling to save his home planet. Despite their different forms and languages, the two use science as a common language to face challenges, developing a friendship along the way. Ryan Gosling of "La La Land" and "Barbie" plays the protagonist middle school teacher Grace, with Sandra Hüller of "Anatomy of a Fall" and "The Zone of Interest" co-starring. Drew Goddard, who also worked on "The Martian," wrote the screenplay, and Phil Lord & Christopher Miller, known for producing and writing the "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" series, directed.
title:Proof of the Man: A black man is murdered in an elevator at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, leaving behind the word 'Stoha' and a poetry collection by Saijo Yaso. Fashion designer Kyoko Yasugi and her son appear and disappear along the investigative trail. Detective Muneyori travels to the United States to trace the black man's past. The unexpected relationship between Kyoko and the black man, as well as the connection between the American detective and Detective Muneyori, comes to light.
title:Puella Magi Madoka Magica the Movi: The first part of a two-part theatrical film reconstruction of the 12-episode TV anime 'Puella Magi Madoka Magica,' which aired from January to April 2011. One day, a mysterious transfer student named Homura Akemi arrives at the middle school attended by Madoka Kaname, an ordinary girl living a mundane life. After school that day, guided by a mysterious voice, Madoka encounters a strange creature calling itself Kyubey, who tells her, 'I want you to make a contract with me and become a magical girl.' The staff from the TV series, who built its unique worldview, including chief director Akiyuki Shinbo, screenwriter Gen Urobuchi (Nitroplus), and the otherworldly space design team Gekidan Inu Curry, have reunited for this film.
title:Pusher: Frank, a highly skilled drug pusher, makes money with his partner Tony by carrying out jobs for drug kingpin Milo. After taking a huge loan from Milo for a large deal, a police raid causes the deal to fail, and Frank loses the money, facing relentless pressure from his boss to repay the debt. A crime action drama that depicts a man spiraling into a hellish debt trap in the underworld of rampant drug trafficking, pushed to his absolute limits, all rendered in dark, stylish visuals. This is Nicolas Winding Refn's landmark debut film, hailed as the Danish film that first achieved worldwide success as a gangster movie.
title:Quatre nuits d'un rêveur: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title:REDLINE:
Based on an original story by Katsuhito Ishii (director of *Shark Skin Man and Peach Hip Girl* and *The Taste of Tea*), director Takeshi Koike—who helmed the "World Record" segment of the omnibus *The Animatrix*—brings this vision to life as an animated feature with a relentless commitment to hand-drawn techniques. The film depicts daredevil racers competing in "REDLINE," a race held once every five years to determine the fastest in the universe, brought to life through overwhelming visuals that took seven years and 100,000 hand-drawn frames to produce.

The cool protagonist JP, sporting a pompadour and leather jacket, is actually a shy and pure-hearted man. To win the heart of his first love, Sonoshee, he decides to enter "REDLINE," an anything-goes car race held in the military nation of "Roboworld." He enters the race in the ultimate machine customized by his childhood friend and genius mechanic, Frisbee, but the car has been rigged with a trap for match-fixing.

The film features a star-studded voice cast, including Takuya Kimura as JP, Yu Aoi as Sonoshee, and Tadanobu Asano as JP’s partner and mechanic, Frisbee. The screenplay was co-written by original creator Ishii alongside Yoji Enokido (*Neon Genesis Evangelion*) and Yoshiki Sakurai (*Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex*). Animation production was handled by Madhouse (*Summer Wars*).

Originally produced and released in 2010, the film saw a revival screening in February 2021 for its 10th anniversary. In December 2025, it will be screened as part of the special feature "Katsuhito Ishii World 30th Anniversary," celebrating the 30th anniversary of Ishii’s directorial debut.
title:RIP SLYME THE MOVIE 25th ANNIVERSA:
A live performance and documentary film featuring RIP SLYME, the pioneering group credited with pushing Japanese hip-hop into the mainstream. Following their major debut in 2001, the group made history with their 2002 sophomore album *TOKYO CLASSIC*, which became the first hip-hop album in Japan to achieve one million copies in sales. Producing a string of hits such as "One," "Rakuen Baby," and "Nettaiya," they paved the way for a generation of artists who followed in their footsteps. In April 2025, the five original members reunited for a limited time leading up to March 22, 2026, the 25th anniversary of their major debut. The release of their new song "Do ON" in May of that year garnered massive attention from both long-time fans and the "Reiwa generation" discovering them for the first time. 

The film captures RIP SLYME’s past and present, blending recent live performances and backstage footage with archival clips, a special New Year’s shrine visit filmed specifically for this project, and interviews with those close to the group. It is directed by Hiro Kanai, the acclaimed director behind hit TV dramas such as *The Confidence Man JP* and *HERO*, who shares a long-standing bond of trust with the members.
title:Red Peony Gambler: Flower Cards Ga: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
title:Rendezvous in Paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title:Rental Family: Brendan Fraser, winner of the Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Whale," stars in this human drama shot entirely in Japan. Directed by Japanese filmmaker HIKARI, who gained attention for her feature debut "37 Seconds" and the drama series "Beef," the film follows a down-on-his-luck actor living in Tokyo who rediscovers himself through working for a rental family service. Philip, an American actor who once dominated toothpaste commercials but has since been largely forgotten, lives in Tokyo, eking out a living in the acting world and blending into the city. One day, he is hired by Tada, who runs a rental family company. The job involves playing the role of a cherished "family member" for clients in exchange for payment. Initially hesitant about delving into others' lives, Philip begins to change as he interacts with the people he meets through his work. Takehiro Hira plays Tada, the rental family company owner; Mari Yamamoto plays Aiko, an actress working for the company; and Akira Emoto plays Kikuo, an aging actor.
title:Reprise: The feature directorial debut of Joachim Trier, a Danish director distantly related to Lars von Trier who studied film in Denmark and England, released in 2006. This is the first work of the "Oslo Trilogy," which also includes his later films "Oslo, August 31st" and "The Worst Person in the World." Philip and Erik are childhood friends who have dreamed of becoming writers since they were kids. One day, they both send manuscripts to a publisher, but only Philip's is accepted. Philip becomes a suddenly famous author, but soon begins to suffer mental instability. Meanwhile, Erik continues writing novels without giving up... Anders Danielsen Lie, who stars in all three films of the "Oslo Trilogy," plays Philip. Selected as Norway's entry for the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, it received high praise, winning the Grand Prix (Best Film), Best Director, and Best Screenplay at the Amanda Awards, Norway's equivalent of the Academy Awards. It received its first theatrical release in Japan as part of the special screening series "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (starting February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita and other venues in Tokyo).
title:Returnees（リターニーズ） 元こども兵 それぞれの再起: Set in Uganda, East Africa, this documentary follows former child soldiers struggling to reclaim their lives and the efforts of a Japanese NPO supporting them. For over 20 years, Uganda was gripped by conflict between the government and the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), an anti-government insurgent group. During the civil war, the LRA abducted more than 30,000 children, forcing boys into combat and girls into forced marriages with soldiers. The LRA continues to operate from neighboring countries, where they still carry out child abductions. In 2023, approximately 140 former child soldiers and their families escaped from these active conflict zones. Known as "returnees," these individuals were kidnapped as children, deeply traumatized, and robbed of their futures. Having grown up in brutal conditions, they lack formal education and struggle to meet even their most basic needs. Shingo Ogawa, a director of the NPO Terra Renaissance, has developed a three-year training program to support their reintegration, standing by them as they work to regain their self-esteem and find a place in society. Recording these efforts over a period of two years, the film captures the former child soldiers as they take their first courageous steps toward a new life.
title:Rhapsody, Rhapsody: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
title:Riceboy Sleeps: Set in 1990s Canada, this drama weaves the bond between a Korean immigrant mother and her son through beautiful 16mm film imagery. Soyoung, who became an unwed mother after losing her lover, moves with her infant son Donghyun to a suburb of Vancouver, Canada. Starting work at a factory, Soyoung faces language and cultural barriers as well as racial discrimination, but raises her son with determination. When Donghyun turns 16, he goes by the English name "David" and has fully adapted to life in Canada, but deep down he yearns to know his roots and the father he has never met. Then one day, receiving shocking news, the mother and son return to Korea for the first time, confronting a painful past. Director and screenwriter Anthony Shim, who himself immigrated from Korea to Canada at age eight, powerfully yet delicately portrays the fluidity of immigrant identity and the conflict and renewal between parent and child. Choi Seung-yoon, active in Korea as a dancer, choreographer, and actor, plays mother Soyoung, and Ethan Hwang of the drama "The Umbrella Academy" plays the teenage Donghyun.
