title:Rich Flu: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title:Rokkoku Kitchen: A documentary that observes people's lives and the present state of Fukushima through the dining tables of those living along National Route 6, commonly known as "Rokkoku," where areas still remain designated as difficult-to-return zones.
title:Romance Express: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.
title:Room for Let: In a large rundown house overlooking the Tsutenkaku Tower in Osaka, a group of eccentric lodgers live... Frankie, in his famous partnership with Kawashima, plays a laid-back jack-of-all-trades who works as a ghostwriter and konnyaku maker. With unique supporting actors like Naniwa and Ozawa, this is a brilliant ensemble comedy that leaves a lasting impression.
title:Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orc: Ryuichi Sakamoto performed with a full orchestra in Japan for the first time in 16 years at the acclaimed concert "Playing the Orchestra 2013." As an updated version, the 2014 Tokyo concert, which he conducted himself, became "Ryuichi Sakamoto | Playing the Orchestra 2014." At this concert, Sakamoto played the piano while conducting all pieces, performing a diverse repertoire—from YMO-era classics to masterpieces like "Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," as well as his film scores—with the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra.
title:Ryuichi Sakamoto | Trio Tour 2012:
World-renowned musician Ryuichi Sakamoto’s "Trio Tour 2012"—a concert series performed in a trio arrangement of piano, cello, and violin—comes to the big screen. In 1996, Sakamoto released the album *1996*, a work that achieved peak musical expression through a simple trio configuration, leading to a highly acclaimed world tour. In 2012, he produced the long-awaited trio album *THREE* and embarked on a 12-show tour of Japan and South Korea alongside long-time collaborator Jaques Morelenbaum (cello) and Judy Kang (violin), who was selected through an online audition. 

The repertoire includes classics from his YMO days, iconic film scores such as "Merry Christmas Mr. Lawrence" and "The Last Emperor," and the new piece "Shizen no Koe." Furthermore, reflecting the tour’s visit to the Tohoku region just one year after the Great East Japan Earthquake, the performance also features the charity song "Kizuna World" and "Yae no Sakura," the main theme for the Taiga drama set in Fukushima. This film captures the complete performance at Tokyo’s Akasaka ACT Theater, a show where a sense of tension and intimacy quietly coexisted. The audio has been specially reconstructed for the cinema to faithfully recreate the atmosphere of the venue to the fullest extent.
title:SAGRADA: El misteri de la creació: A documentary about the Sagrada Família, the century-spanning architectural project conceived by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, under construction since 1882 for over 130 years. Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2005, the Sagrada Família continues to captivate over three million visitors annually from around the world. As construction continues towards a projected completion in 2026, computers have been introduced on site, and staff repeatedly experiment to determine how to best reproduce Gaudí's vision with current technology. Incorporating footage from inside the site, inaccessible to outsiders, and interviews with architectural staff, the film unravels the project surrounding the Sagrada Família, including how the construction period, once said to require '300 years until completion,' has been shortened to a projected completion in 2026.
title:SAKAMOTO DAYS: A live-action film adaptation of the hit comic by Yuto Suzuki, serialized in Shueisha's "Weekly Shonen Jump", starring Ren Meguro of "Snow Man". It comically depicts a legendary retired hitman running a small shop who throws himself into battle to protect his beloved family and peaceful daily life. Sakamoto Taro, once feared as the "strongest ever," falls in love at first sight with a woman named Aoi who works at a convenience store, and promptly retires from being a hitman. After marrying and having a daughter, he becomes the manager of a small shop called "Sakamoto Store" and enjoys a happy family life, having grown so fat that he no longer resembles his former self. One day, a 10 billion yen bounty is suddenly placed on Sakamoto, and assassins from all over the world attack him. With his former subordinate, the esper Shin, as his partner, Sakamoto rises to protect his peaceful daily life. Meguro uses special makeup to portray two contrasting versions of Sakamoto: a plump one weighing an estimated 140 kg and a sleek one who rapidly loses weight when he gets serious, and also takes on full-fledged action scenes. Takahashi Fumiya plays Sakamoto's partner Asakura Shin; Ueto Aya plays Sakamoto's wife Aoi; Yokota Mayuu plays Lu Shaotang, a tai chi expert working at Sakamoto Store with Shin; Tozuki Junki plays Masumo Heisuke, a skilled sniper; Kitamura Takumi plays Nagumo, a member of the hitman world's highest force "ORDER"; Yagi Yusei plays Kamigami; and Nemu Yumemi plays Daibutsu. Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
title:SAYAMA みえない手錠をはずすまで: This documentary follows Kazuo Ishikawa and his wife, Sachiko. Ishikawa was convicted of the 1963 "Sayama Incident"—the murder of a high school girl in Sayama City, Saitama—through a forced confession and fabricated evidence, and he continues to maintain his innocence to this day. Having endured 32 years in prison and 19 years on parole, Ishikawa has lived with the stigma of being a murderer for over half a century. Despite his petitions for a retrial being repeatedly rejected, he and Sachiko continue their fight for justice. Through their unwavering journey and their perspective that they were "unlucky, but not unhappy" despite a lifetime of hardship, the film conveys universal messages about the beauty of life, happiness, love, friendship, and justice.
title:SEX:
The first installment in a trilogy by Norwegian director Dag Johan Haugerud—a former bestselling author and librarian—this film explores three perspectives on "romance," "love," and "sex" set in the Norwegian capital of Oslo. With a comedic touch, it depicts two married men as they reconsider their "masculinity" following unexpected experiences.

The two men, both chimney sweeps with families, find their lives disrupted. One discovers a new sense of excitement after an unexpected sexual encounter with a male client; however, his relationship with his wife becomes strained when he tells her about the experience without a hint of remorse. The other begins to wonder how his own identity is shaped by the gaze of others after dreaming that David Bowie perceives him as a woman. Having lived as "good fathers" and "good husbands," both men must now confront their own sense of masculinity and identity.

The film won three awards at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024, including the Ecumenical Jury Prize. In Japan, it will be released in theaters in September 2025 as part of the special screening series "Oslo: Three Landscapes of Love," alongside the other entries in the trilogy, "LOVE" and "DREAMS."
title:SHIBOYUGI: Playing Death Games to: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
title:SPh: Director Macoto Tezka’s first feature-length 16mm film. "Sph" is an abbreviation for "Spiritual Phenomenon" (fairy phenomenon). Moe Imai plays the heroine, a fairy.
title:Sai: Disaster: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.
title:Sailor Suit and Machine Gun: The boss of a small yakuza gang called Medaka-gumi, who has only four underlings, dies leaving a will stating that his successor must be a blood relative. Around the same time, high school girl Izumi Hoshi is saying her final goodbye at the crematorium to her father Takashi, who died after being hit by a car in front of Narita Airport. Izumi's mother passed away long ago, leaving her truly alone. When Izumi returns to her apartment, a woman named Mayumi is there, carrying a letter from her father that says, 'If I die, please take care of Izumi.' The next day, a crowd of men in black suits lines up in front of her school. Ignoring her friends Tomoki, Tetsuo, and Shuhei, who try to stop her, Izumi heads toward the school gate. The man from the crematorium steps forward and says, 'You're Izumi Hoshi, right?' This man, named Sakuma, takes her to a shabby office and asks her to succeed as the fourth-generation boss of the Medaka-gumi.

Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
title:Sans toit ni loi: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
title:Sarvam Thaala Mayam: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title:Sasuke and His Comedians: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title:Scarborough: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
title:Scarface: A violent action film starring Al Pacino from 'The Godfather' series, depicting the rise and fall of a man climbing Miami's criminal underworld in the 1980s, with extreme violence. Directed by Brian De Palma, written by Oliver Stone, it is a modern remake of Howard Hawks' classic gangster film 'Scarface'. In 1980, many criminals flood into America among Cuban refugees. Tony Montana, an anti-Castro exile arriving in Miami, takes on a hit at a refugee camp for Frank, a Miami drug lord. Tony gains trust through drug deals and murders for Frank, while also falling for Frank's mistress Elvira. As Tony rises in the underworld, his arrogance and insatiable greed drive him toward destruction. Al Pacino embodies Tony's madness and desire with intense performance. Steven Bauer plays Tony's right-hand man Manny, Robert Loggia plays drug lord Frank, and Michelle Pfeiffer plays Frank's mistress Elvira. With domestic screening rights ending at the end of June 2026, a 4K revival screening is held.
title:Sedmikrásky: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title:Sentimental Value: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title:Sgt. Frog: As part of the 20th-anniversary project for the TV anime "Sergeant Keroro," based on the manga by Mine Yoshizaki serialized in "Monthly Shonen Ace" since 1999, this theatrical anime is the first in 16 years since "Keroro Gunso the Super Movie: Creation! Ultimate Keroro, Wonderous Time-Space Island!!" in 2010. It depicts the Keroro Platoon, who were supposed to invade Earth, fighting to protect the planet from a new invader. Sergeant Keroro and his platoon members, who came to Earth to invade but now spend their days idly at their host family's home, encounter mysterious phenomena occurring across the country. Feeling a sense of crisis, the Keroro Platoon rises to the challenge, putting their pride as invaders on the line, but they encounter mysterious letters wherever they go. The screenplay and general direction are handled by Yuichi Fukuda, known for directing the live-action "Gintama" series. The staff includes key members who have supported the series, with Satoshi Ozaki as director, Satoshi Koike as character designer, and BN Pictures handling animation production. Jesse from SixTONES voices the theatrical original characters, the brothers Aruru and Deruru, playing both roles.
title:Shall We Dance?: Directed by Masayuki Suo of "Sumo Do, Sumo Don't" fame, this heartwarming comedy became a huge hit by depicting a middle-aged man rediscovering his life through ballroom dancing. Shohei Sugiyama is an ordinary salaryman with no complaints about his work or family life, yet he feels a vague emptiness. One day, on the train home from work, he spots a woman standing by the window of a dance studio and is captivated by her beauty. Later, he begins learning ballroom dancing at that very studio and becomes deeply absorbed in the world of dance through interactions with a colorful group of fellow students. Koji Yakusho plays the protagonist Sugiyama, while ballerina Tamiyo Kusakari plays Mai. In 2004, the film was remade in Hollywood starring Richard Gere and Jennifer Lopez.

title:Sheep in the Box: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title:Shinpei: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.

title:Shoplifters: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "The Third Murder" and "Our Little Sister," this human drama portrays human connections through the lens of a family that engages in petty crimes together. At the 71st Cannes Film Festival in 2018, it won the Palme d'Or, the top prize, for the first time for a Japanese film since "The Eel" in 1997. It also earned high praise overseas, including a nomination for Best Foreign Language Film at the 91st Academy Awards, the first for a Japanese film in a decade. At the 42nd Japan Academy Film Prize, it won eight awards, including Best Picture. In a working-class district of Tokyo, in an old one-story house seemingly left behind among high-rise apartments, live the homeowner Hatsue, the couple Osamu and Nobuyo, their son Shota, and Nobuyo's younger sister Aki, all dependent on Hatsue's pension. They make ends meet by shoplifting, living on the fringes of society, yet their days are filled with laughter. One winter day, Osamu brings home a little girl shivering on the balcony of a nearby apartment complex, and Nobuyo decides to raise her as a daughter. Triggered by an incident, the close-knit family begins to fall apart, revealing the secrets and desires each of them harbors. Alongside regular Kore-eda collaborators Lily Franky as the father Osamu, who repeatedly shoplifts with his son, and Kirin Kiki as Hatsue, the film marks the first Kore-eda works for Sakura Ando as Nobuyo and Mayu Matsuoka as Aki, Nobuyo's sister.
title:Sing Street: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
title:Sinners: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
title:Sinsin and the Mouse: A human drama based on a story from Banana Yoshimoto's short story collection 'Mitten and Fubin', co-produced by Japan and Taiwan. It quietly depicts a woman carrying loss who, through encounters in a foreign land, gradually finds renewal. Chizumi is a woman living each day with deep grief after losing her mother. As time passes without filling the void in her heart, she is invited by a friend to visit Taiwan. There, she meets Shin-shin, a young man with a Taiwanese mother and a Japanese father. The unfamiliar cityscapes and the accumulation of casual conversations slowly begin to move her frozen heart, and Chizumi, while still carrying her lingering sense of loss, discovers small warmth. Yukino Kishii ('Small, Slow but Steady', 'Just the Two of Us') plays the protagonist Chizumi, and popular young Taiwanese actor Tseng Jing-hua (known for 'The Soul of the Prisoner', 'Your Name Engraved Herein') plays Shin-shin, the young man she meets in Taiwan. The cast also includes Tokio Fujiwara, Seina Nakata, Tokio Emoto, Kayo Ise, Kisuke Iida, and Kimiko Yo. Directed and scripted by Yukinori Makabe ('I Am a Monk.', 'Scoop!').
title:Sirat: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Sirāt: This road movie, blending a fantastical story with cool dance music, follows a father and son's journey through a desert rave party in search of a missing daughter, sparking buzz across Spain and Europe. Luis drives with his son Esteban from the Moroccan mountains deep into the desert to find his daughter, who disappeared after attending a desert rave. They reach an outdoor rave site where reality and hallucination blur, but she is not there. The father and son chase a group of ravers, heading to the next rave site where they believe she went. Sergi López ("Pan's Labyrinth") plays father Luis. Directed and written by Oliver Laxe ("Fire Will Come"), the film is produced by renowned Spanish master Pedro Almodóvar. The title "Siraat" means "path" in Arabic and, in a religious sense, symbolizes the narrow bridge over heaven and hell on Judgment Day. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won four awards including the Jury Prize. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film and Best Sound at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Small Things Like These: Starring Cillian Murphy of "Oppenheimer," this film adapts the bestselling novel "Small Things Like These" by Irish author Claire Keegan. Set against the backdrop of the real-life human rights abuses at Ireland's Magdalene laundries, it depicts the inner conflict and decision of a man who discovers a truth society has long ignored. In 1985, in a small Irish town, coal merchant Bill Furlong lives modestly with his family. One day before Christmas, while delivering coal to a local convent, a girl confined there begs him, "Please get me out of here." Confronted with the reality of young women suffering with no way out, Bill understands it would be wise to look the other way, but his conscience torments him, leading him to make a fateful decision. Emily Watson of "Breaking the Waves" plays the convent's Mother Superior, Sister Mary, winning the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024. Eileen Walsh of "The Magdalene Sisters" plays Bill's wife, Eileen. Murphy, who fell in love with the original novel, personally pushed for the film adaptation and served as a producer for the first time. Directed by Tim Mielants of "Peaky Blinders," the film also features Matt Damon as a producer and Ben Affleck as an executive producer.
title:Snow as Flowers: Niino’s Snow Fest: A documentary by filmmaker Shinkichi Noda, who continually explored the foundations of people's consciousness in rapidly changing Showa-era Japan. This film captures the "Niino Snow Festival" of Nagano Prefecture, seeking to find the enduring spirit of the people within this festival that has continued since medieval times. The Niino Snow Festival has been held since around the 13th century, centered around Izu Shrine and Suwa Shrine in Niino, Anan Town, Nagano Prefecture. People see the falling winter snow as rice flower blossoms, a harbinger of the harvest, and pray for abundant grain. Throughout the night-long festival, masked and costumed performances like "Kyoman" (horse racing), "Okina" (old man), and "Oni" (demon) appear one after another, and the crowd erupts when the spirit of bounty, "Saiho," makes its entrance. Director Noda attempts to read the everyday wishes of farmers for the coming year's production within this sacred festival space. This film is part of the special screening series "Shinkichi Noda Special: Snow is a Flower" (screening from December 6, 2025, at Pole Pole Higashi-Nakano and other theaters nationwide).
title:Solaris: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
title:Song Sung Blue: A musical drama starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson in their first collaboration, based on the true story of a married couple who performed as a tribute band to American national singer Neil Diamond. Mike, who once dreamed of a music career, now can only get on stage by imitating someone else's singing, hitting rock bottom in life. One day, he meets Claire, a woman with the same passion, and they form a tribute band to their beloved Neil Diamond. Starting from a small garage, their voices gradually capture the hearts of the people in their town. But then, a sudden tragedy strikes them. Jackman and Hudson deliver powerful performances of Neil Diamond's classic songs, including 'Sweet Caroline.' The cast includes Michael Imperioli from 'The Sopranos,' Ella Anderson from 'The Glass Castle,' and singer-songwriter King Princess. Based on the 2008 documentary of the same name, Craig Brewer, director of 'Hustle & Flow,' wrote and directed the film. Hudson was nominated for Best Actress at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:Sorda: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title:Sound of Falling: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title:Soylent Green: Directed by Richard Fleischer of "Fantastic Voyage" fame, this 1973 near-future sci-fi film adapts Harry Harrison's novel "Make Room! Make Room!" and depicts various social issues such as overpopulation, extreme weather, food shortages, resource depletion, ecological collapse, and poverty. In 2022, New York City is suffering from explosive population growth, leaving people homeless and food shortages commonplace, while rapid climate change has subjected the city to heat waves. In a world of extreme inequality, most people spend their days idly waiting for the weekly government ration of the nutrient food "Soylent." Amidst this, a murder occurs: Simonsohn, an executive of the Soylent Corporation who just announced the new product "Soylent Green" as the ultimate nutrition, is killed. Homicide detective Thorn takes on the investigation... Charlton Heston of "Ben-Hur" stars as Detective Thorn, with Edward G. Robinson of "Little Caesar" co-starring. A digitally remastered version was revived in theaters in May 2024.
title:Spalovač mrtvol: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:Spider-Man 2: THE RIVER, one of Japan's largest overseas pop culture media outlets, celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2026. "REVIVAL by THE RIVER" is a new project expanding the community of online film fans into the real-world space of movie theaters. THE RIVER brings the films we once longed for back to the big screen. THE RIVER reunites films with their audiences! The commemorative first screening is 'Spider-Man 2'! Two years after the fierce battle with the Green Goblin, college student Peter Parker struggles with part-time jobs and classes while fighting for justice, leading a hectic life. Torn between his love for MJ and his friendship with Harry due to his identity as Spider-Man, Peter accepts his fate. A new enemy, Doctor Octopus, stands in his way. The most powerful action entertainment ever, surpassing its predecessor and achieving historic box office records. Flat rate of 1,600 yen (free tickets, invitation tickets, and various discount services not applicable). Online/TCG members: June 23 (Tue) 18:00~. General sale: June 23 (Tue) 21:00~. Box office sales begin June 24 (Wed). Screenings: July 3 (Fri) ~ July 9 (Thu), one screening per day at 18:10.
title:Spy Game: Brad Pitt and Robert Redford, the duo from 'A River Runs Through It', reunite. A story of the passionate friendship between CIA spies and a desperate rescue mission.
title:Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Gro: The first theatrical feature film in about seven years from the globally popular sci-fi saga "Star Wars". It depicts on a grand scale the story of the lone bounty hunter Mandalorian and the young Force-sensitive being Grogu, as portrayed in the drama series "The Mandalorian". Set in the galaxy after "Star Wars: Return of the Jedi", the era is chaotic, with the New Republic's rule incomplete and outlaws and Imperial remnants running rampant. Amidst this, the orphan Grogu, who possesses immense Force power, is pursued by those who covet his strength. The bounty hunter Din Jarin, aka the Mandalorian, decides to protect him, and as they travel through a dangerous galaxy, they gradually develop a father-son bond. The film shows a grown Grogu using the Force powers he honed under Luke Skywalker's training, and features intense, fast-paced battles against Imperial remnants, delivering the large-scale action unique to the "Star Wars" series. A new character, Colonel Ward, is played by the renowned actress Sigourney Weaver. Dave Filoni, Lucasfilm's Chief Creative Officer, serves as executive producer, and Jon Favreau directs, bringing together the creators behind "The Mandalorian" series.
title:Still Walking: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
title:Stop Making Sense: A live documentary of the rock band Talking Heads. Capturing their 1983 stage performance at the Pantages Theatre with various camera angles, it conveys the raw energy and excitement directly.
title:Stray Kids: The dominATE Experienc:
A live documentary following the world tour of the globally renowned K-pop group Stray Kids.

Stray Kids is an eight-member South Korean boy group that debuted in March 2018 with the mini-album *I am NOT*. They have garnered significant attention as a highly talented group whose members write, compose, and produce their own music. With eight consecutive number-one albums on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart, they have built a massive following not only in Korea and Japan but across the entire globe.

From 2024 to 2025, the group embarked on their largest world tour to date, "dominATE," performing 56 shows across 35 countries and regions. This film follows the tour closely, centering on their electrifying performance at the massive SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. It also features behind-the-scenes footage and exclusive interviews where the members speak candidly about their individual struggles and passions. From their overwhelming stage presence to their unfiltered moments backstage, the film captures the moments that define Stray Kids' identity. The documentary is directed by Paul Dugdale, who has previously worked on live concert films for world-class artists such as Adele and Taylor Swift.
title:Striking Rescue: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
title:Summer Days with Coo: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
title:Supergirl: A DC Universe film following James Gunn's 2025 "Superman," this hero action movie centers on Supergirl / Kara Zor-El, the cousin of Superman / Clark Kent. In a world after Superman saved Earth, Kara Zor-El, who lost her home planet Krypton, lives quietly with her beloved dog Krypto, her only emotional anchor. One day, a mysterious enemy named Krem suddenly appears and poisons Krypto. To obtain the antidote, Kara embarks on a grand cosmic battle alongside Lucy, an alien girl whose family was also taken by Krem, and a vicious bounty hunter robot. Millie Alcock, the young Australian actor who gained attention for the TV series "House of the Dragon," reprises her role as Supergirl / Kara Zor-El from "Superman." Evey Ridley (Netflix's "3 Body Problem") plays the alien girl Lucy Mary Noelle, and Jason Momoa ("Aquaman," "A Minecraft Movie") co-stars as the bounty hunter robot. Superdog Krypto, who appeared in "Superman," also returns. Produced by James Gunn's DC Studios following "Superman," the film is directed by Craig Gillespie ("I, Tonya," "Cruella").
title:TATAR: Screened at the 2nd Japan-Mongolia Film Festival (March 14–27, 2026, at K's cinema).
title:THE A-CARE -Disusebody-: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
title:THE LAST DANCE: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
title:THE LAST PIECE Glow of Stars:
Director: Taiyo Kitamura, Hiroshi Kawaguchi
STARGLOW RUI, STARGLOW TAIKI, STARGLOW KANON, STARGLOW GOICHI, STARGLOW ADAM
title:THE LONG WALK: The first-ever film adaptation of Stephen King's first novel, "The Long Walk," written while he was in college in the 1960s and published under the pseudonym Richard Bachman in 1979. In a near-future America divided by war, a national competition called "The Long Walk" is held as a beacon of hope for a struggling society. Fifty selected teenage boys challenge this contest, where the only requirement is to keep walking. The prize is a staggering sum of money and the fulfillment of one wish. The rules are simple: maintain a pace of 4.8 km/h, receive a warning if you slow down, be executed after three warnings, and keep walking until only one person remains. Surrounded by armored vehicles and under the threat of guns, the boys desperately continue walking in extreme conditions with no rest or sleep allowed... Starring Cooper Hoffman ("Licorice Pizza") and David Johnson ("Alien: Romulus") as the young participants, and Mark Hamill ("Star Wars" series) as the Major who oversees the competition. Directed by Francis Lawrence ("The Hunger Games" series) with a screenplay by J.T. Molner ("Strange Darling").
title:THE ORIGIN OF ULTRAMAN: A documentary produced to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the landmark special-effects drama series 'Ultraman.' The special-effects TV drama 'Ultraman,' which first aired in 1966, achieved a peak viewership rating of 42.8% and sparked a social phenomenon. Even over 60 years since its birth, Tsuburaya Productions continues to release new Ultraman series works, beloved across generations and borders. This film is planned by filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu, known for 'Monsters' and 'Shoplifters,' and features numerous leading creators from film, special effects, and design. Filmmakers Guillermo del Toro, Kore-eda Hirokazu, and Nicolas Winding Refn, game creator Kojima Hideo, anime director Anno Hideaki, and special effects/film director Higuchi Shinji, among others active at the forefront of their fields both in Japan and abroad, offer their unique perspectives to unravel the question, 'What is Ultraman?' The film explores the worldview where the protagonist is a hero yet carefully depicts the background of the kaiju, and the strong appeal of the designs of both Ultraman and the monsters, while also shedding light on the ideas and work of Tsuburaya Eiji and the staff of that era, tracing the journey of how Ultraman spread across the world.
title:TOCHKA トーチカ: An unconventional film that depicts the drama woven by a man and a woman who meet by chance, drawn to the darkness of the "pillbox group," war ruins built on the coast of Nemuro, Hokkaido for border defense at the end of World War II and still standing without being demolished, set almost entirely in a single location. Nemuro, Hokkaido, a town on the border with Russia at Japan's easternmost point. In the winter-barren wilderness, pillboxes built during World War II and now weathered are scattered. A man is staring intently at one of these pillboxes, and a woman inside the pillbox happens to see him. Guided by memories recounted by the man, the two trace back through hidden time. Starring Yoko Fujita from "Dog and Cat" and Shun Sugata from "The Last Samurai." Directed by Hiroyuki Matsumura, a native of Hokkaido. Screened in the "Japanese Cinema: A Different Perspective" section of the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2008. Theatrically released in 2009, with a revival release in 2026.
title:TOKYO BURST-犯罪都市-: STORY: In the dark city of East Asia, Shinjuku's Kabukicho district. A man walks with a swagger, cutting through the wind: Aiba Shiro, a rookie detective at the Shinjuku Central Police Station. Born and raised in Kabukicho, Aiba, a former bōsōzoku gang leader, is always causing trouble due to his physical strength and hot-blooded nature. One day, Korean National Police Agency detective Choi Si-woo arrives in Japan, pursuing a heinous internationally wanted criminal syndicate. From day one, the two clash and are on the verge of conflict, but with information that the wanted criminals are hiding in Kabukicho, they form an impromptu partnership and begin a joint investigation. As they investigate while remaining at odds, a certain group robbery incident triggers a massive conflict between a violent yakuza group and Kabukicho's largest host club group. Furthermore, the criminal syndicate joins the fray, and Shinjuku, transformed into a battlefield, is enveloped in chaotic darkness. And lurking behind it all is a vast conspiracy involving state power.
title:TOKYOタクシー: Master filmmaker Yoji Yamada, directing his 91st film, brings together Baisho Chieko and Kimura Takuya as leads in this human drama about the joys of life, based on the 2022 French film "A Taxi for Paris." Taxi driver Koji Usami is tasked with driving 85-year-old Sumire Takano from Tokyo's Shibamata to a nursing home in Hayama, Kanagawa. Sumire asks him, "For my last look at Tokyo, there are a few places I'd like to stop by," and Usami follows her instructions, driving her around various locations. As they share the journey, Sumire gradually opens up and reveals her surprising past. The chance encounter between a taxi driver and his passenger sets both their hearts and lives in motion. Alongside Baisho as Sumire and Kimura as driver Usami, Aoi Yu, making her sixth appearance in a Yamada film since "My Wife is a Rose: Family is Tough III," plays the young Sumire. Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
title:TRAVERSE 2 Next Level: The sequel to the action film "TRAVERSE," starring martial arts karateka Jun Tabei. Five years have passed since the battle against the Japanese branch of the massive crime syndicate "Sasori" (Scorpion). To escape the syndicate's reach, Jun Takanashi and his stepdaughter Rina have been living quietly in a remote mountain area, concealing their names and identities. However, Sasori dispatches the "Cleaners"—an elite unit of former soldiers—to track them down. Eventually, the Cleaners locate the father and daughter and launch an assault. Following the previous film, Jun Tabei, who brings his experience as an action actor to the role, returns to star as the protagonist Jun Takanashi. Newcomer Saki Nakano was selected through auditions to play his stepdaughter, Rina. Zen-tetsu Haku, who served as the action director for the first film and is an active stuntman, takes the helm as director.
title:TRUE KYOHEI SAKAGUCHI SHOW 坂口恭平生活:
A documentary capturing the life and creative output of Kyohei Sakaguchi, a multi-disciplinary artist active as a writer, painter, musician, and architect. Born in Kumamoto Prefecture in 1978, Sakaguchi is known for numerous works, including *0-Yen House*, a photo book documenting the dwellings of the homeless, and *How to Build an Independent State*, which reexamines the role of government and the nation. In 2011, spurred by a lack of trust in the government’s response to the Great East Japan Earthquake, Sakaguchi declared the establishment of a "New Government" in his hometown of Kumamoto and began accepting evacuees at his base, "Zero Center." Since 2012, he has made his personal phone number public to continue "Inocchi no Denwa" (Telephone of Life), a telephone consultation service for those struggling with suicidal ideation. Sakaguchi is also open about his own experience with bipolar disorder, at times sinking into deep depression to confront himself.

New director Yuki Komiya, making his feature debut, began following Sakaguchi over a long period after visiting a solo exhibition and filming a live performance as an audience member. The film records Sakaguchi's daily life in Kumamoto, as well as his exhibitions and events across the country. Even as filming was interrupted when Sakaguchi fell into a deep depression during production, the documentary vividly captures the process of him giving birth to new words while facing a fundamental "loneliness" he has carried since before his childhood. Director Komiya personally edited footage previously released on YouTube to complete this theatrical version.
title:Tange Sazen and the Pot Worth a Mi: A commotion over a pot that reveals the hiding place of a large sum of money draws in the swordsman Sanzen... A delightful gem showcasing the talent of Yamanaka, who lightly and skillfully portrays Daigoro's signature role of Sanzen.
title:Tange Sazen: Heavenly Clouds, Eart: Master director Takashi Kato depicts the process by which Tange Sazen loses his right eye and right arm, with a realism unprecedented in conventional sword-fighting films. Based on the original story by Fumio Hayashi. Ordered by Soma clan lord Nakamura Daizen to steal the famous swords Ken'un and Konryu, Sazen sneaks into the dojo of Onozuka Tessai but only manages to take Ken'un, losing his right eye to Tessai's blade. Hearing this, Daizen abandons Sazen and plots to gather men to attack the dojo again. Enraged by his master's cold treatment, Sazen storms the dojo once more to seize Konryu.
title:Tange Sazen: The Million Ryo Pot: Known as a masterpiece by early Showa period master Tomu Uchida, who died at just 28, this period drama stars Denjiro Okochi as the ronin Tange Sazen. Tange Sazen, a ronin living at an archery range and working as a bodyguard, and the proprietress Ofuji take in Chobian, the son of a man stabbed to death at the shop. Chobian carries a certain pot around carefully, using it as a goldfish bowl, but it actually contains a hidden map to a million ryo. This is one of only three surviving films by Uchida, most of whose original prints have been lost. It was remade in 2004 as "Tange Sazen: The Million Ryo Pot" starring Etsushi Toyokawa.
title:Ten Dark Women: A black comedy directed by Kon Ichikawa and scripted by Natto Wada, weaving together a philandering man, his wife, and nine lovers. TV producer Matsukichi Kazama, despite having a beautiful wife named Futaba, is cheating with nine women. The wife and lovers are vaguely aware of each other's existence and fully know that Matsukichi is a womanizer, yet for some reason they cannot leave him. One day, the wife and a stage actress lover named Ichiko come up with a plan to kill Matsukichi. It is a fictional scheme meant to vent their frustration with him, but timid Matsukichi becomes convinced that his lovers are trying to kill him and consults his wife. The wife readily admits to the plan and then, to eliminate the lovers, suggests staging a fake murder: they gather the lovers for a meeting to denounce Matsukichi, and at that gathering, pretend to shoot him dead with a pistol.
title:That Day, on the Beach 4K Restorat: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title:The Bibi Files: A documentary that delves into the corruption allegations against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Following the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel by the Islamic fundamentalist organization Hamas, the Israeli military began its assault on the Gaza Strip, leading to the seemingly endless Gaza-Israel conflict with massive loss of life. A key figure in this conflict is Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a charismatic leader whose hardline political stance is controversial. He is also the first sitting Israeli prime minister to be criminally indicted. In 2017, as the corruption investigation progressed, parts of police interrogation records of Netanyahu and his associates were secretly leaked to the film's production team. These records documented collusion with business and media circles, bribery, and provision of benefits. The film features testimonies from former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, a former head of the domestic intelligence agency Shin Bet, Netanyahu's former spokesperson, and prominent investigative journalists. It exposes how corruption led to national decay, and how Netanyahu colluded with far-right forces to maintain his long-term rule and avoid conviction, pushing democracy into crisis. Netanyahu himself sought to stop the film's release and threatened legal action; it was banned from screening in Israel. Alex Gibney, known for 'Taxi to the Dark Side' and 'Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room,' served as executive producer, and Alexis Bloom, director of 'Anita: Speaking Truth to Power,' directed the film.
title:The Big Lebowski: A comedy directed and written by the Coen brothers (Joel and Ethan), who won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay for 'Fargo,' about a man mistaken for a millionaire with the same name and caught up in a kidnapping plot. Los Angeles, 1991. The Dude, an unemployed middle-aged man living a carefree, day-to-day existence, is mistaken for millionaire Jeffrey Lebowski and threatened by two thugs for a debt. Angered, the Dude barges into Lebowski's mansion to demand compensation but is turned away. A few days later, summoned by Lebowski, the Dude is asked to deliver the ransom for Lebowski's kidnapped wife, Bunny. The cast features an ensemble of distinctive actors, including Jeff Bridges in the lead role, John Goodman, and Steve Buscemi.
title:The Cell: The Campbell Institute on the outskirts of Chicago. Young psychologist Catherine is researching technology to enter the human subconscious and dreams. She receives a request to look inside the mind of a serial killer who derives sexual pleasure from watching a woman drown while trapped in a glass cell.
title:The Chatterboxes: A comedy about a prideful feud between a deaf Japanese family and a Kurdish family, told through Japanese Sign Language and Kurdish. Natsumi Koga lives with her deaf father and younger brother, who run an electronics shop. One day, their family gets into a minor conflict with a Kurdish family living in the same town. Natsumi, who can hear, and Hiwa, the only member of the Kurdish family who speaks Japanese, are drafted as interpreters for their respective families. As they interpret for each other, a bond of trust grows between Natsumi and Hiwa, but the conflict between the two families only deepens. Then one day, a mysterious drawing by Natsumi's younger brother Shun escalates into an incident that engulfs the entire town. Nagisa Nagashima of "The End of Love" plays the protagonist Natsumi. Kazuyoshi Kezuka, a deaf ramen shop owner in Tokyo's Nishi-Nippori, makes his acting debut as Natsumi's father. Hideaki Nasu of the TV drama "Deaf Voice: Court Sign Language Interpreter" and Akito Imai of "The Two Worlds of My Life" play the father's friends. Shunya Itabashi of "Laughing Kaibutsu" plays a community organizer planning a town revitalization project, and Karin Ono of "Animation x Paralympic: Who Is the Hero?" plays a teacher at a school for the deaf. The film is directed by Ken Kawai, known for works like "Nanno-chan's Second World War" and who is himself a CODA (Child of Deaf Adults).
title:The Cremator: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:The Curse of the Cat People: The directorial debut of Robert Wise, the master behind "West Side Story" and "The Sound of Music," made in 1944. This is a sequel to the cult horror film "Cat People" directed by Jacques Tourneur. A lonely, imaginative girl named Amy finds a beautiful ring in a dilapidated old house in her neighborhood. When she returns home and makes a wish on the ring, a beautiful woman named Irena appears before her. Amy becomes friends with Irena, whom only she can see, but...
title:The Day the Earth Stood Still: A flying saucer suddenly arrives in Washington. An alien named Klaatu lands and, concerned for Earth's future, demands that humanity abandon nuclear weapons. He declares that if his demand is not accepted, he will shut down all energy on Earth...
title:The Devil Wears Prada 2: A sequel to the 2006 hit film "The Devil Wears Prada," based on the bestselling novel of the same name by American author Lauren Weisberger, set 20 years later. Miranda rules the fashion world as the charismatic editor-in-chief of New York's top fashion magazine "Runway." Andrea, who was once hired as her assistant and endured grueling days under her strict perfectionism, now works as a news reporter. One day, learning that Miranda and her right-hand man Nigel are facing a crisis, Andrea returns to "Runway" as a features editor. She also reunites with her former assistant colleague Emily, who has become an executive at a luxury brand and holds the key to "Runway's" survival. As their dreams and ambitions clash, events take an unexpected turn. The cast reunites from the previous film, including Meryl Streep as Miranda, Anne Hathaway as Andrea, Emily Blunt as Emily, and Stanley Tucci as Nigel. David Frankel returns as director, and Aline Brosh McKenna as screenwriter.
title:The Fifth Horseman Is Fear: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:The Four Times: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title:The Gaze of Sisyphus: A youth suspense film depicting the struggles and growth of a university student working on a documentary about an incident that occurred in a certain local city. University student Mayu Kuroda is tasked with creating a documentary for a class project based on her own high school experience. Back then, rumors spread that a male teacher, Nitta, had engaged in inappropriate sexual acts with her senior in the broadcasting club, Nojima, whom she admired. Articles in weekly magazines and social media posts drastically changed Nojima's life. Feeling this situation was unjust, Mayu intended to create a work that would serve as a warning about the information society by reflecting on that time. However, as she proceeds with research and filming alongside her university classmates, she is confronted with the reality that the local community is not welcoming the reopening of the case. Furthermore, facts she didn't know at the time and the various intentions of those involved and related parties come to light. Director Hiroki Inoue, highly acclaimed domestically and internationally for the short film 'Aza' and the VR live-action film 'Nagisa ni te', depicts social issues such as bullying, reputational damage via social media, and the insularity of local communities through an original script. Luna Toyota, in her first lead film role, naturally and delicately portrays the protagonist Mayu. Co-stars include Koshu Hirano from the special effects drama 'Ultraman Z', Kohei Yamashita from 'Toritsukushima', Yu Takaoka from the short film 'Tsunagaru', and Yuri Some no from 'Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!'.
title:The Girl Who Leapt Through Time: The first anime adaptation of Yasutaka Tsutsui's classic novel, previously adapted into TV dramas and films. A youth sci-fi drama depicting high school girl Makoto, who gains the power of "time leap" to travel to the past by chance, and realizes the preciousness of irreplaceable moments in life as she repeatedly redoes the past. Second-year high school student Makoto Konno gains the power to "time leap" back to the past after accidentally cracking a walnut found in the school science lab. Using this power, Makoto fully enjoys her carefree daily life, singing karaoke as much as she wants with her male friends Chiaki Mamiya and Kosuke Tsuda, and making spectacular plays in baseball. No matter what happens, she can go back in time and reset as many times as she wants. But this fun everyday life was supposed to continue... Directed by Mamoru Hosoda, who had worked on theatrical versions of "Digimon Adventure" and "ONE PIECE" and later became a leading Japanese animation director with films like "Summer Wars," "The Boy and the Beast," and "Mirai." Character design by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto ("Neon Genesis Evangelion"), animation production by Madhouse. Riisa Naka voices the protagonist Makoto, and Sachie Hara made her voice acting debut as Makoto's aunt, Kazuko Yoshiyama. Initially released in only 6 theaters in 2006, it gained popularity through word-of-mouth and achieved a long run exceeding 8 months. In 2021, it was re-released with the immersive 4DX system as part of a project commemorating the 10th anniversary of Hosoda's production company, Studio Chizu.
title:The Glenn Miller Story: Young trombonist Glenn Miller was always in search of a new sound. He joined a prestigious orchestra but left to focus on arranging. The turning point in his music came from his beloved wife Helen. Following her advice, he formed his own band and eventually achieved unprecedented popularity and fame. However, when World War II began, he volunteered for the Air Force. In late 1944, the plane carrying Glenn Miller disappeared over the English Channel... An emotional musical film, with numerous hit songs coloring the love and bond between the couple played by James Stewart and June Allyson!
title:The Green Ray: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title:The Handmaiden: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
title:The Inugami Family: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
title:The Last Dance: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
title:The Last Hero: The International A-Class 500cc final (All-Japan Road Race Championship, Round 8) is held at the UGO Circuit. The fateful showdown between bike racers Akio Kitano and Keishi Oki ends just before the finish line when Oki overtakes Kitano, pushing the decisive battle to the final round. Kitano uses his handsome looks and sexual prowess to secure funding from multiple patrons to maintain his team. When Christine Adams, heir to a billion-dollar fortune and owner of an international conglomerate, arrives in Japan, Kitano quickly approaches her and successfully secures funding. Finally, Kitano faces the final race, but...
title:The Last Viking: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
title:The Lavender Hill Mob: A crime comedy that depicts, with ironic humor, how two men's gold bullion heist plan takes an unexpected turn. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Charles Crichton, who was later nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director for 'A Fish Called Wanda.' Henry, a serious man who has worked as a bank security guard for 20 years, conspires with his friend Pendlebury, a souvenir shop owner, to steal a shipment of gold bullion. After successfully pulling off the heist, they process the gold into miniature Eiffel Towers to smuggle it abroad, but in a lounge at the Eiffel Tower in Paris, they accidentally sell them to a group of schoolchildren on a trip from England... Alec Guinness of 'Star Wars' fame plays Henry, and Stanley Holloway of 'My Fair Lady' plays Pendlebury. A young Audrey Hepburn appears in a single scene. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:The Life of Chuck: A human mystery film adaptation of Stephen King's 2020 short story "The Life of Chuck," directed by Mike Flanagan of "Doctor Sleep." As massive natural and man-made disasters strike the Earth one after another, the world is nearing its end. With no internet or social media, mysterious advertisements suddenly appear everywhere on street signs, TVs, and radios, reading: "Thanks to Charles Krantz. For 39 great years, thanks, Chuck." When high school teacher Marty rushes out of his house to see his ex-wife Felicia, the deserted city is filled with Chuck's ads. As Marty and Felicia, who have safely reunited, gaze at the stars, feeling the apocalypse approaching, and hold hands, the scene shifts to the perspective of the man in the ads, Chuck, and a story tracing his life unfolds through beautiful imagery. Tom Hiddleston of the "Avengers" series plays the protagonist Chuck, with Chiwetel Ejiofor of "12 Years a Slave," Karen Gillan of the "Guardians of the Galaxy" series, Jacob Tremblay of "Wonder," and Mark Hamill of the "Star Wars" series co-starring. Mandy Moore, choreographer of "La La Land," choreographs the dance scenes. It won the Audience Award, the top prize, at the 2024 Toronto International Film Festival.
title:The Living Dragon: Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Jet Li, Donnie Yen... Yasuaki Kurata is the one and only active action actor who has engaged in fierce battles with countless legends. Now 80 years old and celebrating 60 years as an action actor, this legend takes on a new challenge!
