title:あゝ特別攻撃隊: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
title:いしぶみ: A theatrical release version re-edited from a special 70th post-war anniversary program broadcast on Hiroshima TV in August 2015. It reveals the portraits of 321 first-year students of the former Hiroshima Prefectural Hiroshima Second Middle School, who lost their lives in the atomic bombing and for whom a memorial stone was erected along the Motokawa River, based on the writings of their bereaved families. While building on a reading drama broadcast on the same station in 1969, composed by Matsuyama Zenzo, it adds original elements such as projection performances using wooden boxes and interview footage by Ikezawa Akira.
title:いのちのかたち 画家・絵本作家 いせひでこ: This documentary follows the four-year creative journey of painter and picture book author Hideko Ise, who sensed "life" in the fallen trees left behind in the areas devastated by the Great East Japan Earthquake. In Watari, Miyagi Prefecture, where 300 lives were lost, the village of Yoshidahama—once famous for its beautiful coastline—was left in ruins by the tsunami. Though Ise initially found herself unable to paint in the disaster zone, facing a single black pine tree remaining in Watari moved her to naturally pick up her sketchbook and begin to draw. The film is directed by Shinichi Ise, who has crafted numerous human documentaries capturing the essence of daily life, including *The Shape of Wind*, *It’s Okay*, and *Beside: A Journey from March 11*.
title:いろは:
Twenty-two-year-old Iroha lives at home, dissatisfied with her current self and facing an uncertain future. One day, her older sister Karen returns for the first time in five years. Karen is free-spirited and lives for romance—a woman who, unlike Iroha, has always made bold choices in life. But the reality she carries with her is this: "I'm pregnant. But I don't know who the father is."

There are three possibilities: a wealthy heir, an older man with a violent streak, and an ex-boyfriend burdened by debt. In each relationship, there remains an ambiguity that falls short of being called "love." Why does Karen keep repeating romances she knows will only end in pain? Dragged along on the search for the father, Iroha travels across Nagasaki Prefecture with her sister, witnessing the loneliness and the desperate need for validation that lie beneath the surface of romance.

The sister who seemed so strong was, in truth, longing to be loved more than anyone else. Contrary to her glamorous exterior, she had been constantly entrusting her self-worth to others. At the same time, Iroha realizes that she herself had been running away from being hurt by avoiding love altogether.

More important than being chosen by someone else is acknowledging yourself. Before being loved by another, you must accept yourself. Clashing and baring their true feelings, the sisters finally come to understand each other's weaknesses. Carrying their love without answers and their own imperfect selves... the sisters' journey continues.
title:えんとこの歌 寝たきり歌人・遠藤滋: This documentary captures the life of Shigeru Endo, who, despite being confined to his bed by cerebral palsy, interacts with young caregivers and composes numerous tanka poems from his bedside. The film is directed by Shinichi Ise, a friend of Endo since their student days, who previously helmed the 1999 documentary *Entoko*, which also followed Endo’s daily life. Despite his physical limitations, Endo organized his own caregiver network called "Entoko" (meaning both "where Endo is" and "a place of connections"). As his disability progressed over more than 35 years in bed, Endo began writing tanka in his late 50s, using poetry to give voice to the cries of his soul. Through the deep emotional connection between Endo and his caregivers, the film portrays people living in a way that honors and sustains life exactly as it is.
title:おかえりの湯: Produced with full cooperation from the Tokyo Somei Onsen SAKURA hot spring facility, this heartwarming fantasy depicts human connections and renewal set in a hot spring. Directed by Taiichiro Natsume ("First Love Comedian"), the film stars Toru Kazama, with Yuna Hoshino, who gained attention in "Kamen Rider Geats," as the heroine. Sayama, the manager of the hot spring facility, helps a young amnesiac woman named Sakura who has collapsed, and gives her a job at the spa since she has nowhere to go. Sakura's sincere work ethic and mysterious demeanor soothe the guests, bringing a warm atmosphere to the spa. Watching over Sakura, Sayama immerses himself in his hobby of rakugo (traditional comic storytelling), preparing for a performance at the banquet hall. However, on the day before the show, Sakura suddenly disappears. Along with a letter she left behind, Sayama quietly reflects on his time with her as he performs the rakugo piece "Sugagamo no Kitsune" on stage. The cast includes Toru Kazama as Sayama, Yuna Hoshino as Sakura, along with Yuma Ishigaki, Yoji Tanaka, Daisuke Shima, Tamao Sato, Riko Kawase, Mari Irikawa, Sayaka Mizuse, and Kiyoshi Beat.
title:おくりもの: This is the feature debut of 2003 by Michelangelo Frammartino, a solitary and distinctive filmmaker in Italian cinema. Starring the director's grandfather, Angelo Frammartino, it quietly depicts the final days of an old man's life with unique humor, set in a small Calabrian village on the verge of abandonment due to depopulation. An old man lives in a depopulating rural village in southern Italy. One day, young men who help him bury his old dog leave behind a cell phone and a scrap of paper—a nude photo taken for personal purposes. Later, the old man notices a woman in the village; she is the person in the photo. Using no professional actors, filming with local residents, the film creates a quiet visual poem exploring universal themes of "tradition and modernity," "life and death," and "community and solitude." It will have its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 in a 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title:おしり前マン 復活のおしり前帝国: A feature-length animated film by Takashi Taniguchi—who gained fame for his unique independent animations on YouTube—based on his original work, "Oshiri Mae Man." Maejiri, a man whose buttocks are located on the front of his body, is an ordinary salaryman, but his true identity is "Oshiri Mae Man," a hero who protects the peace of the city. One day, a drug called "Shiri-maenare" that moves people's buttocks to the front begins circulating, plunging the town into unprecedented chaos. While investigating the cause, Oshiri Mae Man tracks it back to a certain pharmaceutical company. There, he discovers a document titled "Oshiri Mae Empire Resurrection Plan" and learns of an organization plotting to revive the legendary "Oshiri Mae Empire" to rule over the people. Realizing the gravity of the situation, Oshiri Mae Man resolves to train under his former master, "Oshiri Mae Legend" (the previous Oshiri Mae Man). Just as with his short films, Taniguchi personally handles the majority of the production for this feature-length version, including direction, screenplay, animation, voice acting, and music.
title:おててつないで:
Actor Yuki Sugawara took on a total of 26 roles—including director, screenwriter, producer, cinematographer, and lead actress—to complete this medium-length film. Drawing on over a decade of experience as a bridal photographer and film crew member, Sugawara channels the "regret of failing to be honest with loved ones" she felt after her father’s death into this story of a distorted parent-child relationship, told with a touch of surreal humor.

Yoshihisa Sunaga, a nursing assistant, lives with his 31-year-old daughter, Yui. Their relationship is strained, with Yui maintaining a cold, rebellious attitude toward him. One day, Yoshihisa is fired following a blunder at work. While Yui views the situation with detached optimism, Yoshihisa’s circumstances grow increasingly dire. Though they have lived under the same roof for years, the father and daughter know next to nothing about each other. When Yoshihisa finally reveals a secret to Yui, their lives are forced to change.

Veteran actor Kiyofumi Kaneko, known for the *Midnight Diner* series, stars as the awkward Yoshihisa, while Sugawara herself plays his distant daughter. The film was an official selection for the "A Certain Viewpoint" category at the 26th TAMA NEW WAVE in 2025.
title:おばあちゃんの秘密: A home drama set in Tainai City, Niigata Prefecture, depicting a cross-generational connection between a grandmother with a secret longing and her granddaughter. Kamishita Riri, living in Tokyo, visits Tainai City to sort through the belongings of her deceased grandmother, Tokiko, as per her will. Inside the house where Tokiko lived alone after her husband's death, Riri discovers 131 letters exchanged between her grandmother and a man other than her husband. Hurt by her parents' discord, Riri is perplexed by her beloved grandmother's secret but begins to trace her footsteps and memories. The memories of Tainai City and her grandmother's secret slowly melt Riri's heart, and she gradually overcomes her own conflicts. Hidden within is a certain feeling that Tokiko, who entrusted Riri with sorting her belongings, wanted to convey to her. Takei Shizue plays the deceased grandmother Tokiko, vividly embodying the emotional fluctuations of a woman who lived with a hidden love in a realistic manner. Shimada Airisu, known for 'Fish Eye' and 'I'll Come to Parent-Teacher Conference Tomorrow,' freshly portrays the granddaughter Riri, who grows while being perplexed by her grandmother's secret. Imazeki Akiyoshi, known for 'Ren Ren Tofu' and 'Aiko Sixteen,' serves as original creator and director, with Kobayashi Hirotoshi, known for 'Beyond the Starry Sky,' handling the screenplay.
title:おへその大将: Set in a slum along the Hirano River in eastern Osaka. A fine human drama depicting the interactions between the so-called 'Apache tribe,' who make a living by stealing scrap metal, and a town doctor (Frankie) who strives to stand by them. Michiyo Aratama, playing his wife, also delivers a remarkable presence.
title:お別れの歌:
Beyond the goodbye, I found the living present.

People live their lives through birth and meeting, parting and reuniting. Through repeated mistakes and the occasional small miracle, the "precious things" we hold in our hearts grow one by one. Until the day we finally wave goodbye to everything, we live quietly, clutching what is irreplaceable.

The latest film from director Keisuke Shibata, who has steadily built a reputation for noteworthy works. A slapstick rhapsody of
title:お嬢さん: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
title:お気楽探偵アトレヤ: A film screened at "Indian Movie Week 2020" (September 11 – October 9, 2020, at Kinema Omori / from September 25, 2020, at Shinjuku Piccadilly).
title:お祭りの日:
Director Yuki Horiuchi—who earned high praise at various domestic indie film festivals, including winning the Grand Prix at a student film festival for the dialogue-driven drama *At the End of the Night*, which depicted the end of summer for youths struggling to grow up—returns with an ensemble piece about those who don't go to the festival on the day of a summer celebration.

A man in a coffee shop tries to persuade the school's "Madonna" to star in his independent film. People at a bus stop wait endlessly for a bus that shows no sign of coming. Someone, enraged that the festival's fireworks display was canceled, steals fireworks to set them off themselves. Two girls wake up hungover to find their air conditioner remote missing and search for it while retracing their memories of the night before. A girl works her shift at a cafe. On the day of the festival, the ordinary summer lives of these people who aren't attending begin to intertwine.

The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 24th TAMA NEW WAVE competition. It stars Masahiro Mera, who also appeared in *At the End of the Night*.
title:お笑えない芸人: A fusion of individuality from promising young creators. Directed by Yuka Nishida, a graduate of Kyoto University of the Arts, who now belongs to STARDUST CREATORS as a screenwriter. This film is her graduation project, made when she was 22. It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
title:お終活3 幸春！人生メモリーズ: The third installment in the human comedy series that explores family dynamics and second chances through the theme of "shukatsu" (end-of-life planning), following "Oshukatsu: Jukushun! Jinsei, Hyakunen Jidai no Sugoshikata" and "Oshukatsu: Saishun! Jinsei Rhapsody." Aya, the eldest daughter of Shinichi and Chikako Ohara, finally decides to marry her fiancé Ryota. However, just before the wedding, a casual remark from Aya causes a rift in their relationship, escalating into a major commotion involving both families. Meanwhile, Shinichi's junior colleague Kato struggles to accept his mother Toyoko's progressing dementia, speaking harshly to her. Chikako gently tells Kato, "Even with dementia, the heart doesn't forget." Continuing from the previous two films, director Hideyuki Kazuki helms this installment, incorporating the latest end-of-life planning trends and knowledge while depicting family bonds with light humor and a warm perspective. The cast reunites familiar faces from the series, including Tsurube Shofukutei as Shinichi Ohara, Junko Takahata as his wife Chikako, Ayame Goriki as their daughter Aya, along with Yuki Matsushita, Masahiko Nishimura, Norika Fujiwara, Renji Ishibashi, Kumiko Fujiyoshi, LiLiCo, Kunikazu Katsumata, and Yoshihiko Hakamada. Guest stars include Keiko Mita as Toyoko, who has dementia, and Fumiyo Kohinata as her son Kato, who supports her despite his own inner conflict.
title:お艶殺し:
A noir romance inspired by Junichiro Tanizaki's 1915 novel *The Murder of Otsuya*. Produced as part of the "TANIZAKI Reimagined" film project commemorating the 140th anniversary of Tanizaki’s birth, the film depicts the warping of love and obsession into violence as a man’s weakness and a woman’s presence become inextricably entwined. 

After serving time for copper wire theft, Shinsuke Abe is released from prison and begins working as a live-in employee at a surveying company. Soon, he is confronted by Santa Tokui, the childhood friend who instigated the crime, and Tsuya Yanagida, Shinsuke’s former lover. Though the theft had been Santa’s idea, Shinsuke had shouldered the full blame and served the sentence alone. While Shinsuke still harbors feelings for Tsuya, she is now involved with Santa. However, their reunion rekindles their mutual attraction, leading them to begin a secret affair behind Santa’s back. Amidst this tension, an irreversible tragedy unfolds.

The film stars Yugo Mikawa (*Cloud*, *Dish Up*), Remi Naoki (TV drama *Sayonara, Teacher*), and Jun Matsuo (*Red Bridge*, *Six Loners*). It is directed by Yoshihiro Tokijo, who previously wrote the screenplay for Toshiki Sato’s *Wandering Bonbon Candy*.
title:かもめ食堂: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
title:きれっぱしの愛: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
title:きれっぱしの愛［上映後ｲﾍﾞﾝﾄ］: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
title:こころの通訳者たち What a Wonderful World: A documentary capturing people's efforts to convey sign language to those who cannot see. At Cinema Chupki Tabata in Tokyo's Kita Ward, Japan's only universal theater, all screenings include audio guides and subtitles. This documentary records three stage sign language interpreters striving to make theater enjoyable for deaf people. To convey this footage to visually impaired people, a group of unique members begins creating an "audio guide." The thoughts of the stage sign language interpreters eventually overlap with those of the audio guide creators, connecting hearts beyond language and disability. The director is Reo Yamada of "Living in the Margins: The Work of Director Sunao Katabuchi."
title:この夏の星を見る: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title:この子は誰: Selected for the Competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival (2025). Screened at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:これって生きてる？: A couple whose smooth-sailing life takes a turn and their marriage falls apart. The disheartened husband, Alex, finds a new purpose in life by turning their marital woes into comedy at a comedy club.
title:さよなら、僕の英雄: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
title:しあわせな選択: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title:しわ: This feature-length animated film is based on the graphic novel *Wrinkles* by Spanish cartoonist Paco Roca, a work exploring the themes of aging and dementia that won the Excellence Award at the 15th Japan Media Arts Festival. Emilio, a former bank manager, begins to show early signs of dementia and is moved into a residential care facility. There, he shares his daily life with a colorful cast of characters: his shrewd, money-conscious roommate Miguel; Antonia, who hoards butter and tea for her visiting grandson; and Dolores, who devotedly cares for her husband Modesto, an Alzheimer’s patient. One day, realizing he has been prescribed the same medication as Modesto, Emilio discovers the truth about his own condition. The film won Best Animated Film and Best Adapted Screenplay at the 29th Goya Awards—Spain’s equivalent to the Oscars—and is directed by the talented young animator Ignacio Ferreras.
title:じっちゃ！:
Set against the seasonal landscapes of Tsugaru City, Aomori Prefecture, this human comedy depicts the bond between a granddaughter who moves from Tokyo and her grandfather, a local melon farmer. Yuki Mikami relocates to Tsugaru City to live with her grandfather, Taisuke, through the Local Revitalization Cooperator program. Assigned to the Tourism and Brand Strategy Division at the city hall, she struggles with her unfamiliar duties to promote the city’s charms nationwide, yet finds solace in her daily life with her grandfather. After a whirlwind year, a colleague she has feelings for approaches her with a business opportunity in Tokyo. Just then, Taisuke, who has rarely spoken of his past, reveals a secret he has kept for 40 years—a story of a hidden bond that kept him in Aomori all those years.

Shizuka Nakamura (*Tida*) stars as the granddaughter, Yuki, alongside veteran actor Takehiko Ono as Taisuke. The supporting cast includes Kai Ogasawara of the dance and vocal group "BULLET TRAIN," Takeshi Nadagi, Harumi Shuhama, and Kanji Tsuda. Directed and written by Toshimitsu Chimura (*100-Second Fist King*, *Keno-shiru*), the film highlights the scenery and landmarks of Tsugaru City. It was produced to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the incorporation of Tsugaru City.
title:そして彼女たちは: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
title:そして父になる: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
title:それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星: The 37th theatrical film in the beloved national children's anime "Anpanman" based on Takashi Yanase's original work. With "promise" as the story's keyword, it depicts the new character Pantan, a red panda traveler, joining forces with Anpanman, Cream Panda, and other friends he meets on his journey to face challenges. To keep a precious promise made long ago with an adventurer, the red panda Pantan travels in search of a treasure said to be on the Rainbow Star shining in the night sky. During his journey, he is sprayed with Baikinman's baby spray and turned into a child. Helped by Anpanman and his friends, Pantan tells them about his journey and his regret over breaking a precious promise. Hearing this, Uncle Jam encourages him, saying, "What matters is the will to keep a promise," and Pantan decides to set out again with renewed determination. Cream Panda joins Pantan on his journey as they head for their destination, the Rainbow Star... Guest voice actor Tao Tsuchiya plays Pantan. The comedy duo "EXIT" members Rintaro and Daiki Kanekina also appear. Directed by Hiroyuki Yano, who has worked extensively on the TV anime series and theatrical films. The screenplay is by Shoji Yonemura, also a veteran of the TV series and films.
title:ただ空高く舞え: Based on the autobiographical writings of Captain G.R. Gopinath, the founder of India's first low-cost carrier "Air Deccan," this drama depicts the journey of men striving to establish an airline. After being unable to be by his father's side at the time of his death because economy seats were fully booked, Air Force officer Nedumaaran sets out to launch India's first budget airline alongside two of his former comrades. Though many looked down on their passion or mocked their ambition, they remain undeterred by the noise around them, pushing forward toward their dream of founding an airline. Tamil cinema star Suriya takes the lead role, with Sudha Kongara (Final Round) directing.
title:ちびっ子レミと名犬カピ: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
title:てっぺんの向こうにあなたがいる: This drama marks Sayuri Yoshinaga's 124th film appearance and is modeled after Junko Tabei, the first woman to successfully summit the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. It portrays a female mountaineer who staked her entire life on reaching the 'top.' In 1975, as deputy leader and climbing captain of the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, Junko Tabe became the first woman in the world to summit Everest. Her achievement astonished the world and brought light to herself, her friends, and her family, but it also cast a deep shadow. Her challenges as a mountaineer continued, and in her later years, even while battling illness and after being given a terminal diagnosis, Junko continued to smile, involve those around her, and climb mountains. The cast includes Yoshinaga as Junko Tabe, a character based on Junko Tabei; Koichi Sato as her husband Masaaki; Yuki Amami as Etsuko Kitayama, Junko's ally and Everest climbing partner; and Non as the young Junko. The film is directed by Junji Sakamoto, who previously directed Yoshinaga in 'The Light of the North' and reunites with her after 13 years.
title:とうちゃん:
A short human drama that delicately portrays the emotional shifts of a man marrying a single mother and her young son. Yuta, who is dating single mother Yoko, spends time with her son, Daisuke, on the first night he stays over at her apartment. When Yuta and Yoko tell Daisuke they have decided to get married, he seemingly accepts the news at first, but... The film captures a single day in the life of a family about to take a new step forward at the end of summer.

The film stars Shinji Matsubayashi (*Icchorai*, *GOLDFISH*), Asami Shibuya (*The Kingdom (or About That House)*, *Waiting for the Pianist*), and Sorami (*Good Luck My Road*). It is directed by Ken Nishioka, who continues to create original short works such as *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*. After screening in the Japan Premiere section of the 19th Sapporo International Short Film Festival, the film will have a standalone release at Theater Guild Daikanyama and other venues in 2025. In 2026, it will also be released theatrically as part of "The Ken Nishioka Short Film Special," featuring a triple bill of his short films: *Tochan*, *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*, and *Where the Balloon Goes*.
title:どうしようもない10人: Set in a future where Japan has been partitioned into three territories by the United States, China, and Russia, this gun-action spectacle follows ten individuals driven by greed through a web of betrayal and deception, culminating in intense dual-pistol shootouts. Following a revolution where the citizenry slaughtered every politician, Japan has been left in ruins. Yahei, who has come into possession of a miraculous bulb known as "Manzu no Moto," amasses a fortune by selling "Manzu"—a single grain of which can satisfy hunger for an entire day. However, his wealth is stolen by a man wearing a Tengu mask. Realizing the thief is actually Dragon, the man who abandoned his family, Yahei hires an assassin named Ageha to do the job. But after taking down Dragon, Ageha vanishes and cuts off all contact. As a cycle of violence and greed continues among various assassins, the whereabouts of the money remain a mystery. It is then that Yahei receives a mysterious invitation. At the designated location, the assassins lie in wait, and a final battle to the death among the ten gathered souls begins. The film stars Shigefumi Fukuzawa, known for his roles in *Ohsama Sentai King-Ohger* and the NHK Taiga drama *Berabou*. It marks the directorial debut of Hiroyasu Kitagawa, who served as chief assistant director on major productions such as *Bayside Shakedown THE FINAL* and *The Wolverine*.
title:どうすればよかったか？: Documentary filmmaker Tomoaki Fujino records over 20 years the story of his older sister, who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia, and his parents, who kept her from seeing a psychiatrist. His sister, eight years older, was caring and excellent. Influenced by their parents, she entered medical school to become a doctor. One day, she suddenly started screaming things that weren't true. Schizophrenia was suspected, but her parents—a doctor and a researcher—refused to acknowledge the illness and kept her away from psychiatric care. Doubting their judgment, Fujino tried to persuade them but failed, and left home with a lingering sense of unease. Eighteen years after his sister's onset, Fujino, having studied filmmaking, began recording his family's life whenever he visited home. He filmed family outings and dinner scenes, engaged his parents in conversation, and kept talking to his sister, but her condition worsened. Eventually, his parents installed a chain and padlock on the front door to confine her inside.
title:なみのおと: The first installment of the Tohoku documentary trilogy co-directed by Ko Sakai (*Home Sweet Home*) and rising filmmaker Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who garnered acclaim for *PASSION* and *THE DEPTHS*. This documentary gathers the "dialogues" of those affected by the tsunami during the Great East Japan Earthquake. Traveling south from the Taro district of Miyako City in Iwate Prefecture to the town of Shinchi in Fukushima’s Soma District, the film captures family members and friends as they speak with one another about the disaster and its aftermath. By focusing on everyday conversation rather than tragic imagery of the disaster zones, the film distills the raw emotions of the survivors that emerge through their shared words.
title:なんでかね～鶴見 ガーエーにはまだ早い: A drama set in Yokohama's Tsurumi Ward, an area with a large population of people of Okinawan heritage that gained attention as one of the settings for the NHK morning drama "Chimudondon," using the traditional Okinawan performing art of Eisa as a motif. The Tsurumi Eisa group "Shiokaze" is focusing on recruiting new members to further energize their Eisa performances, but they struggle to gather people. Mina, one of the core members, works selling loco moco bowls from a food truck and dreams of one day owning her own live music venue as an artist playing the sanrele, a hybrid of the sanshin and ukulele. One day, Mina meets a young man named Eito, who is from Okinawa. Bonding over their shared Okinawan roots, they chat about their lives. When Mina learns that Eito is from Koza, the heartland of Eisa, she forcefully invites him to join Eisa, saying "Just come watch practice," but... This is the second installment in the series following "That's Why, Tsurumi," which also explored Tsurumi and Okinawa. Directed and written by Atsushi Watanabe, who also worked on the previous film.
title:ひちりん: A human drama written, directed, and starring Yudai Kamishi, known for "Hitokuzu" and "Nebagigi New World." Set in a small yakiniku restaurant in Osaka, it depicts the rebirth of a man burdened by sin and people trying to live again. At a small yakiniku restaurant called "Sashinohana" in a corner of Osaka, Sakurako, who lost her husband, runs the place with support from her elementary school son Ken'nosuke, but she can't match her late husband's flavor, customers dwindle, and she's in a tough spot. One day, a taciturn man named Futoshi Maekawa visits the shop asking to be hired. Having once worked at a yakiniku restaurant in Asakusa, Tokyo, Futoshi has been living on the run from a past incident caused while trying to protect his family. Seeing Sakurako desperately protecting the shop reminds him of his late mother, and as he cuts meat and lights the charcoal grill day by day, he gradually forms a family-like bond with Sakurako and Ken'nosuke. Kamishi also serves as director, screenwriter, producer, and plays Futoshi himself. The cast includes Ai Furukawa, Minatsu Tokutake, Shinzo Hotta, Kazuki Namioka, Naomasa Rokuroku, Mineko Nishikawa, Kanji Tsuda, and Ikkei Watanabe.
title:ひつじ探偵団: An unconventional mystery film starring Hugh Jackman, depicting sheep whose beloved owner is murdered as they struggle to find the culprit. In a peaceful English countryside town, shepherd George lives alone surrounded by his beloved sheep. He reads detective novels to them every night, and the sheep actually understand the stories and look forward to this time. One day, George is found dead. The sheep refuse to believe it was an accident and, led by their smartest leader Lily, launch an investigation. As they follow clues, they discover George had a huge inheritance. Determined to avenge their beloved George, the sheep race to find the killer. Hugh Jackman plays the victimized shepherd George, with Oscar-winning actress Emma Thompson, Nicholas Galitzine from "The Idea of You," and Nicholas Braun from the TV series "Succession" co-starring. Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Patrick Stewart, and Bryan Cranston voice the sheep. Based on the 2005 bestselling novel of the same name by German author Leonie Swann, directed by Kyle Balda of the "Minions" series.
title:ひとしずく:
This drama depicts the struggles and growth of a young woman who moves to Minamiosumi, Kagoshima—the southernmost town on Japan’s mainland—to serve as a member of the Local Revitalization Corps. 24-year-old Kasumi Sakamoto, born and raised in Tokyo, felt stuck in a rut, unsure of what she wanted to do with her life. Drawn by a chance job posting and a longing for rural living, she decides to restart her life by relocating to Minamiosumi. Though initially bewildered by the gap between her ideals and reality, Kasumi gradually begins to take root in the community through tears and laughter.

The film is the theatrical debut of director Daiyu Yamashita, who himself moved to Minamiosumi in 2017 to work in the Local Revitalization Corps. In 2019, Yamashita traveled across all 47 of Japan’s prefectures in a mini-car, interviewing over 200 corps members and local government officials to write the screenplay. Based on his own experiences and the authentic voices he gathered, he portrays the true feelings of people from various walks of life with a warm and empathetic gaze. In addition to professional actors, the film features many local residents.
title:ひとりたび: The third feature film by director Yuho Ishibashi, known for 'Goodbye' and 'When Morning Comes, I Feel Empty.' This human drama follows a woman in her 30s, stuck in her career and love life, as she reexamines her way of living by relying on memories of her first love from her student days. Misaki, a 32-year-old working in Tokyo, feels uncomfortable at the company she has worked for for many years and quits, returning to her family home without any clear prospects for the future. Attending a local class reunion, she learns that her first love from her school days has already passed away. This event gradually reawakens the memories and emotions that had been frozen inside Misaki. The screenplay is written by Naho Uemura, noted for 'Ichiko,' 'Crescent Moon and Cat,' and 'Zakken!' The lead role is played by Rei Okamoto, who is widely active in films like 'Tea Drinking Friends,' as well as dramas, commercials, and stage. The film brings together three women of the same generation—Okamoto (born 1991), Ishibashi (born 1990), and Uemura (born 1988)—to delicately weave a story about the anxieties of a woman in her 30s about the future and her encounter with past memories. The cast also includes Koki Osamura, Akane Sakanoue, Mari Hamada, Hideko Hara, and Mitsuru Hirata.
title:ひなぎく: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title:ひめゆり: During the final stages of the Pacific War, in Okinawa where fierce battles engulfed even civilians, female students aged 14 to 19 were forced into the battlefield to serve as nurses, and many of them lost their lives. This documentary delves into the truth of the "Himeyuri Student Corps," whose story has been repeatedly told in films and dramas. Through the invaluable testimonies of 22 survivors recorded over 13 years, the harsh fate imposed on these young girls comes to light.
title:ひゃくえむ。: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title:ひゃくえむ。【背景美術展 開催記念上映】: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title:ほどなく、お別れです: Based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Amone Nagatsuki, winner of the Shogakukan Bunko Novel Award Grand Prize, starring Minami Hamabe and Ren Meguro, directed by Takahiro Miki ("Ao Haru Ride," "Tomorrow I Will Date Yesterday's You"). It depicts a heroine who joins a funeral company and, together with her supervising funeral planner, aims to create the "best possible funeral." Misu Shimizu, struggling with job hunting, has a secret she can't tell anyone: she can hear the voices of the deceased. A fateful encounter changes her life when Reiji Urushibara, a funeral planner who notices her ability, invites her into the world of funeral planning. Guided by something, Misu becomes an intern at the funeral company "Bando Kaikan." Teaming up with Urushibara, she confronts the question "What is a funeral that satisfies not only the surviving family but also the deceased?" through various families' funerals, including a husband who lost his pregnant wife and a couple who lost their young daughter. Eventually, Misu comes to admire Urushibara's sincere dedication to the deceased and their families, and decides to pursue a career as a funeral planner herself. Hamabe plays Misu, Meguro plays Urushibara, with a stellar cast including Mochika Yamada, Ken Mitsuishi, Mirai Shida, Keisuke Watanabe, Kotone Furukawa, and Takumi Kitamura. The script is by Takuro Honda (drama "Lion's Snack"), supervised by Yoshikazu Okada, known for various hit works.
title:ぼくらの居場所: A Canadian drama that captures the lives of people on the fringes of society with an honest gaze, following three children living in harsh circumstances as they form bonds at a local community education center. In Scarborough, a diverse, multicultural neighborhood in eastern Toronto. Bing, a Filipino boy who fled his mentally ill father's violence to come to this town; Sylvie, a girl of Indigenous heritage living in a shelter with her family of four; and Laura, a girl neglected and tossed about by her parents—these three find a safe haven at the education center run by social worker Hina. Despite their difficult circumstances, they nurture a small but meaningful bond... The lead roles are played by three children making their film debut, and the supporting cast includes non-professional actors from Scarborough. The film is based on Canadian author Catherine Hernandez's debut novel "Scarborough," which she adapted from her own experiences. Directors Shasha Nakai and Rich Williamson, highly acclaimed in the documentary field, made their narrative feature debut with this film. It won eight awards, including Best Picture and Best Director, at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.
title:まなぶ 通信制中学 60年の空白を越えて: This documentary, filmed over five years, captures the lives of elderly students attending a correspondence junior high school after being unable to receive compulsory education due to various circumstances during the post-war chaos. These correspondence courses were established for those who could not complete their three years of middle school during the turmoil of the war and its aftermath. At Kanda Hitotsubashi Junior High School in Chiyoda—one of the few remaining institutions of its kind—elderly students arrive to attend their lessons. Twice a month on their days off, they receive instruction from teachers the age of their children or grandchildren. Though bewildered by school life after a 60-year hiatus, their expressions overflow with the joy of learning as they return to their youth. Overcoming the hardships of caregiving and personal illness, they share their family stories and laugh together during breaks. Through their school life, the film explores why people still strive to learn even as they approach the final chapters of their lives. Directed by Naoko Ota, director of "Under the Moonlight: Memories of a Night High School."
title:みつかるまで:
Directed by Takusho Tsunemoto, known for "A Pale Woman," this medium-length film was shot on 16mm as a 2002 practical project for the Film School of Tokyo’s advanced course. It depicts the encounter between a female painter who can no longer paint and a man drawn to her, following the fate that awaits them both. 

Yoshimi, a painter who once held high ideals, lost her sense of self after a professional setback and now spends her days pickpocketing on trains. A mysterious young man named Tetsushi appears before her, telling her that the sight of her running through the city at night was like a shooting star. From then on, he begins to follow her, always wearing an affable smile. 

Yuka Itaya stars as the protagonist Yoshimi, with Kenji Mizuhashi playing Tetsushi, a young man whose friendly grin hides a deep-seated fragility. Although it has primarily been shown at film festivals and special screenings, the film will receive its standalone theatrical release at Cinema Ris in Jimbocho, Tokyo, in 2026—24 years after its production.
title:みつけた、みつけた 分別と多感: A romantic drama adapting Jane Austen's 1811 novel 'Sense and Sensibility,' relocated to modern-day South India. Directed by Rajiv Menon and featuring music by A. R. Rahman, the duo behind 'Mridangam: The Beat of Passion,' this film was released in 2000. In a prestigious family in Tamil Nadu, South India, the reserved and intelligent elder sister Sowmya works as a school principal, while her free-spirited younger sister Meenakshi, who loves poetry and South Indian classical music, lives in a dreamy haze. After their grandfather's death, the family estate passes to a distant relative, forcing the mother and daughters to start a new life in the bustling city of Chennai. Meenakshi meets a young businessman who loves poetry and a former soldier who lost a leg in war and now grows flowers, while Sowmya encounters a man aspiring to be a film director. Through their respective loves and careers, the sisters gradually discover their own paths in life. Tabu, known for 'The Namesake' and 'Life of Pi,' plays Sowmya; Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, known for 'Robot,' plays Meenakshi; and Ajith Kumar, Mammootty, and Abbas co-star.
title:みやこ: The second film from documentary filmmaker Tetsuo Yamaya, who earned high acclaim for *Living: 25 Years After the Mass Suicide on Tokashiki Island, Okinawa* (1971), produced during his studies at Waseda University. Minna Island, Okinawa, is a land unsettled by property disputes. Following the lives of residents who migrated to Miyako Island at the recommendation of the Ryukyu Government only to be forced into grueling migrant labor in Aichi Prefecture, the film questions what "Miyako" truly means to them.
title:みんな、おしゃべり！: A comedy about a prideful feud between a deaf Japanese family and a Kurdish family, told through Japanese Sign Language and Kurdish. Natsumi Koga lives with her deaf father and younger brother, who run an electronics shop. One day, their family gets into a minor conflict with a Kurdish family living in the same town. Natsumi, who can hear, and Hiwa, the only member of the Kurdish family who speaks Japanese, are drafted as interpreters for their respective families. As they interpret for each other, a bond of trust grows between Natsumi and Hiwa, but the conflict between the two families only deepens. Then one day, a mysterious drawing by Natsumi's younger brother Shun escalates into an incident that engulfs the entire town. Nagisa Nagashima of "The End of Love" plays the protagonist Natsumi. Kazuyoshi Kezuka, a deaf ramen shop owner in Tokyo's Nishi-Nippori, makes his acting debut as Natsumi's father. Hideaki Nasu of the TV drama "Deaf Voice: Court Sign Language Interpreter" and Akito Imai of "The Two Worlds of My Life" play the father's friends. Shunya Itabashi of "Laughing Kaibutsu" plays a community organizer planning a town revitalization project, and Karin Ono of "Animation x Paralympic: Who Is the Hero?" plays a teacher at a school for the deaf. The film is directed by Ken Kawai, known for works like "Nanno-chan's Second World War" and who is himself a CODA (Child of Deaf Adults).
title:めぐる面影、今、祖父に会う: The feature directorial debut of Huang Wen-ying, who has served as the production designer for many of director Hou Hsiao-hsien’s works. This family drama follows an art director who returns to her family home to care for her father, reflecting on the life of her grandfather who lived through the Japanese colonial era. Fu-yue, a professional in film production design, temporarily leaves the set to return to her hometown and support her ailing father. As she spends her days there, conversations with an architect she contacted for a set build cause her heart to drift back to the era her grandfather once inhabited. Ariel Lin, who rose to fame in the Taiwanese drama version of "Itazura na Kiss," stars as the protagonist Fu-yue. Vic Chou, known for his role as Hanazawa Rui in "Meteor Garden," plays a dual role as both the architect she is drawn to and her grandfather in his youth. Hou Hsiao-hsien serves as producer.
title:めぐる／エイン: On the morning of a job interview, college student Megumi wakes from a nightmare. It is a recurring memory of the death of her younger sister, Nao, who had been tormented by bullying. Having overslept, Megumi rushes to the station, bumping into a man in a suit as she slips onto a train just before departure. That split-second delay alters the fate of Keiichi, a middle-aged man on his way to the hospital. Meanwhile, on the station platform, Yuki, a high school student harboring deep emotional scars, and Meguru, a young man studying for his university entrance exams, share a chance encounter. One person’s step ripples outward, touching the lives and futures of others. As their lives intersect, diverge, and occasionally collide, they ultimately find a small, fragile glimmer of hope.
title:もしも脳梗塞になったなら: A socially conscious drama directed by Takafumi Ota (known for *Sunflower Hill 1983 Summer* and *The House of the Rising Sun*), based on his own personal battle with a stroke. Film director Ryutaro Otaki, who lives alone, suddenly suffers a cerebral infarction one day. His heart function drops to 20%, he loses half his vision, and he finds himself unable to speak properly. Even when he calls friends, they don't believe him, and when he posts about his condition on social media, he is met only with irrelevant advice and online harassment. Just as he is driven to the brink of dying alone, helping hands are extended to him from unexpected sources. The protagonist, Ryutaro Otaki, is played by Shunsuke Kubozuka, who starred in *Hanagatami* by director Nobuhiko Obayashi, under whom Ota studied. The cast also features Takemi Fujii as the sister, Misato Tanaka as the mother, and Tomoko Fujita and Shiro Sano as the friends who support Otaki online.
title:やさしさ: A featured film in the "Central Asia Past and Present Film Festival Vol. 3: Uzbekistan Special."
title:やまない症動 死ねない難病に挑むテレビマンの記録: Unstoppable Impulse: Challenging an Incurable Disease... Watch related works: Minding the Gap, FLEE, The Biggest Little Farm, The Act of Killing, Navalny, Citizenfour, Assassins, Documentary of Baby Assassins, The Yokai's Grandson, The Unnameable Dance.
title:ゆきははなである 新野の雪まつり: A documentary by filmmaker Shinkichi Noda, who continually explored the foundations of people's consciousness in rapidly changing Showa-era Japan. This film captures the "Niino Snow Festival" of Nagano Prefecture, seeking to find the enduring spirit of the people within this festival that has continued since medieval times. The Niino Snow Festival has been held since around the 13th century, centered around Izu Shrine and Suwa Shrine in Niino, Anan Town, Nagano Prefecture. People see the falling winter snow as rice flower blossoms, a harbinger of the harvest, and pray for abundant grain. Throughout the night-long festival, masked and costumed performances like "Kyoman" (horse racing), "Okina" (old man), and "Oni" (demon) appear one after another, and the crowd erupts when the spirit of bounty, "Saiho," makes its entrance. Director Noda attempts to read the everyday wishes of farmers for the coming year's production within this sacred festival space. This film is part of the special screening series "Shinkichi Noda Special: Snow is a Flower" (screening from December 6, 2025, at Pole Pole Higashi-Nakano and other theaters nationwide).

title:ゆっくり あるく 川村浪子、84歳のダンス: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.

title:ゆれる:
Directed and written by Miwa Nishikawa, who rose to prominence with her 2002 debut *Wild Berries*, this second feature film explores the psychological conflict between two brothers following a fatal fall in a mountain valley. 

Takeru Hayakawa, a successful and busy photographer living in Tokyo, returns to his hometown for the first time in years to attend the first anniversary of his mother’s death. His older brother, Minoru, lives with their father and works at the family gas station, where their childhood friend Chieko Kawabata works part-time. The three of them visit a remote valley filled with childhood memories. While Takeru is off taking photographs, he spots Minoru and Chieko crossing a suspension bridge in the distance—only for Chieko to fall to her death moments later. As a trial unfolds to determine whether the death was an accident or a crime, Takeru finds himself increasingly unsettled as Minoru begins to reveal a side of himself he has never seen before. 

Starring Joe Odagiri as the younger brother Takeru and Teruyuki Kagawa as the older brother Minoru, with Yoko Maki and Masato Ibu in supporting roles. The film was officially selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 59th Cannes Film Festival in 2006 and received numerous domestic accolades.
title:よあけの焚き火:
Real-life father and son Motonari and Yasunari Ohkura, Noh performers of the Okura school of Kyogen, star as themselves in their first feature film—a human drama that uses traditional performing arts to explore the universal theme of "passing things down." This marks the feature-length directorial debut of Koichi Doi, who served as an assistant director to Kohei Oguri and has worked extensively in television documentaries.

Born into a Kyogen family with a 650-year legacy, Motonari Ohkura brings his 10-year-old son, Yasunari, to a mountain training hall that he himself visited with his father and brother as a child. Just as his father once did for him, Motonari guides his son through the basics, including cleaning the hall, while subjecting him to rigorous training. Bewildered by his father’s uncharacteristic severity, Yasunari nearly gives up on his practice. One day, a local girl named Sakiko visits the hall. Having lost her parents in a disaster years earlier, Sakiko is captivated by the sight of the younger Yasunari training so earnestly. As Yasunari, carrying the weight of a family history within the unbroken lineage of Kyogen, and Sakiko, who has lost her family, share a quiet connection, a small sense of resolve begins to bloom in both their hearts.
title:よき⾕の物語: A new feature film from director José Luis Guerín, who captivated the world with 'In the City of Sylvia' (2007) and was called 'the most outstanding filmmaker in contemporary Spain' by fellow Spanish director Víctor Erice. Despite his sparse output, Guerín continues to create masterpieces that lightly transcend the boundaries between fiction and documentary. This is his long-awaited new film, his first in ten years since 'The Academy of Muses' (2015), now arriving in Japan. To commemorate the release of 'The Good Valley Story,' the beautiful masterpiece 'In the City of Sylvia' will also be revived. Please enjoy Guerín's world on the big screen. The Vallbona district, located on the outskirts of Barcelona, Spain. This place, named 'The Good Valley,' is surrounded by rivers and railway tracks, an isolated land left behind by development, yet it also seems like an ideal paradise blessed with nature so rich it's hard to believe it's near a big city. Here, families who moved in from the mid-20th century live together with a new generation of immigrants who have arrived recently. Although their cultures and lifestyles differ, the children play together in the river, and everyone eats, drinks, sings, and dances well, finding a moment of peace. A new railway expansion plan is proposed for this urban oasis. A residents' information meeting is held, and some people are forced to relocate...

title:よみがえる声: A documentary co-directed by Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean filmmaker who turns 90 in 2025, and her daughter Park Ma-i, depicting the stories of the voiceless buried in history. Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean born in Mie Prefecture in March 1935, gained attention for her correspondence with Lee Jin-woo, a second-generation Zainichi Korean juvenile death row inmate in the 1958 Komatsugawa Incident, published as "Sin, Death, and Love." She subsequently published collections of testimonies uncovering the voices of Zainichi Koreans forcibly conscripted under colonial rule and those exposed to the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Switching from pen to camera, she made her directorial debut in 1986 with the documentary "Another Hiroshima" about Korean A-bomb victims. She has since produced documentary works such as "Song of Ariran: Testimony from Okinawa," "Nuchigafu (Life's Blessing): Testimony from the Place of Mass Death," and "Silence: The Rising Comfort Women." This film refocuses on the realities and contemporary challenges of Korean A-bomb victims, a lifework for Park Soo-nam, and is based on 16mm film she has been shooting for about 40 years. It depicts the voiceless stories of Koreans affected by the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forced laborers taken to Nagasaki's Battleship Island (Gunkanjima), former Korean civilian employees in the Battle of Okinawa, and women forced into Japanese military sexual slavery.
title:わたしの聖なるインド: A documentary following over 100 days of peaceful resistance by Muslim women living in India. In December 2019, India's Modi government enacted the Citizenship Amendment Act, which deliberately excludes Muslims, heightening fears among Muslims of losing their citizenship. As criticism of the bill grew, police stormed the campus of Jamia Millia Islamia University, a protest hub, injuring 200 people and making numerous arrests. In protest against this violent response and the discriminatory law, a massive sit-in began in Shaheen Bagh, a Muslim neighborhood in South Delhi. At its center were Muslim women who, arguing that the government's religious discrimination and crackdown on protests were unconstitutional, blocked a major highway for over 100 days while continuing their daily lives. This nonviolent movement resonated with many, spreading across India beyond generations, cultures, and religions. However, tensions escalated around the Delhi legislative elections, leading to a forced police eviction. Directed by Muslim woman Nousheen Khan, the film traces the historical resistance movement by Muslim women, who have been politically and socially rendered invisible, while overlaying her own story of liberation and transformation. It won the Audience Award at the Yamagata International Documentary Film Festival 2023 (screened under the title 'My Ideal Country').
title:わたしの頭はいつもうるさい: A film themed around the 'quarter-life crisis,' a psychological state common among people in their late twenties to thirties who feel vague anxiety and restlessness about the future, unable to live the life they imagined. Directed by and starring Reimi Miyamori, it won the Actor Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for independent films. Nozomi, a 25-year-old woman who moved to Tokyo to become a novelist, is struggling and going nowhere. In her mind, 18-year-old Nozomi, living a rural high school life, asks her if she has truly followed through on her words and made it big in Tokyo. While resisting a frustrating life where she wants to change but cannot, the 25-year-old Nozomi confronts her 18-year-old self and begins to notice various things she had never faced before. This is the debut feature film of Reimi Miyamori, a graduate of the Nihon University College of Art's Film Department who began making films during the COVID-19 pandemic. She served as director, screenwriter, producer, and lead actress. It was screened in theaters as part of the 'Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024' (May 9 – June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title:わんぱく天使: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.
title:わんわん忠臣蔵: A puppy named Rock rises up with stray dogs to defeat Killer the tiger, who killed his mother. Drawing on 'Chushingura' and Sazanami Iwaya's children's literature 'Koganemaru,' this film more consciously adopts Disney's style compared to earlier feature-length works. The stateless urban depictions and the action in a snow-covered amusement park, inspired by an idea from Osamu Tezuka, exude a chic and modern sensibility.
title:アイ・ワズ・ア・ストレンジャー: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
title:アウトウォーターズ 裂けた砂漠: A found footage horror film that uses avant-garde visuals and storytelling to depict four men and women visiting a desert who encounter unimaginable terror. Three memory cards are discovered in the Mojave Desert, containing horrifying footage. One day, Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle come to the Mojave Desert in California to shoot a music video. But when night falls, strange sounds, lights, and inexplicable phenomena begin to occur. Soon, the four are swallowed by a rift in reality, and the camera captures the nightmare that befalls them. Robbie Banfitch, a multi-talented filmmaker, screenwriter, actor, and musician from New Jersey, makes his feature-length directorial and screenwriting debut, also starring in the lead role.
title:アギト 超能力戦争:
Commemorating the 55th anniversary of the Kamen Rider franchise, this supernatural action film is a cinematic adaptation of the 2001 tokusatsu TV drama *Kamen Rider Agito*, which holds the record for the highest average viewership ratings among all Kamen Rider series since the Heisei era. Set in a chaotic world where many have awakened to psychic abilities, the story depicts a fierce struggle centered on Makoto Hikawa, a police officer who possesses no special powers.

Bizarre corpses—half-frozen and half-burned—are discovered. The deaths are the work of psychics who have gone on a rampage. To resolve the crisis, the Metropolitan Police Department’s Special Armed Unit for Unidentified Lifeforms, known as the "G-Unit," is deployed. Young officer Ruriko Aoi confronts the psychics using the state-of-the-art reinforced armor "G6," but she is forced to retreat in the face of their overwhelming power. title:アグリーシスター 可愛いあの娘は醜いわたし: —Prince Julian of the Kingdom of Swellandia (Isaac Kamuroot) is the object of every lady’s desire. In hopes of winning his hand in marriage, they strive day after day to refine their grace and beauty.—
title:アサンテサーナ―わが愛しのタンザニア―: Sakata, a member of the Japan Overseas Cooperation Volunteers (JOCV) working in Tanzania, travels across the vast wilderness by truck to deliver aid supplies from developed nations—arriving at the port of Dar es Salaam—to various villages, occasionally assisting with local labor. His close partnership with Juma, a local agricultural leader, has earned the deep trust of the residents, but one day, a decisive conflict arises between them. After interacting with JOCV members during a private trip, director Senkichi Taniguchi sought to depict their activities without romanticization. Eschewing the help of major film companies, he realized this soulful project by filming in Tanzania, a country where almost no films were being produced at the time.
title:アダムの原罪: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title:アニエスによるヴァルダ: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
title:アバウトアス・バット・: A restaurant in the metropolis of Manila. A lonely literature professor and an aspiring young writer engage in a 90-minute, single-location, non-stop conversational drama revolving around the secrets of a deceased lover.
title:アフリカン・カンフー・ナチス2 逆襲のロボトラー: The sequel to the kung fu action hit "African Kung Fu Nazis"—which gained notoriety for its outlandish premise of Adolf Hitler and Hideki Tojo secretly surviving and battling martial artists in their Ghanaian exile. After WWII, a surviving Hitler fled to Ghana to plot world domination, only to be stopped by a local youth named Addy. Hitler finally died, and peace seemed to have returned to the world. However, years later, Hitler somehow returns from the dead and runs for the presidency of Ghana. Backed by Propaganda Minister Goebbels and the Japanese Ambassador to Ghana, Raiden, Hitler quickly captures the hearts of the nation. Addo, the younger brother of the late Addy, plunges into battle to save his homeland using the kung fu passed down from his brother. Standing in his way is Hitler, who has undergone a shocking transformation into the giant robot "Robotler." Japan-based German filmmaker Sebastian Stein returns to direct, write, edit, and star as Hitler. The new Japanese character Raiden is played with power by former professional sumo wrestler turned performer Gotchanko.
title:アメリと雨の物語: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title:アラビアンナイト シンドバッドの冒険: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
title:アリス（1988）: The debut feature film from visionary Czechoslovakian animator Jan Švankmajer. Based on Lewis Carroll’s novel *Alice's Adventures in Wonderland*, the film brings to life a surreal and grotesque world through a unique fusion of live-action and stop-motion animation. While passing a tedious afternoon in a cluttered room, a young girl named Alice begins playing "Alice" with her dolls. Suddenly, a taxidermied White Rabbit displayed in a glass case springs to life. Checking its pocket watch in a frantic rush, the rabbit vanishes into a desk drawer. Alice follows, and before she knows it, she has wandered into a bizarre and unsettling world.
title:アリババと40匹の盗賊: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
title:アリババと４０匹の盗賊: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters.
