title:アワーミュージック: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title:アンソロジー・フィルムアーカイブスの創設者たち: This program features works by Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), Peter Kubelka (1934–), Stan Brakhage (1933–2003), and James Broughton (1913–1999)—key figures who played a central role in the founding of Anthology Film Archives—as well as Marjorie Keller’s *The Fallen World* (1983), which features P. Adams Sitney (1944–2025).
title:アンデルセン物語: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's words, 'My life is a fairy tale,' this musical drama weaves together tales like 'The Red Shoes' and 'Thumbelina' while depicting Andersen's boyhood. The night sky sparkles with colorful stars, and the orchestra's melodies envelop the story. The art by Reiji Koyama and the music by Seiichiro Uno sweetly bring this fairy-tale world to life.
title:アン・リー ／はじまりの物語: A biographical musical film chronicling the tumultuous life of Ann Lee, a real-life religious leader who founded the utopian "Shaker" sect in the 18th century, starring Amanda Seyfried of "Mamma Mia!" and "Les Misérables." Born into a poor blacksmith's family in 18th-century England, Ann grows up as a devout woman. After the heartbreaking experience of bearing four children, all of whom die, she receives a revelation that she is the female reincarnation of Christ. Her way of life, preaching equality of gender and race, attracts many followers but also invites persecution from those who resent or fear her. Eventually, she crosses to America with just eight followers, seeking a utopia where they can realize an ideal life based on gender and racial equality, but further hardships await her there. Co-stars include Lewis Pullman of "Top Gun: Maverick" and Thomasin McKenzie of "Last Night in Soho." Directed by Mona Fastvold, who co-wrote the script with her partner, director Brady Corbet of "The Brutalist." The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025.

title:アヴァンチュール L’Aventura: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title:イエス イエスソングス ライヴ・イン・ロンドン1972: A concert film capturing the performances of the British progressive rock band Yes at the Rainbow Theatre in London on December 15 and 16, 1972. Formed in London in 1968, Yes is counted among the "Big Four of Progressive Rock" alongside ELP, King Crimson, and Pink Floyd. Known for albums like "Fragile" (1971), "Close to the Edge" (1972), and "Owner of a Lonely Heart" (1983), they won a Grammy Award in 1985 and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2017. They enjoy worldwide popularity, having held a 50th-anniversary tour for "Close to the Edge" in 2022, which included shows in Japan in September of that year. This film captures the band's performances over two nights, December 15 and 16, 1972, at the Rainbow Theatre in London, as part of the "Close to the Edge Tour" that began in North America in July of the same year, promoting their 5th album "Close to the Edge." It documents the breathtaking performances of the band during their golden age and was produced and theatrically released in the United States in 1975.
title:イット・フォローズ: A horror film depicting the terror of a woman stalked by "It"—a mysterious entity that brings death to anyone it catches. Despite its low budget, the film's innovative concept earned praise from Quentin Tarantino and became a sensation across the United States. Jay is a 19-year-old college student who spends the night with a man, only for his demeanor to suddenly shift. Finding herself tied to a chair, Jay is told that he has passed "It" on to her, and that if "It" catches her, she will surely die. While "It" can be passed to someone else, if that person dies, it returns to the previous host. Jay attempts to outrun the ever-approaching "It," but... Written and directed by up-and-coming filmmaker David Robert Mitchell in his second feature film, the movie stars Maika Monroe (*The Guest*).
title:イミディエイト ファミリー: A music documentary tracing the journeys and bonds of four session musicians who supported the American West Coast sound. In the early 1970s, musicians Danny Kortchmar (guitar), Waddy Wachtel (guitar), Leland Sklar (bass), and Russ Kunkel (drums) participated in recordings for artists like Carole King, James Taylor, Jackson Browne, and Linda Ronstadt, who lived around Laurel Canyon in Los Angeles. Later called the supergroup "The Immediate Family," their solid playing and musical understanding contributed to the birth of many classic songs, continually supporting the artists' expressions. Through interviews with the four musicians themselves and the renowned artists they made music with, the film reveals moments of creation in the studio's closed space and the deep bonds between musicians. It also explores projects each participated in solo, depicting their rise to becoming popular musicians. Directed by Denny Tedesco, who also directed the music documentary "The Wrecking Crew" about the session musicians who supported the American music scene of the 1960s and 70s.
title:インサイド・ルーウィン・デイヴィス 名もなき男の歌: The Coen brothers, directors of "No Country for Old Men" and "True Grit," won the Grand Prix at the 66th Cannes Film Festival in 2013 with this film. Loosely based on the life of Dave Van Ronk, a musician who represented the 1960s folk scene, it humorously depicts a week in the life of a struggling young folk singer. In the winter of 1960s New York, singer-songwriter Llewyn keeps performing at live houses but can't seem to make it big. On the verge of giving up on making a living through music, he still manages to get by with the help of his friends. Oscar Isaac, who appeared in "Robin Hood" and "Drive," plays Llewyn and also performs the songs. The music is by T Bone Burnett of "O Brother, Where Art Thou?" and "Crazy Heart."

title:インビジブルハーフ:
An immersive youth horror film, this story follows a young girl targeted by a transparent monster visible only when she touches her smartphone. Director Masaki Nishiyama, who garnered attention for his 2021 vertical short film *Sma-Horror!*, makes his feature-length debut with this project. Drawing from the "shadows" of loneliness and alienation he felt during his own student years, Nishiyama spent six years bringing this vision to life.

Elena, a girl of mixed heritage, transfers to a high school in a rural town. Struggling to fit in, she finds herself unable to open up to Akari, a cheerful classmate who tries to befriend her. However, following the death of the class troublemaker, Nyan—who was never seen without earphones plugged into her phone—strange phenomena begin to occur around Elena. Haunted by footsteps heard through her earphones and pursued by a "monster" visible only when she holds her smartphone, Elena soon finds herself unable to let go of her device, just like Nyan.

Sierra Risa, an actor and director who has been making films since age 14, stars as Elena. Miyu Okuno plays her friend Akari, while Runa Hirasawa portrays the troubled Nyan. The VFX are handled by Cao Moji (Shoichiro Sato), a long-time collaborator of Nishiyama who also contributed to the CG for the Academy Award-winning *Godzilla Minus One*. The film was nominated for Best International Feature at the 33rd Raindance Film Festival in the UK.
title:イン・タイム ドーナル・ラニー: A featured title of the Ireland Film Festival 2026 (May 29 – June 11, 2026, at YEBISU GARDEN CINEMA).
title:イート・ザ・ナイト:
A youth thriller that explores the precariousness of the modern world through the lives of siblings immersed in an MMORPG (Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Game). Acclaimed internationally for their short films, young French filmmaking duo Caroline Poggi and Jonathan Vinel approach the MMORPG not as a "virtual world" but as a vital place to belong, utilizing a bold, genre-defying narrative style.

Pablo, a young man earning a living as a drug dealer, and his teenage sister, Apolline, share a deep bond forged through the online RPG "Darknoon." Their world is shaken when the game's sudden shutdown is announced. Meanwhile, Pablo falls for a mysterious young man named Night and becomes consumed by the relationship, leaving his sister alone and refusing to face the impending end of the game. As Pablo’s reckless choices provoke the wrath of a rival gang and the end of their digital lives draws near, their actual reality begins to unravel at its core.

The film stars Théo Cholbi (*The Night of the 12th*) as Pablo, newcomer Lila Gueneau as Apolline, and Erwan Kepoa Falé (*Winter Boy*) as Pablo’s lover, Night.
title:ウィスキー・ガロア: A comedy inspired by the real-life 1941 shipwreck of a cargo vessel carrying a large quantity of whiskey off the coast of Scotland. Based on the 1947 novel of the same name by British author Compton Mackenzie, this film was directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' It is one of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s. Set in Britain during World War II. As Nazi Germany intensifies its air raids on London, the rationing of whiskey—considered 'the water of life'—is halted. Just then, a cargo ship carrying about 260,000 bottles of whiskey runs aground off a small Scottish island. Just before the ship sinks, the islanders rescue the captain and crew, salvage as much whiskey as possible, and hide it in a cave on the island. Soon, officials arrive to recover the whiskey, leading to a battle of wits with the islanders. A remake was produced in 2016 and released in Japan under the title 'Whiskey and Two Brides.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:ウィンチェスター銃'73: The Winchester rifle, a legendary gun said to be one in tens of thousands. A drama of joys and sorrows unfolds around the people who come into possession of this rifle one after another, with all episodes converging into a single finale. A masterfully structured classic Western.
title:エイタロウ:
A human comedy filmed entirely on location in Kagoshima Prefecture that depicts the realistic life of an actor living in the provinces. The film was produced as a work of fiction based on the life of Eitaro Tokuda, an actor active locally in Kagoshima.

33-year-old Eitaro lives in Kagoshima, working as a contract employee for a beer company to support his wife and child while harboring a deep-seated desire to make a living as an actor. While he appears to lead a peaceful life on the surface, he feels a growing sense of anxiety, fearing he will be forgotten in the countryside. Amidst this, he is beset by the appearance of a certain woman, pressure from his workplace, and a nightmare-like turn of events. Driven into a corner, Eitaro attempts to stage a grand tragedy entrusted to him by a loved one, but...

Tokuda, who in real life also works for a beer company to support his family, plays the protagonist Eitaro himself, while the supporting cast consists entirely of unknown local residents. For the filming of the stage play that serves as the finale, a total of 500 extras participated as the audience. Rikei Kubo—director of the documentary *Nishiharamura*, assistant director of *Blood and Bones*, and producer of *Climber's High*—makes his feature-length narrative directorial debut.
title:エウレカ Eureka: Directed by Kiyoshi Aoyama of 'Helpless,' this human drama depicts the journey of recovery for people traumatized by a bus-jacking incident. It won the FIPRESCI Prize and the Ecumenical Jury Prize at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival in 2000. A bus-jacking occurs in a regional city in Kyushu, and many passengers are killed. The only survivors are the driver, Sawai, and two siblings: junior high school student Naoki and elementary school student Kozue. All three are deeply scarred. Two years later, Sawai, who had disappeared leaving his family behind, returns to town. Around the same time, a series of murders occur in the area, and suspicion falls on Sawai. Learning that the siblings are living alone, Sawai visits their home and begins living with them. Joined by the siblings' cousin, Akihiko, the four set out on a journey in a bus driven by Sawai... Kōji Yakusho plays Sawai, while real-life siblings Shō Miyazaki and Aoi Miyazaki play Naoki and Kozue. Following director Kiyoshi Aoyama's death in March 2022, a digital master complete version was released in theaters that May as a memorial screening.
title:エス:
Director Masahiro Ota, who has built a career in short films and commercials, presents a feature film based on his own experience of being arrested. The story depicts the reunion and eventual rift among a group of friends who gather following the news of a film director's arrest.

When young filmmaker Shinichi Someda is arrested, his former theater colleagues from university reunite for the first time in years to draft a petition for leniency. The group includes Takano, a struggling actor who was set to star in Someda's latest project; Suzumura, a senior who prides himself on having the deepest bond with Someda; and Chiho, who married another man after her feelings for Someda became hopelessly complicated. Though they all gathered with the shared desire to help their friend, things take an unexpected turn...

In 2011, Director Ota was arrested on suspicion of violating the Prohibition of Unauthorized Computer Access Act and spent over 30 days in a detention center. In 2015, he released the short film "Something Like Cheering Up Sonoda," using his own crime as a motif. This was followed in 2016 by the feature-length version, "The Sonoda Event," which screened in the Feature Film Competition at the SKIP CITY INTERNATIONAL D-Cinema FESTIVAL and won the Grand Prix at the Fukui Film Festival. With this latest film, Ota once again draws inspiration from his personal history to craft a compelling narrative.
title:エス（インターナショナル版）:
The international version of director Masahiro Ota's film "S." Based on Ota's own experience of being arrested, this unique conversational drama depicts the reunion and subsequent rift among a group of friends who gather following the arrest of a young film director.

When young filmmaker Shinichi Someda is arrested, his former university theater friends, including Chiho, reunite for the first time in years to draft a petition in his support. They were supposed to be united in their cause, but...

As seemingly casual conversation flows non-stop, Chiho—who was meant to be wishing for Someda’s return—eventually begins to expose her raw, intense impulses. Director Ota, who was arrested in 2011 on suspicion of violating the Prohibition of Unauthorized Computer Access Act and spent over 30 days in a detention center, drew inspiration from his own life for this story. The original 110-minute version was produced in 2023 and released theatrically in 2024. Following screenings at various international film festivals, including the Dhaka International Film Festival in Bangladesh, this 100-minute international version will be released in April 2026.
title:エディントンへようこそ: From Ari Aster, director of 'Midsommar', and following 'Beau Is Afraid', this thriller stars Joaquin Phoenix and depicts how a local election in a small town locked down during the COVID-19 pandemic escalates into a nationwide crisis. In 2020, the small town of Eddington, New Mexico, USA. Forced into a suffocating quarantine due to the pandemic lockdown, residents' frustration and anxiety are about to explode. Amidst this, town sheriff Joe clashes with ambitious Mayor Ted, who wants to save the town by attracting an IT company, over a minor dispute about wearing masks, and suddenly declares his candidacy for mayor. The fire of Joe and Ted's quarrel spreads, and social media erupts with fake news and hatred. Meanwhile, Joe's wife Louise becomes captivated by the inciting videos of cult leader Vernon, sinking into conspiracy theories. As suspicion, controversy, and rage swirl, violence begets violence, and criticism and conspiracy shroud the truth, the town of Eddington hurtles toward the brink of destruction. Joaquin Phoenix plays Sheriff Joe, Pedro Pascal plays Mayor Ted, Emma Stone plays Joe's wife Louise, and Austin Butler plays cult leader Vernon. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title:エド・ケンパー: A psychological thriller depicting the life of real-life serial killer Ed Kemper, who terrorized America in the early 1970s. In 1969, Ed Kemper, who had been institutionalized at age 15 for murdering his grandparents, is released at 21. Ignoring his psychiatrist's advice, he returns to his estranged mother, who had dominated and psychologically abused him since childhood through verbal abuse and neglect. This twisted mother-son relationship triggers Ed's pathological desires toward women, leading to a series of murders. Despite his brutal crimes, Ed skillfully blends into society and evades police attention. Director Chad Ferrin, known for extreme and experimental horror, sensationalizes the warped psychology of Kemper, a killer who significantly influenced early FBI criminal profiling. Regular Ferrin collaborators Brandon Kirk and Susan Priver play Ed Kemper and his mother, respectively.
title:エリカ: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years. Exploring the boundary between love and obsession, it thrillingly depicts human madness. Tatsuki, a 23-year-old who has never had a girlfriend, meets Erica, a beautiful woman working at a café, and is captivated by her kindness. Their relationship deepens, but Erica's suggestive words and actions, along with inexplicable events around Tatsuki, gradually cast an unsettling shadow over his daily life. Eventually, Erica's abnormal obsession and madness are revealed, dragging Tatsuki into an inescapable fate. Starring Ayumu Mochizuki, who rose to fame with the two-part film "Solomon's Perjury." The heroine Erica is played by Mei Hayashi, who has worked as a model since elementary school and made her acting debut in the 2024 drama "Goodbye, Teacher." The cast also includes Hayato Takao, Kurea Hatsuki, Moeka Koizumi, and Itsuki Fujiwara. The screenplay was written by Tete Inoue of "Initiation Love."
title:エリス＆トム ―ボサノヴァ名盤誕生秘話―: In February 1974, Elis Regina, one of Brazil’s greatest singers, and Antônio Carlos Jobim (Tom Jobim), who achieved worldwide fame in the 1960s with the massive hit "The Girl from Ipanema," gathered in Los Angeles to collaborate on the album *Elis & Tom*. Even now, half a century later, it remains a Bossa Nova masterpiece that shines brilliantly in the music history of not only Brazil but the world. However, behind the scenes of the recording, various problems and frictions were brewing. The chemistry between Elis, the pop star, and Tom, the founder of Bossa Nova who preferred the simple music of the good old days, was disastrous. Furthermore, a rift formed between Tom and César Camargo Mariano, Elis's husband at the time and the album's arranger. What exactly happened during the recording of their album? This must-see documentary delves into those secrets.
title:エレノアってグレイト。: Actress Scarlett Johansson makes her feature directorial debut with this lighthearted drama about the friendship between a powerful elderly woman and a motherless student, sparked by a lie, set against the backdrop of her own Jewish cultural roots. Based on a script by first-time feature screenwriter Tory Kamen, drawing on her own grandmother's and family history, Johansson directs with humor and wit. Eleanor, an elderly woman living in New York, feels a void after losing her longtime friend Bessie. One day, intending to attend a tea party, she accidentally wanders into a support group for Holocaust survivors. There, she improvises a story about Bessie's life, recounting her Holocaust memories. Inspired by the dramatic story, journalism student Nina approaches Eleanor, and a new friendship blossoms. But Eleanor's lie takes on a life of its own, sparking a major uproar. June Squibb ("Thelma") plays the unconventional Eleanor, and Erin Kellyman ("Solo: A Star Wars Story") plays Nina. Rita Zohar, herself a Holocaust survivor, plays Eleanor's late friend Bessie.
title:エンドレス・サマー: A documentary that follows surfers on a global journey of discovery and adventure in search of an eternal summer, this film has been cherished as a pinnacle of surf cinema since its 1966 release. Director Bruce Brown (of *On Any Sunday*) handled the camera himself, embarking on a quest for the perfect wave and summer alongside 21-year-old Mike Hynson—revered as a "master" by legendary surfers—and 18-year-old Robert August, who had been surfing since the age of six. From teaching children to surf in Ghana and hitchhiking through Nigeria to crossing the equator and traveling from Cape Town to Cape St. Francis in South Africa, and connecting with locals in Australia and New Zealand, the film captures their ultimate surf trip across the globe. Originally released in Japan in 1968, the film returns to theaters in July 2024 in a digitally remastered edition.
title:オステンデ:
The 2011 debut film from Argentine director Laura Citarella, who has garnered significant international acclaim after her four-hour-plus mystery epic *Trenque Lauquen* was named the best film of 2023 by France’s *Cahiers du Cinéma*. The story follows a woman who becomes immersed in the fictions lurking within everyday life.

After winning a radio quiz contest, Laura stays at a hotel in Ostende, near Buenos Aires. It is the off-season at the resort, and while waiting for her boyfriend to join her, she begins to observe a middle-aged man staying at the hotel with two young women. Intrigued by the man’s peculiar behavior, Laura lets her imagination run wild as she attempts to unravel the secret narrative that may be unfolding around him...

The film makes its Japanese theatrical debut as part of the special screening program "Laura Citarella Retrospective: Resonating Secrets," held in conjunction with the theatrical release of *Trenque Lauquen*.
title:オスロ、8月31日: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).
title:オニオン・フィールド:
"The Onion Field," a film adaptation of the novel by Joseph Wambaugh—the bestselling author of *The New Centurions* and *The Choirboys*—featuring a star-studded cast, is set to screen at Cinemart Shinjuku as part of the "Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpieces 2" selection starting Friday, May 15, followed by a nationwide rollout.

One night in 1963. Karl and Ian, young police officers who have just been partnered, pull over a car for a traffic violation. The driver is Greg
title:オビ・オバ 文明の終わり: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:オラン・イカン: Starring Dean Fujioka, this creature horror film depicts a life-or-death struggle between humans and a merman on a deserted island near Indonesia during World War II. In 1944, near the end of the war, a Japanese prisoner transport ship is sunk by an Allied attack. Saito, a Japanese soldier, and Bronson, a British prisoner of war, wash ashore on a deserted island, still bound together by chains. Despite their mutual hostility and inability to communicate, the two men soon discover that the island is home to the "Orang Ikan," a merman monster from Malay mythology. Faced with the terrifying creature, the two attempt to work together to survive, but the arrival of other Japanese soldiers causes the carnage to escalate. Eventually, the creature's nest and a fetus are discovered inside a cave, and the battle takes an unexpected turn. Dean Fujioka delivers a powerful performance as the non-English-speaking Saito, starring alongside British actor Callum Woodhouse as Bronson. Alan Maxson, who played one of King Ghidorah's heads in *Godzilla: King of the Monsters*, serves as the suit actor for the Orang Ikan. Mike Wiluan, based in Indonesia and Singapore, wrote and directed the film, with renowned Singaporean filmmaker Eric Khoo serving as a producer.
title:オールド・オーク: British master Ken Loach delivers the final chapter of his 'North East England Trilogy', following 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Missed You'. Set in a former mining town in Northern England, 'The Old Oak' is the last remaining pub cherished by locals. About 30 years after the town's vibrant heyday, it now faces harsh times, but owner TJ Ballantine struggles to keep it going through trial and error. However, when the town begins accepting Syrian refugees, the pub—once a place of solace—turns into a battleground for belonging. Wrestling with the pub's uncertain future, TJ meets Yara, a Syrian woman with a camera, and unexpectedly forms a friendship. Scripted by Paul Laverty, Loach's longtime collaborator, the film is portrayed with warmth and realism. Dave Turner, who appeared in 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Miss You', plays pub owner TJ. Winner of the Audience Award at the 2023 Locarno Film Festival, and screened in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival.

title:オールド・ボーイ: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title:オールド・ボーイ 4K: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title:オーロラの涙: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title:オー・パン・クぺ: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title:オー・パン・クペ: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title:カインド・ハート: A suspense comedy that follows the trail of a serial murder spree by a young man burning with ambition and a thirst for revenge, laced with biting black humor. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Robert Hamer, known for 'It Always Rains on Sunday.' The story is told in flashback form as Louis, a young man of aristocratic blood from the D'Ascoyne family, writes his memoirs in his prison cell, recounting how he systematically murders his relatives to avenge his mother's disownment and reclaim his status. The renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai,' plays all eight members of the D'Ascoyne family who are killed by Louis. Dennis Price plays the protagonist Louis, and Joan Greenwood leaves a strong impression as the cold, calculating heroine. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:カウント・ベイシー: A documentary exploring the life and music of Count Basie, the American jazz pianist who built the golden age of swing jazz. Starting his career as a jazz pianist in his twenties, Count Basie met many top musicians in Kansas City, Missouri, joined the Blue Devils in 1928, and later honed his skills with the Bennie Moten Orchestra before forming his own Basie Orchestra. Fusing jazz and blues and revolutionizing rhythm, he was hailed as the 'King of Swing' and remains beloved by jazz fans and musicians across generations in Japan. The film focuses not only on his public triumphs but also on his private life, which Basie rarely discussed. Through home videos, photo albums, and letters from his family, it reveals his love for his daughter Diane, born with cerebral palsy, and his wife Catherine, who supported the African American civil rights movement. Featuring interviews with current Basie Orchestra members, friends like Quincy Jones and Annie Ross, and archival materials, the documentary traces his legacy and the turbulent social history of 20th-century America. Directed by British filmmaker Jeremy Marre, known for many music documentaries including 'Roots Rock Reggae.'
title:カミング・ホーム: A human drama starring the acclaimed actor Ben Kingsley, humorously depicting a lonely elderly man who, after getting caught up in a bizarre commotion with his neighbors, rediscovers the joy of life. Milton, a 79-year-old man living in a small town in western Pennsylvania, continues to live alone despite his daughter Denise worrying about his early symptoms of dementia. One night, an unidentified flying object from the sky crashes into Milton's yard, shaking his peaceful daily life. When no one around him takes him seriously, Milton shares the secret of the flying object with his neighbors Sandy and Joyce, who are around his age and also witnessed it. The three, each carrying their own loneliness, rediscover the forgotten joys of life and face their futures. Harriet Sansom Harris ("The Bodybuilder") plays Sandy, Jane Curtin ("Coneheads") plays Joyce, and Zoe Winters (series "Succession") plays Milton's daughter Denise. The director is Mark Turtletaub, known as a producer for "Little Miss Sunshine" and "Loving."
title:カリギュラ 究極版:
The "legendary notorious masterpiece" descends in its ultimate form!

Despite being plagued by a series of production disasters, *Caligula* achieved unprecedented box office success upon its release and continues to command a massive global following. Forty-five years later, footage long thought to have been destroyed has been miraculously discovered. Re-edited from over 90 hours of raw material, the "true *Caligula*" has finally been resurrected!

Pandemonium! Infamy! The great tyrant who shook the foundations of cinema returns in a completely new form, reborn for a new era!

The "Ultimate Edition" is a re-edit of the historical epic "Caligula," which depicts the Roman Emperor Caligula, often described as the most decadent in history. In the 1st century AD, the Roman imperial family had fallen into deep corruption under the second emperor, Tiberius. Caligula, the great-grandson of the first emperor, was repulsed by his grandfather Tiberius's perverse sexual proclivities, yet he watched for his chance to seize the throne. When Tiberius eventually fell ill, Caligula plotted his assassination and ascended as the third emperor. After taking a woman named Caesonia as his wife to secure an heir, he began his formal reign and gained immense popularity among the people, but he soon found himself unable to suppress his burgeoning inner desires.

Malcolm McDowell ("A Clockwork Orange") stars as Emperor Caligula, with Helen Mirren ("The Queen") as Empress Caesonia and Peter O'Toole ("Lawrence of Arabia") as the former emperor Tiberius. Produced with a massive budget by Penthouse founder Bob Guccione, the film was directed by erotic cinema master Tinto Brass, with a screenplay by Gore Vidal ("Is Paris Burning?"). Interspersed with shocking scenes that challenge moral boundaries, the film depicts the madness of the tyrant Caligula through a unique lens. Despite being plagued by production troubles, including lawsuits and the firing of the director, it became a massive hit upon its 1979 release. In 2023, this "Ultimate Edition" was created, re-edited from over 90 hours of original footage.
title:カルテットという名の青春:
This documentary offers an authentic look at the youthful days of four young musicians as they charge full speed toward their dreams. Originally broadcast on BS Asahi in 2011 and recipient of the 49th Galaxy Award, the program has been re-edited for this theatrical release. It carefully portrays the emotional nuances of the four musicians—now active on both domestic and international stages—during their formative years.

Music students Taro Uemura (violin), Madoka Sakitsu (violin), Mariko Hara (viola), and Dai Miyata (cello), whose talents were recognized early on, formed the Jupiter Quartet Japan. Through intense practice and the collision of their passions and talents, they grew to be hailed as "Japan’s finest young quartet." With high confidence, they entered the ARD International Music Competition in Munich, the most prestigious challenge for any quartet, only to face elimination in the first round. Experiencing a major setback for the first time in their lives, the four set out on a journey to find a sound that could truly resonate with the world.

Following them over a period of four years, the film captures the radiant days of young people devoting themselves wholeheartedly to their craft. Actor and singer Tomoyo Harada serves as the narrator.
title:カーンターラ 神の降臨: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.
title:ガガ 英雄たちに栄光あれ: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the strict censorship of the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film depicts the miserable existence of people living under corrupt power and bureaucracy. A man trapped on a giant space station is forced, like other prisoners, to volunteer for exploration of a distant planet. Landing on Planet Australia 458, he is welcomed as a hero, but soon realizes that freedom comes at a high price. His violent life is broadcast live for the entertainment of the planet's inhabitants. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:ガザからの声 Episode1 「アハマドの物語」／ガザからの声 E: Ahmad al-Gharban, from Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, survived an Israeli military attack on March 22, but lost both his legs and his fingers. His twin brother Muhammad, his uncle, and his six-year-old cousin were killed. Ahmad had dreamed of becoming a performer, having studied at a circus school alongside his late brother. The displacement camp where the family now lives is situated on the former site of the Islamic University of Gaza, a place where drones circle overhead day and night.
title:ガザからの声 Episode2 「ミュージシャン・アハマドのメッセー: Ahmad Abu Amsha is a musician and a father of five. He once earned his living performing concerts. Originally a resident of Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza, he has been displaced 12 times since the start of the war and currently lives in a camp within the Unknown Soldier's Square in western Gaza. When a ceasefire was announced in January 2025, he returned to Beit Hanoun, only to find his home and studio reduced to rubble. Nevertheless, he remained there, pitching a tent inside a room that was still relatively intact. In March 2025, following the collapse of the ceasefire, he moved to Al-Rimal, where he resides today.
title:ガザからの声 Episode2「ミュージシャン・アハマドのメッセージ: The second installment of "Voices from Gaza," a documentary project that brings to the world the reality of the Gaza Strip in 2025 and the voices of those living there—truths that remain hidden behind fragmented news clips and social media videos. Ahmad Abu-Amsha, a musician and father of five, lived in Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza but has been forced to evacuate 12 times since the start of the war. Following a ceasefire announcement in January 2025, he returned to Beit Hanoun only to find his home and music studio reduced to rubble. In March of the same year, as fighting resumed and his life of displacement continued, Ahmad resolved to support the spirits of his community through music. Alongside fellow musicians, he began teaching instruments and song to children to help ease the anxieties of war. For him, music is a form of resistance and the most powerful way to project his voice to the world. Sending a message to artists worldwide that "silence in the face of injustice is complicity," Ahmad continues to play, aiming to bring joy to as many children as possible. This film is a joint project between Gaza-based production company Aleph Multimedia and Tokyo-based distributor Uplink; Aleph conducted the local filming and reporting, while Uplink handled editing, distribution, and the theatrical release. The film will be released simultaneously in theaters and online.
title:ガリバーの宇宙旅行: Toei Animation's first sci-fi feature. It is also the first feature-length film solely directed by Kuroda Yoshiro, whose highly designed compositions and musical style highlight the allegorical world. Ambitious meta-cinematic structures are employed, marking a breakthrough for a new generation at Toei Animation. The princess's secret revealed at the end carries a critique of civilization, an idea proposed by then-animator Hayao Miyazaki.
title:ガールズ＆パンツァー もっとらぶらぶ作戦です！ 第3幕: The third act of a four-part theatrical series adapting the official spin-off manga *Girls und Panzer: Motto Love Love Sakusen desu!* from the hit anime *Girls und Panzer*, which follows high school girls dedicated to the fictional martial art of "Sensha-do" (tankery). Even as intense Sensha-do matches rage on, the girls are busy enjoying their boisterous
title:キャット・ピープルの呪い: The directorial debut of Robert Wise, the master behind "West Side Story" and "The Sound of Music," made in 1944. This is a sequel to the cult horror film "Cat People" directed by Jacques Tourneur. A lonely, imaginative girl named Amy finds a beautiful ring in a dilapidated old house in her neighborhood. When she returns home and makes a wish on the ring, a beautiful woman named Irena appears before her. Amy becomes friends with Irena, whom only she can see, but...
title:キュア: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title:キラークイーン Phantom School:
This is the sequel to the indie sci-fi action film "Killer Queen Beyond School," which followed the battles of a high school girl whose hands were transformed into tentacles by a parasitic alien. Introducing the new element of the multiverse, the film depicts the next chapter in protagonist Reina’s fight.

Reina Gouriki, who gained special powers after an encounter with an extraterrestrial, and her best friend Anzu Mikawa find themselves visiting entrepreneur Annie Tachibana after a streamer friend leaks footage of Reina in combat. However, Annie is secretly researching the artificial creation of multiverses, and the three are accidentally pulled into an alternate dimension. There, they learn of a "phantom school" that may hold the key to returning home, but during their search, Anzu becomes possessed by the vengeful spirit of Annie's deceased lover.

Saraha returns to the lead role alongside Aiko and other original cast members, joined by a new supporting cast. Director Yusuke Takahashi—who also serves as screenwriter, cinematographer, editor, and VFX supervisor—further deepens the unique "tentacles x youth x sci-fi" world established in the first film.
title:キラー・オブ・シープ: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:ギデンズ・コーの功夫: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title:ギデンズ・コーの功夫（カンフー）: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title:クッチャー兄弟作品集: Twin brothers Mike (1942–) and George Kuchar (1942–2011) were based in New York from the 1960s through the 1970s, releasing low-budget films that incorporated camp aesthetics and queer representation. *Hold Me While I'm Naked* is George Kuchar’s masterpiece, depicting the anguish of a sexually frustrated filmmaker; it was also selected for The Village Voice’s "100 Best Films of the 20th Century." *Sins of the Fleshapoids* is Mike Kuchar’s first solo directorial effort, a comic-book-style sci-fi film that influenced John Waters. *I, An Actress* is one of many short films George Kuchar produced while teaching at the San Francisco Art Institute, capturing the screen test of an aspiring actress.
title:クニコからはじまる話: A woman armed with a knife breaks into the office of a paranormal documentary production company. After injuring an employee, she reveals her motive: to "save humanity." She is apparently obsessed with a conspiracy theory claiming that "unless a certain videotape is returned to its rightful place, the human race will perish." The production crew tracks down the man spreading these theories online. He reveals that the video was once submitted to the "Shi-gazo" series and is a clip so terrifying it surpasses even the legendary "Kuniko." The crew unearths the tape and sets out to uncover the true identity of what is captured on screen. However, this was merely the entrance to a labyrinth with no exit, where countless horrors writhe in the shadows...
title:クベーラ:
Set in a Mumbai swirling with greed, this Indian crime action thriller depicts a homeless young man caught in a conspiracy as he stands up against a national-level evil. To monopolize the vast oil rights lying in the Bay of Bengal, wealthy Mumbai businessman Neeraj Mithra teams up with former CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) ace investigator Deepak Tej to plot a massive money-laundering scheme. As their cover, they choose the nameless homeless—those abandoned by society. Deva Kallam, a simple-hearted young man living as a beggar in the slums, unknowingly finds himself burdened with immense wealth, becoming a target for the organization's assassins. Driven into a corner, he plunges into a brutal battle for survival.

Director Sekhar Kammula, previously acclaimed for his delicate human and romantic dramas, delivers a profound and thrilling portrayal of the dark underbelly of a society ruled by violence and greed. Internationally active actor Dhanush, known for *The Gray Man* and *The Extraordinary Journey of the Fakir*, stars in the lead role, delivering a powerful performance as Deva, the simple young man living in the shadows of society. Nagarjuna Akkineni of *Brahmāstra* plays former CBI agent Deepak, while Rashmika Mandanna of the *Pushpa* duology portrays the heroine Samaira, who holds the key to the story. The title "Kubera" refers to the god of wealth and treasure in Indian mythology.
title:クルージング: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
title:グレン・ミラー物語: Young trombonist Glenn Miller was always in search of a new sound. He joined a prestigious orchestra but left to focus on arranging. The turning point in his music came from his beloved wife Helen. Following her advice, he formed his own band and eventually achieved unprecedented popularity and fame. However, when World War II began, he volunteered for the Air Force. In late 1944, the plane carrying Glenn Miller disappeared over the English Channel... An emotional musical film, with numerous hit songs coloring the love and bond between the couple played by James Stewart and June Allyson!
title:ゲキ×シネ「紅鬼物語」:
"Beni-oni Monogatari," performed in Tokyo and Osaka in early summer 2025 as Gekidan Shinkansen's 45th-anniversary production, has been adapted into a "Geki×Cine" film, allowing audiences to experience the troupe's stage performance on the big screen. Starring Rei Yuzuka—the former Flower Troupe top star making her first stage appearance since leaving the Takarazuka Revue—this Shinkansen-style "fairy tale" unfolds, depicting the destiny of a woman born as an ogre who fell in love with a human.

Once upon a time, long, long ago. It was an era when ogres appeared in the capital and terrorized the people. Sakagami Kinnosuke, a vassal of the nobleman Minamoto no Ao, is attacked by an ogre but manages to fight back and repel it. When he reports this to Ao, fellow vassal Usui Shima suggests that the mysterious disappearance of Ao's wife might also be the work of an ogre. One morning ten years ago, Ao's wife Beniko and daughter Fuji vanished without a trace, leaving behind footprints in the garden that appeared to belong to an ogre. Believing even now that Beniko and Fuji are still alive, Ao resolves to find the ogres' stronghold and bring them back, heading to the Onmyoji Abe no Hechima with Kinnosuke and the others. Meanwhile
title:コードギアス 亡国のアキト 最終章「愛シキモノタチヘ」: The final chapter of "Code Geass: Akito the Exiled," a side story to the hit anime "Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion." The final battle unfolds, featuring the "Alexander Liberté," an upgraded version of the Type-01 Knightmare Frame piloted by the protagonist Akito. Although Yukiya’s bomb successfully reduced the Euro Britannian forces by a third, the wZERO unit remains at a severe disadvantage, besieged at Castle Weisswolf. With Ashley—a former enemy—now fighting by his side, Akito prepares for the ultimate showdown against his rampaging brother, Shin. Facing the final conflict, Akito cuts his hair as a sign of his resolve and entrusts it to Leila.
title:コーナー・オブ・ジ・アース カムチャツカ:
The journey began on February 24, 2022, at Abu Dhabi Airport. Australian filmmakers Spencer Frost and Guy Williment, along with surfers Fraser Dovell and Letty Mortenson, planned a trip to Kamchatka in the Russian Far East in search of new waves along its frozen coastline. This adventure documentary chronicles the friendship and journey of these young men as they take on the overwhelming wilderness of Russia's remote Kamchatka Peninsula.

Bordered by the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of Okhotsk and home to over 150 volcanoes, Kamchatka is a true hidden frontier. It is said that until around 1991, access was prohibited not only for foreigners but even for Russian citizens. Because it remains largely unexplored, it is considered one of the most precious places on Earth, where vast, untouched nature still thrives.

With little local information available, the group relied on a surfer living in Kamchatka. After two years of preparation via smartphone, their visas were finally issued, and they were ready to depart. However, just one hour before boarding their flight to Moscow at a transit airport, unbelievable news flashed across the television: Russia had invaded Ukraine. Amidst the chaos, they had no choice but to continue their journey to Kamchatka, where their friend was waiting.

Upon setting foot in the region, they were met with Mi-8 helicopters, snowmobiles, and campsites buried in snow. There, they finally met their Kamchatkan friend for the first time. This is a heartwarming adventure documentary that reaffirms the power of friendship to connect people across different nations and backgrounds.
title:ゴダール・ソシアリスム: A visual poem by French master Jean-Luc Godard, depicting modern Europe with overwhelming visual beauty and masterful editing. It is Godard's first feature film shot entirely in digital, his first in six years since 'Our Music.' Set on a luxury cruise ship touring the Mediterranean, it consists of three movements: the first movement 'Such Things' depicts human drama over gold lost during the Spanish Civil War; the second movement 'Where to, Europe' is a political comedy about a family living in the French countryside; and the third movement 'We Humans' explores history and culture across six locations related to human history, using countless quotations and collages. Utilizing various video formats and freely incorporating images, words, sounds, and even digital noise, it is depicted with overwhelming density and speed, full of rebellious spirit. Musician Patti Smith, guitarist Lenny Kaye, and philosopher Alain Badiou appear as themselves. Screened as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title:ゴリラホール:
Set at the real-life music venue "GORILLA HALL OSAKA," this youth ensemble drama depicts the struggles and growth of young people living for music. Asako works at Gorilla Hall while pursuing her own musical dreams, but her band "GIRL TALKING ABOUT LOVE," for which she is the guitarist and vocalist, is struggling against the harshness of reality. Meanwhile, her boyfriend Ichiya is finding success as the frontman of the band "SUMMER JOE," steadily climbing the ladder to stardom. When a major label announces an audition, both Ichiya’s band and Asako’s group are given a chance to compete. Despite her doubts, Asako takes a new step forward with her bandmates, only to be confronted by an unexpected reality on that very stage.

Kansai-based singer-songwriter AIK makes her acting debut in her first starring role as Asako, with Wataru Momma ("Manji Reverse") playing her boyfriend, Ichiya. The supporting cast features Arata Furuta, Ayumi Ito, Tomomitsu Yamaguchi, and Tomoka Kurotani. Koji Uehara ("Before the Rainbow Falls") wrote and directed the film, with music by Kj (Dragon Ash, The Ravens) and actor Kyosuke Yabe serving as executive advisor.
title:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第1話/第2話: The first continuous TV drama (10 episodes) helmed by Kore-eda, who considers TV dramas a more formative experience than films. It includes devices that suggest connections to his past films, such as casting and character settings. It was screened at the International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2013.
title:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第3話/第4話: Ryota, troubled by the small triangular hat he found in the forest, discovers a notebook that appears to have been written by Eisuke. It is a notebook recording the places where Kuna is said to appear. Guided by his father's words, Ryota walks around town and hears an unexpected fact from Naho, whom he meets by chance.
title:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第5話/第6話: Ryota has returned to work, but his own project is progressing smoothly under his subordinate's leadership, and he is increasingly losing his presence. Meanwhile, as Eisuke diligently pursues rehabilitation, Toshiko grows more suspicious about the relationship between her husband and Naho's mother.
title:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第7話/第8話: Eisuke is discharged from the hospital and returns home. The family gathers around the dinner table for the first time in a while to celebrate his homecoming. Amid this, Ryota confronts Eisuke about a photo of a plot of land for sale that was tucked inside a notebook, but he is confused and angered by his father's response.
title:ゴーイング マイ ホーム 第9話/第10話: On the day of the event to search for Kuna, as the group searches for her in the forest, the feelings each of them has been harboring gradually come to the surface. As the event draws to a close, Ryota receives a phone call from Toshiko.
title:ゴーレム: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of Polish dystopian cinema, produced while navigating the strict censorship of the socialist regime during the late 1970s and 1980s. The film depicts the harsh reality of clones created for human evolution through a style that represents the pinnacle of sharp satire and surrealism. A man arrested on suspicion of murder is interrogated by the police, but he cannot recall the details of the crime or even his own life. He is eventually returned to a world of madmen, deranged dentists, murderous doctors, and scientists who believe the secret of human creation lies within the walls of a cast-iron oven. The man’s journey to discover who he is and what it means to be human intersects with them all. The film will receive its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special retrospective "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The Apocalypse Tetralogy" (opening February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title:サイボーグ009怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title:サイボーグ009／サイボーグ009 怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title:サイボーグ００９ 怪獣戦争: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works").
