title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第1巻「若鮎の巻」:
This is the first volume of an epic six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, that chronicles the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII from age 84 to 90. Nizaemon was a mainstay of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras. In 1987, as the "Wakaayu-no-kai"—a study group for young Kamigata Kabuki actors—prepared for its eighth independent performance, the camera follows Nizaemon XIII as he provides supervision and acting instruction. The featured plays are "Ichijo Okura Monogatari" from *Kiichi Hogen Sanryaku no Maki* and "Domomata" from *Keisei Hangonko*, with the film tracking the process from the rehearsal room to the final stage performance. The rehearsal footage captures Nizaemon meticulously instructing on every detail, from pronunciation to physical movement, conveying the raw intensity of the practice space. 

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The Ode to Hayachine*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第2巻「人と芸の巻 上巻」:
The second volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, recording the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who supported the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This is the first half of the "The Man and His Art" segment, following Nizaemon over a four-year period from age 84 to 88, capturing his occasional discourses on his craft, his stage performances, and his daily life.

The film includes footage of rehearsals and performances from 1987, featuring "Numazu" from *Iga-goe Dochu Sugoroku* (Nakaza, Osaka), "Daimonjiya" from *Kamiko Jitate Ryomen Kagami* (National Theatre, Tokyo), and *Kotobuki Soga no Taimen* (Minamiza, Kyoto). The latter was a milestone performance marking his 35th consecutive appearance at the Minamiza’s *Kaomise* festival, and the camera captures Nizaemon as he receives commendations and interviews. Furthermore, it depicts his daily routine
title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第3巻「人と芸の巻 中巻」:
The third volume of a monumental six-part documentary series totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, capturing the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—between the ages of 84 and 90. This is the middle installment of the "Man and Art" section, which turns the camera toward Nizaemon’s artistic discourse, stage performances, and personal life over a four-year period from age 84 to 88.

The film features his 1988 performances at Tokyo’s Kabuki-za, including the "Gakumonjo" and "Domyoji" scenes from *Sugawara Denju Tenarai Kagami* and the "Hanawatashi" scene from *Imoseyama Onna Teikin*. It further captures a "Gathering to Hear Artistic Talks" with his patrons; rehearsal footage for his role as Okina in *Kotobuki Shiki Sanbaso* for the opening of Omiya Sonic City; a gathering of supporters in Matsumoto, Nagano; reflections on a short story he wrote at age 23; his passion for trains; a scene of him plucking a shamisen at a Gion teahouse; and the Kataoka family’s Obon traditions.

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and because it has never been released on home video or streaming platforms, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will receive their first Japanese theatrical screening in 17 years.
title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第4巻「人と芸の巻 下巻」: The fourth volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, this film chronicles the life of the legendary actor Nizaemon Kataoka XIII—a pillar of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This installment serves as the second half of the "Man and His Art
title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第5巻「孫右衛門の巻」: The fifth volume of a monumental six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, which captures the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—the legendary actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. The camera focuses on the rehearsals and stage performances of the "Fuin-giri" and "Ninokuchi-mura" scenes from *Koi Bikyaku Yamato Orai* (The Love Messenger on the Yamato Highway) held at the Kabukiza Theatre in Tokyo in 1989. During dress rehearsals, a red lamp was placed at the edge of the *hanamichi* runway to serve as a marker for Nizaemon, whose eyesight had weakened, yet he could no longer see even that guide. On stage, Nizaemon performed the role of Magoemon, with Kataoka Takao as Chubei and Nakamura Jakuemon as Umekawa. The beginning of this volume also includes interview footage from the 1988 publication of Nizaemon’s photo book *Fushi*, featuring the master himself alongside his sons Gato, Hidetaro, and Takao. The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The
title:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第6巻「登仙の巻」:
The sixth volume of a comprehensive six-part, 10-hour and 46-minute documentary following the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—a master actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. Capturing Nizaemon’s final years from age 88 to 90, the film records performances including "Sanmon" from *The Golden Gate and the Paulownia Crest* (1991, Minamiza, Kyoto), "Arakawa no Sakichi" from *Eight Views of Ryogoku* (1992, Minamiza), "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" from *The Treasury of Loyal Retainers of the Genroku Era* (1992, Misonoza, Nagoya), "The Carriage Pull" from *Sugawara and the Secrets of Calligraphy* (1992, Minamiza), *The Auspicious Sanbaso* (1993, Meijiza reopening, Tokyo), *The Felicitous Soga Confrontation* (1993, Meijiza), "The Inner Garden" from *Kiichi Hogen’s Book of Strategy* (1993, Minamiza), and his final stage appearance in "The State Barge on the Lake" from *The Eight-Array Guardian Castle* (1993, Minamiza), portraying a man dedicated to his craft until the very end. 

In the "Artistic Discussion" segment, he reflects on "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" and recalls seeing Matsumoto Koshiro in "The Inner Garden" at the Imperial Theatre 70 years earlier. The film also features their 62nd wedding anniversary celebration and interviews with his wife, Kiyoko, his second daughter, Yuko, and his fifth daughter, Shizuka. Directed by Sumiko Haneda, known for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, opportunities for theatrical screenings have been limited, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will be screened in Japanese theaters for the first time in 17 years.
title:武田純一郎作品集: Following the suspension of production at the former Tokyo Cinema, Junichiro Takeda established Cine Science (now ICAM) in 1968, going on to produce numerous scientific films utilizing microscopic photography. This program features three works: *The History of Rats Written in Chromosomes*, which reveals the history of rats as a species through chromosome analysis; *From Egg to Human*, which traces the mystery of the birth of life accompanied by narration from sisters Eriko and Kyoko Kishida; and *The Wonder of Holes*, which employs both microscopic and outdoor photography to unravel the functions of various holes, pores, and tubes of all sizes.
title:歩いても 歩いても: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.

title:歴史は女で作られる: Max Ophüls, director of *La Ronde* (1950), helms this epic depicting the romantic escapades of the real-life 19th-century beauty and dancer Lola Montès, brought to life through the brilliant hues of Technicolor and the grand scale of CinemaScope. Although it was one of the most expensive French productions of 1956, it is famously known as a "cursed masterpiece" after the studio re-edited the film against the director’s wishes, sparking controversy and leading to its commercial failure. In 19th-century Paris, after a troubled childhood, Lola Montès becomes a circus dancer and gains notoriety through a series of high-profile affairs. Eventually, she finds her way to Bavaria, where she captivates King Ludwig I. The film was revived in 2011 with a digitally remastered version.
title:死ねばいいのに: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
title:死亡遊戯で飯を食う。 44:CLOUDY BEACH: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.

title:死神バーバー: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
title:残されたヘッドライン:
A documentary film compiling Japanese newsreel footage that has been lost to history. Behind the evolution of news from newspapers and radio into visual media were the "newsreels" once screened in cinemas. This work features a careful selection of footage across various fields filmed from the Meiji era to the early 1950s, with a primary focus on the early Showa period. Produced with the cooperation of Chunichi Eigasha—a company that created theatrical newsreels during the Showa era—the film weaves together culture, politics, entertainment, social customs, and incidents that have faded with time. 

Categorized into "War," "Disasters and Accidents," "Infrastructure," and "Culture and Customs," the film presents rare footage, including some being shown for the first time in Japan. Highlights include the threat of the dictator Hitler, a legendary snake-handling nude dancer, the enforcement of the Prostitution Prevention Act, and the personal effects, final letters, and hidden stories of the Kamikaze Special Attack Units. The narration is provided by Yuichi Mayama, the Nippon TV news anchor who brought the news into living rooms across the nation throughout the Showa and Heisei eras.
title:殺しの分け前 ポイント・ブランク: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.

title:殺し屋1: A violent action film based on the popular manga of the same name by Hideo Yamamoto, directed by Takashi Miike. Set in a yakuza apartment building in Shinjuku's Kabukicho district, it depicts a surreal battle between insane men with thorough violence. The boss of the Anjo-gumi yakuza group, based in Kabukicho, suddenly disappears. Kakihara, a masochist who loved the violence given by the boss, persistently searches the city. Eventually, he learns of a hitman named Ichi, and upon witnessing his deranged killing style, feels an excitement akin to love. Tadanobu Asano plays Kakihara, with bleached hair and a face full of scars, and Nao Omori plays Ichi, a weak-willed man who turns into a crying killing machine. The cast includes Shinya Tsukamoto, Suzuki Matsuo, SABU, and Jun Kunimura. The screenplay is by Sakichi Sato, known for 'The Golden Grasslands.' A 4K remastered version will be re-released in May 2026.
title:殺し屋のプロット: Directed by, starring, and produced by Michael Keaton, this crime noir follows an aging hitman losing his memory as he attempts one final perfect crime. John Knox is a contract killer with an unconventional past, holding two PhDs and having served as a former Army reconnaissance officer. Upon being diagnosed with a rapidly progressing form of dementia that will erase his memory within weeks, he resolves to retire from the trade. But just as he prepares to walk away, his estranged son, Miles, appears on his doorstep. Miles tearfully confesses to murdering the man who raped his daughter and begs his father to help cover up the crime. Racing against his own fading mind, Knox sets out to pull off one last perfect crime for the sake of his son. Alongside Keaton as Knox, the film stars Al Pacino as his confidant Xavier, Academy Award winner Marcia Gay Harden (Pollock) as his ex-wife Ruby, and James Marsden (X-Men series) as Miles.
title:殺し屋１ ４K:
The boss of the Anjo-gumi has suddenly vanished, along with 300 million yen of the gang's funds. Kakihara (Tadanobu Asano), an ultimate masochist who lived for the violence inflicted upon him by his boss, believes the man has been abducted but is still alive, and begins a relentless search through Kabukicho. Eventually, he learns of the existence of a killer named Ichi (Nao Omori) and feels a thrill akin to love at the sight of his brutal handiwork. "I want to meet Ichi soon." "I want to taste the despair before I'm killed." Despite their paths crossing without meeting time and again, Kakihara’s heart races at the prospect of their encounter. Now, the moment of their meeting draws closer with every passing second...

*Screening in 2K at this theater.
title:水俣一揆 一生を問う人々: Director Noriaki Tsuchimoto, who brought global attention to Minamata disease with *Minamata: The Victims and Their World*, returns to the subject in this feature-length documentary. On March 20, 1973, the Kumamoto District Court ruled in favor of the patients, ordering Chisso Corporation to pay damages and establishing its legal liability for the disaster. Following the verdict, direct negotiations unfolded at Chisso’s headquarters as patients sought compensation for lifelong medical care and living expenses. This film closely follows the actions of the patients involved in these talks. Utilizing synchronized sound recording, the film captures the raw intensity of the negotiations, providing a meticulous record of the patients' struggle.
title:氷血: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area. The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
title:汚れた英雄: The International A-Class 500cc final (All-Japan Road Race Championship, Round 8) is held at the UGO Circuit. The fateful showdown between bike racers Akio Kitano and Keishi Oki ends just before the finish line when Oki overtakes Kitano, pushing the decisive battle to the final round. Kitano uses his handsome looks and sexual prowess to secure funding from multiple patrons to maintain his team. When Christine Adams, heir to a billion-dollar fortune and owner of an international conglomerate, arrives in Japan, Kitano quickly approaches her and successfully secures funding. Finally, Kitano faces the final race, but...
title:決断するとき: Starring Cillian Murphy of "Oppenheimer," this film adapts the bestselling novel "Small Things Like These" by Irish author Claire Keegan. Set against the backdrop of the real-life human rights abuses at Ireland's Magdalene laundries, it depicts the inner conflict and decision of a man who discovers a truth society has long ignored. In 1985, in a small Irish town, coal merchant Bill Furlong lives modestly with his family. One day before Christmas, while delivering coal to a local convent, a girl confined there begs him, "Please get me out of here." Confronted with the reality of young women suffering with no way out, Bill understands it would be wise to look the other way, but his conscience torments him, leading him to make a fateful decision. Emily Watson of "Breaking the Waves" plays the convent's Mother Superior, Sister Mary, winning the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024. Eileen Walsh of "The Magdalene Sisters" plays Bill's wife, Eileen. Murphy, who fell in love with the original novel, personally pushed for the film adaptation and served as a producer for the first time. Directed by Tim Mielants of "Peaky Blinders," the film also features Matt Damon as a producer and Ben Affleck as an executive producer.
title:沓掛時次郎 遊侠一匹: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title:沖縄狂想曲: A documentary that spotlights various issues occurring in Okinawa, delving into the reality of Okinawa and Japan. Directed by Takafumi Ota, known for social issue works such as "The House of the Rising Sun" and "Documentary: The Battle of Okinawa - Unknown Memories of Sorrow," the film investigates numerous problems facing Okinawa, including the Henoko base issue, the International University helicopter crash, Osprey noise and crash incidents, as well as historical events like the Koza riot and the Yumiko-chan incident. Experts including former major newspaper editorial board members, prominent university professors, a former mayor, and former prefectural government executives thoroughly explain realities that major media cannot report. Furthermore, the film introduces the challenges of former Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota, the true intent behind former Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama's statement "at least outside the prefecture," and a parliamentary question by Taro Yamamoto of Reiwa Shinsengumi.
title:沢田美由紀のガマランドにお邪魔します:
Set in the mysterious amusement park "Gamaland," this medium-length horror film employs a found-footage format to depict an inexplicable story surrounding Miyuki Sawada. Gamaland was a real-life location once symbolized by its iconic, giant toad statue. A VHS tape recorded there, steeped in the atmosphere of the early Heisei era, captures a date between a couple, Kohei Shimizu and Miyuki Sawada—but the footage gradually transforms into something deeply unsettling.

The film is directed by Koki Nishii, the filmmaker behind the YouTube channel "Filmest TV," which specializes in recreating modern subjects with a 1980s and 90s aesthetic. Nishii, who also made waves with the September 2024 YouTube drama *Tomochika Suspense Theater: Sotoyu Meguri Mystery - Dogo Striptease Girl Serial Murders*, served as screenwriter and editor, and appears in the film under the name "Nishii." The cast features Tsubasa Nakahara (Masashi Yamamoto’s *DUDE*) as Miyuki Sawada and Takeo Gozu (Netflix’s *Tokyo Swindlers*). The film is produced by NOTHING NEW, a label garnering attention for horror works such as *Chilled* (winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival), the short film anthology *NN4444*, and the medium-length horror *Shiki*.
title:河内山宗俊: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title:河童のクゥと夏休み: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
title:津田寛治に撮休はない:
A "new sensation" mystery featuring actor Kanji Tsuda—who has portrayed a vast array of roles across countless films and television dramas—playing himself as a lead for the first time. Kanji Tsuda is a face familiar to every film enthusiast. Leading a hectic life filled with filming, rehearsals, meetings, and events, the concept of a "day off from shooting" is non-existent to him. However, starting from a certain day, inexplicable events begin to occur around Tsuda, and he starts to suspect that someone is stalking him. As his mental state gradually deteriorates, Tsuda begins to lose his sense of self, eventually suffering from strange hallucinations. A shocking truth awaits him.

Tetsu Watanabe, Hiromi Iwasaki, Ryo Shinoda, Ren Komai, Shunya Itabashi, and film director Noboru Iguchi appear as themselves. The cast also includes Yuri Hirasawa as Tsuda’s daughter Sachi, Motoki Kobayashi as film director Sadahisa Kasanashi, Ryu Ichinose as popular young talent Rento Oshikida, and Yumiko Nakamura as Tsuda’s manager Seiko Kumi. The film is directed and written by Takayuki Kayano, known for "Danshari Paradise" and "Journey Beyond the Night."
title:海よりもまだ深く: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title:海灘的一天: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title:海街diary: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title:海辺のポーリーヌ: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title:海辺の一日: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title:海辺の恋:
The 1963 feature debut of Guy Gilles—a director currently being rediscovered as a "forgotten master of the Nouvelle Vague"—is an autobiographical work that captures the fleeting love of youth. On a summer shore, Geneviève and Daniel, a sailor, find love in each other's arms. But when the vacation ends, he returns to the port city of Brest while she goes back to Paris. Hoping for a reunion, they continue to write to one another. Their story expands with the arrival of Guy, another sailor returning from the Algerian War, as the paths and emotions of the three quietly interweave. 

Starring Daniel Moosmann and Geneviève Thénier, the film also features director Guy Gilles himself as the sailor Guy, with a supporting cast of legendary actors including Jean-Pierre Léaud, Jean-Claude Brialy, Alain Delon, and Juliette Gréco. Impressed by Gilles’ 1959 short *Au biseau des baisers*, the master Jean-Pierre Melville provided partial funding for the film. A winner of the Critics’ Prize at the Locarno Film Festival, it will be released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title:消えない光: Screening at the "Finland Film Festival 2025" (November 8–14, 2025 / Eurospace, Tokyo). Screening at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title:済州島四・三事件 ハラン: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.

title:火葬人: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title:災 劇場版: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.

title:炎かがよへ:
This historical drama depicts the life of Ashina Moritaka, the 18th head of the Ashina clan, which ruled the Aizu region (modern-day Fukushima Prefecture) for 400 years starting from the Kamakura period. Though he earned the respect of even Oda Nobunaga, Moritaka’s life ended at the age of just 24.

The Nikaido clan, defeated in battle by the Ashina—a powerful Sengoku-era daimyo family based in Mutsu Province—offered their young heir, Moritaka, as a hostage. Following his first battle at age 14, Moritaka has a fateful encounter with the warlord Satake Yoshishige, leading to a relationship that would eventually transcend a mere military alliance. When the Ashina heir, Ashina Morioki, dies young of illness, the clan leader Ashina Moriuji chooses the hostage Moritaka to marry Morioki’s widow, Hikohime, and Moritaka ascends as the 18th head of the house. After consolidating power, Moritaka one day encounters a vassal, Oba Sanzaemon, performing a beautiful dance and finds himself captivated.

Towa Araki, known for his roles in the NHK Taiga drama "Segodon" and the serial TV novel "Hanbun, Aoi," stars as Moritaka. He is joined by Motonosuke, an actor and influencer, and Hina Higuchi, a former member of Nogizaka46. The film is directed and written by Keita Matsuda ("The Restaurant at the Edge of the World," "Flowers Blooming on the Shore").
title:炎のごとく: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
title:炎上: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title:無こその存在 あるいは鮎子の人生:
A social drama depicting the darkness of a crumbling Japan through the story of a young woman living at the bottom of a stratified society who dreams of terrorism, and the mysterious Italian man who helps her. 

Ayuko Amami, a woman in her 20s, commits repeated acts of fraud and theft using matching apps. Her accomplice is Otoya Yamaguchi, whom she met on an app a year ago; they are "comrades in terrorism," a bond that is neither friendship nor romance. The two plan a large-scale terrorist attack targeting the Ministry of Finance, but unable to even find a route to acquire firearms, they continue their fraudulent activities. One day, they are caught in an undercover sting operation led by Detective Sasaki. While Otoya is arrested on the spot, Ayuko manages to escape. During her flight, she is rescued by Leo, a foreign tour guide who happens to be passing by. Upon learning of Ayuko’s terrorist plot, Leo introduces her to Manjiro Haruki, a high-profile wanted terrorist, but...

Ayumi Sakuma (Fast Break) stars as Ayuko, with Diego Martina—a multi-talented scholar of Japanese literature, translator, poet, and illustrator—playing Leo, and Naoya Serizawa (NHK’s Hanbun, Aoi) as Otoya. The film is written and directed by Gen Takahashi, known for works such as Confessions of a Dog and GOTH.
title:焼け石と雨粒: The debut feature film by Director Yuya Kushida, a graduate of the Japan Institute of the Moving Image, completed in 2022. This coming-of-age drama draws on the director's own experiences of heartbreak to depict young people struggling to navigate unconventional relationships. Akira Ujita, a part-time worker, develops feelings for a clerk at a local supermarket, but unsure of how to handle his emotions, he begins stalking them. He reaches out to Satsuki, a high school classmate and art student, for advice, but finds himself gradually drawn to her instead. As Akira and Satsuki confront their pasts and their current realities, they grow closer, until a pivotal event occurs between them. The film stars Hiroki Sano, who gained recognition for his role in Kohei Igarashi's "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," which screened at the Venice International Film Festival. Although it received only a single theatrical screening following its completion in 2022, the film finally sees a full theatrical release in 2026, four years later.
title:熊蟲萬壽無彊クマムシばんじゅ・きわみなし The Space Bea: A documentary focusing on the theme of "life strategies," examining how life forms adapt by changing themselves in response to their environment. Tardigrades survive extreme environments. The Okinawa ruby goby changes sex within its society. Ginkgo biloba creates a "sea" within its seeds to nurture swimming sperm. These life forms have persisted by employing strategies of self-transformation in tune with their surroundings. This feature-length film weaves together three subjects into a single narrative, revealing their quiet wisdom. It integrates the short documentary "The Space Bears 4 Ever: Life Strategies"—which records the daily lives, feeding, molting, reproduction, and cryptobiosis of three species of tardigrades living in moss on roadsides in Tokyo and Chiba—with two other short documentaries produced by the same team (cinematography by Tsuneya Taniguchi, directed by Yuki Suzuki, produced by Kazuo Okada): "Sex Change: Society and Sex Reversal in the Okinawa Ruby Goby" and "The Sea Within the Seed: Ginkgo Sperm and the Reproductive Evolution of Plants."
title:熱狂をこえて: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title:父と家族とわたしのこと:
A documentary that quietly observes people confronting inherited pain through the lens of war trauma. In recent years, the fact that many returning soldiers suffered from severe PTSD has increasingly come to light. The deep scars etched into their hearts are sometimes passed down to children and grandchildren in the form of domestic violence or addiction, leading to the breakdown of family relationships. 

The film follows three individuals: a woman who grew up suffering severe abuse from her father and went on to abuse her own daughter; a man whose childhood memories of his veteran father’s verbal abuse toward his mother left deep scars that eventually led to violence against his own wife; and a woman who developed complex PTSD due to abuse from her mother—who was devoted to a new religious movement—and who continues to struggle with her relationship with her own daughter. As the investigation delves into the roots of the "difficulty in living" shared by these three, a common thread emerges: their fathers or grandfathers all served in the war. 

The film is directed by Hyoma Shimada, who has documented individuals striving to stand on their own feet while being at the mercy of massive forces like war and national division in works such as "I'm Just Going to North Korea for a Bit" and "Live, Live, Live." The music was composed by Takashi Watanabe, known for "The Great Passage."
title:牛乳屋フランキー: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
title:特急にっぽん: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.

title:犬王: A feature-length musical anime directed by Masaaki Yuasa (*Lu Over the Wall*), adapting Hideo Furukawa’s novel *Tales of the Heike: Inu-Oh*, which was modeled after the real-life Noh performer Inu-Oh who flourished during the Nanboku-cho and Muromachi periods. In the capital of Kyoto, a child is born into the Hiei-za family of Omi Sarugaku. This child would grow up to be the Noh performer Inu-Oh, who would later drive the masses into a frenzy, but his physical form is so bizarre that the adults cover his body in clothing and hide his face behind a mask. One day, Inu-Oh meets Tomona, a blind boy and biwa priest. Bound by a firm friendship as business partners to survive the world, the two unleash their respective talents and produce a string of hits. As Inu-Oh captivates audiences on stage, he transforms a part of his body with every performance, gradually attaining a singular beauty. The film features character designs by Taiyo Matsumoto, the manga artist of *Ping Pong* (which Yuasa previously adapted), and a screenplay by Akiko Nogi (*I Am a Hero*).
title:犬神家の一族: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
title:猫を放つ: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title:甘い罠: Screened as part of "Eiga no Kuni Masterpiece Selection II: Claude Chabrol’s Unreleased Masterpieces," a series showcasing previously unreleased works in Japan by the French New Wave master who passed away in 2010. Based on American author Charlotte Armstrong’s *The Chocolate Cobweb*, this psychological crime drama explores the conflict between good and evil lurking in the depths of the human heart, set to the strains of classical masterpieces including Liszt’s piano piece "Funérailles."
title:田名網敬一作品集: A leading figure in Japan’s underground art scene, Keiichi Tanaami has worked prolifically across a wide range of genres, including painting, collage, sculpture, animation, experimental film, and installation. This program screens eight of his works that influenced Japanese experimental cinema, produced by drawing on the methodologies and techniques he cultivated as a designer.
title:田園に死す: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title:男子有情: In 1886, as the Freedom and People's Rights Movement surged once again, three spirited students, including Shimada (Oka), took to the streets of Tokyo to sing "Enka"—songs of resistance against the old shogunate system—to appeal to the common people. Their headmaster, seeing great promise in their futures, urged them to enter a newspaper’s essay contest as a stepping stone to success. However, in an attempt to save Shigeyo (Hanai), the woman he loves, Shimada becomes a suspect in a murder case and is put on trial. This entertaining film skillfully captures the spirit of the Meiji era and the rhythmic 7-5 meter of Enka. Presented in a new print from Toho’s original master.
title:発掘されたアニメーション映画: *Dental Health* is a live-action educational film that utilizes animation to explain the importance of dental hygiene. *Chiyogami Cartoon: The Dango’s Whereabouts* features Kabuki music, a rarity for an animated film. *Thumbelina* is a silhouette animation based on the Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale. *Weather School (Supervised by the Central Meteorological Observatory)* is a short film providing an accessible explanation of meteorology for children, with animation production subcontracted to Nihon Doga (now Toei Animation). *The Dull Sword* [New Longest Version] and *Fairy Tale: The Piggyback Ghost*—both of which premiered as new prints in the screening program "Excavated Films 2018"—have undergone their first digital restoration and conversion to DCP for this occasion.
title:発掘されたサイレント映画: "The Green Horseman" is a Fuji Eiga production starring Denmei Suzuki. Although only a small portion survives (the original was 10 reels), it is a rare contemporary drama centered on horse racing. "In Search of Mother" is the second film adaptation following Hiroshi Inagaki’s 1931 version, also starring Chiezo Kataoka. While the original film is in extremely poor condition and incomplete, it is a precious surviving work. These will be screened alongside the 16mm version of "A Straightforward Boy," which premiered at the 2023 "TIFF/NFAJ Classics."
title:発掘された教育劇映画: *Glory of the Village: Promotion of Side Jobs for Rural Revitalization* is an educational drama advocating patriotic frugality. After completing his military service, a young man named Okubo returns to his village; distressed by the moral decay of the inhabitants, he makes a success of a side business and becomes a model for the community. A key highlight is the restoration of the vibrant tinting and toning applied to the original film elements. *Patriotic Tale: Kimigayo*, based on an original story and screenplay by Chiaki Tsukuda, portrays the economic struggles of a farming village against the backdrop of the Russo-Japanese War.
title:白い車に乗った女:
A suspense thriller marking the first collaboration between Jung Ryeo-won (*My Lovely Sam Soon*) and Lee Jung-eun (*Parasite*). The film depicts the course of a mysterious murder case in a snow-covered rural town through an unpredictable and original narrative.

At dawn, a writer named Do-gyeong arrives at a hospital with an unconscious woman in her car. When police officer Hyeon-ju questions the distraught Do-gyeong, she claims the woman is her sister and that they were fleeing from her sister's violent fiancé. However, it is soon revealed that the two are complete strangers, and the man alleged to be the fiancé is found dead in the snow. As the credibility of Do-gyeong's testimony is called into question, Hyeon-ju struggles to uncover the truth behind the incident, but...

Jung Ryeo-won plays the writer Do-gyeong, who holds the key to the case, winning the Korean Fantastic Actor Award at the 26th Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival in 2022 for her performance. Lee Jung-eun plays Hyeon-ju, a police officer who must confront her own trauma while conducting the investigation. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Ko Hye-jin.
title:白夜: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title:白夜（1971）:
Following his 1969 film "A Gentle Woman," French master Robert Bresson directed this drama, adapting a short story by the literary giant Dostoevsky. Jacques, a lonely young painter, spends his days fantasizing about meeting his ideal woman and recording his thoughts into a tape recorder. One night, on the Pont Neuf bridge over the Seine, he encounters Marthe, a beautiful woman with a look of despair. Marthe explains that her lover left to study in America a year ago, promising to meet her in a year's time once he was in a position to marry; however, a year has passed, and he has failed to appear. Harboring passionate feelings for Marthe, Jacques does everything he can to help her reunite with her promised lover, yet the man does not show. Before long, Marthe’s heart also begins to be drawn toward Jacques.

The setting has been moved from the 19th-century Petersburg of the original story to the Paris of the time of filming. In Japan, the film was first released in theaters in 1978, followed by a 35mm new print release in 2012. A 4K restored version will receive a revival release in 2025, with another revival scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpieces Selection."
title:白衣の男: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title:看我今天怎麼說: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title:真夜中の河: An independent film written and directed by actor Yusuke Nagumo, a native of Miyakojima, Okinawa, based on his own experiences as a sewage worker. Starring former child actor Hiroki Ida (now Kunihiko Ida), the film also features appearances by numerous well-known actors close to Nagumo. Uehara (Ida), who moved from Okinawa to Tokyo to pursue his dream of acting, scrapes by working as a film extra while supporting himself with a part-time job cleaning sewers. As he crawls through an underground world that stands in stark contrast to the city's hustle and bustle, Uehara begins to find hope through his interactions with a colorful cast of coworkers.
title:真実: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title:真田風雲録: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title:真空地帯: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
title:眩暈 VERTIGO: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
