Documentary of Baby Assassins
The Spectre's Grandson
The Unnameable Dance
title:鍵: A bold, original film adaptation of Junichiro Tanizaki's novel 'The Key', which explores the depths of sexuality through the alternating diaries of a married couple. Starring Mitsuru Fukikoshi, it lays bare a dying man's obsessive attachment and pure love for his younger wife. Kenzo Kenmochi, who runs a construction company, is told by his doctor he has only six months to live. Worried about his much younger wife Ikuko, he schemes to push her into an affair with his subordinate Kimura. As Kimura and Ikuko grow closer, things go according to plan, but Kenzo cannot let go of his feelings for Ikuko. Despite his physical decline, his jealousy intensifies. When he secretly reads Ikuko's diary, he finds her feelings of strong attraction to Kimura's body. Mitsuru Fukikoshi humorously plays the clumsy, jealousy-consumed Kenzo. Kei Kanno plays his wife Ikuko, and Keisuke Koide plays Kimura. The film is directed and written by Shinji Imaoka, known for scripting 'The Zombie Child' and directing 'Reiko and the Dolphin', with Minoru Matsumoto co-writing the screenplay.
title:鍵から抜け出した女: An adventure-action romance feature film adaptation of the short story of the same name by Juza Unno, who published numerous science fiction novels from the pre-war to post-war eras and is known as the "father of Japanese SF." After losing her father, Haruko Homura travels to Kofujima, the island where his villa remains. There, Haruko learns that her father was a detective and encounters Junichi Kitagawa, an escapee from a facility on the island. This meeting draws Haruko into a mysterious incident involving her late father. The protagonist, Haruko, is played by singer-songwriter Saki in her first solo lead role in a feature film; she also performs the theme song. The cast includes Soji Arai (Apple TV’s *Pachinko*, NHK special drama *Queen of Mars*), Yuki Hashiguchi (*The First Job*), and Shiro Sano, an avid reader of Unno’s work. The film is written and directed by Takumi Takashina, who earned three consecutive PFF Award selections at the Pia Film Festival and makes his theatrical debut with this film.
title:長安のライチ:
Chang’an, the capital of the Tang Dynasty. Li Shande, a low-ranking official, receives a life-altering command from the Emperor: “Deliver fresh lychees from the far southern region of Lingnan to Chang’an to celebrate the birthday of Consort Yang.” Lychees are notoriously perishable, making it nearly impossible to transport them thousands of kilometers from Lingnan to Chang’an without spoiling. Success means a path to promotion, but failure means certain death.

Tricked into the impossible role of “Lychee Envoy” by a colleague’s scheme, Li Shande heads to Lingnan. There, he joins forces with an unlikely group of allies, including the daughter of a lychee orchard master, a merchant investing in the plan, and a young man oppressed as a slave. With the deadline looming, the fruit rotting, and the murky power struggles of the imperial court swirling around him, Li Shande faces overwhelming odds. Now, an unprecedented “Lychee Transport Mission” that will shake the course of history is about to begin!
title:長篠: Director Gempa Miyashita, who depicted the father of Takeda Shingen in *Nobutora*, returns with a historical drama centered on the Battle of Nagashino, which took place during the era of Shingen's son, Katsuyori. Revolving around the Battle of Nagashino—a major turning point that led to the decline of the Takeda clan following their defeat by
title:阿飛正傳: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
title:陽なたのファーマーズ フクシマと希望: This documentary follows the journey of farmers in Fukushima Prefecture who, after being forced out of business by the nuclear accident, made a comeback and embarked on a new challenge: balancing agriculture and power generation through a method called "solar sharing." In 2012, Megumi Kondo, an organic farmer in Nihonmatsu City, Fukushima Prefecture, was driven to close his business by the disaster. He found a way forward through solar sharing (agrivoltaics)—generating solar power on active farmland—and in 2021, he began a new path as a farmer who also produces electricity. Because selling electricity provides farmers with a stable income, allowing them to strive for better crops and to recruit and train young successors, Kondo calls solar sharing a "new form of part-time farming." He continues this challenge alongside young farmers like Haru Tsukada, who was scouted by Kondo after graduating from an agricultural high school, and Yuki Kanno, who entered the field in his mid-30s. While depicting these young farmers and those seeking to learn about the intersection of agriculture and energy, the film offers a hopeful glimpse into the possibilities for solving social issues in Japan. The film is directed by Hiroyasu Obara (*The Judge Who Stopped Nuclear Power Plants and the Farmers Who Will Stop Them*). The theme song and narration are provided by Emi Shirasaki, vocalist of the musical group Shang Shang Typhoon and founder of the band "Tohoku 6-ken Roll Show!!," which she established following the Great East Japan Earthquake to honor the Tohoku region, including her native Yamagata Prefecture.
title:雲と大地のはざまで: A Peruvian film that, through the eyes of a boy living under the vast Andes Mountains caring for alpacas, depicts the prayers embedded in the lives of the people there and the conflict surrounding mining development. In a small Peruvian village surrounded by the majestic Andes Mountains over 4,000 meters high, 8-year-old Feliciano makes it his daily routine to take his alpacas grazing with his loyal dog Rambo. His family makes a living by shearing and selling the wool from the alpacas they care for. In the year before the FIFA World Cup, Feliciano dreams of the Peruvian national team qualifying and advancing to the finals in Russia, listening excitedly to radio broadcasts. He believes this peaceful daily life will last forever, but soon a conflict arises between the villagers and mining companies threatening nature, and one day a major incident engulfs the entire village. Around the same time, a young alpaca named Ronaldo, whom Feliciano especially adored, disappears. The director is Franco García Becerra, for whom this is his second feature film. The role of the protagonist Feliciano is played by Alberto Merma, selected through open auditions and workshops. The film won the Special Prize in the Generation Kplus section and the Special Jury Prize in the Ibero-American Film section at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024.
title:霧のごとく: Directed by Taiwan's Yu-Hsun Chen, known for "The Girl Who Leapt Through Time" and "The Tropical Fish," this is a story of hope and rebirth set against the backdrop of the "White Terror" era in 1950s Taiwan, when many citizens were arrested and executed on suspicion of being anti-government. In the 1950s, under martial law in Taiwan. A young girl named A-Yue, living in Chiayi, learns that her brother, captured as an anti-government element, has been executed in Taipei. With a small amount of money and her brother's keepsake watch in hand, she heads to Taipei alone, only to find that a hefty fee is required to claim his body. At her wit's end, she is tricked by a suspicious man and nearly sold into a brothel, but is rescued by a rickshaw puller named Zhao Gongdao. Originally from Guangdong, China, he came to Taiwan as a soldier for the Nationalist army and has been unable to return home, living hand-to-mouth ever since. Having lost his army comrades to the White Terror and finding no direction in life, Gongdao is moved by A-Yue's determination and decides to lend her a hand. Caitlin Fang ("A Girl from America") plays A-Yue, Will Or ("The Staggering Girl") plays Zhao Gongdao, and popular Taiwanese singer and actor 9m88 co-stars. The film won four awards, including Best Feature Film, at the 62nd Golden Horse Awards in 2025.
title:青春: Acclaimed Chinese director Wang Bing, world-renowned for documentaries such as *Tie Xi Qu: West of the Tracks*, *Three Sisters*, and *Dead Souls*, observes the lives of young people working in small garment factories within one of China's massive economic zones. The film is set in the Yangtze River Delta, a region centered around Shanghai that has long sustained China’s rapid economic growth. Focusing his camera on anonymous workers in their late teens and twenties in the town of Zhili, Wang Bing records the realities of their labor and daily existence. In addition to screening in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, the film won Best Documentary at the 60th Golden Horse Awards and the Douglas Edwards Experimental Film Award at the 49th Los Angeles Film Critics Association Awards.
title:韓国ミュージカル ON SCREEN「モーツァルト！」:
One of the entries in the "Korean Musical ON SCREEN" cinema series, which brings masterpieces of Korean musical theater to the big screen. This screening features the 2020 production of "Mozart!" starring singer and actor Kim Junsu as the composer, accompanied by special footage including interviews with the cast and crew and behind-the-scenes glimpses.

Hailed as a "miracle child," Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart lives in the world of music alongside his father and sister. As a young man, he leaves his hometown for Vienna to test his talents in the wider world. While he marries Constanze, a daughter of the Weber family where he resided, and works tirelessly, the overwhelming brilliance of his childhood eventually fades, leading him into a desolate life. Always by his side is Amadé, the "incarnation of talent," watching him with cold eyes.

The renowned duo of Michael Kunze (book and lyrics) and Sylvester Levay (music and arrangements) explores Mozart's life, shining a spotlight on both the light and shadow of his existence. Since its 1999 premiere in Vienna, the musical has gained worldwide acclaim. It debuted in South Korea in 2010, becoming a massive hit that drew approximately 100,000 spectators in just one month.
title:韓国ミュージカル ON SCREEN「笑う男」:
Part of the "Korean Musical ON SCREEN" cinema series, which brings masterpieces of Korean musical theater to the big screen, this installment features the 2018 premiere production of the original musical "The Man Who Laughs."

England, late 17th century. Gwynplaine, a boy whose mouth was mutilated to be used as a sideshow attraction, finds a dying baby named Dea in the snow and encounters Ursus, a traveling performer living in a nearby hut. Years later, the grown Gwynplaine has become known as "The Man Who Laughs" due to the scars on his mouth. Alongside the blind Dea, he becomes a celebrity by performing his own life story in plays under Ursus's guidance. One day, an aristocrat takes an interest in their show, causing the fates of Gwynplaine and Dea to shift dramatically.

Based on the novel "The Man Who Laughs"—which Victor Hugo, the literary giant behind "Les Misérables," considered his own masterpiece—the production features a book and direction by Robert Johanson, lyrics by Jack Murphy, and music by Broadway hitmaker Frank Wildhorn. Following its 2018 world premiere in South Korea, the musical was also staged in Japan in 2019 and 2022, where it drew widespread acclaim for its delicate human drama and epic score.
title:響け！情熱のムリダンガム: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title:風たちの午後: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title:風たちの午後 デジタルリマスター版: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title:風と女と旅鴉: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
title:風の武士: A samurai yet not a samurai! A shogunate spy who sniffs out darkness and delivers death—he is the Wind Samurai. This suspenseful ninja romance by Ryotaro Shiba weaves together the strange fate and love of Shinzo and Miki, caught in a conspiracy surrounding the phantom land of "Arai" in the Kumano mountains. Sleeping gold, a princess's love, and approaching evil swords! Director Takashi Kato, with ace star Hashizo Okawa, crafts a thrilling ninja suspense epic, connecting Edo and the wilderness with swords and romance.
title:風琴 あるリードオルガン修復家のあしあと: A documentary following Teruo Wakui, a restorer of reed organs. Once a common sight in school classrooms, these wooden reed organs (pump organs) were known as "fukin" (wind instruments) during the Meiji era. By pumping the foot pedals, an airflow is created, causing air to vibrate small metal pieces called reeds inside the instrument to produce sound. Imported from Europe and the United States in the late 19th century, they were eventually produced by numerous Japanese manufacturers as well. They became a staple not only in churches and schools but also in private homes during the mid-Showa period. Today, however, there are no manufacturers left in the world that produce reed organs. Teruo Wakui, a tuner and restorer living in Nagano Prefecture, is one of the few individuals capable of repairing and maintaining these complex instruments. He is involved in the restoration of organs from both Japan and abroad, including historically significant masterpieces. This film follows Wakui’s restoration projects across Japan while exploring the history of the reed organ and the various people who sustain its enduring charm.
title:風船の行方:
A 2006 short film by director Ken Nishiyasu, whose works—produced in a signature style where he handles everything from production and screenwriting to editing and cinematography—have been screened at various film festivals. This human drama focuses on a mother and daughter, depicting the subtle nuances of their fluctuating emotions through delicate direction.

In a family restaurant at night, Michiko and her daughter, Mana, sit facing each other. Having raised her daughter alone while overwhelmed by the demands of daily life, Michiko carries a deep sense of fatigue and loneliness. Eventually, these emotions are directed toward Mana, and she impulsively leaves the restaurant.

The film was released theatrically as part of "The Ken Nishiyasu Short Film Special," a triple feature showcasing three of his works: *To-chan*, *Buri no Omisoka*, and *Fusen no Yukue*.
title:香港四徑大步走: The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, participants must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles or portable music players, which would be advantageous on the undulating mountain paths. It is an event of extreme physical and mental challenge. This film captures 18 runners who took on the HK4TUC pushing their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong, rarely seen before. The director is Robin Lee, a British director born and raised in Hong Kong. The film began a limited release in Hong Kong at the end of 2024, but word-of-mouth spread rapidly and the number of screens increased sharply. It gained further attention when the major star Chow Yun-fat, known for the 'A Better Tomorrow' series and 'Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon', highly praised it, saying 'every Hong Kong person should watch it'. Supported not only by sports enthusiasts but also by general film fans, it became the biggest surprise hit of 2025, attracting 150,000 viewers. Additionally, it has won numerous awards, including the Best New Director Award at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards, the Audience Award at the 22nd Hong Kong Asian Film Festival, the Recommended Film Award at the 31st Hong Kong Film Critics Society Awards, and the Jury Special Award at the 2025 Hong Kong Directors' Guild Awards, earning high praise as a documentary.
title:香港四徑大歩走 英題：Four Trails: A surprise smash hit that ranked in Hong Kong's box office top ten for eight weeks! Highly praised by Chow Yun-fat ("A Better Tomorrow" series)! An unimaginably grueling drama about runners! The Hong Kong Four Trails Ultra Challenge, commonly known as HK4TUC, requires runners to consecutively complete four trail courses in Hong Kong and reach the finish line within a time limit of 72 hours (3 days). The total course length is 298 km, comparable to the distance between Tokyo and Nagoya, with a cumulative elevation gain of 14,500 m, equivalent to seven full marathons or two ascents of Mount Everest. Furthermore, runners must procure their own water and food from shops along the way, and strict rules prohibit the use of poles (advantageous on undulating mountain paths) and portable music players, making it an event of extreme physical and mental hardship. This film captures 18 runners competing in the HK4TUC as they push their limits, set against the beautiful natural landscapes of Hong Kong rarely seen before.
title:骨までしゃぶる: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title:骨を掘る男: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
title:鬪ふ男: In post-war Tokyo, shortly after demobilization, Ankichi (Oka) and Tomezo (Hirosawa) experience a fateful reunion. The two were once companions in the shoeshine trade. Tomezo, now a *rokkyoku* performer, invites Ankichi to a vaudeville theater. The *rokkyoku* narrative performed there is none other than the life story of a "fighting man"—the chronicle of Ankichi’s own past, in which he risked his life to protect a woman (Hanai) and her younger brother during the war. The lyrical scenes, where Hirosawa’s narration and Ankichi’s life synchronize to brilliant effect, represent the true essence of director Tamizo Ishida, a prolific creator of *rokkyoku* films. This is a new print from the original master held by Toho.
title:鰤の大晦日:
A 2014 short film by director Ken Nishioka, who built his filmmaking career in the United States and has had his independent works screened at festivals both in Japan and abroad. This slice-of-life drama, set amidst the frantic atmosphere of the year-end, explores a couple's relationship and their sense of distance from those around them.

New Year's Eve in Tokyo. Shiho and her husband Junpei receive a whole yellowtail as a year-end gift, but they are at a loss as to how to handle it, unable to fillet the fish themselves. As they contact friends and acquaintances to find someone to take it, they not only struggle to find a recipient but also face insensitive remarks about their lack of children. Carrying a sense of displacement, Shiho remembers an uncle she has long been estranged from and heads out into the city with her husband.

The film won the Encouragement Award at the 16th Nagaoka Indie Movie Competition and was an official selection at the 9th Sapporo International Short Film Festival. It was released theatrically as part of the "Ken Nishioka Short Film Special," a triple feature including *Tochan*, *Yellowtail New Year's Eve*, and *Where the Balloon Goes*.
title:麻雀放浪記: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
title:黒い十人の女: A black comedy directed by Kon Ichikawa and scripted by Natto Wada, weaving together a philandering man, his wife, and nine lovers. TV producer Matsukichi Kazama, despite having a beautiful wife named Futaba, is cheating with nine women. The wife and lovers are vaguely aware of each other's existence and fully know that Matsukichi is a womanizer, yet for some reason they cannot leave him. One day, the wife and a stage actress lover named Ichiko come up with a plan to kill Matsukichi. It is a fictional scheme meant to vent their frustration with him, but timid Matsukichi becomes convinced that his lovers are trying to kill him and consults his wife. The wife readily admits to the plan and then, to eliminate the lovers, suggests staging a fake murder: they gather the lovers for a meeting to denounce Matsukichi, and at that gathering, pretend to shoot him dead with a pistol.
title:黒牢城: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title:그 자연이 네게 뭐라고 하니: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:너와 나의 5분: Set in early 2000s South Korea, when Japanese pop culture was restricted, this coming-of-age drama tenderly follows a shy transfer student and a popular class president who bond over J-Pop. In 2001, Gyung-hwan transfers to a high school in Daegu, Korea's most conservative city. A huge fan of then-taboo Japanese music and anime, he secretly listens to Japanese songs on his MP3 player during lunch. Teased as an 'otaku' by classmates, he discovers that his deskmate, class president Jae-min, also secretly loves Japanese culture. Sharing earphones on the bus after school while listening to J-Pop, they gradually grow closer. One day, Gyung-hwan confesses a secret to Jae-min, but afterward, Jae-min's attitude suddenly changes. Making his feature debut, director Eom Ha-nul wrote the script based on his own teenage experiences as a fan of Japanese culture, weaving in diverse Japanese pop culture from the 1990s. Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title:되살아나는 목소리: A documentary co-directed by Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean filmmaker who turns 90 in 2025, and her daughter Park Ma-i, depicting the stories of the voiceless buried in history. Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean born in Mie Prefecture in March 1935, gained attention for her correspondence with Lee Jin-woo, a second-generation Zainichi Korean juvenile death row inmate in the 1958 Komatsugawa Incident, published as "Sin, Death, and Love." She subsequently published collections of testimonies uncovering the voices of Zainichi Koreans forcibly conscripted under colonial rule and those exposed to the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Switching from pen to camera, she made her directorial debut in 1986 with the documentary "Another Hiroshima" about Korean A-bomb victims. She has since produced documentary works such as "Song of Ariran: Testimony from Okinawa," "Nuchigafu (Life's Blessing): Testimony from the Place of Mass Death," and "Silence: The Rising Comfort Women." This film refocuses on the realities and contemporary challenges of Korean A-bomb victims, a lifework for Park Soo-nam, and is based on 16mm film she has been shooting for about 40 years. It depicts the voiceless stories of Koreans affected by the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forced laborers taken to Nagasaki's Battleship Island (Gunkanjima), former Korean civilian employees in the Battle of Okinawa, and women forced into Japanese military sexual slavery.
title:만약에 우리: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title:만약에 우리／ONCE WE WERE US: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title:브로커: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title:수유천: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:아가씨: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
title:악마가 이사왔다: A romantic comedy from director Lee Sang-geun, who previously scored a massive hit in Korea with 'EXIT' and reunites with Im Yoon-ah. It follows a woman possessed by a demon who shows completely different faces by day and night, and the kind-hearted young man who falls for her. On leave from work, Gil-gu falls in love at first sight with Seon-ji, a baker who moves in downstairs. But when he encounters her late that night, she is entirely different. Her father Jang-su explains that Seon-ji is gentle and bright by day, but at 2 AM a demon awakens, transforming her. Gil-gu agrees to Jang-su's odd request to watch over Seon-ji at night. She drags him out every night, running wild and selfishly bossing him around. Im Yoon-ah, a Girls' Generation member known for films like 'EXIT' and drama 'The King's Chef', plays Seon-ji. Ahn Bo-hyun, from the drama 'Spring Fever', plays Gil-gu. Song Dong-il, known for the 'Reply' series, plays Seon-ji's protective father Jang-su.
title:어쩔수가없다: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title:올드보이: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title:우리의 하루: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title:친절한 금자씨: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title:한란: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
title:헤어질 결심: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞『ニュー・ボーイ／クリスティ』ライブ演:
◆ **Christy**
Original Title: Christy
Director: Brendan Canty
Cast: Danny Power, Diarmuid Noyes, Emma Willis
Story: After being kicked out of his foster home, 17-year-old Christy seeks refuge with his estranged older brother, Shane, and his family. However, their relationship is strained, and Christy begins running with his delinquent cousins. Shane tries desperately to save his younger brother, but... Set in the impoverished district of Knocknaheeny, this film explores the bond between brothers struggling with aimless anger and frustration. Despite being Director Canty's debut feature, it received critical acclaim at the Berlin International Film Festival and other festivals worldwide, winning numerous awards. (2025)

◆ **Co-feature: New Boy (Short Film)**
Original Title: An Buachaill Nua
Director: Diarmuid Timmons
Cast: Diarmuid de Faoite, Michael Redahan, Finn O'Hara, Noah Guller
Story: 1970s Ireland. Set in Sligo, the home of poet W.B. Yeats known for its beautiful rural landscapes, this film offers a fresh depiction of the interaction between a transfer student who arrives late on his first day and the local boys. It was an official selection at the 79th BAFTA Awards, the Toronto Irish Film Festival, and numerous other film festivals. (2025)
title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞『三人の女強盗』トークイベント: An attempted bank robbery occurs in a rural town, perpetrated by three women who seem the least likely to commit such a crime. As the story explores why they turned to crime, the pasts that haunt them are gradually revealed. The film features a narrative where various issues intertwine and unravel like a jigsaw puzzle, alongside a brilliant ensemble cast of Ireland’s leading actresses, including Carrie Crowley (The Quiet Girl) and Bríd Brennan (Brooklyn). (2025)
title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞イン・タイム ドーナル・ラニー: This documentary offers a multi-faceted look at the life of Dónal Lunny, a leading figure in Irish music, through his own words, testimonials from fellow musicians, and live performance footage. Having formed numerous bands and collaborated with a wide array of artists since the 1960s, the film explores Lunny’s unwavering devotion to the music of his homeland, his deep ties to Japan, and his journey of overcoming tragedy to find the inspiration that drives him today. (2025)
title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞ニュー・ボーイ／クリスティ:

Story: After being kicked out of his foster home, 17-year-old Christy seeks refuge with his estranged brother Shane and his family. However, their relationship is strained, and Christy begins hanging out with his delinquent cousins. Shane tries his best to save his younger brother, but... Set in the impoverished district of Knocknaheeny, the film explores the bond between brothers harboring aimless anger and frustration. Despite being Director Canty's debut, it received critical acclaim at film festivals both in Ireland and abroad, including the Berlin International Film Festival, and won numerous awards. (2025)

title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞フィルム／まずは踊れ:
<<Commemorating the 120th Anniversary of Playwright Samuel Beckett>>

◆ Dance First
Director: James Marsh
Cast: Gabriel Byrne, Fionn O'Shea, Sandrine Bonnaire
Story: The life of Samuel Beckett is brought to the screen in elegant monochrome. From his childhood in Dublin and his time in the Resistance during the war to his encounters with his wife Suzanne and James Joyce, the film meticulously examines the light and shadow of the Nobel Prize-winning author's life. Two Irish actors portray Beckett: Gabriel Byrne (*The Usual Suspects*) as the older Beckett, and Fionn O'Shea (*Dating Amber*) as his younger self. (2023)

◆ Double Feature: Film
Director: Alan Schneider
Cast: Buster Keaton
Story: A man flees into an apartment room while hiding his face. As if fearing the gaze of others, he drives out the dogs and cats, tears down the portraits on the walls, and covers the mirrors... This is the only film screenplay Beckett ever wrote, an intense silent short praised by Gilles Deleuze as "the greatest Irish film." Buster Keaton, in his later years, plays the protagonist whose face is rarely shown; his physical performance is a must-see. (1965)
title:＜アイルランド映画祭2026＞父の祈りを: 1974. Gerry is arrested as a suspect in a bombing believed to have been carried out by the IRA (Irish Republican Army). Before long, the authorities set their sights on his father, Giuseppe, and under torture, the two are coerced into confessing to crimes they did not commit... A dramatic, socially conscious human drama based on a shocking real-life case of wrongful conviction in the midst of the Northern Ireland conflict. Featuring brilliant performances by three-time Academy Award winner Daniel Day-Lewis and Pete Postlethwaite (The Usual Suspects). (1993)
title:Ｗの悲劇: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
title:｢アヴァンギャルド広告｣シリーズより: The field of cinema preserved and screened by Anthology has long been categorized as "experimental," "avant-garde," or "independent," sparking ongoing debate regarding the validity of such terms. In particular, the label "non-commercial"—carrying the connotation of resistance against the commercialism epitomized by Hollywood—has been widely regarded as an all-encompassing descriptor. However, the "Avant-Garde Advertising" series, held at Anthology starting in November 2025, sheds light on instances where even filmmakers embodying purity and radicalism produced sponsored works with promotional intent, prompting a redefinition of these fundamental distinctions. Are the works presented here a form of experimentation, an avant-garde incursion into enemy territory, a reflection of the reality that everyone must work to earn a living, or perhaps all of the above? Through this program, questions are raised that remain open to a multitude of answers.
title_norm:100 meters: Togashi, born with natural speed, has always used it to gain friends and a place to belong. Meanwhile, transfer student Komiya runs recklessly, trying to forget his painful reality. Togashi teaches Komiya how to run faster, and after school the two practice together. Finding something to devote himself to, Komiya greedily chases new records. Gradually, through the 100-meter dash, their relationship grows into something between rivals and best friends.
title_norm:1975年のケルン・コンサート: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title_norm:2045 films workshop vol.1:
This short film omnibus marks the first independent project from "2045," a label comprised of next-generation creators from BABEL LABEL—a content studio behind numerous films and dramas. The collection features three works directed by young filmmakers belonging to the label.

"24 Frames of Nonsense" (directed by Ren Akiba) is a fantasy love story that weaves together fiction and non-fiction to depict a film director struggling with the script for their commercial feature debut while confronting their own past and present. "For My Grief" (directed by Hitomi Tatsumura) is an ensemble drama that follows four couples who love in their own ways and choose to part for their own reasons, portraying the act of cherishing the people and the time that were undeniably there. "Yomosugara" (directed by Mikumo Yoshimura) is a human drama about a young person who, despite turning their passion into a career, is driven to the brink by the gap between ideal and reality, chronicling a single night they spend in a mysterious cafe they happen to stumble upon.

The directors include Ren Akiba, who made his feature debut with "Tokyo Escape"; Hitomi Tatsumura, who is also an actor known for her lead role in "Angels"; and Mikumo Yoshimura, a prolific creator of short films and music videos who gained recognition for her Nihon University College of Art graduation project "The Last Train." title_norm:2046: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
title_norm:20th century women: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title_norm:20センチュリー・ウーマン: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
title_norm:2部／3部)濱⼝⻯介監督特集上映突然、偶然、必然: Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, now in their late 30s, believed they were close friends who could share anything—until they discovered Jun's secret. Born from a citizen-participation improvisational acting workshop in Kobe, this three-part film features mostly first-time actors and was created through unprecedented methods. It won the Best Actress award at the 68th Locarno Film Festival.
