Shim Hyun-seo, a child actor known for 'The King of Pigs', plays transfer student Gyung-hwan, and Hyun Woo-seok, from 'The School Nurse Files', plays class president Jae-min. Gong Min-jung ('Kim Ji-young: Born 1982') and Lee Dong-hwi ('The Roundup: Punishment') co-star.
title_norm:47系統: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:5時から7時までのクレオ: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
title_norm:90 meters: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title_norm:90メートル: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
title_norm:adams sake: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:affeksjonsverdi: Swedish director Joachim Trier, who gained international attention with "The Worst Person in the World," crafts a family drama centered on the tangled bonds of love and hate inherent in the parent-child relationship. Nora, an actress thriving in Oslo, and her sister Agnes, who chose family life and lives quietly with her husband and son. One day, their father Gustav, a film director who abandoned the family when they were young and has been out of contact for years, reappears and offers Nora the lead role in his first autobiographical film in 15 years. Filled with anger and disappointment toward her father, Nora firmly refuses, and soon the popular young American actress Rachel is cast instead. When Nora learns that the film will be shot at the family's old home, a place filled with memories, uncontrollable emotions surge within her once again. Renate Reinsve, who also starred in "The Worst Person in the World," plays the protagonist Nora, with acclaimed actor Stellan Skarsgård as her father Gustav. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas plays sister Agnes, and Elle Fanning plays the popular American actress Rachel. The film won the Grand Prix at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received nine nominations across eight categories, including Best Picture, and won the award for Best International Feature Film.
title_norm:after life: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
title_norm:after the storm: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title_norm:afternoon breezes: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
title_norm:agatha and the limitless read: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title_norm:agatha et les lectures illimi: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
title_norm:ah special attack corps: A war film depicting the fleeting youth of kamikaze pilots who perished in vain at the end of the Pacific War. This is the directorial debut of Yoshio Inoue, based on a script by Kimiyuki Hasegawa (known for "The Squirrel and the American: Gunshot in the Ruins"). Yoshio Inoue was born in Tokyo in 1926, graduated from Urawa High School's humanities track, joined Daiei in February 1938, and studied under Seiji Hisamatsu, Kon Ichikawa, and Yasuzo Masumura. Cinematography by Toru Watanabe (known for "The White Path Across the River").
title_norm:aikatsu stars! the movie: The theatrical film of the TV anime 'Aikatsu Stars!', which began airing in April 2016 as a new series following the popular idol anime 'Aikatsu!'. It depicts the struggles of girls, including the protagonist Yume Nijino, who enrolls at Yotsusei Gakuen aiming to become the top idol. In this first theatrical film of 'Aikatsu Stars!', the story is set on a southern island where the characters come for an event. It revolves around the rumored 'Legendary Dress' said to be sleeping on the island, and depicts the friendship between Yume and Laura Sakuraba, as well as the school's top four-idol unit 'S4' taking the stage together. The short film 'Aikatsu! The Targeted Magical Aikatsu! Card' is shown simultaneously.
title_norm:air doll: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title_norm:ali baba and the forty thieve: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
title_norm:all of a sudden: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title_norm:alpine fire: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title_norm:amélie et la métaphysique des: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:another home: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:arabian nights the adventures: Toei Animation's first departure from traditional Japanese or Chinese settings follows a young sailor's romantic voyage. The screenplay was an unusual collaboration between Morio Kita, a recent Akutagawa Prize winner with experience as a ship's doctor, and Osamu Tezuka. Staff went to great lengths to depict waves, sometimes painting as many as 300 polka dots on a single cel, and the resulting animation—over 10,000 drawings—imbues the ocean adventure with remarkable realism.
title_norm:asako i & ii: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
title_norm:at the triangle intersection: A documentary observing a 99-year-old woman and her son and daughter-in-law, who were affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster and live in disaster recovery public housing, over a three-year period from 2018 to 2021. Seven years after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, a family forced to evacuate from Namie Town, Fukushima, wavers between returning to their hometown and choosing a new life. Having closed their long-running printing business due to the disaster and living in disaster recovery public housing in Iwaki City, the roles and relationships within the family quietly change. Tetsu, the 99-year-old mother, clings to memories of her birthplace, Okuma Town, even as her memory fades. Her taciturn son Takemasa respects his mother but leaves most of her care to his wife Shigeko. Shigeko, who has continued to bear this role, begins to reexamine her taken-for-granted position within the family and her own way of living. Through the family's daily life in flux, the film questions what "home" is and what "I" is. Directed by Toru Yamada, who has continued making films in Fukushima since the Great East Japan Earthquake.
title_norm:au hasard balthazar: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:au pan coupé: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:beyond the fire the life of j: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title_norm:blue moon: From director Richard Linklater, known for the 'Before' trilogy beginning with 'Before Sunrise' and the six-time Oscar-nominated 'Boyhood,' this conversation piece stars his longtime collaborator Ethan Hawke and depicts a night spent at a party attended by legendary Broadway lyricist Lorenz Hart. On the evening of March 31, 1943, the night of the premiere of the musical 'Oklahoma!,' created by his longtime composing partner Richard Rodgers with a new collaborator, Lorenz Hart—the lyricist behind hits like 'The Lady Is a Tramp' and 'My Funny Valentine'—was invited to a party at the Broadway restaurant Sardi's. Over the course of that night, Hart confronts his own swirling emotions of love, jealousy, anxiety, and longing. Ethan Hawke plays Lorenz Hart, alongside Margaret Qualley as Elizabeth, the woman Hart pines for; Andrew Scott as his former partner Richard Rodgers; and Bobby Cannavale as Eddie, the bartender Hart trusts as a confidant. The film was screened in the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, where Andrew Scott won the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Actor. It was nominated for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actor (Ethan Hawke) at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:bonne chance: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
title_norm:boy meets girl: The feature debut of French maverick Leos Carax, released in 1983. It depicts the encounter of two lonely souls wandering through the Paris night in beautiful black-and-white imagery, winning the Youth Prize at the 37th Cannes Film Festival and generating buzz at festivals worldwide. Alex, a young man whose best friend stole his girlfriend, has a fateful encounter with Mireille, a woman who just fought with her lover. Alex falls in love with Mireille at first sight, but they soon meet with an unexpected tragedy. The roles of Alex and Mireille were played by then-newcomers Denis Lavant and Mireille Perrier. The protagonist Alex, played by Lavant, later reappeared in transformed forms in 'Bad Blood' and 'The Lovers on the Bridge', forming what is known as the 'Alex Trilogy' along with this film. Jean-Yves Escoffier handled the cinematography and continued as cinematographer for the subsequent two films. In Japan, it was first theatrically released in July 1988, following the release of 'Bad Blood' in February of the same year. A 4K restored version was re-released in January 2026.
title_norm:boyfriends and girlfriends: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title_norm:brand new landscape: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:bring her back: After their father dies, brother Andy and his visually impaired sister Piper come to live with foster mother Laura. Also living there is a boy named Oliver who does not speak. Andy feels uneasy about Laura's seemingly excessive affection, but a new life for the siblings begins under her care. From a certain day onward, unsettling events begin to occur one after another in the house. Furthermore, there are mysterious circular motifs scattered around the house, and the presence of Oliver. When these seemingly unrelated elements all connect, Laura's hidden 'terrifying wish' is revealed.
title_norm:broker: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
title_norm:bugonia: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
title_norm:burn: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title_norm:by the stream: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:call me dragon: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title_norm:catching the stars of this su: A drama based on the award-winning novel by Mizuki Tsujimura, depicting the complex emotions of junior high and high school students during the COVID-19 pandemic, set in Tokyo's Shibuya Ward, Tsuchiura City in Ibaraki Prefecture, and Goto City in Nagasaki Prefecture. In 2020, with school attendance and club activities restricted due to the pandemic, Aya Tanimoto, a second-year student in the astronomy club at Ibaraki Prefectural Sunaura High School, proposes an 'Online Star Catch Contest'—a competition using remote meetings to conduct simultaneous astronomical observations across different locations. The activity, joined by students from the Goto Islands in Nagasaki and central Tokyo, eventually spreads nationwide and sparks a miracle. Hiyori Sakurada, known for 'The Fake Diary,' stars as Aya. Rinataro Mizusawa plays her classmate; Arisa Nakano and Ikoi Hayase play students from Nagasaki; Soiya Kurokawa and Anna Hoshino play students from Tokyo; and Takashi Okabe plays the astronomy club advisor. Tamaki Yamamoto, who gained attention for the 2019 short film 'One Night After' and the streaming drama 'Today You're Restless, You're Burning,' makes his feature-length commercial film debut as director. Mash Morino, known for the drama 'Keke no Hi no Kekeke,' writes the screenplay. Haruka Nakamura, known for 'Look Back,' provides the music.
title_norm:chaser game w a match made in: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
title_norm:chuckle chuckle: A fusion of individuality from promising young creators. Directed by Yuka Nishida, a graduate of Kyoto University of the Arts, who now belongs to STARDUST CREATORS as a screenwriter. This film is her graduation project, made when she was 22. It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
title_norm:citizen kane: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title_norm:climbing for life: This drama marks Sayuri Yoshinaga's 124th film appearance and is modeled after Junko Tabei, the first woman to successfully summit the world's highest peak, Mount Everest. It portrays a female mountaineer who staked her entire life on reaching the 'top.' In 1975, as deputy leader and climbing captain of the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, Junko Tabe became the first woman in the world to summit Everest. Her achievement astonished the world and brought light to herself, her friends, and her family, but it also cast a deep shadow. Her challenges as a mountaineer continued, and in her later years, even while battling illness and after being given a terminal diagnosis, Junko continued to smile, involve those around her, and climb mountains. The cast includes Yoshinaga as Junko Tabe, a character based on Junko Tabei; Koichi Sato as her husband Masaaki; Yuki Amami as Etsuko Kitayama, Junko's ally and Everest climbing partner; and Non as the young Junko. The film is directed by Junji Sakamoto, who previously directed Yoshinaga in 'The Light of the North' and reunites with her after 13 years.
title_norm:close to the bone: A documentary following Ryusho Gushiken, who has spent over 40 years collecting the remains of those who died in the Battle of Okinawa. It is said that nearly 3,000 sets of remains—of local residents, former Japanese soldiers, American soldiers, and people from the Korean Peninsula and Taiwan—still lie in southern Okinawa Island, the site of fierce fighting. Gushiken, now 70, began collecting remains at age 28 and has found approximately 400 sets. From fragments he gathers—crushed and scattered small bones, pieces of teacups, shrapnel, and traces of flamethrowers—he infers whether the remains are those of soldiers or civilians, how they met their end, and offers his thoughts and prayers. Film director Katsuya Okuma, who himself lost a great-aunt in the Battle of Okinawa, accompanies Gushiken on his collection efforts, searching for traces of his great-aunt's life. Interweaving archival footage of the Battle of Okinawa, the film illuminates Okinawa's history and present.
title_norm:cléo de 5 à 7: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.

Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
title_norm:comedy in front of the statio: The 15th installment of the 'Ekimaé Series,' which produced 24 films starring Frankie, Morishige, and Bando. Riding the unprecedented manga boom, this film features Frankie as a manga artist and is a legendary oddity, with appearances by 'Obake no Q-taro' and 'Osomatsu-kun' within the story.
title_norm:cranko: A film about the life of genius choreographer John Cranko, who elevated the Stuttgart Ballet from a small regional company in Germany to world-class status, made with the full cooperation of the ballet company. It depicts the untold story behind the creation of his masterpiece "Onegin" and his true face, cut short by an untimely death at the age of 45, all colored by spectacular dance performances by current star dancers. John Cranko, an up-and-coming choreographer active in England, is prosecuted for homosexual acts after a police sting operation. Forced to leave London in 1960, he becomes a guest artist with the Stuttgart Ballet through connections. Finding a place in the company that accepts him without prejudice, he becomes artistic director the following year in 1961, creating works and a company that express beauty and passion with free-thinking ideas. In 1969, the ballet company is invited to the Metropolitan Opera House in New York and rises to the top of the world overnight. Sam Riley, known for "Maleficent" and "Control," stars, passionately portraying Cranko, a man overflowing with passion and innovative talent but who sometimes hurts others due to being too pure in his pursuit of art. Directed and written by Joachim A. Lang, known for "The Man Who Produced Hitler" and who has covered the Stuttgart Ballet for many years.
title_norm:cruisin: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
title_norm:cry out: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
title_norm:cure: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
title_norm:cyborg 009 and the monster wa: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
title_norm:daisies: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
title_norm:dans la ville de sylvia: This film follows a young aspiring painter wandering through places of memory, searching for traces of Sylvia, a woman he loved six years ago. It constructs an obsessive love story reminiscent of Alfred Hitchcock's 'Vertigo' (1958) with meticulously calculated sound and imagery, resulting in a groundbreaking work unlike anything seen before. The film was shot entirely on location in Strasbourg, France, an ancient city where medieval streetscapes and cutting-edge railways coexist without dissonance, creating a stateless atmosphere. The masterful sound design, which orchestrates the city's noises—the murmur of people, the passing of trams—like a symphony, and the beautiful, luminous chain of images captured through glass reflections and tram windows, transport the viewer into an unknown, otherworldly space.
title_norm:das versprechen architekt bv: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:days of being wild: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
title_norm:deaf: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title_norm:deathstalker: From Steven Kostanski, the mad genius director of "Psycho Goreman" (2020) and member of Canada's notorious effects collective Astron-6, who has contributed special effects to Hollywood blockbusters like "Resident Evil: Retribution" (2012) and "Pacific Rim" (2013). His two latest films, "Frankie Freako" and "Deathstalker," will be released sequentially in Japan starting July 3rd at Cinemart Shinjuku and other theaters nationwide. Kostanski, who wrote and directed both films, is known for his unique creature designs reminiscent of classics like "E.T." (1982), "Gremlins" (1984), and "The Goonies" (1985), blending 80s-style monster panic with absurdist black humor, creating a devoted fanbase. These new films bring his signature style to Japan. "Deathstalker" is a reboot of the 1984 cult classic "Deathstalker" (executive produced by Roger Corman). It reconstructs the sword-and-sorcery world with Kostanski's signature nightmarish horror and gore, infused with comedy and darkness. Daniel Bernhardt ("The Matrix Reloaded," "John Wick") stars as the titular Deathstalker. Slash, guitarist of Guns N' Roses, contributes to production and music. Synopsis: In a chaotic world ruled by sword and sorcery, the kingdom of Abraxion suffers under attacks from the sudden appearance of the crimson knight order, the Dread Knights, and is in decline. Unsettling rumors spread that this war is a precursor to the resurrection of the ancient sorcerer Necromemnon. Amidst this, the insolent wandering warrior Deathstalker comes into possession of a cursed amulet, making him a target for the Dread Knight's assassins. To break the curse and repel the approaching evil, Deathstalker embarks on a perilous journey, eventually being drawn into a battle that will decide the fate of the world.
title_norm:decision to leave: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
title_norm:den sidste vikin: Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen, known for writing "Riders of Justice," "The Good Life," and "After the Wedding," delivers a human drama starring his frequent collaborator Mads Mikkelsen. After serving time for a robbery, Anker is released and reunites with his brother Manfred, who hid a large sum of money during the heist, for the first time in 15 years. However, Manfred not only has forgotten the hiding place but also believes he is John Lennon. The two set out on a journey to find the bag of hidden money, but the trip gradually transforms into a journey of self-reflection for both of them. Mikkelsen plays Manfred, who has lost his memory and believes he is John Lennon, embodying this eccentric and unique character. Anker is played by Nikolaj Lie Kaas, another frequent collaborator of Jensen's. The film had its world premiere in the Out of Competition section of the 2025 Venice International Film Festival and became a massive hit in its native Denmark, breaking the country's all-time box office record for a live-action film.
title_norm:detective conan fallen angel: The 29th theatrical film in the nationally hit series "Detective Conan", based on the manga by Gosho Aoyama. Conan, Ran, Sonoko, and Kogoro, along with motorcycle enthusiast Sera Masumi, encounter a mysterious black motorcycle speeding out of control while on their way to the "Kanagawa Motorcycle Festival" in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district. Kanagawa Prefectural Police traffic officer Hagiwara Chiharu chases the black bike but narrowly misses catching it. Conan and the others arrive at the festival venue, where a new white motorcycle called "Angel" equipped with cutting-edge technology is being unveiled. News then arrives that the runaway black bike has appeared in Tokyo. After evading the Metropolitan Police Department's pursuit, the black bike, whose body closely resembles the "Angel", is dubbed the "Black Angel" or "Lucifer", and the chase continues. In Chiharu's mind, memories of her younger brother Hagiwara Kenji and his colleague Matsuda Jinpei flash by. Hagiwara Chiharu, praised by Ran as the "Goddess of the Wind" for her driving skills, makes her first appearance in a theatrical film, engaging in intense motorcycle action against the mysterious black bike "Lucifer". Chiharu is voiced by Miyuki Sawashiro, who took over the role from Atsuko Tanaka, who passed away in August 2024. Guest voice actors Ryusei Yokohama and Mei Hata make their voice acting debuts. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, who handled direction for "Detective Conan: Black Iron Submarine".
title_norm:die my love: Director Lynne Ramsay ("We Need to Talk About Kevin," "You Were Never Really Here") presents a psychological drama starring Jennifer Lawrence and Robert Pattinson, depicting a couple torn between love and madness. It was screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival and nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama. Grace, a writer who moves to a countryside town with her husband Jackson, begins a new life. Peaceful days are shattered after childbirth: her writing stalls, and the pressure and loneliness of childcare, along with fragmentary hallucinations, gradually distort her reality. As the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs, Grace's mind quietly but surely collapses. Jennifer Lawrence, who won the Academy Award for Best Actress for "Silver Linings Playbook," plays Grace and also serves as a producer, drawing on her own childbirth experience to embody the loneliness and anxiety of a postpartum woman. Robert Pattinson ("The Batman") plays Jackson. The film is based on the novel "Die, My Love" by Ariana Harwicz, with Martin Scorsese as a producer.

title_norm:digimon adventure: The first theatrical film in the "Digimon" series. From a midnight computer screen, a strange creature named "Botamon" is born! While Tai is uneasy, his little sister Kari is overjoyed. Botamon evolves into Agumon! Suddenly, the Digital World, home to digital monsters, appears. A bird-like monster charges at Agumon. But then, another change occurs in Agumon's body... Evolution into the giant monster "Greymon" begins! Two colossal monsters clash—what will be the outcome of this fierce battle?
title_norm:distance: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.
title_norm:distance ディスタンス: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.
title_norm:doggie march: A puppy named Rock rises up with stray dogs to defeat Killer the tiger, who killed his mother. Drawing on 'Chushingura' and Sazanami Iwaya's children's literature 'Koganemaru,' this film more consciously adopts Disney's style compared to earlier feature-length works. The stateless urban depictions and the action in a snow-covered amusement park, inspired by an idea from Osamu Tezuka, exude a chic and modern sensibility.
title_norm:doppel:
Director Kenji Tani, known for *Reminiscence Journey Reenact*, helms this drama depicting the life of a young rookie actor set within a popular theater troupe. Troupe Byakuya, which enjoys a cult following, shifts its creative direction to cater to a new fan base after a stage adaptation of a manga becomes a massive hit. Noboru Mitsui, a newcomer to the troupe, feels frustrated and anxious that the current style is preventing him from honing his craft. With the support of the troupe’s star actor, Miyabayashi, Noboru appeals to the leader, Terada, expressing his desire to perform the kind of edgy plays they once did, and is subsequently cast as the lead in their next production. Tasked with playing an "emotionless killer," Noboru undergoes extreme character preparation as Terada’s demands during rehearsals grow increasingly severe. Eventually, Noboru begins to feel a growing anger toward himself for being unable to discard the very desire to "act."

Daisuke Morisaki, formerly of the global boy group BLANK2Y, makes his film debut as the lead, Noboru Mitsui. He is joined by Shohei Hashimoto, a veteran of numerous "2.5D" stage plays, as the troupe’s star Yosuke Miyabayashi; Yusuke Hino from the tokusatsu drama *Kamen Rider Gavv* as Tomoyuki Sotodate, a former member who holds the key to the story; voice actor and actor Shintaro Asanuma, also an active playwright and director, as the troupe leader Nao Terada; and Taro Hasegawa, the film’s screenwriter and an actor/director himself, as theater writer Harumitsu Fujimaki.
title_norm:doppel 舞台挨拶１:
Daisuke Morisaki’s First Starring Role as a Rookie Theater Member
Co-starring Shohei Hashimoto, Yusuke Hino, and Shintaro Asanuma
The film *DOPPEL* is set for a limited one-week screening at Cinemart Shinjuku from April 17 (Fri) to April 23 (Thu)!

Director Kenji Tani—whose previous work *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact* began as a crowdfunding project before gaining widespread acclaim across 30 theaters nationwide in 2024—returns with his latest film, *DOPPEL*. It has been officially confirmed for a special one-week run at Cinemart Shinjuku from April 17 (Fri) to April 23 (Thu).

2025 | Blu-ray | Color | 46 min | *DOPPEL* Film Partners

This project marks another collaboration between Kenji Tani and Cast Corporation, the agency of Ryo Matsuda (star of *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact*). Featuring Daisuke Morisaki in his first leading role and Shohei Hashimoto as his co-star, this film presents a new story set in the world of theater, following in the footsteps of *Reminiscence Journey Re-enact*.

**■ Main Trailer and Poster Visual Unveiled**
The main trailer begins with the protagonist, rookie actor Noboru Mitsui (Daisuke Morisaki), declaring, "I am an actor," providing a glimpse into the film's narrative.
The footage introduces the challenges faced by Noboru as he is cast as an "emotionless killer," alongside the troupe’s star actor Yosuke Miyabayashi (Shohei Hashimoto), whom Noboru looks up to. We also see the troupe’s director, Nao Terada (Shintaro Asanuma), appearing visibly enraged, and former member Tomoyuki Sotodate (Yusuke Hino), who exudes an unsettling aura. title_norm:double clutch: Centered on the bond between a young man (Go) who dreams of becoming a racer and his older sister (Matsuzaka), who works as a station vendor by day and a hostess by night to support him and fulfill his dream. The story also unfolds a passionate love affair between the sister and a teacher (Chii), as well as a gentle romance between the young man and the teacher's sister-in-law (Morishita). However, one day, a tragic event strikes the close-knit siblings. The teacher, whom the sister trusted, turns out to be married; he impregnates her and ultimately murders her. Enraged for his sister, the young man seeks revenge, double-clutching his car into a deadly car chase against the teacher.
title_norm:drive my car: Inheriting the original story of a man's loss and hope after losing his wife, this is a remarkable narrative where the story and the play within the film resonate contrapuntally, boldly incorporating theatrical elements from timeless works like 'Uncle Vanya' and 'Waiting for Godot.' It won four awards including Best Screenplay at the 74th Cannes Film Festival and won the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 94th Academy Awards.
title_norm:driving madeleine: A human drama about a taxi driver who, while driving an elderly lady preparing for the end of her life, gets swept up in a journey across Paris exploring her past. Charles, a grumpy taxi driver on the verge of losing his license with no money or days off, is in the biggest crisis of his life. Then he agrees to drive 92-year-old Madeleine to the opposite side of Paris. Madeleine, who is preparing for her final affairs, asks Charles to make one detour after another. The streets of Paris where she lived her life hold many secrets, and with each detour, Madeleine's surprising past is revealed. This drive gradually transforms both their lives. Dany Boon plays Charles, and French chanson legend Line Renaud plays Madeleine. The film is directed and written by Christian Carion.
title_norm:eddington: From Ari Aster, director of 'Midsommar', and following 'Beau Is Afraid', this thriller stars Joaquin Phoenix and depicts how a local election in a small town locked down during the COVID-19 pandemic escalates into a nationwide crisis. In 2020, the small town of Eddington, New Mexico, USA. Forced into a suffocating quarantine due to the pandemic lockdown, residents' frustration and anxiety are about to explode. Amidst this, town sheriff Joe clashes with ambitious Mayor Ted, who wants to save the town by attracting an IT company, over a minor dispute about wearing masks, and suddenly declares his candidacy for mayor. The fire of Joe and Ted's quarrel spreads, and social media erupts with fake news and hatred. Meanwhile, Joe's wife Louise becomes captivated by the inciting videos of cult leader Vernon, sinking into conspiracy theories. As suspicion, controversy, and rage swirl, violence begets violence, and criticism and conspiracy shroud the truth, the town of Eddington hurtles toward the brink of destruction. Joaquin Phoenix plays Sheriff Joe, Pedro Pascal plays Mayor Ted, Emma Stone plays Joe's wife Louise, and Austin Butler plays cult leader Vernon. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:eleanor the great: Actress Scarlett Johansson makes her feature directorial debut with this lighthearted drama about the friendship between a powerful elderly woman and a motherless student, sparked by a lie, set against the backdrop of her own Jewish cultural roots. Based on a script by first-time feature screenwriter Tory Kamen, drawing on her own grandmother's and family history, Johansson directs with humor and wit. Eleanor, an elderly woman living in New York, feels a void after losing her longtime friend Bessie. One day, intending to attend a tea party, she accidentally wanders into a support group for Holocaust survivors. There, she improvises a story about Bessie's life, recounting her Holocaust memories. Inspired by the dramatic story, journalism student Nina approaches Eleanor, and a new friendship blossoms. But Eleanor's lie takes on a life of its own, sparking a major uproar. June Squibb ("Thelma") plays the unconventional Eleanor, and Erin Kellyman ("Solo: A Star Wars Story") plays Nina. Rita Zohar, herself a Holocaust survivor, plays Eleanor's late friend Bessie.
title_norm:epic elvis presley in concert: A visual work by director Baz Luhrmann, who helmed the 2022 biographical film "Elvis," using cutting-edge technology to revive Elvis Presley in the modern era. Elvis Presley, hailed as the "King of Rock and Roll" for his innovative music and charismatic stage performances, lived a 42-year life as a darling of the times. During the production of the biopic "Elvis," director Baz Luhrmann and his team discovered a treasure trove in Warner Bros.' vault: footage shot for "Elvis: That's the Way It Is" (covering his August 1970 Las Vegas engagement) and "Elvis on Tour" (recording his 1972 nationwide tour), as well as unreleased 8mm film and unheard audio of Elvis discussing his career. This film centers on the legendary Las Vegas shows and iconic performances from the nationwide tour, restoring countless precious images over more than two years using state-of-the-art restoration/remastering technology. Using over 70 songs including hits like "Can't Help Falling in Love" and "Suspicious Minds" as well as rare performances like "Oh Happy Day," it synchronizes Elvis's overwhelming vocals with his own words, delicately and boldly reconstructing the footage for an immersive cinematic experience.
title_norm:epic エピック エルヴィス・プレスリー・イン・コンサー: A visual work by director Baz Luhrmann, who helmed the 2022 biographical film "Elvis," using cutting-edge technology to revive Elvis Presley in the modern era. title_norm:epic／エピック エルヴィス・プレスリー・イン・コンサー: An overwhelming 97-minute immersive experience that invites you to a stage where a superstar poured out his heart and soul! The film’s opening races through the first half of Elvis’s life—from his childhood and his debut performances met with high-pitched screams to his television appearances and his time in the service—utilizing abundant footage from his starring roles in films like *G.I. Blues* and *Blue Hawaii*. Accompanied by his own voice reflecting on his musical awakening and his true feelings about his film career, the experience is, in essence, Elvis telling the story of his own life. Then, putting an end to his Hollywood era, Elvis makes his comeback to the stage, fueled by a burning passion for the music he loves. Centered on his 1970 and 1972 Las Vegas residency performances, rehearsals, and press conferences, the narrative of Elvis’s life continues, interweaving footage from his 1970 and 1972 US tours and personal home videos from Graceland.
title_norm:erica: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years. Exploring the boundary between love and obsession, it thrillingly depicts human madness. Tatsuki, a 23-year-old who has never had a girlfriend, meets Erica, a beautiful woman working at a café, and is captivated by her kindness. Their relationship deepens, but Erica's suggestive words and actions, along with inexplicable events around Tatsuki, gradually cast an unsettling shadow over his daily life. Eventually, Erica's abnormal obsession and madness are revealed, dragging Tatsuki into an inescapable fate. Starring Ayumu Mochizuki, who rose to fame with the two-part film "Solomon's Perjury." The heroine Erica is played by Mei Hayashi, who has worked as a model since elementary school and made her acting debut in the 2024 drama "Goodbye, Teacher." The cast also includes Hayato Takao, Kurea Hatsuki, Moeka Koizumi, and Itsuki Fujiwara. The screenplay was written by Tete Inoue of "Initiation Love."
title_norm:erica エリカ: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years.
