title_norm:kokuho: A human drama depicting the tumultuous life of a man born into a yakuza family who dedicates his life to the path of art as a Kabuki actor. A talked-about sensation that has taken the Japanese film world by storm, finally screening!
title_norm:kraft der utopie – leben mit: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:kubo and the two strings: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
title_norm:kubo／クボ 二本の弦の秘密: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
title_norm:kung fu: A wuxia fantasy action film directed by Taiwanese director Giddens Ko of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'You Are the Apple of My Eye,' starring Ko Chen-tung, who collaborated with Ko on those two previous films. Director Giddens Ko, also active as a novelist, adapts his own internet-published novel 'Kung Fu' for the screen, weaving in homages to Hong Kong and Taiwanese wuxia films from the 1980s and 90s throughout. Underachieving high school student Yuan Zai and his best friend A Yi encounter a mysterious drifter, Huang Jun, who has awakened from a 500-year slumber. Witnessing Huang Jun's overwhelming martial arts prowess as a kung fu master, Yuan Zai and A Yi become his disciples. Their classmate Yi Jing, on whom Yuan Zai has a secret crush, also joins their training. They soon learn of the centuries-old feud between Huang Jun and his junior disciple Lan Jin, and uncover a momentous secret hidden within 'kung fu' that could shake heaven and earth. Ko Chen-tung plays Yuan Zai, Berant Zhu of 'Black Education' plays A Yi, Wang Jing of 'The Secrets in the Lattice' and 'The Return of the Condor Heroes' plays Yi Jing, veteran actor Tai Li-len plays the mysterious kung fu master Huang Jun, and Liu Kuan-ting of 'The Girl Who Robbed Time' plays Huang Jun's nemesis Lan Jin.
title_norm:kyoto hippocrates: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title_norm:kék pelikan: An animated film that visualizes an astonishing true story from 1990s Hungary in Eastern Europe, incorporating documentary materials. In 1990s Hungary, after the fall of the Iron Curtain opened the door to Western Europe, foreign travel was liberalized, and many people turned their eyes to the outside world. However, international train tickets were expensive and out of reach for ordinary people. Amidst this, three young men—intellectual Akos, fearless Pecha, and swimming enthusiast Laci—find a way to forge tickets. They dissolve the blue carbon ink "Pelikan Blue" from the company Pelikan, used on the tickets, with household detergent and rewrite the destinations. After enjoying overseas trips with forged tickets, they decide to distribute "tickets to freedom" to other young people in similar situations. The plan seems to go smoothly, but eventually, a police investigation begins, escalating into a major uproar that shakes the nation. Directed by László Csáki, known for his distinctive animation style, who conducted meticulous research over ten years and blends documentary materials like archival footage and interview audio with hand-drawn animation.
title_norm:köln 75: A music youth film that goes behind the scenes of the concert given by world-famous jazz pianist Keith Jarrett at the Cologne Opera House in Germany on January 24, 1975, centering on the then-18-year-old female promoter. Vera Brandes, a music-loving high school student living in Cologne, Germany, starts a part-time job booking tours for musicians visiting Germany, partly as an act of rebellion against her strict father. Just as her work begins to gain momentum thanks to her innate vitality, she visits the Berlin Jazz Festival and is stunned by the performance of American piano genius Keith Jarrett. Determined to make Keith's Cologne concert happen, she overcomes numerous difficulties to arrange the event, but on the day, a problem arises: a different type of piano than the one Keith had requested is provided. As the start time approaches, Keith refuses to play, putting the concert in jeopardy... Based on historical facts, this film adapts the little-known true story of how the legendary concert, also known as the live album masterpiece "The Köln Concert," was nearly cancelled due to a last-minute crisis but was saved by the quick thinking and resourcefulness of an 18-year-old female promoter. German rising star Mala Emde plays Vera, and John Magaro, known for "First Cow" and "Past Lives," plays Keith Jarrett.
title_norm:la fiebre de los ricos: A thriller dripping with black humor that depicts the collapse of capitalist society following the outbreak of a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" that only infects the wealthy. Directed and written by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia of the "The Platform" series, which sharply depicted social inequality, it thrillingly portrays the chaos brought about by a reversal of values. Laura, a high-ranking producer at a streaming platform company, prioritizes her career over her family and is on the verge of success in the glamorous film industry. But just then, a mysterious disease called "Rich Flu" suddenly spreads worldwide, killing wealthy people one after another. As wealth transforms from a symbol of success into a "mark of elimination," capitalist society collapses and the world descends into chaos. In this extreme situation, Laura makes a decision. Mary Elizabeth Winstead, known for films like "Gemini Man" and "Birds of Prey," plays the career-driven Laura who neglects her family. Raf Spall, who has appeared in major works like "Life of Pi" and "Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom," plays Tony, her husband who is exasperated with her yet gets caught up in the unprecedented pandemic alongside her. Timothy Spall, known for the "Harry Potter" series and "Mr. Turner," plays the billionaire Sebastian Snail.
title_norm:la vérité: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title_norm:lady jane 終幕式「破の刻」 final stag:
A documentary capturing the four-night final event held after the closure of LADY JANE, a venerable Shimokitazawa jazz bar that brought the curtain down on its 50-year history in April 2025.

Since its founding in 1975, LADY JANE served as a cornerstone of Shimokitazawa’s cultural scene. Visited by a multitude of artists and intellectuals—including Seitaro Kuroda, Ryuichi Sakamoto, Yusaku Matsuda, Kotaro Sawaki, and Miyuki Nakajima—the bar was a crucible where encounters between diverse talents sparked countless cultural and artistic movements. The live performances held every weekend transcended genres and career levels, serving as a beacon for aspiring artists and a space for new connections and creativity for veterans.

Though the bar closed to much regret on April 13, 2025, a final event titled "LADY JANE 50th Anniversary: 'Ha no Toki' Closing Ceremony" began just a few days later on April 17 at Shimokitazawa The Suzunari. The theater featured a recreation of the bar's interior, and the stage brought together a stellar lineup of performers connected to the establishment, including a twin-drum set by Takeo Moriyama and Tatsuya Nakamura, as well as Yoshihide Otomo, Akira Sakata, Eiko Ishibashi, Jim O'Rourke, Mariko Hamada, and actors Tomoko Nakajima and Kyoko Koizumi. From the audience, leading figures in theater, film, music, and literature, along with many supporters and associates, looked on. This film captures the essence of those four nights and brings them to the silver screen.
title_norm:lady jane 終幕式破の刻〜 final stage:
LADY JANE: the legendary Shimokitazawa jazz bar that stood for 50 years. This documentary captures the four nights of final live performances held following its closure.

Founded in 1975, LADY JANE was a legendary establishment loved by actor Yusaku Matsuda and immortalized in song by Miyuki Nakajima. A cultural crossroads where music, film, literature, and theater intersected
title_norm:lady vengeance: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title_norm:lami de mon amie: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
title_norm:largent: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:late shift: A social human drama that depicts the relentless hard work and unexpected troubles constantly falling on nurses in an understaffed, full hospital ward, which became a huge hit in Switzerland. Directed by Swiss screenwriter and filmmaker Petra Volpe, it realistically and thrillingly portrays the urgent, universal problem of hospital realities. Florie, a dedicated and highly professional nurse working in a state hospital, faces an even busier late shift than usual because a colleague is out sick. The ward is full, and she also has to train nursing students. Despite the situation, Florie treats patients with anxiety and loneliness sincerely, but she falls into an unmanageable situation and eventually faces a major trial. Leonie Benesch, known for 'The Teachers' Lounge' and 'September 5,' stars.
title_norm:lavventura: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title_norm:le bonheur: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:le quattro volte: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
title_norm:le rayon vert: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title_norm:leave the cat alone: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:legend of the eight samurai: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
title_norm:les rendez vous de paris: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
title_norm:like father, like son: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:lintérêt dadam: The second feature from Belgian director Laura Wandel, who gained attention with her 2021 debut 'Playground', is a human suspense drama depicting one night's events surrounding a 4-year-old boy hospitalized in a pediatric ward and his mother, told from the perspective of a nurse trying to support them. Four-year-old Adam is admitted to a pediatric center with a broken left arm. Malnourished and underdeveloped, his bones are brittle. The court rules that Rebecca, an immigrant single mother, has not been providing Adam with proper nutrition and issues an order restricting her visits. Nurse manager Lucie, herself a single mother, tries to support Rebecca, who fears losing custody and being separated from her son. But Rebecca's reckless actions and pressure from superiors and colleagues push Lucie into a corner. Léa Drucker ('Close') plays nurse Lucie, torn between her desire to save the mother and child and the judicial system the hospital must follow. Anamaria Vartolomei ('Happening') plays isolated single mother Rebecca. The film is produced by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne. It opened the Critics' Week at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:little amélie or the characte: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:little remi and famous dog ca: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
title_norm:local reporter: A pollution issue arises in a town in the Tohoku region, and the media war heats up... An excellent film in which Frankie plays a newspaper reporter, depicting the struggles of journalists who, while grappling with the difficulties of maneuvering in a rural setting, burn with passion for producing community-focused articles.
title_norm:lost land: Directed by Akio Fujimoto, who has garnered international attention for "Where I Belong" and "The Girls at the Seashore," this road movie is based on the testimonies of the Rohingya, often called "one of the most persecuted ethnic groups in the world." It depicts a young refugee brother and sister, driven from their homeland, risking their lives to cross borders in search of their family. Blending unrelenting reality with fantastical imagery, the film portrays the harrowing journey of refugees smuggling themselves across borders from a child's perspective. Five-year-old Shafi and his nine-year-old sister Somiir, living in a refugee camp, set out with their aunt for distant Malaysia, hoping to reunite with their family. Unable to obtain passports, they are led by smugglers onto a fishing boat, and despite facing the fury of nature, pursuit by security forces, and the threat of human trafficking, they desperately overcome the grueling journey. The cast includes over 200 Rohingya people, led by the siblings Somiir and Shafi in the lead roles. Their voices and gazes, as people who have themselves been driven from their homeland, lend the film a powerful realism despite their lack of acting experience. The film received high praise at film festivals worldwide, including winning the Special Jury Prize in the Orizzonti section at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025, the first time a Japanese director has won this award.

title_norm:maborosi: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title_norm:magical secret tour: A crime drama about three women who have drifted through life, who deepen their bond through gold smuggling and reclaim their respective lives. Director Chihiro Amano ("Mrs. Noisy") was inspired by a real 2017 incident in which housewives were arrested for gold smuggling at Chubu Centrair International Airport. She co-wrote the original script with Madoka Kumagai, with whom she also worked on "Sato-san and Sato-san." Large-scale location shooting was conducted in Singapore, depicting the glamorous yet perilous journey of gold smuggling. Wakako, a mother of two living a peaceful life, learns that her husband has been fired from his company for embezzlement. To pay off her husband's debts, she becomes involved in gold smuggling in Singapore, where she meets Kiyoe, a non-regular researcher struggling with student loan repayments, and Mayu, an unmarried pregnant woman with zero savings. After successfully smuggling gold and getting a taste for it, the three decide to start smuggling on their own. For the first time, they gain money, freedom, and the joy of living authentically, spending a magical time together—but... Kasumi Arimura plays Wakako, the mother of two who learns of her husband's embezzlement; Haru Kuroki plays Kiyoe, the indebted researcher; Sara Minami plays Mayu, the unmarried pregnant woman; Akihisa Shiono plays Wakako's husband Takashi; Yuzu Aoki plays Kiyoe's colleague Shiina; and Takumi Saito plays Takashi's boss Tanoue.
title_norm:mahjong horoki: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
title_norm:maria: A youth drama about a girl who, after learning her late mother loved visual kei bands, discovers herself and grows through encounters with music and visual kei culture. Maria, a high school student raised by a single mother, suddenly loses her mother. While sorting through her belongings, she finds CDs, photos, and a diary from her mother's youth, along with an unplayable demo tape named 'MARIA'—the same as her own name. To uncover her mother's secrets, Maria visits a live house and encounters visual kei music. Hina Kikuchi, a model and actor known for 'Oshi no Ko' and 'The Suicide Note,' stars in her first solo lead film role. Masataka Fujishige co-stars as Kanata, a former visual kei musician; Sahel Rosa as Kyoko, Maria's mother's friend; and Tomoko Fujita as Miki, Maria's grandmother. Directed by Daisuke Miyazaki ('Yamato (California),' 'VIDEOPHOBIA'). Filmed at the iconic live house 'Meguro Rokumeikan,' a mecca for visual kei bands, the film also features 1990s visual kei CDs, posters, and fans (bangyaru).
title_norm:mark antony: This Indian sci-fi action film comically and eccentrically depicts a gangster's son who obtains a phone that allows him to talk to people in the past and tries to rewrite fate. In 1975, mad scientist Chiranjeevi invents a telephone that can call people in the past. Using it, he can avert disasters about to befall his past self or loved ones, or make choices that lead to profit. However, Chiranjeevi gets caught in a gang war at a bar while celebrating, and the phone goes missing. Twenty years later, auto mechanic Mark stumbles upon the phone and learns its special abilities and how to use it. This phone eventually sparks a massive upheaval involving Mark's foster father, gang boss Jackie; Jackie's son Madan; and Mark's deceased father, Antony. In Japan, Vishal plays dual roles as mechanic Mark and his gangster father Antony, while S. J. Surya, known for "Jigarthanda Double X," co-stars as Antony's partner Jackie.
title_norm:marty supreme: A drama starring Timothée Chalamet, set in 1950s New York, inspired by the life of real-life table tennis player Marty Reisman. Marty Mauser, who dreams of becoming the world's number one table tennis player in America where the sport has low popularity, works at a relative's shoe store to raise funds to participate in the World Championships. After losing to Japanese player Endo at the World Championships held in London, Marty aims to compete in the next World Championships in Japan. With his mistress Rachel pregnant, his player eligibility revoked by the table tennis association, and his funds running out, Marty tries every possible way to raise money for the trip... Gwyneth Paltrow plays Kay, a retired famous actress; Grammy-winning artist Tyler Okonma, known as Tyler, The Creator, plays Marty's friend; Odessa A'zion plays Marty's girlfriend; Kevin O'Leary plays Milton, Kay's husband and president of an ink company; and Japanese Deaflympics table tennis representative Kōto Kawaguchi plays Japanese player Endo. Directed by Josh Safdie ("Uncut Gems," "Good Time"), the film was nominated for nine Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor.
title_norm:masters of the universe: A new live-action film adaptation of the popular "Masters of the Universe" series, based on the action figures created by Mattel in 1981, which have been expanded across comics, animation, and other media, and previously adapted into the 1987 live-action film "Masters of the Universe" starring Dolph Lundgren. Prince Adam of the planet Eternia is sent to Earth as a child to protect him from war, and grows up hiding his identity. Fifteen years later, guided by the legendary Power Sword he accidentally discovers, he returns to his homeworld and learns that Eternia is under the control of his archenemy Skeletor. To save Eternia and its people, Adam transforms into the warrior He-Man and plunges into a deadly battle against the forces of evil. Directed by Travis Knight ("Bumblebee", "Kubo and the Two Strings"), with a screenplay by Chris Butler ("Missing Link"). Nicholas Galitzine, who has gained attention for roles in "Red, White & Royal Blue" and "The Idea of You", plays the lead role of Adam/He-Man. Camila Mendes ("The Revenge Swap", "Upgraded") plays the warrior Teela, who fights alongside He-Man; Jared Leto ("Tron: Ares") plays the villain Skeletor; and Idris Elba plays Man-At-Arms, a father figure to He-Man, in a star-studded cast.
title_norm:materialists: A love story directed and written by Celine Song of 'Past Lives,' set in the modern marriage market, depicting a love triangle with beautiful imagery. Lucy, a matchmaker at a New York dating agency, is a professional at matching clients' high ideals and detailed conditions, and a materialist who judges love not only by emotion but also by asset value. Leading a busy, work-focused life, she receives a passionate approach from Harry, a wealthy investor she meets at the wedding of a couple she matched. Meanwhile, at the same reception, Lucy reunites with her ex-boyfriend John, who was working as a waiter. They had loved each other, but she couldn't endure the poor life with John, who was drifting between part-time jobs while pursuing his dream of becoming an actor. Lucy begins a relationship with Harry, who is perfect in family background, personality, and education, but her feelings for John, who hasn't given up on his dream, are rekindled. When a client gets involved in an incident, Lucy finds herself at a crossroads in both work and love. Dakota Johnson of the 'Fifty Shades' series plays protagonist Lucy, Chris Evans of the 'Captain America' series plays struggling actor John, and Pedro Pascal of 'Welcome to Eddington' plays investor Harry.
title_norm:mazinger z vs the great dark: A theatrical version of the TV anime "Mazinger Z," featuring a piloted giant robot as the protagonist. Director Nobutaka Nishizawa heightened the drama by entrusting the robot with the protagonist's worries and pain, depicting the invincible Mazinger Z fighting while battered and broken. The surprise appearance of the successor Great Mazinger, ahead of the TV series, astonished children. "Mazinger Z" achieved strong revenue from merchandise licensing, sparking a trend of incorporating merchandising into projects from the planning stage onward.
title_norm:memorizu: Starring Tasuku Emoto, this drama explores themes of family memory and records. Yuta, who lives with his wife and daughter in Tokyo, travels to a rural town in Kyushu to care for his father-in-law Makoto, who has broken his leg, until he recovers. While helping out at Makoto's old-fashioned photo studio, Yuta exchanges videos taken on his smartphone with his wife and daughter back in Tokyo. Even without major events, the accumulation of daily trivial records and memories quietly and vividly reveals the long span of a family's life. Moka Kamishiraishi ("Shōgun," "Girl Encounters") plays Yuta's wife Yuki, who continues working and raising their child in Tokyo. Issey Ogata plays Makoto, the taciturn father-in-law, and Yū Kashii plays a character symbolizing precious family memories. Director Miu Sakanishi, who gained attention for short films while at Kyoto University of Art and Design and later worked as an assistant director for Yūya Ishii and a making-of cameraman for Yūichirō Doi, makes her feature-length directorial debut.
title_norm:merrily we roll alon: A filmed recording of the Broadway musical 'Merrily We Roll Along,' which won four Tony Awards, screened in theaters. Based on the play of the same name by George S. Kaufman and Moss Hart, this musical, which premiered in 1981, features music by the legendary Stephen Sondheim, creator of numerous masterpieces including 'Sweeney Todd.' The story depicts the tumultuous 30-year relationship between Frank, a successful Hollywood producer; Mary, a former best-selling author; and Charlie, a Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright, told in reverse chronological order. This recording captures the 2023–24 Broadway production starring Maria Friedman, which was a huge hit. Jonathan Groff, known for the Netflix series 'Mindhunter' and as the voice of Kristoff in Disney's 'Frozen,' plays producer Frank; Daniel Radcliffe of the 'Harry Potter' series plays playwright Charlie; and Lindsay Mendez, a veteran of numerous Broadway musicals, plays former best-selling author Mary. At the 2024 Tony Awards, the production won Best Revival of a Musical, Best Actor in a Musical (Jonathan Groff), Best Featured Actor in a Musical (Daniel Radcliffe), and Best Orchestrations.
title_norm:message from space: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
title_norm:metライブビューイング2025 26 ガブリエラ・リーナ: The eighth installment of the 2025-26 season of "MET Live Viewing," which records and screens the latest opera performances at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. Based on Mexican painters Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera, this production reverses the setting of the classic Italian opera "Orfeo ed Euridice," depicting a deceased wife returning from the underworld to her husband for just one day in "Frida and Diego: The Last Dream" (recording of the performance staged on May 30, 2026). In 1957, on Mexico's Day of the Dead. Diego, who lost his wife Frida three years earlier, is tormented by age and grief, longing to reunite with her. Meanwhile, Frida, freed from suffering in the underworld, is told by La Catrina, the guardian of the dead, that she should accompany Diego at the end of his life, and reluctantly agrees to return to the earthly world for only 24 hours. Diego and Frida have a moving reunion, but Frida is bound by a rule that she must not touch the living.
title_norm:metライブビューイング2025 26 チャイコフスキー《: The seventh installment of the "MET Live Viewing" 2025-26 season, which captures and screens the latest opera performances from the New York Metropolitan Opera House in cinemas. This recording features Tchaikovsky's opera "Eugene Onegin," a tragedy of love and misunderstanding between a pessimistic young nobleman and an innocent girl, set to lyrical, famous melodies (recording of the performance staged on May 2, 2026). In 1820s Russia, at the estate of a landowner, sisters Tatyana and Olga are visited by Olga's fiancé Lensky, who brings his friend Eugene Onegin. Tatyana falls in love with Onegin at first sight and writes him a letter confessing her feelings, but Onegin gives a cold reply. Months later, at a ball celebrating Tatyana's name day, Onegin dances only with Olga, provoking Lensky to challenge him to a duel, in which Onegin kills him. Years later, returning from his wanderings, Onegin reunites with Tatyana, who has become a duchess.
title_norm:metライブビューイング2025 26 ワーグナー《トリス:
The sixth production of the 2025–26 "MET Live Viewing" season, which brings the latest performances from the Metropolitan Opera (MET) in New York to the big screen. This installment features Wagner’s ultimate opera of love—a work overflowing with sensual music—presented through an innovative new production by Yannick Nézet-Séguin and the rapturous vocals of Lise Davidsen (scheduled to be recorded on March 21, 2026).

In the legendary Middle Ages, the Irish princess Isolde sets sail for Cornwall to enter a political marriage with King Marke, traveling on a ship helmed by the King’s nephew and loyal vassal, Tristan. Because Tristan is the slayer of her former fiancé, Isolde harbors a complex mix of love and hate toward him and attempts a double suicide by poison. However, her maid Brangäne gives her a love potion instead, leading the two to fall into a maddening passion. Although Isolde continues her trysts with Tristan even after becoming Queen, King Marke and his courtier Melot eventually return to the site of their secret meeting, where Tristan is gravely wounded by Melot’s sword.
title_norm:michael: A biographical film depicting the life of Michael Jackson, the "King of Pop," beloved across eras and borders for his overwhelming vocal ability and innovative dance performances. Directed by Antoine Fuqua of "Training Day" and "The Equalizer" series, it portrays Michael's story—how he transcended music to greatly impact the world—alongside his many hit songs. Michael Jackson, under his ambitious father Joseph's strict training, achieved early success as a member of the Jackson 5. Meeting legendary producer Quincy Jones, he created numerous historic hits as a solo artist and quickly became the darling of his era. But behind the glory lay the loneliness of a precocious genius, the shackles of his authoritarian father, and the struggle between his love for his family and the visions overflowing within him. The film stars Michael's real-life nephew Jaafar Jackson as Michael, with Juliano Krue Valdi as young Michael, Colman Domingo as father Joseph, Nia Long as mother Katherine, Kendrick Sampson as Quincy Jones, and Miles Teller as longtime lawyer John Branca. The screenplay was written by John Logan of "Gladiator," and the film was produced by Graham King of "Bohemian Rhapsody."

title_norm:mid august commotion: On August 6, 1945, the atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima, and Japan's defeat became all but certain. The Prime Minister's secretary, Nakajima, sounds out senior statesmen about accepting the Potsdam Declaration. But this peace faction's moves provoke the resistance-minded military officers. Unable to persuade the army and out of options, the Prime Minister petitions for an Imperial Conference to be held.
title_norm:milton bituca nascimento: Called the 'Voice of Brazil,' Milton Nascimento, affectionately known as Bituca, led MPB (Brazilian popular music post-bossa nova) alongside contemporaries Gilberto Gil, Caetano Veloso, and Chico Buarque, and collaborated with countless international musicians. This documentary film traces Milton's life and music while following his global farewell concert tour, announced upon turning 80 in 2022. In the first half, Milton's troupe tours Europe and the Americas, receiving ecstatic welcomes. Pat Metheny, Spike Lee, Quincy Jones, and Wayne Shorter speak about Milton, and there are scenes of collaboration with Esperanza Spalding and Herbie Hancock. Milton reflects on his childhood raised as an adopted son, converses with his own adopted child on the road, and shares memories of his benefactor, singer Elis Regina. The second half begins with the landscapes of Minas Gerais, the highland region of inland Brazil that is Milton's home and musical origin. Friends like Chico, Caetano, and Gil, collaborating poets like Márcio Borges and Ronaldo Bastos, and younger musicians who admire Milton, discuss the appeal and depths of his music. Inescapable negative histories, such as racism and Brazil's 20-year military dictatorship starting in 1964, are also revealed. Then, the farewell concert finale approaches: the concert at Mineirão, the football stadium in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. Members of Clube da Esquina (Corner Club), the title of a landmark 1972 album and the name for the family of Minas musicians centered around Milton—Lô Borges, Beto Guedes, Wagner Tiso, and Toninho Horta—share behind-the-scenes stories and perform together.
title_norm:missing part: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.

title_norm:mobukos love: Director Taichi Kazama, known for the TV drama "Silent," adapts manga artist Akari Tamura's comic into a live-action film, a love story about the first crushes of "supporting characters" who have quietly lived on the fringes of society. Shy and reserved college student Nobuko Tanaka identifies with the term "mob," meaning crowd, extra, or non-major character, and has lived her life watching from afar as other protagonists shine. Then, she notices Hiroki Irie, a young man working part-time at the same supermarket. Touched by Irie's natural thoughtfulness, Nobuko gradually becomes drawn to him. Through her encounter with Irie, she begins to struggle to break free from the shell that has bound her, and while sometimes confronted with harsh realities, she perseveres with the support of her coworkers. Meanwhile, Irie also notices Nobuko's quiet kindness and looks straight at her. The accumulation of small, everyday moments eventually gives them both the strength to take a step forward. Hiyori Sakurada ("The Diary of a Substitute Lie") plays Nobuko, aka Mobuko, and Taisei Kido ("Yukite Kaeranu") plays Hiroki Irie, the object of her first love. The cast also includes Ikoi Hayase as Nobuko's junior coworker Abe, Erika Karata as senior coworker Shinozaki, Takuya Kusakawa as fellow part-timer and Irie's friend Kaneko, Tsubasa Araki as new part-timer Ono, and Kanji Furutachi as store manager Orihara.
title_norm:mononoke the movie chapter ii: The concluding chapter of the theatrical trilogy based on the TV anime "Mononoke," itself a spin-off from the "Bakeneko" segment of the 2006 Fuji TV Noitamina omnibus anime "Ayakashi." It delves into the greatest secret long hidden within the Ooku (the shogun's harem) and depicts the fierce battle between the protagonist, the Medicine Seller, and the most fearsome mononoke of all, the Serpent God, which threatens to shake the Ooku to its foundations. After a deadly struggle with the Medicine Seller, who carries a exorcism sword, and a Tengu umbrella, followed by a decisive battle with the Fire Rat, peace finally seems to have returned to the Ooku. However, the Medicine Seller senses a lingering presence and remains on guard. Around this time, the shogun's official wife, Sachiko, gives birth to a long-awaited son, but the infant soon dies. Sachiko, who had hoped to change her formal marriage to the shogun by bearing an heir, is physically and emotionally exhausted and becomes entangled in a conspiracy that could overturn the Ooku's very existence. Hokuto Mizorogi, the priest of the "Mizusama" faith within the Ooku, watches the events unfold with a solemn expression. At the same time, unnatural earthquakes, as if a giant creature is crawling, occur frequently within the Ooku, and bizarre incidents happen where maids are twisted and crushed to death. Before the Medicine Seller, who rushes to the scene, appears the mononoke Serpent God, taking the form of a giant snake.
title_norm:monster: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title_norm:motherland: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
title_norm:mothertongue:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.
title_norm:mouchette: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:mrs. warrens profession: One of the National Theatre Live series, which films and screens selected acclaimed stage productions from the UK's Royal National Theatre in cinemas. This recording captures 'Mrs. Warren's Profession', featuring five-time Laurence Olivier Award winner Imelda Staunton performing alongside her real-life daughter Bessie Carter. Vivie Warren is a young woman with progressive ideas. Her mother, however, while upholding the old patriarchal system, has built a fortune by exploiting that very system. But a heavy price lies hidden behind it all. This play by Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw, known for 'Pygmalion' and a Nobel laureate in Literature, is directed by Dominic Cooke, who has also worked on screen productions such as the BBC series 'The Hollow Crown' and the film 'The Memory of Justice'. The cast also includes Kevin Doyle from 'Downton Abbey' and Robert Glenister from 'Into the Sky'.
title_norm:my brothers weddin: A director's cut, completed in 2007 through re-editing, of Charles Burnett's second feature film from 1983. Burnett, an influential figure in American independent cinema who consistently depicts the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, presents a tragicomedy of a working-class young man torn between family, friendship, and identity. It quietly reveals class differences within the Black community, psychological gaps between generations, and the frustration of young people left behind by social success, all from the gaps in everyday life. Pierce, a 30-year-old helping his parents run their dry-cleaning shop, drifts aimlessly through his days with no clear future. His childhood friends are either in prison or already dead. When his brother, a lawyer, marries a woman from a wealthy family, Pierce's discomfort and feelings of inferiority grow. Around this time, Pierce reunites with his best friend Soldier, just released from prison, and finds himself caught between his sense of duty to his family and his loyalty to his friend, forced to make a choice. In Japan, this 4K restored version will have its theatrical premiere at the special screening series 'Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues' (from February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:my mind is always racin: A film themed around the 'quarter-life crisis,' a psychological state common among people in their late twenties to thirties who feel vague anxiety and restlessness about the future, unable to live the life they imagined. Directed by and starring Reimi Miyamori, it won the Actor Award at the 18th Tanabe Benkei Film Festival, a gateway for independent films. Nozomi, a 25-year-old woman who moved to Tokyo to become a novelist, is struggling and going nowhere. In her mind, 18-year-old Nozomi, living a rural high school life, asks her if she has truly followed through on her words and made it big in Tokyo. While resisting a frustrating life where she wants to change but cannot, the 25-year-old Nozomi confronts her 18-year-old self and begins to notice various things she had never faced before. This is the debut feature film of Reimi Miyamori, a graduate of the Nihon University College of Art's Film Department who began making films during the COVID-19 pandemic. She served as director, screenwriter, producer, and lead actress. It was screened in theaters as part of the 'Tanabe Benkei Film Festival Selection 2024' (May 9 – June 5, 2024 at Theatre Shinjuku / June 20–26, 2024 at Theatre Umeda).
title_norm:nameless: A film adaptation of the psycho-violent manga "Nanashi" by Sato Jiro—who is active not only as an actor but also as a screenwriter and film director—marking his first work based on a manga. Sato stars and wrote the script, with Hideo Shijo of "Bad Summer" directing. A brutal murder occurs at a family restaurant in the afternoon. Security cameras capture a bald middle-aged man who appears to be the culprit, but he holds no weapon. The footage records the bizarre sight of people spurting blood and collapsing just from the man approaching and lightly touching them. Investigating police identify the bald man as "Taro Yamada," who was questioned for shoplifting 11 years earlier. When investigators rush to Yamada's home address, they find a decomposed female corpse. Sato plays the protagonist, serial killer Yamada. Takaya Kamikawa plays Teruo, the patrol officer who becomes the namesake for the nameless orphaned young Yamada. MEGUMI plays Hanako Yamada, who grew up with Yamada in the same children's home and lives with him. Kuroudo Yashima plays Detective Kunieda, who works tirelessly to stop Yamada.
title_norm:national theatre live hamlet: One of the 'National Theatre Live' productions, where the UK's Royal National Theatre films selected acclaimed stage performances for cinema screenings. This recording features 'Hamlet' starring Sri Lankan-born actor Hiran Abeysekara, who won the Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actor for his performance in 'Life of Pi' at the Royal National Theatre. Surrounded by power and privilege, the young Prince Hamlet wavers between duty and doubt. He confronts the ultimate question: 'To be, or not to be.' Directed by Robert Hastie, who became Associate Artistic Director of the Royal National Theatre in January 2025, offering a contemporary perspective on Shakespeare's masterpiece. Co-stars include Alistair Petrie, known for 'The Bank Job' and 'Rush,' Ayesha Dharker, known for 'Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones,' and Francesca Mills, known for the Netflix series 'The Witcher: Blood Origin.'
title_norm:naughty angel: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.

title_norm:never give up: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.
title_norm:new dawn: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:new group: The second theatrical release from director Yuta Shimotsu, who gained attention for his 2024 commercial film debut "May the Lord Be with You". It comically and seriously explores the underlying psychology of human behavior in group activities, specifically through the lens of group gymnastics, with a unique worldview. High school girl Ai, who has family problems, is shy and unable to assert her own opinions. Transfer student Yu, who has returned from overseas, is the type to speak her mind clearly and struggles to fit into the group-oriented, harmony-focused activities of Japanese schools. Ai is interested in Yu, but Yu grows frustrated with Ai's inability to express herself. One day, a student in the schoolyard freezes on all fours. Soon, other students begin lining up beside him in the same position, forming a massive human pyramid. Strangely, the school encourages participation in the human pyramid as a "good thing," and the stacked students all wear serene expressions. As students gather one after another and obey without a word, Ai herself becomes dazed and nearly joins the pyramid. The situation eventually escalates into a collective supernatural phenomenon engulfing the entire region. Anna Yamada (from the "Golden Kamuy" series) plays the protagonist Ai, and Yuzu Aoki (from "5 Centimeters per Second") plays the transfer student Yu. Pierre Taki delivers a bizarre performance as the principal who leads the group. The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 29th Fantasia International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:new love in tokyo: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title_norm:no other choice: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
title_norm:nobody knows: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
title_norm:nothing but bones: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
title_norm:notre musique: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:nouvelle vague: From the director of "Boyhood" and the "Before" series, Richard Linklater, comes a film that goes behind the scenes of Jean-Luc Godard's "Breathless"—a landmark work of the French New Wave, the revolutionary film movement that emerged in the late 1950s. It depicts the young people who sparked a revolution in film history, along with their vibrant interactions with the leading filmmakers of French cinema. In 1959, France. Jean-Luc Godard, a 28-year-old critic writing for the film magazine "Cahiers du Cinéma," begins production on his feature directorial debut, "Breathless," starring French up-and-coming actor Jean-Paul Belmondo and American starlet Jean Seberg. Those around him are thrown off by Godard's innovative and freewheeling shooting methods, but the set, fueled by a shared passion for filmmaking, is filled with energy. Following the style of "Breathless," the film is shot in black and white in the Academy ratio (1:1.37), almost entirely in French, and the cast, except for Zoey Deutch as Jean Seberg, is made up of mostly unknown actors. Guillaume Marbeck, who worked as a photographer and model, was cast as the protagonist Godard. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:o bi, o ba the end of civiliz: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
title_norm:o bi, o ba. koniec cywilizacj: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. title_norm:oldboy: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
title_norm:on fallin: This human drama depicts the loneliness and division in modern society through the daily life of an immigrant woman working in a massive logistics center in Scotland, ultimately finding a faint glimmer of hope. Aurora, a Portuguese immigrant, works as a picker in a huge logistics center on the outskirts of Scotland. Her days are mostly spent walking through countless aisles following scanner instructions and retrieving items from shelves. Conversations with colleagues are limited to brief breaks, and after her shift, she drags her tired body back to a shared house for immigrant workers. Interactions among residents are superficial, relationships never deepen, and her rootless days continue monotonously. One day, Aurora accidentally breaks her smartphone. Losing this modern necessity—her means of workplace communication and her "companion" for passing time—slowly but surely begins to change her daily life. Portuguese-born, Scotland-based Laura Carreira wrote and directed her first feature film based on her own experiences as an immigrant, winning the Best Director Award at the 72nd San Sebastián International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:once we were us: Summer 2008, Seoul. University students Uno and Jeong-won meet fatefully on a long-distance bus. Uno, who dreams of becoming a game creator, and Jeong-won, who aspires to be an architect. Supporting each other through their urban days filled with dreams and anxieties, they eventually fall in love, deeply and truly. However, faced with the harshness of reality that youth cannot resist, they choose to part ways. Ten years later, in the summer of 2024, they coincidentally reunite on a flight to Seoul. As they look back on their memories, Uno asks Jeong-won a question he has kept buried deep in his heart: 'What if, back then...'
title_norm:one last throw: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title_norm:oslo, 31. august: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).
