title_norm:the monkey king 2: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
title_norm:the monkey king 3: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
title_norm:the mountain: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
title_norm:the mouths: A film adaptation of the bestselling novel 'A Survey About the Mouth' by author Senkin, who sparked the mockumentary horror boom with 'About a Certain Place in the Kinki Region.' Published in 2024, the palm-sized, 60-page story became a huge sensation on social media for delivering a solid scare in such a short format. Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the 'Ju-On' series, it marks Rihito Itagaki's first solo lead role in a live-action film. A group of university students hear a rumor about a 'cursed tree' in a cemetery known as a haunted spot and visit it for a test of courage. The next day, one of the group members mysteriously disappears. Since then, inexplicable phenomena begin to occur around the students who visited the cemetery, and they are gradually driven into a corner. Guided by the baffling testimonies of the five students, a terrifying truth emerges. Rihito Itagaki plays Shota Murai, one of the university students. The cast also includes Keito Tsuna as Tatsuya, Ai Yoshikawa as An, MOMONA (ME:I) as Mirei, Shuto Mori (BUDDiiS) as Horita, a student who visits the cemetery for fun, Tomoki Nishiyama (TAGRIGHT) as Kawase, who is forcibly taken to the cemetery by Horita, Shido Nakamura as Detective Kusabe, who pursues the missing student, and Tokio Emoto as journalist Nishi.
title_norm:the naked spur: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
title_norm:the ninth configuration: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
title_norm:the old oak: British master Ken Loach delivers the final chapter of his 'North East England Trilogy', following 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Missed You'. Set in a former mining town in Northern England, 'The Old Oak' is the last remaining pub cherished by locals. About 30 years after the town's vibrant heyday, it now faces harsh times, but owner TJ Ballantine struggles to keep it going through trial and error. However, when the town begins accepting Syrian refugees, the pub—once a place of solace—turns into a battleground for belonging. Wrestling with the pub's uncertain future, TJ meets Yara, a Syrian woman with a camera, and unexpectedly forms a friendship. Scripted by Paul Laverty, Loach's longtime collaborator, the film is portrayed with warmth and realism. Dave Turner, who appeared in 'I, Daniel Blake' and 'Sorry We Miss You', plays pub owner TJ. Winner of the Audience Award at the 2023 Locarno Film Festival, and screened in competition at the 76th Cannes Film Festival.
title_norm:the origin of ultraman: A documentary produced to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the landmark special-effects drama series 'Ultraman.' The special-effects TV drama 'Ultraman,' which first aired in 1966, achieved a peak viewership rating of 42.8% and sparked a social phenomenon. Even over 60 years since its birth, Tsuburaya Productions continues to release new Ultraman series works, beloved across generations and borders. This film is planned by filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu, known for 'Monsters' and 'Shoplifters,' and features numerous leading creators from film, special effects, and design. Filmmakers Guillermo del Toro, Kore-eda Hirokazu, and Nicolas Winding Refn, game creator Kojima Hideo, anime director Anno Hideaki, and special effects/film director Higuchi Shinji, among others active at the forefront of their fields both in Japan and abroad, offer their unique perspectives to unravel the question, 'What is Ultraman?' The film explores the worldview where the protagonist is a hero yet carefully depicts the background of the kaiju, and the strong appeal of the designs of both Ultraman and the monsters, while also shedding light on the ideas and work of Tsuburaya Eiji and the staff of that era, tracing the journey of how Ultraman spread across the world.
title_norm:the orphan brother: Summoned by Toei's top brass seeking a weighty drama, screenwriter Sumie Tanaka was brought on board. The story follows aristocratic siblings reduced to slavery, overcoming their suffering through social advancement. Animators strongly objected to the narrative's obliviousness to societal power structures, yet the breathtakingly beautiful Yamato-e style visuals, where backgrounds and characters harmonize perfectly, captivate the viewer.
title_norm:the outside man: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
title_norm:the outwaters: A found footage horror film that uses avant-garde visuals and storytelling to depict four men and women visiting a desert who encounter unimaginable terror. Three memory cards are discovered in the Mojave Desert, containing horrifying footage. One day, Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle come to the Mojave Desert in California to shoot a music video. But when night falls, strange sounds, lights, and inexplicable phenomena begin to occur. Soon, the four are swallowed by a rift in reality, and the camera captures the nightmare that befalls them. Robbie Banfitch, a multi-talented filmmaker, screenwriter, actor, and musician from New Jersey, makes his feature-length directorial and screenwriting debut, also starring in the lead role.
title_norm:the power of utopia living wi: A documentary about Chandigarh, the planned city built in India by Le Corbusier, the master of modernist architecture who left behind numerous legendary buildings. In 1947, India and Pakistan gained independence, and Punjab was divided between the two countries. With the state capital Lahore belonging to Pakistan, India needed to build a new capital. Prime Minister Nehru wanted a city symbolizing faith in the future and democracy, entrusting Le Corbusier with designing the planned city of Chandigarh. Born in the wilderness at the foot of the Himalayas, the "Shining City" of Chandigarh aimed to be a human-centered utopia where natural order and modern technology were in perfect harmony, symbolizing a new India. How has this city transformed 70 years after its birth? The film traces the buildings and their history, while residents—architects, urban activists, and artists—discuss the challenges Chandigarh faces and its enduring charm. Screened as part of the special program "Le Corbusier and Doshi: Modernism in India" (from May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:the presidents cake: Lamia, chosen as the 'honorable' cake maker, goes out to town with her grandmother and friend the rooster to search for cake ingredients──
title_norm:the promise, architect bv dos: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
title_norm:the reality behind what we se: The film opens with footage of the tsunami from the Great East Japan Earthquake (courtesy of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism). The new work by Gozo Yoshimasu, 'A Water Tree Stands on the Planet,' born at the climax of this film, was completed after the poet's long struggle. Yoshimasu had been unable to write poetry since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. 'At the beginning of human life, there is amniotic fluid and bathwater; at the end, there is the water of the dying that moistens the lips,' says Yoshimasu. 'Water,' the source of life for humanity, has been an important theme for poets throughout history. However, the poet who directly witnessed the scars of the great tsunami lost his words to the impact of water that strips everything away. Instead of writing poetry, Yoshimasu began daily copying the poems of the Showa-era philosopher Takaaki Yoshimoto in rice-grain-sized characters, like a sutra transcription. The camera captures this strange and fascinating scene. 'Beside the Poem,' written over four years and which he calls 'Monster-kun,' is a massive work of nearly 700 pages. Within it, the actual voice of the representative Japanese poet Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) resounds, sanukite stones ring, and finally, an eerie scene unfolds as he flings ink onto paper like Jackson Pollock (USA, 1912–1956), the founder of action painting. Deviating from the act of writing, time accumulates on a single sheet of paper, creating an object-like state. This becomes a 'practice writing book' over a long period, leading to the gestation of a new work. One day, learning that Kyoto has as much groundwater as Lake Biwa (Japan's largest lake), the poet seeks a new path for poetic creation in Kyoto's water veins. The poet's tentacles begin to reach the water of Kyoto, which holds a giant cradle of water. Then, before Yoshimasu appears the phantom of Yasunari Kawabata, winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature. Resonating with the talent of seeing phantoms in Kawabata, who stayed in Kyoto and devoted himself to creative work, the poet gropes for the thread of his own poetic creation. What the poet's senses finally touch is the great Eastern spirit, the water god, the dragon. Yoshimasu hears the voice of water's destiny and takes up his brush. The story of Gozo Yoshimasu depicted in this film shows the path of a poet, standing at the abyss of creative despair, 'gaining new life.' The backdrop, like Kawabata's masterpiece 'The Old Capital' which earned him the Nobel Prize, is vividly colored by Kyoto's four seasons, Zen temples, and karesansui (dry landscape gardens).
title_norm:the resurrection of the golde: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
title_norm:the samurai and the prisoner: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:the second is a christian: Kyoko, a nun at St. Saffron Church on Mount Rokko, plays hymns on the organ. Haruhiko Tenryu, the second-generation head of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza clan, is deeply in love with Kyoko because of her refined beauty, and has even forced his underlings to be baptized as Christians. Also harboring feelings for Kyoko is Detective Jindai, whose family runs a Tendai sect temple, presenting another formidable obstacle. However, Kyoko herself secretly harbors feelings for Eiji, whom she met fatefully one stormy day. As the feelings of those around her intertwine, Kyoko's destiny begins to move in an unexpected direction.
title_norm:the sheep detectives: An unconventional mystery film starring Hugh Jackman, depicting sheep whose beloved owner is murdered as they struggle to find the culprit. In a peaceful English countryside town, shepherd George lives alone surrounded by his beloved sheep. He reads detective novels to them every night, and the sheep actually understand the stories and look forward to this time. One day, George is found dead. The sheep refuse to believe it was an accident and, led by their smartest leader Lily, launch an investigation. As they follow clues, they discover George had a huge inheritance. Determined to avenge their beloved George, the sheep race to find the killer. Hugh Jackman plays the victimized shepherd George, with Oscar-winning actress Emma Thompson, Nicholas Galitzine from "The Idea of You," and Nicholas Braun from the TV series "Succession" co-starring. Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Patrick Stewart, and Bryan Cranston voice the sheep. Based on the 2005 bestselling novel of the same name by German author Leonie Swann, directed by Kyle Balda of the "Minions" series.
title_norm:the smashing machine: The untold story of mixed martial artist Mark Kerr, who rose to fame during the early days of the "PRIDE" tournament that captivated all of Japan, is brought to film by Dwayne Johnson—also known as the wrestler The Rock—who stars and produces. Making his MMA debut in 1997, Mark Kerr rose undefeated to the top. After consecutive wins in the UFC, he also made a stunning run in Japan's PRIDE, becoming feared as "the strongest man in the hominidae family," but the pressure quietly eroded his mind. Kerr gradually became dependent on painkillers, and his relationship with his girlfriend Dawn deteriorated. After experiencing his first defeat, he finally confronts his own weakness and decides to step back into the ring to rebuild his life. Dwayne Johnson, inspired by the 2002 documentary of the same name, personally secured the film rights and carefully portrays the vulnerable side of a tough man. Emily Blunt plays Kerr's girlfriend Dawn, and Japanese actors including Tadanobu Asano, Satoshi Ishii, Yasuko Mitsuura, and Tomoyasu Hotei also appear. Benny Safdie, highly acclaimed for his co-directed works with his brother Josh such as "Uncut Gems," makes his solo directorial debut with this film, winning the Silver Lion for Best Director at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025. A team led by Japanese makeup artist Kazuhiro Tsuji handled the special effects makeup, earning a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards.
title_norm:the stin: A blockbuster hit from director George Roy Hill, who reunited with stars Paul Newman and Robert Redford after 'Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.' Chicago in the 1930s. Young con man Hooker, whose partner was killed by a powerful gangster, teams up with gambler Gondorff to pull off the ultimate scheme for revenge. A brilliant crime drama with a twist-filled plot and crisp pacing. Won 7 Academy Awards in 1973, including Best Picture, the most of any film that year.
title_norm:the super mario galaxy movie: The second film in the series of "The Super Mario Bros. Movie", which animated the world of Nintendo's "Super Mario" game series and became a massive hit in 2023, grossing over $13 billion worldwide. Twin plumbers Mario and Luigi, while helping Princess Peach in the Mushroom Kingdom, take care of the captured King Koopa and solve everyone's problems. One day, they meet a new partner, Yoshi. Then, triggered by Princess Peach's birthday party, they embark on a new adventure across space to thwart the evil ambitions of Koopa's son, Bowser Jr. In addition to familiar faces from the first film like Mario, Luigi, Princess Peach, Koopa, and Toad, new characters from the original game series appear, including Yoshi, Rosalina, and Bowser Jr. Produced jointly by Chris Meledandri of Illumination (known for the "Minions" and "Sing" series) and Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto. Directors Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic, and screenwriter Matthew Fogel return, along with the original voice cast including Chris Pratt, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Day, and Jack Black, as well as the Japanese dub cast including Mamoru Miyano, Ayasa Shida, Yu Hatakeyama, Kenta Miyake, and Tomokazu Seki.
title_norm:the testament of ann lee: A biographical musical film chronicling the tumultuous life of Ann Lee, a real-life religious leader who founded the utopian "Shaker" sect in the 18th century, starring Amanda Seyfried of "Mamma Mia!" and "Les Misérables." Born into a poor blacksmith's family in 18th-century England, Ann grows up as a devout woman. After the heartbreaking experience of bearing four children, all of whom die, she receives a revelation that she is the female reincarnation of Christ. Her way of life, preaching equality of gender and race, attracts many followers but also invites persecution from those who resent or fear her. Eventually, she crosses to America with just eight followers, seeking a utopia where they can realize an ideal life based on gender and racial equality, but further hardships await her there. Co-stars include Lewis Pullman of "Top Gun: Maverick" and Thomasin McKenzie of "Last Night in Soho." Directed by Mona Fastvold, who co-wrote the script with her partner, director Brady Corbet of "The Brutalist." The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:the third murder: Lawyer Shigemori (Fukuyama) takes on the defense of Misumi (Yakusho), who has been arrested on suspicion of murdering the president of the company where he worked. Misumi had previously been sentenced to life imprisonment for a robbery-murder committed 30 years ago and was on parole. Misumi's testimony shifts back and forth repeatedly. Eventually, an unexpected connection emerges between the victim's daughter, Sakie (Hirose), and Misumi... This film, framed as a courtroom suspense, questions ethical issues that lie outside legal judgment.
title_norm:the traveler: The feature-length debut of Iranian master Abbas Kiarostami, made in 1974, this human drama freshly depicts the funny yet poignant adventures of a boy struggling desperately to watch a soccer match. Gassem, a 10-year-old boy attending elementary school, is obsessed with soccer, often neglecting his homework and classes, earning constant scolding from his teacher and mother. Determined to go see an important match held in the capital, Tehran, he tries every trick to get money for transportation and a ticket, including stealing from home and deceiving his friends... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title_norm:the truth: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title_norm:the unforgiven: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.
title_norm:the vacation begins: Satoshi Kimura, director of 'Strange Lovers from Another Planet' and 'The Melancholic After-School of Yoyogi Johnny', takes on the classic French genre of 'vacation film' with this dialogue-driven drama. At the start of summer, Yuka, freshly divorced from Haruki after three years together, visits a seaside town on vacation with her best friend Shina and Shina's boyfriend Dazai. Yuka and Dazai were once in love, and reuniting with him rekindles her feelings. Meanwhile, Shina finds herself drawn to Tenma, a poet living in the seaside town. The film creates '1:1' scenes where characters enter the frame in pairs, unfolding the story through a chain of different combinations. The emotion of 'liking' determines each character's formation, shifting relationships as they cross paths. Yu Imari ('Soirée', 'A Janitor') plays Yuka, Ei Adachi ('If Tokugawa Ieyasu Became Prime Minister') plays Dazai, Yuki Shinho ('YOUNG&FINE') plays Shina, Takeo Yamaguchi ('BADBOYS THE MOVIE') plays Tenma, and Ryo Igarashi ('Before Dawn') plays Haruki.
title_norm:the voices of the silenced: A documentary co-directed by Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean filmmaker who turns 90 in 2025, and her daughter Park Ma-i, depicting the stories of the voiceless buried in history. Park Soo-nam, a second-generation Zainichi Korean born in Mie Prefecture in March 1935, gained attention for her correspondence with Lee Jin-woo, a second-generation Zainichi Korean juvenile death row inmate in the 1958 Komatsugawa Incident, published as "Sin, Death, and Love." She subsequently published collections of testimonies uncovering the voices of Zainichi Koreans forcibly conscripted under colonial rule and those exposed to the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Switching from pen to camera, she made her directorial debut in 1986 with the documentary "Another Hiroshima" about Korean A-bomb victims. She has since produced documentary works such as "Song of Ariran: Testimony from Okinawa," "Nuchigafu (Life's Blessing): Testimony from the Place of Mass Death," and "Silence: The Rising Comfort Women." This film refocuses on the realities and contemporary challenges of Korean A-bomb victims, a lifework for Park Soo-nam, and is based on 16mm film she has been shooting for about 40 years. It depicts the voiceless stories of Koreans affected by the atomic bombs in Hiroshima and Nagasaki, forced laborers taken to Nagasaki's Battleship Island (Gunkanjima), former Korean civilian employees in the Battle of Okinawa, and women forced into Japanese military sexual slavery.
title_norm:the way we talk: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:the world of hans christian a: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's words, 'My life is a fairy tale,' this musical drama weaves together tales like 'The Red Shoes' and 'Thumbelina' while depicting Andersen's boyhood. The night sky sparkles with colorful stars, and the orchestra's melodies envelop the story. The art by Reiji Koyama and the music by Seiichiro Uno sweetly bring this fairy-tale world to life.
title_norm:throw away your books, rally: A grandmother who is a habitual shoplifter, a father who is a war criminal, and a sister with an obsessive love for rabbits. Raised in a dysfunctional family, "I" am always thinking of running away from home, while "he" is placed in a privileged environment. Burdened by a restless, pent-up passion with nowhere to go, "I" encounters strange people and wanders through a city where fantasy and memory blend together.
title_norm:till we meet again: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
title_norm:tochka: An unconventional film that depicts the drama woven by a man and a woman who meet by chance, drawn to the darkness of the "pillbox group," war ruins built on the coast of Nemuro, Hokkaido for border defense at the end of World War II and still standing without being demolished, set almost entirely in a single location. Nemuro, Hokkaido, a town on the border with Russia at Japan's easternmost point. In the winter-barren wilderness, pillboxes built during World War II and now weathered are scattered. A man is staring intently at one of these pillboxes, and a woman inside the pillbox happens to see him. Guided by memories recounted by the man, the two trace back through hidden time. Starring Yoko Fujita from "Dog and Cat" and Shun Sugata from "The Last Samurai." Directed by Hiroyuki Matsumura, a native of Hokkaido. Screened in the "Japanese Cinema: A Different Perspective" section of the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2008. Theatrically released in 2009, with a revival release in 2026.
title_norm:tochka トーチカ: An unconventional film that depicts the drama woven by a man and a woman who meet by chance, drawn to the darkness of the "pillbox group," war ruins built on the coast of Nemuro, Hokkaido for border defense at the end of World War II and still standing without being demolished, set almost entirely in a single location. Nemuro, Hokkaido, a town on the border with Russia at Japan's easternmost point. In the winter-barren wilderness, pillboxes built during World War II and now weathered are scattered. A man is staring intently at one of these pillboxes, and a woman inside the pillbox happens to see him. Guided by memories recounted by the man, the two trace back through hidden time. Starring Yoko Fujita from "Dog and Cat" and Shun Sugata from "The Last Samurai." Directed by Hiroyuki Matsumura, a native of Hokkaido. Screened in the "Japanese Cinema: A Different Perspective" section of the 22nd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2008. Theatrically released in 2009, with a revival release in 2026.
title_norm:tokijiro lone yakuza: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title_norm:tokyo burst: STORY: In the dark city of East Asia, Shinjuku's Kabukicho district. A man walks with a swagger, cutting through the wind: Aiba Shiro, a rookie detective at the Shinjuku Central Police Station. Born and raised in Kabukicho, Aiba, a former bōsōzoku gang leader, is always causing trouble due to his physical strength and hot-blooded nature. One day, Korean National Police Agency detective Choi Si-woo arrives in Japan, pursuing a heinous internationally wanted criminal syndicate. From day one, the two clash and are on the verge of conflict, but with information that the wanted criminals are hiding in Kabukicho, they form an impromptu partnership and begin a joint investigation. As they investigate while remaining at odds, a certain group robbery incident triggers a massive conflict between a violent yakuza group and Kabukicho's largest host club group. Furthermore, the criminal syndicate joins the fray, and Shinjuku, transformed into a battlefield, is enveloped in chaotic darkness. And lurking behind it all is a vast conspiracy involving state power.
title_norm:tokyo burst 犯罪都市: STORY: In the dark city of East Asia, Shinjuku's Kabukicho district. A man walks with a swagger, cutting through the wind: Aiba Shiro, a rookie detective at the Shinjuku Central Police Station. Born and raised in Kabukicho, Aiba, a former bōsōzoku gang leader, is always causing trouble due to his physical strength and hot-blooded nature. One day, Korean National Police Agency detective Choi Si-woo arrives in Japan, pursuing a heinous internationally wanted criminal syndicate. From day one, the two clash and are on the verge of conflict, but with information that the wanted criminals are hiding in Kabukicho, they form an impromptu partnership and begin a joint investigation. As they investigate while remaining at odds, a certain group robbery incident triggers a massive conflict between a violent yakuza group and Kabukicho's largest host club group. Furthermore, the criminal syndicate joins the fray, and Shinjuku, transformed into a battlefield, is enveloped in chaotic darkness. And lurking behind it all is a vast conspiracy involving state power.
title_norm:tokyo melody: A legendary lost documentary of Ryuichi Sakamoto filmed in 1984. Featuring precious interviews, recording sessions, and footage of YMO's 'Open Rehearsal' concert, along with scenes of 1980s Tokyo.
title_norm:tokyo story: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic. Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
title_norm:tokyo taxi: Master filmmaker Yoji Yamada, directing his 91st film, brings together Baisho Chieko and Kimura Takuya as leads in this human drama about the joys of life, based on the 2022 French film "A Taxi for Paris." Taxi driver Koji Usami is tasked with driving 85-year-old Sumire Takano from Tokyo's Shibamata to a nursing home in Hayama, Kanagawa. Sumire asks him, "For my last look at Tokyo, there are a few places I'd like to stop by," and Usami follows her instructions, driving her around various locations. As they share the journey, Sumire gradually opens up and reveals her surprising past. The chance encounter between a taxi driver and his passenger sets both their hearts and lives in motion. Alongside Baisho as Sumire and Kimura as driver Usami, Aoi Yu, making her sixth appearance in a Yamada film since "My Wife is a Rose: Family is Tough III," plays the young Sumire. Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
title_norm:tokyoタクシー: Master filmmaker Yoji Yamada, directing his 91st film, brings together Baisho Chieko and Kimura Takuya as leads in this human drama about the joys of life, based on the 2022 French film "A Taxi for Paris." Takaya Sakaguchi plays Sumire's fiancé Ogawa, and Yuka plays Usami's wife Kaoru. The cast also includes Runa Nakajima, Misuzu Kanno, Lee Jun-young, and Takashi Sasano.
title_norm:tony takitani: A love story adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story of the same name, directed by Jun Ichikawa of 'Tokiwa: The Manga Apartment' and 'Tsugumi,' starring Issey Ogata and Rie Miyazawa. Tony Takitani, born as the son of a trombonist, loses his mother shortly after birth and grows up carrying loneliness. After working at a design company, he becomes an independent illustrator, falls in love with a woman, and marries her. But their happy days are short-lived; his wife dies in an accident. Feeling his loneliness, he hires a woman who closely resembles his late wife as an assistant and tries to get used to her death by having the assistant wear the vast collection of clothes his shopaholic wife left behind... Issey Ogata plays the protagonist Tony Takitani and his father, Rie Miyazawa plays Tony's wife and the woman who resembles her, with Hidetoshi Nishijima providing narration. The music is composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto. The film won the Special Jury Prize, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Youth Jury Award at the 57th Locarno International Film Festival in 2004. A 4K remastered version was re-released in 2026.
title_norm:topsy turvy journey: Conductor Goichi (Frankie) on the Tohoku Main Line receives passionate advances from his childhood friend, geisha Sakura (Baisho), but secretly has his eye on another woman. The third installment of the 11-film "Travel Series" starring Frankie Sakai, directed by comedy master Segawa.
title_norm:toy story 5: The fifth installment in Disney and Pixar's beloved 'Toy Story' series, which has always explored the bond between toys and children. It depicts Woody and Buzz joining forces once again to face an unprecedented threat from modern technology. Buzz, Jessie, Forky, and the others living with Bonnie are enjoying their usual daily life. However, everything changes when the latest electronic tablet, the 'Lilypad,' arrives. Seeing Bonnie absorbed in the multi-functional device, the toys begin to doubt their own purpose. As anxiety spreads that 'toys are no longer needed,' Woody receives an SOS from his friends and returns to Bonnie's side, reuniting with Buzz. The legendary duo stands up to a new threat to protect the place of toys. Directed and written by Andrew Stanton, known for 'Finding Nemo' and 'WALL-E,' who has also worked on the 'Toy Story' series as a story and scriptwriter, bringing a new story as a creator who has supported the series. The co-director is Kena Harris, who directed the Pixar short 'Alberto's Letter.' The Japanese dub features the familiar cast including Toshiaki Karasawa as Woody, George Tokoro as Buzz, Yumi Kusaka, and Ryo Ryusei.
title_norm:trainspottin: A youth film that portrays the cheerful yet miserable lives of young people addicted to drugs, becoming an iconic work of 1990s British pop culture. Renton, a heroin addict living in Edinburgh, Scotland, spends his aimless days hanging out with fellow heroin addicts Sick Boy and Spud, and the violent, alcoholic Begbie. One day, after being arrested for shoplifting, Renton decides to reform, moves to London, and gets a job. However, Begbie and Sick Boy, on the run after a robbery, show up one after another, and Renton gets fired. When they return home, they attend the funeral of their friend Tommy, who turned to drugs after a breakup. Amid overwhelming despair, Renton and the others take a big gamble to change their lives... This is Danny Boyle's second directorial work and the breakout film for Ewan McGregor and Robert Carlyle.
title_norm:trophy: The protagonist is Sohui, a 14-year-old Zainichi Korean girl. She attends a Korean school and devotes herself to Korean dance in her club activities. One day, at an exchange event with a Japanese school, she becomes friends with a Japanese girl named Mirai over their shared love of K-Pop, and Sohui gradually connects with the outside world. To earn money for tickets to their favorite K-Pop idol's concert, the two decide to sell unused items from Sohui's house on a flea market app. Surprisingly, the item that sells for a high price is a North Korean CD owned by Sohui's father, Sanju, who is the principal of the Korean school. Emboldened, Sohui and her friend even sell a "medal" awarded to Sanju by his homeland, North Korea.
title_norm:tully: Marlo, a mother of three including a newborn, is given a night nanny by her brother. Initially hesitant, she soon bonds deeply with Tully, a nanny who is thoughtful, surprising, and at times challenging.
title_norm:turbulence: A situational survival thriller set in the inescapable space of a floating hot air balloon, depicting the threats of nature and human conflict. To repair his relationship with his wife Amy, who is grieving a miscarriage, ambitious CEO Zach joins a hot air balloon tour crossing the Italian Dolomites with her. A mysterious woman named Julia joins them, and the flight with the three passengers begins. But high in the sky, Julia suddenly reveals that she had a secret meeting with Zach the previous day, accusing him of infidelity. Zach denies it, but suspicion swirls, and Julia suddenly pulls a knife. During the struggle, the pilot falls out, and the balloon goes out of control. With the radio dead and the balloon reaching an oxygen-thin altitude of 16,000 feet, battered by turbulence and storms, the three are forced into extreme choices with no escape. Directed by Claudio Fae of 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter,' with a screenplay by Andy Mason, who wrote and produced 'Air Lock: Underwater Emergency Shelter' and '47 Meters Down.' The cast includes Hera Hilmar of 'Mortal Engines' as Amy, Jeremy Irvine of 'War Horse' as Zach, and Olga Kurylenko, known as a Bond girl from 'Quantum of Solace,' as Julia.
title_norm:turbulence fear takes flight: A situational survival thriller set in the inescapable space of a floating hot air balloon, depicting the threats of nature and human conflict. To repair his relationship with his wife Amy, who is grieving a miscarriage, ambitious CEO Zach joins a hot air balloon tour crossing the Italian Dolomites with her. The cast includes Hera Hilmar of 'Mortal Engines' as Amy, Jeremy Irvine of 'War Horse' as Zach, and Olga Kurylenko, known as a Bond girl from 'Quantum of Solace,' as Julia.
title_norm:twiggy: A documentary exploring the life and allure of Twiggy, the legendary British model who captivated the world in the 1960s. Debuting at age 16 in 1965, Twiggy quickly rose to stardom, and with her famously slender, twig-like figure and unique fashion sense, she overturned conventional standards of beauty. Becoming an icon of the Swinging London youth culture, she revolutionized the fashion world, sparking a global miniskirt boom. Later, pursuing her own forms of expression, she also found success as an actress and singer, notably starring in Ken Russell's 1971 musical film "The Boy Friend," which drew significant attention. Through Twiggy's own words, rare archival footage, and interviews with those connected to her—including Brooke Shields, Dustin Hoffman, Paul McCartney, and Sienna Miller—the film portrays her life as a woman and mother, her struggles, and her choices. The director is actress Sadie Frost, who also helmed the documentary "Mary Quant: The Legend of Swinging London."
title_norm:twinkle twinkle, killer kane: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
title_norm:two zero four six: A sci-fi love story written and directed by Hong Kong master Wong Kar-wai, starring Asian superstars Tony Leung, Takeshi Kaneshiro, and Zhang Ziyi. Set in the 1960s, following "Days of Being Wild" and "In the Mood for Love," it weaves in episodes from those films. In 1967, during Hong Kong's turbulent era, writer Chow, unable to forget a past love and engaging in fleeting relationships with women, begins writing a near-future sci-fi novel titled "2046" at his hotel. The novel's characters board a train where androids serve as stewardesses, heading toward "2046," a place where lost love can be found. Chow reflects his own daily life in the novel, projecting himself onto the male protagonist as he writes. It won Best Actor (Tony Leung) and Best Actress (Zhang Ziyi) at the 24th Hong Kong Film Awards in 2005, and the New York Film Critics Circle Award for Best Foreign Language Film. In 2022, a 4K restored version was screened as part of "WKW4K" at theaters including Cinemart Shinjuku, Grand Cinema Sunshine, and Cinema City.
title_norm:un homme est mort: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
title_norm:un simple accident: A suspense thriller by Iranian master Jafar Panahi, winner of the Palme d'Or at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025. It thrillingly and humorously depicts people wrongfully imprisoned seeking revenge. Vahid, once unjustly imprisoned, accidentally encounters a man he believes was his torturer guard. He forcibly restrains the man and digs a hole in the wilderness to bury him, but the man's ID card shows a different name. The man claims it's a case of mistaken identity. Blindfolded during imprisonment, Vahid never saw his torturer's face. Unsure if this is the right man, Vahid pauses revenge and visits a friend who was also tortured by the same guard. Panahi, banned from filmmaking by the Iranian government for opposition activities, drew inspiration from his own two imprisonments and the real voices of cellmates. Having won the Golden Lion at Venice for 'The Circle' and 'No Bears', and the Golden Bear at Berlin for 'Taxi', Panahi achieved the feat of winning top prizes at all three major festivals with this film. A French co-production, it was France's entry for Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards and received a nomination.
title_norm:unchained: Directed by Keisuke Yoshida of "Himeanole" and "Missing," this drama portrays boys who cannot understand pain or common sense, and the adults who continue to confront them head-on. Yoshida wrote the original script based on the juvenile delinquents he encountered during his own sensitive adolescence and the community surrounding them. Nishiken Go, a former half-gray area gangster and ex-convict, runs a full-time residential rehabilitation facility called "Mirai no Sato" in a coastal provincial town. Drawing on his own experiences, Nishiken tackles troubled children with all his might, but his rehabilitation methods, which do not shy away from corporal punishment, are criticized by educators. One day, a middle school teacher named Fuyuko consults him about an uncontrollable student, Kaito, and Yu, who has just been released from a juvenile detention center. Meeting the two, Nishiken instantly sees through Kaito's madness. Kaito's mother, exhausted by his severe domestic violence, decides to entrust her son to "Mirai no Sato." However, Kaito causes trouble with the other residents, escapes, and is arrested for assault. Wataru Ichinose of the Netflix drama "Sanctuary" stars as Nishiken, while the newcomer Hayato Uesaka is cast as the delinquent boy Kaito. Kaho plays middle school teacher Fuyuko, Atsushi Shinohara and Fusako Urabe play Kaito's parents, Iori Wada plays Kaito's delinquent friend Yu, and Nanami Yamazaki and Mansaku Takada play the facility's residents.
title_norm:une belle course: A human drama about a taxi driver who, while driving an elderly lady preparing for the end of her life, gets swept up in a journey across Paris exploring her past. Charles, a grumpy taxi driver on the verge of losing his license with no money or days off, is in the biggest crisis of his life. Then he agrees to drive 92-year-old Madeleine to the opposite side of Paris. Madeleine, who is preparing for her final affairs, asks Charles to make one detour after another. The streets of Paris where she lived her life hold many secrets, and with each detour, Madeleine's surprising past is revealed. This drive gradually transforms both their lives. Dany Boon plays Charles, and French chanson legend Line Renaud plays Madeleine. The film is directed and written by Christian Carion.
title_norm:une femme fidèle: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title_norm:une part manquante: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems. Jay, a Frenchman working as a chef in Tokyo, marries a Japanese woman but divorces her. Due to differences in the joint custody systems of Japan and France, he is separated from his beloved daughter Lily. Unable to give up hope, he becomes a taxi driver, wandering the city while searching for traces of his daughter. Nine years later, just as Jay decides to return to France, his daughter Lily, now a grown girl, coincidentally gets into his taxi. Without Lily knowing the driver is her real father, and Jay unable to reveal himself, they spend a brief moment together. The cast includes Judith Chemla, known for 'A Woman's Life' and 'Our Arias for Mother,' Tsu Yu from 'TAXi (2),' Yumi Narita from 'Don't Stop the Camera!' and 'Mari's Story,' as well as Shinnosuke Abe, Toshihiro Yashiba, Moro Agata, and Haruko Uchida.
title_norm:une part manquante また君に会えるまで: A drama directed by Guillaume Senez, who also teamed up with Romain Duris in 'Our Struggles,' with Duris starring. Set primarily in Japan, it depicts the changing forms of modern families under the universal themes of parent-child bonds and love, against the backdrop of the differences between Japanese and French social systems.
