title_norm:useful ghost: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title_norm:vacuum zone: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
title_norm:vagabond: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
title_norm:varda by agnès: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
title_norm:varda par agnès: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
title_norm:vertigo: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
title_norm:virus: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
title_norm:walk slow: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.
title_norm:wall engravings: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:want to be a shellfish: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
title_norm:warrior of the wind: A samurai yet not a samurai! A shogunate spy who sniffs out darkness and delivers death—he is the Wind Samurai. This suspenseful ninja romance by Ryotaro Shiba weaves together the strange fate and love of Shinzo and Miki, caught in a conspiracy surrounding the phantom land of "Arai" in the Kumano mountains. Sleeping gold, a princess's love, and approaching evil swords! Director Takashi Kato, with ace star Hashizo Okawa, crafts a thrilling ninja suspense epic, connecting Edo and the wilderness with swords and romance.
title_norm:was a stranger: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
title_norm:we live in time この時を生きて: Director John Crowley (*Brooklyn*) crafts a poignant love story that interweaves the timelines of a couple cherishing the irreplaceable moments of their limited time together. Almut, a rising star chef, and Tobias, a recent divorcee in the depths of despair, fall in love after a fateful encounter. Despite their differing personalities—the free-spirited Almut and the cautious Tobias—they navigate life’s hurdles, eventually building a home and deepening their bond as they welcome a daughter. However, when Almut learns her time is running out, she shares a surprising resolution with Tobias. Florence Pugh (*Midsommar*) and Andrew Garfield (*The Amazing Spider-Man* series) star as Almut and Tobias. The film features a screenplay by Nick Payne (*The Sense of an Ending*) and is executive produced by Benedict Cumberbatch.
title_norm:we who dwell in the mountains: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:what does that nature say to: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:what should we have done: Documentary filmmaker Tomoaki Fujino records over 20 years the story of his older sister, who began showing symptoms of schizophrenia, and his parents, who kept her from seeing a psychiatrist. His sister, eight years older, was caring and excellent. Influenced by their parents, she entered medical school to become a doctor. One day, she suddenly started screaming things that weren't true. Schizophrenia was suspected, but her parents—a doctor and a researcher—refused to acknowledge the illness and kept her away from psychiatric care. Doubting their judgment, Fujino tried to persuade them but failed, and left home with a lingering sense of unease. Eighteen years after his sister's onset, Fujino, having studied filmmaking, began recording his family's life whenever he visited home. He filmed family outings and dinner scenes, engaged his parents in conversation, and kept talking to his sister, but her condition worsened. Eventually, his parents installed a chain and padlock on the front door to confine her inside.
title_norm:wheel of fortune and fantasy: Trivial love talk between best friends, a student seeking guidance from a professor, female friends reuniting after 20 years... A first 'short story collection' woven from three tales themed around 'coincidence.' With a small production system ensuring ample rehearsal and shooting time, it carefully captures the actors' light yet delicate expressions. Won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:where is the friends house: An Iranian film that vividly captures a boy's journey to find his friend's house to return a precious notebook he accidentally took home, bringing director Abbas Kiarostami international fame. At a primary school in the village of Koker in northern Iran, Mohammad is severely scolded by his teacher for doing his homework on a piece of paper instead of a notebook and is told he will be expelled if it happens again. However, his best friend Ahmad, who sits next to him, accidentally takes Mohammad's notebook home. Panicked that Mohammad will be expelled without his notebook, Ahmad searches for his friend's house in a distant neighboring village to return it, but struggles to find it... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title_norm:whisper／小さな祈り: A short film completed after a seven-year production period following director Takashi Miwa's previous work 'a whisper' released in 2017. Miwa, a filmmaker who is also an actor and taught himself stop-motion animation, infuses this work with his own despair and hope for the world, depicting those who continue to pray in a world where things are breaking and being lost, through uniquely original visuals. The film has won numerous awards at film festivals around the world, including Best Inspiration at the WSXA Amsterdam International Film Festival 2025 in the Netherlands and Best Animation in the Short Film category at the Austin International Art Festival 2024 in the USA.
title_norm:why wait, just die: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
title_norm:winchester 73: The Winchester rifle, a legendary gun said to be one in tens of thousands. A drama of joys and sorrows unfolds around the people who come into possession of this rifle one after another, with all episodes converging into a single finale. A masterfully structured classic Western.
title_norm:wind, woman and road: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
title_norm:wir bergler in den bergen sin: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:wish: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
title_norm:women’s testimonies pioneerin: In 1982, under the sponsorship of socialist researcher Kiyomizu Ishidō, a roundtable discussion was held with pioneering female activists who had participated in the launch of the popular labor movement from the Taishō to Shōwa eras. Those gathered were Setsu Tanno (wife of Masanosuke Watanabe), Utako Nabeyama (wife of Sadachika Nabeyama), Misao Fukuoka (wife of Kyōji Koreeda), and Mina Yamauchi (wife of Naokazu Tachibana). Although they had once worked together in the movement, decades later, after the war, some held different positions, making such a gathering rare. At the request of the host, Mr. Ishidō, who said, 'I want to record this for posterity,' director Haneda filmed the discussion. Time passed without the footage being released, but driven by the director's strong desire to 'preserve the history of these women,' additional filming was done as much as possible to compile the work. In this film, the discrimination and subjugation experienced by these female activists are told in their own words. It is a work that quietly questions what true women's liberation really is.
title_norm:ws tragedy: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
title_norm:wの悲劇: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
title_norm:xixi: This documentary, the feature debut of Taiwanese director Wu Fan, captures the bond she forms with the unique Chinese dancer XiXi, whom she met by chance in Berlin, portraying the vibrant lives of two women. While studying in Europe from Taiwan, director Wu Fan meets XiXi, a Chinese contemporary dancer, in Berlin. Deeply drawn to XiXi, who dances like a free bird, Wu Fan begins filming her daily life. XiXi's journey, wandering Europe as a dancer in search of a free soul, appears beautiful to Wu Fan's eyes, like a wild bird unafraid to take flight. At the same time, XiXi lavishes love on her daughter Nina, whom she is allowed to see occasionally while staying in touch with her ex-husband Mederic. Eventually, Wu Fan's camera begins to capture the deep wounds hidden in XiXi's past. This becomes a catalyst for Wu Fan herself to confront her own family trauma. The film won the Emerging International Filmmaker Award at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival 2024.
title_norm:xixi（シィシィ）、私を踊る: This documentary, the feature debut of Taiwanese director Wu Fan, captures the bond she forms with the unique Chinese dancer XiXi, whom she met by chance in Berlin, portraying the vibrant lives of two women. While studying in Europe from Taiwan, director Wu Fan meets XiXi, a Chinese contemporary dancer, in Berlin. Deeply drawn to XiXi, who dances like a free bird, Wu Fan begins filming her daily life. XiXi's journey, wandering Europe as a dancer in search of a free soul, appears beautiful to Wu Fan's eyes, like a wild bird unafraid to take flight. At the same time, XiXi lavishes love on her daughter Nina, whom she is allowed to see occasionally while staying in touch with her ex-husband Mederic. Eventually, Wu Fan's camera begins to capture the deep wounds hidden in XiXi's past. This becomes a catalyst for Wu Fan herself to confront her own family trauma. The film won the Emerging International Filmmaker Award at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival 2024.
title_norm:you are the film: A youth comedy directed by Makoto Ueda, head of the theater group "Europe Kikaku," known for writing screenplays for numerous hit films like "Summer Time Machine Blues" and "River, Don't Flow On." This is his feature directorial debut, set in the real-life building "Shelbo Shimokitazawa" in Shimokitazawa, employing innovative gimmicks. At the cinema Tollywood on the second floor of "Shelbo Shimokitazawa," Madoka, a playwright from Shimokitazawa, and Kazuma, a band musician from Sangenjaya, each go to see a movie. An impossible structure emerges where each other's events are projected onto the screen as a film. Meanwhile, problems arise at the shops adjacent to the cinema, "Good Heavens" and "Mikazuki Rock." Madoka and Kazuma try to solve the problems using this structure, but their films influence each other, and the situation spirals in unexpected directions. Starring Maria Ito ("Summer Film ni Notte") as Madoka the playwright and Kai Inowaki ("Musicophilia") as Kazuma the band musician. The cast also includes Oshiro Maeda and Hinako Kikuchi as members of Madoka's theater troupe, Suzuyuki Kaneko and Yusuke Mikawa as members of Kazuma's band, Takafumi Imai as a semi-delinquent who frequents "Mikazuki Rock," and the comedy duo "The Geese" as a pair of detectives. Additionally, members of Europe Kikaku, including Gota Ishida, Shintaro Kanamaru, and Riko Fujitani, play unique characters.
title_norm:you can succeed, too: The pinnacle of Japanese musicals, depicting a salaryman struggling in the battle for foreign tourists in Tokyo just before the Olympics. Throughout the film, talented performers sing and dance, and Frankie's astonishing physical abilities leave you in awe. The grand group dance in 'Man Alone' is especially breathtaking.
title_norm:young mothers: An ensemble drama by Belgian masters Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, known for "The Child" and "The Kid with a Bike," depicting five young mothers living in a mother-child support facility. The five girls—Jessica, Perla, Ariane, Julie, and Naima—live together in a facility that supports women who became pregnant young. Without anyone to rely on and facing various problems like poverty and violence, they become mothers while confused, troubled, and unable to find a model for the family they should aim for. Struggling not to be swallowed by the overwhelming loneliness, the girls who still wish "to love" sometimes lean on others and choose their own paths to follow. Lukas Dhont, director of "Close," is listed as a co-producer. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025, it won the Best Screenplay Award and the Ecumenical Jury Prize.
title_norm:yuho no border: A documentary tracing the journey and present life of Yuho Asaka, one of Japan's pioneers of peer counseling. Born in Fukushima City, Fukushima Prefecture in 1956, Yuho Asaka has a condition characterized by brittle bones. From a young age, she was forced to give up on learning and grew angry at a society that discriminates and excludes based on disability and gender. Always searching for her place in the world, Asaka connected with the cerebral palsy activist group "Fukushima Prefecture Aoi Shiba no Kai" and, drawing on the independent living movement and feminism she encountered while studying in the U.S., helped establish Japan's first independent living center. She also participated in international conferences and helped spark changes to the Eugenic Protection Law. The film follows Asaka's relentless pursuit of freedom, while also depicting her sister Aiko, who was caught in the turbulent relationship between their father and Yuho; her daughter Sora, who was born with the same condition and works at an overseas institute advocating for the rights of people with disabilities while attending graduate school; and the young caregivers who share daily life with her in a free-spirited relationship. Yumiko Asano, producer of "What Could Have Been?," makes her directorial debut, with Tomoaki Fujino, director of that same film, handling cinematography, editing, and production.
title_norm:yurie: This drama depicts a chef with communication difficulties and a free-spirited Korean woman who comes to learn Japanese cuisine. As they repeatedly try to revitalize the restaurant, they gradually break free from their rigid values. It is the feature-length debut of director Harumi Ikemoto, whose short film 'The Hunt' won the Excellence Award in the short film category at the 2023 SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival. Three years after losing his father, George Uehara took over the restaurant 'Yurie.' Although his cooking skills are solid, he is forced to accept the reality that the restaurant has recently seen fewer customers. Then Kim Juri, who came to Japan from Korea to learn Japanese cuisine, appears and starts working part-time at the restaurant. Despite clashing due to their differing values, they gradually grow closer and try various ideas to boost the restaurant's business. Sho Aoyagi, a member of 'Gekidan EXILE' active in films and dramas, plays George, a chef who struggles to express his thoughts and feelings and has some communication difficulties. Yeon-su Ha, who moved her base of operations from Korea to Japan and appeared in the NHK morning drama 'The Tiger's Wing,' plays Kim Juri, the part-time worker who initially keeps her distance from George due to her free-spirited nature. Yusuke Mikawa, known for 'Cloud,' co-stars as Iwakura, another part-time employee who watches over the two.
title_norm:zabriskie point: Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, who won top prizes at all three major film festivals (Berlin, Venice, Cannes) in the 1960s, made this film after moving to America in 1970. Set in Los Angeles and Death Valley, it depicts the psychological landscape of love between a man and a woman. In the late 1960s, amidst the peak of counterculture, with university protests raging and students clashing with armed police, Mark grows tired of futile debates at student gatherings. He grabs a gun and confronts the police officers cracking down on campus, but misses his chance to fire and flees. He then steals a Cessna at an airfield and takes to the sky. Meanwhile, Daria, a secretary at a Los Angeles real estate company, is driving across the vast desert to attend a meeting. The two meet by chance and arrive at Zabriskie Point, overlooking Death Valley... The leads are newcomers Mark Frechette and Daria Halprin, whom Antonioni scouted on the streets. The soundtrack effectively features music by Pink Floyd, Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, Kaleidoscope, John Fahey, The Rolling Stones, and The Youngbloods. Released in Japan in 1970, it also had a late-show release in 1996. A revival release is scheduled for 2026, the first in 30 years.
title_norm:zakken! the cosmos beneath ou: A youth story based on the manga 'Zakken!' (published by Shogakukan), which was developed from a real club activity, the 'Weed Research Club,' at Tokyo Metropolitan Hibiya High School, by screenwriter and film director Naho Uemura and the scenario creation team 'Monogatari Lab,' with Uemura herself writing and directing the film adaptation. It delicately and freshly depicts a teenage girl lost and unsure of herself, who discovers her own identity through the weeds growing at her feet, which she had never paid attention to before. Spring of her first year of high school. Sugano Yukari, an ordinary girl who isn't passionate about anything and just goes through the motions, meets her classmate Tokuda Mimi, nicknamed 'Dokudami-chan,' who loves weeds and is fascinated by their vitality. Slightly eccentric but with a straightforward and pure heart, Yukari gradually opens up to her. Dokudami-chan dreams of reviving the 'Zakken,' or 'Weed Research Club,' and Yukari, while hesitant about her enthusiasm, begins activities with her aimed at reviving the club, but... Luna Nakajima, who has starred in films like 'A Town of Old Houses' and 'Tore!' and won the Japan Academy Prize for Newcomer for 'Tokyo Taxi,' plays Sugano Yukari, and Miyu Oshima, known for the NHK morning drama 'Omusubi' and the drama 'Bokutachi nchi,' plays Tokuda Mimi, taking on the lead roles.
title_norm:ástin sem eftir er: In a small rural town in Iceland, artist Anna lives with her responsible eldest daughter Ida, her mischievous twin sons Grímur and Þorgils, and her dog Panda, while searching for her path as an artist. Though she married young and is supposedly "no longer a couple" with her ex-husband Magnús, he can't seem to cut ties, constantly finding excuses to visit, share meals, and even join picnics. Before she knows it, they slip back into a daily life as if they were "still a family"—but what comes next?
title_norm:éloge de lamour: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:кин дза дза!: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
title_norm:солярис: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
title_norm:جاده خاکی: A car races across the desolate landscape of Iran. In the back seat, the father entertains his exuberant younger son; in the passenger seat, the mother sways to an old pop song; and in the driver's seat, the eldest son stares silently ahead. While the younger son, unaware of the purpose of the trip, frolics innocently, the family arrives near the Turkish border...
title_norm:خانه‌ی دوست کجاست؟: An Iranian film that vividly captures a boy's journey to find his friend's house to return a precious notebook he accidentally took home, bringing director Abbas Kiarostami international fame. At a primary school in the village of Koker in northern Iran, Mohammad is severely scolded by his teacher for doing his homework on a piece of paper instead of a notebook and is told he will be expelled if it happens again. However, his best friend Ahmad, who sits next to him, accidentally takes Mohammad's notebook home. Panicked that Mohammad will be expelled without his notebook, Ahmad searches for his friend's house in a distant neighboring village to return it, but struggles to find it... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title_norm:قضية الغرباء: An ensemble drama inspired by the reality that 14 million people were forced to flee abroad to escape the long devastation of the Syrian civil war, depicting families torn apart by conflict and those around them from multiple perspectives. Set across four countries—Syria, Turkey, Greece, and the United States—the story unfolds in five chapters, intersecting the lives of five families. As the civil war between government forces and rebel groups intensifies in Syria's dictatorship, Syrian doctor Amira decides to cross dangerous borders with her daughter to reach safety. Syrian border guard Mustafa distrusts the brutal government forces and struggles between being a soldier who follows orders and a human with a conscience. Turkish smuggler Marwan seeks to earn money by loading refugees onto boats bound for Greece to move his sick son to America. Poet Fathi boards that boat with his wife and child, facing mortal danger. Greek coast guard Stavros discovers refugees navigating stormy seas and strives to save lives. Film producer and humanitarian activist Brandt Andersen, who made the 2020 short film "Refugee" as his starting point, makes his feature directorial, screenwriting, and producing debut with this meticulously researched work. Yasmin Al-Masri reprises her role as doctor Amira from the short, and Omar Sy returns as smuggler Marwan.
title_norm:مسافر: The feature-length debut of Iranian master Abbas Kiarostami, made in 1974, this human drama freshly depicts the funny yet poignant adventures of a boy struggling desperately to watch a soccer match. Gassem, a 10-year-old boy attending elementary school, is obsessed with soccer, often neglecting his homework and classes, earning constant scolding from his teacher and mother. Determined to go see an important match held in the capital, Tehran, he tries every trick to get money for transportation and a ticket, including stealing from home and deceiving his friends... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
title_norm:जवान: A thrilling action film from the 'King of Bollywood', Shah Rukh Khan, in his first collaboration with a young Tamil film crew. It depicts the righteous struggle of subway hijackers who steal a ransom from arms dealers.
title_norm:சர்வம் தாளமயம்: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
title_norm:மார்க் ஆண்டனி: This Indian sci-fi action film comically and eccentrically depicts a gangster's son who obtains a phone that allows him to talk to people in the past and tries to rewrite fate. In 1975, mad scientist Chiranjeevi invents a telephone that can call people in the past. Using it, he can avert disasters about to befall his past self or loved ones, or make choices that lead to profit. However, Chiranjeevi gets caught in a gang war at a bar while celebrating, and the phone goes missing. Twenty years later, auto mechanic Mark stumbles upon the phone and learns its special abilities and how to use it. This phone eventually sparks a massive upheaval involving Mark's foster father, gang boss Jackie; Jackie's son Madan; and Mark's deceased father, Antony. In Japan, Vishal plays dual roles as mechanic Mark and his gangster father Antony, while S. J. Surya, known for "Jigarthanda Double X," co-stars as Antony's partner Jackie.
title_norm:ಕಾಂತಾರ: A legendary suspense-action film set in South India, centered on the ancient ritual of 'Bhuta Kola' (spirit worship). It powerfully depicts the strange fate of a land protected by divine grace and became a long-running hit in India. About 170 years ago, a vast forest was granted to the indigenous people by the oracle of the god Panjuruli. The village of Kadu Bettur has long performed the Bhuta Kola ritual and maintained peace through divine protection, even when landlords tried to reclaim the land. However, the newly appointed forest officer Murali attempts to incorporate the villagers' land into a state-designated protected forest. As the village faces a crisis of survival, Shiva, a buffalo race champion whose father was a Bhuta Kola performer, opposes the forest department to protect the village's peace, leading to an incident. Rishab Shetty, who has an unusual background of juggling jobs in water vending and real estate before entering the film industry, directed, wrote, and starred in the film, passionately playing Shiva, the village's biggest rogue.
title_norm:ผีใช้ได้ค่ะ: In Bangkok, Thailand, where dust pollution is severe, March (Wisarut Himmarat) spends his days in grief after losing his beloved wife Nat (Davika Hoorne) to a respiratory disease. One day, Nat's soul returns, inhabiting a vacuum cleaner, and the two reaffirm their love. Meanwhile, at the factory run by March's family, the spirit of a deceased employee possesses the machinery, bringing operations to a halt. Rejected by family troubled by the spirit and by society, Nat tries to prove her true love for her husband and her own existence as a 'useful ghost' by helping with the factory's exorcism...
title_norm:〈主婦〉の学校: A documentary covering a coeducational home economics school in Iceland. Founded in 1942 in Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland, 'The School of Housewives' is a small home economics school where students live together in a dormitory and learn practical household management skills. Once common worldwide, home economics schools that trained women, who had few educational opportunities after compulsory education, to become good housewives have largely declined with the changing times. Amidst this, this school became coeducational in the 1970s, attracting students regardless of gender who seek wisdom and skills for 'living in the present.' Through the students learning the art of enjoying an independent life, the film gently questions our approach to daily living and housework.
title_norm:「ひゃくえむ。」メイキングドキュメンタリー 真剣（ガチ）に: A making-of documentary for *Hyakuemu.*, the 2025 theatrical anime adaptation of Uoto's manga directed by Kenji Iwaisawa (*On-Gaku: Our Sound*). Utilizing the rotoscoping technique—where animation is created by tracing over live-action footage—the documentary provides close-up coverage of every department, from live-action filming to animation production and sound design, recording the trajectory of the film's completion. It captures the behind-the-scenes process from multiple perspectives, offering a rare look at the live-action shoots that form the foundation of the rotoscoping process, the production of key animation and background art, and the final sound and visual checks. The film vividly portrays the long journey from the project's inception to its conclusion, highlighting the staff's meticulous dedication and trial-and-error process as a single animated work takes shape. This documentary allows viewers to relive the four-year production period and the immense passion poured into the project. It is composed and edited by Ayumu Miyazaki, who also served as the editor for the main feature.
title_norm:「魔女っ子メグちゃん」シリーズ: A work that marked a turning point in the "witch girl" genre, featuring a tomboyish heroine and the introduction of a rival witch. The sleek character designs by Shingo Araki, the European-style cityscapes by Isamu Tsuchida, and the romance-filled Meg all realized the planning slogan of "beautiful, cute, and chic." Talent from Mushi Production, including the original creator Hiromi Pro and director Susumu Sakaguchi, also joined the project. The final episode, directed by Yugo Serikawa, masterfully drives Meg into a heartbreaking farewell. 72 episodes total.
title_norm:「魔法のマコちゃん」シリーズ／「魔法使いチャッピー」シリー: An ambitious work based on the fairy tale "The Little Mermaid," incorporating romantic elements to raise the target age range from the traditional witch girl series. Character design was handled by Shinya Takahashi, and director Yugo Serikawa's direction fills Mako's daily life with the lyricism of a melodrama tinged with tragedy. 48 episodes total.
title_norm:『 丹下左膳餘話 百萬兩の壺』 ＊デジタル上映: A commotion over a pot that reveals the hiding place of a large sum of money draws in the swordsman Sanzen... A delightful gem showcasing the talent of Yamanaka, who lightly and skillfully portrays Daigoro's signature role of Sanzen.
title_norm:『 沓掛時次郎 遊俠一匹』 ＊デジタル上映: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title_norm:『open house』: Synopsis: Director Isao Yukisada’s little-known feature debut. Set amidst the chaotic atmosphere of the 1990s, the film lyrically depicts three men and women drifting through life, burdened by a sense of alienation.
title_norm:『あじさいの歌』: Synopsis: An old Western-style mansion on a hill—there, an eccentric father and his sheltered daughter (Ashikawa) reach a turning point in their lives after a chance encounter with a young man (Ishihara) they unexpectedly take in. You are sure to be captivated by Ashikawa’s radiance as she matures from a somber girl into an independent woman.
title_norm:『いのちの朝』: Synopsis: Fuyuko (Ashikawa) supports her household by working at an insurance company. She asks her father, a painter, to paint her portrait, but... This literary masterpiece depicts the profound bond between a struggling artist and the daughter who devotedly supports him. Ashikawa is breathtakingly beautiful, portraying a strong-willed woman with poise and dignity.
title_norm:『しろばんば』: Synopsis: Early Taisho era. This film depicts the growth of a boy raised by an elderly woman in a mountain village on the Izu Peninsula. A masterpiece of literary drama, it was adapted and filmed by master director Keisuke Kinoshita from the autobiographical novel by the literary giant Yasushi Inoue. Incidentally, "Shirobamba" refers to the snow bug. Ashikawa plays the role of the boy’s fleeting "Madonna."
title_norm:『エレノアってグレイト。』トークイベント付: Eleanor is left with a gaping hole in her heart after the death of her longtime best friend, Bessie. Her estranged family won't give her the time of day. Then one day, thinking she's going to a casual tea party, she accidentally stumbles into a support group for Holocaust survivors. Intending it as a one-time lie, she begins to tell the story of her deceased friend Bessie's life, recounting her memories of the Holocaust. A journalism student named Nina, inspired by the dramatic story, grows close to Eleanor, and Eleanor's heart soars with this new friendship. But as her harmless lie takes on a life of its own, it spirals into a huge commotion.
title_norm:『カウント・ベイシー』トークイベント付: Count Basie, who brought the blues into jazz and sparked a rhythm revolution, built the golden age of swing jazz and was hailed as the 'King of Swing'. In Japan, he has captivated many jazz fans for years, and his music remains highly popular in the repertoires of student big bands and wind ensembles. This film focuses not only on his brilliant public career but also on his little-known private life, which Basie himself rarely discussed. The film's production team discovered numerous home movies shot by his family, vast photo albums, letters, and other valuable materials. It reveals his family love for his daughter Diane, who was born with cerebral palsy, and his wife Catherine, who supported the African American civil rights movement from its early days and interacted with Martin Luther King Jr. and his wife. The film also features members of the still-active Basie Orchestra and friends like Quincy Jones and Annie Ross. Through their portrayals of Basie and valuable archival materials, including collaborations with Frank Sinatra and Billie Holiday, his life's journey and the turbulent social history of 20th-century America are brought into sharp relief.
title_norm:『ビトゥーカ ミルトン・ナシメント フェアウェルツアー』ト: Called the 'Voice of Brazil,' Milton Nascimento, affectionately known as Bituca, led MPB (Brazilian popular music post-bossa nova) alongside contemporaries Gilberto Gil, Caetano Veloso, and Chico Buarque, and collaborated with countless international musicians. This documentary film traces Milton's life and music while following his global farewell concert tour, announced upon turning 80 in 2022. In the first half, Milton's troupe tours Europe and the Americas, receiving ecstatic welcomes. Pat Metheny, Spike Lee, Quincy Jones, and Wayne Shorter speak about Milton, and there are scenes of collaboration with Esperanza Spalding and Herbie Hancock. Milton reflects on his childhood raised as an adopted son, converses with his own adopted child on the road, and shares memories of his benefactor, singer Elis Regina. The second half begins with the landscapes of Minas Gerais, the highland region of inland Brazil that is Milton's home and musical origin. Friends like Chico, Caetano, and Gil, collaborating poets like Márcio Borges and Ronaldo Bastos, and younger musicians who admire Milton, discuss the appeal and depths of his music. Inescapable negative histories, such as racism and Brazil's 20-year military dictatorship starting in 1964, are also revealed. Then, the farewell concert finale approaches: the concert at Mineirão, the football stadium in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. Members of Clube da Esquina (Corner Club), the title of a landmark 1972 album and the name for the family of Minas musicians centered around Milton—Lô Borges, Beto Guedes, Wagner Tiso, and Toninho Horta—share behind-the-scenes stories and perform together.
title_norm:『人情紙風船』 ＊デジタル上映: The final work of renowned early Showa period director Tomu Uchida, who died of illness at just 28, this is a humanistic period drama. In the Edo period, Shinzo, a barber living in a poor tenement, runs a gambling den and catches the eye of yakuza. Strapped for cash, he tries to pawn his barber tools but is refused. Meanwhile, Matajuro, a ronin living in the same tenement, seeks employment with a samurai his father once served, but is completely ignored. One day, Shinzo accidentally kidnaps the pawnshop owner's daughter and brings her back to the tenement... An adaptation of Kawatake Mokuami's kabuki play "Kamiyui Shinzo."
title_norm:『倖せは俺等のねがい』 ＊デジタル上映: A couple working at a factory, on the verge of marriage and moving into their long-awaited new home, are saddled with four distant relatives' children... The third directorial work by the renowned actor Uno, who captures the modest happiness of ordinary people. Frankie won the Blue Ribbon Award for Best Actor for this film and 'The Sun of the Meiji Restoration'.
title_norm:『天外者』七夕上映会 vol.6: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a great man who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was called a rare 'Tengaramon' (a person with extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, who previously collaborated on 'Ask This of Rikyu' and '1890', it is an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Tomoatsu Godai (later known as Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores the internal strife over expelling foreigners versus opening the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire to 'see a free dream' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to create a country where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Godai's ally Ryoma Sakamoto, Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki (who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate), Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito (who became Japan's first Prime Minister), and Aoi Morikawa plays the courtesan Haru. [Admission Fee] Flat rate of 1,000 yen. *As this is a special screening, various tickets, free passes, and shareholder discount coupons cannot be used. In the late Edo period, in a corner of Japan shaken by Perry's arrival, two young samurai who keenly sense the arrival of a new era race forward at full speed. Tomoatsu Godai (Haruma Miura) and Ryoma Sakamoto (Shohei Miura). For some reason, both are being targeted by many samurai. Their lives, which see far into Japan's future, begin to intersect at this moment. Expel the barbarians or open the country? Godai ignores the intense internal strife and looks to the world. Then, he meets the courtesan Haru (Aoi Morikawa) and is driven by the desire to 'see a free dream,' joining forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki (Takanori Nishikawa), and Hirobumi Ito (Yuki Morinaga) to create a country where everyone can dream.
