title_norm:寝る映画:
A film featuring a screenplay generated by ChatGPT, with its ethereal visuals and music also brought to life through AI. As the characters experience a virtual world while asleep, they discover a profound connection to the film's core themes: "seeing with the heart" and "touching with sound."

Yuki is blind, and her husband Ken is deaf. Despite their bond, a certain distance lingers between them. One day, the couple joins a clinical trial premised on the idea that "disabilities can be overcome within an AI-generated virtual reality." While their bodies sleep in the physical world, they awaken in a virtual realm where their sight and hearing have been restored. Amidst the strange occurrences of this world, they begin to sense each other’s presence more deeply than ever before.

Positioned as "unconscious immersive cinema" designed to be experienced while the viewer sleeps, this experimental film attempts to reach the subconscious by layering poetic phrases, music, and subtitled imagery throughout. It is directed by Tsuyoshi Sone, widely known as the cinematographer of "One Cut of the Dead."
title_norm:尋秦記 バック・トゥ・ザ・パスト: A historical sci-fi action film and sequel to the 2001 TV series 'A Step into the Past', based on a popular Hong Kong novel. After time-traveling to the Warring States period and deeply influencing history, former Hong Kong police VIP protection officer Xiang Shaolong lives quietly in seclusion with his wife and child. His former disciple, the King of Qin, whom Xiang helped ascend the throne, remains wary of his master, their conflict smoldering. Meanwhile in modern Hong Kong, Ken, the time machine inventor imprisoned for 20 years for Xiang's failure to return, is released. Having lost everything, he plots to seize the Qin throne and become the First Emperor himself, traveling back to the Warring States with his daughter Gary and others. Attacked by Ken, the King of Qin flees and ends up at Xiang Shaolong's refuge. Louis Koo and Raymond Lam, who also starred together in the 2024 hit 'Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In', reprise their roles as Xiang Shaolong and the King of Qin, also performing the theme song. Alongside original TV series cast members, the film features Michael Miu ('White Storm'), Bai Baihe ('Monster Hunt'), and Wu Yue ('Ip Man: The Finale'). Hong Kong action star Sammo Hung serves as action director.
title_norm:小川のほとりで: Korean master Hong Sang-soo directs an ensemble drama set at a women's university in Seoul, depicting the romantic entanglements of students and adults surrounding a theater festival. At a women's university in Seoul, with the theater festival approaching, textile artist Jon-hee, who works as a lecturer, invites her uncle Si-on, a famous actor and stage director, as a temporary director to fill a gap caused by a love scandal on campus. As they begin creating a short play for the festival, various events unfold over ten days, including the aftermath of the students' love affairs and the budding romance between a senior professor and Si-on. Actress Kim Min-hee, Hong Sang-soo's partner in both public and private life, stars as Jon-hee and won the Best Performance Award at the 77th Locarno International Film Festival in 2024. The cast also includes regulars from Hong Sang-soo's films: Kwon Hae-hyo as Jon-hee's uncle Si-on, Cho Yun-hee as the professor who admires Si-on, and Ha Seong-guk as the fired director who was dating three people. In Japan, it was screened under the title 'Suyuchon' at the 25th Tokyo Filmex in 2024. It was theatrically released in 2025 as the second film in the 'Monthly Hong Sang-soo' project, a series of five consecutive monthly new releases celebrating the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:小春日和 indian summer:
This human drama depicts a troubled and isolated nursing assistant searching for her own way of life through a series of encounters. The film was planned and produced by Tomoko Kusube, a psychiatrist and actress, who drew from her own experience battling cancer to convey the importance of living a positive life.

Koharu Sakaguchi, burdened by worries she cannot share with anyone, flees her home after a clash with her father. Unable to return due to her feelings of guilt, she begins working as a nursing assistant at a hospital. Through her interactions with patients facing their illnesses in their own ways—such as "The Cancers," a trio of women living brightly despite their battle with cancer, and Yuki Yamamoto, who chooses to be discharged to spend her remaining days at home—Koharu gradually begins to confront her own life. One day, she suddenly recalls a precious message from her beloved grandmother, Suzuko, and makes a firm resolution.

Misaki Mizumura (*Move Forward as You Are*) stars as Koharu Sakaguchi, with Yura Chihara as Hiyori Sakaguchi, Kaoru Yumi as Grandmother Suzuko, Rie Shibata as cancer patient Yuki Yamamoto, Kappa Kunikida as Yuki’s husband Takashi, and Shiro Sano as Dr. Hiroshi Ueda. The film is directed by Isao Matsumoto (*Let’s Meet at Angie’s Bar*).
title_norm:少女ムシェット: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
title_norm:少年ジャックと魔法使い: Directed by Yasuji Yabushita with animation direction by Akira Daikuhara for Toei Animation's 10th anniversary film. Based on the heroic epic 'Beowulf,' this version features Jack driving a car, a witch arriving by helicopter, and a struggle to rescue comrades turned into demons in the witch's castle. Seiichiro Uno's cheerful music won the Mainichi Film Concours Music Award.
title_norm:山の焚火: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
title_norm:岡本万太: The protagonist, Manta Okamoto (Sojiro Sanada), is a 26-year-old part-timer. Plagued by mounting irritation over life’s minor inconveniences, he lives in constant fear of whether he can suppress his own impulses. For Manta is a man of uncontrollable rage. Once a month, his stress reaches a breaking point—his "Limit Day." To cope, he locks himself away at home, strapped to a bed with restraints. Because these days strike without warning, he frequently misses work, leading to a cycle of being fired and drifting from one job to the next. One day, Nakamura (Masaki Miura), a former senior colleague from a publishing house that let him go, approaches him with a new opportunity. The job is simple: store some cardboard boxes for a few days in exchange for a large sum of money. But...
title_norm:市民ケーン: A human drama produced, directed, co-written, and starring the 25-year-old prodigy Orson Welles, hailed as a masterpiece in film history. Based on real-life newspaper magnate William Randolph Hearst, it depicts the tumultuous life of a wealthy tycoon through innovative visual techniques and narrative structure. The wealthy newspaper magnate Kane dies, leaving behind the mysterious word "Rosebud." A newsreel editor assigned to investigate the meaning of the word interviews people who knew Kane in life, including his ex-wife and business partners. What emerges is the lonely life of a man who had everything. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 14th Academy Awards in 1942.
title_norm:帰って来たドラゴン: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title_norm:幕末ヒポクラテスたち: A period drama set at the end of the Edo period, when traditional Chinese medicine doctors and Western-trained Dutch medicine doctors coexisted, starring Kuranosuke Sasaki as the village Dutch medicine doctor Daisuke Okura. In a village on the outskirts of Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, Daisuke Okura is a tolerant, curious Dutch medicine doctor who saves common people regardless of wealth or status. He is constantly engaged in fierce arguments with the Chinese medicine doctor Gensai, his sworn enemy. One day, Okura saves a hot-tempered young man named Shinsa through surgery, an event that drastically changes both their lives. Director Kazuki Omori, known for the ensemble drama 'Hippocrates' about Kyoto medical students, conceived this film based on the 1960 film 'Fundoshi Doctor,' which depicted a warm-hearted doctor and his wife, setting it in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period to portray the dawn of modern Japanese medicine. When Omori passed away in 2022 while preparing for filming, the project nearly became a phantom, but Akira Ogata, director of 'The Independent Teenage Chorus' and a former assistant director to Omori, carried on his will and brought it to completion. Kuranosuke Sasaki plays Okura. Takeshi Naito, who made his film debut in 'Hippocrates,' plays Okura's rival Gensai, and Akira Emoto, who played a resident doctor in 'Hippocrates,' appears as the mysterious samurai Danzo. Additionally, Shizuka Muroi, who made her film debut in Omori's 'Hear the Wind Sing,' provides narration, and Takuya Nishioka, who has known Omori since the 1970s, wrote the screenplay, with many cast and crew members associated with Kazuki Omori participating.
title_norm:幕末太陽傳: Saheiji, left penniless at a Shinagawa pleasure quarter at the end of the Edo period... A masterpiece by Kawashima and Frankie, and a classic in Japanese film history. In this ensemble comedy where late-Edo period patriots and courtesans mingle, Frankie's light and agile movements as he navigates through the chaos are the film's core.
title_norm:幸せの、忘れもの。: A Spanish film that delicately portrays the story of a woman living in a world without sound and her family. Ángela, who is deaf, and her husband Héctor, who gently supports her, communicate through the irreplaceable language of sign language. Ángela works in a pottery workshop, surrounded by the comforting smell of clay and trusted colleagues, living a quiet and peaceful life. However, a certain 'happy event' begins to gradually shatter her daily life. As she wavers in her sense of alienation, Ángela tries to grasp the 'true happiness' that flickers between the silent world and the world outside... Directed by emerging filmmaker Eva Libertad, who also works as a playwright and sociologist, this film is based on her highly acclaimed 2021 short film 'Sorda.' Starring Miriam Garlo, a deaf actress and Libertad's real sister, the film reflects the director and her sister's long-standing personal experiences, capturing the subtle misunderstandings between deaf and hearing people and the different feelings of alienation each holds. It won the Panorama Audience Award and the Art Cinema Award at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025, as well as the Golden Biznaga (Best Film), Audience Award, Best Actress, and Best Actor at the 28th Málaga Film Festival in Spain.
title_norm:幸福（しあわせ）: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:幻の光: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
title_norm:幻を見るひと: A documentary depicting Yoshimasu Gozo, a leading contemporary Japanese poet, as he visits Kyoto, a city rich with groundwater, questions the meaning of life through dialogue with 'water' and the changing seasons, and ultimately creates a poem. Witnessing the tsunami damage from the Great East Japan Earthquake in 2011, Yoshimasu was struck speechless by the impact of water that strips everything away. Seeking a new meaning for water, he visits Kyoto, known for its abundant groundwater. In Kyoto, a basin surrounded by deep mountains, Yoshimasu travels tracing the 'water' of the city, visiting places like Ryukyoin, where Kawabata Yasunari wrote 'The Old Capital,' as well as Daigo-ji, Myoshin-ji, Daitoku-ji, and Kifune Shrine. The film captures Yoshimasu's sensibility, which remains virginal even as he approaches 80, and his precious creative process.
title_norm:幻を見るひと〜京都の吉増剛造〜: The film opens with footage of the tsunami from the Great East Japan Earthquake (courtesy of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism). The new work by Gozo Yoshimasu, 'A Water Tree Stands on the Planet,' born at the climax of this film, was completed after the poet's long struggle. Yoshimasu had been unable to write poetry since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. 'At the beginning of human life, there is amniotic fluid and bathwater; at the end, there is the water of the dying that moistens the lips,' says Yoshimasu. 'Water,' the source of life for humanity, has been an important theme for poets throughout history. However, the poet who directly witnessed the scars of the great tsunami lost his words to the impact of water that strips everything away. Instead of writing poetry, Yoshimasu began daily copying the poems of the Showa-era philosopher Takaaki Yoshimoto in rice-grain-sized characters, like a sutra transcription. The camera captures this strange and fascinating scene. 'Beside the Poem,' written over four years and which he calls 'Monster-kun,' is a massive work of nearly 700 pages. Within it, the actual voice of the representative Japanese poet Akiko Yosano (1878–1942) resounds, sanukite stones ring, and finally, an eerie scene unfolds as he flings ink onto paper like Jackson Pollock (USA, 1912–1956), the founder of action painting. Deviating from the act of writing, time accumulates on a single sheet of paper, creating an object-like state. This becomes a 'practice writing book' over a long period, leading to the gestation of a new work. One day, learning that Kyoto has as much groundwater as Lake Biwa (Japan's largest lake), the poet seeks a new path for poetic creation in Kyoto's water veins. The poet's tentacles begin to reach the water of Kyoto, which holds a giant cradle of water. Then, before Yoshimasu appears the phantom of Yasunari Kawabata, winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature. Resonating with the talent of seeing phantoms in Kawabata, who stayed in Kyoto and devoted himself to creative work, the poet gropes for the thread of his own poetic creation. What the poet's senses finally touch is the great Eastern spirit, the water god, the dragon. Yoshimasu hears the voice of water's destiny and takes up his brush. The story of Gozo Yoshimasu depicted in this film shows the path of a poet, standing at the abyss of creative despair, 'gaining new life.' The backdrop, like Kawabata's masterpiece 'The Old Capital' which earned him the Nobel Prize, is vividly colored by Kyoto's four seasons, Zen temples, and karesansui (dry landscape gardens).
title_norm:廃用身: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
title_norm:復活の日: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
title_norm:心と体と シネマカリテと また逢える: A slaughterhouse on the outskirts of Budapest. Mária, who struggles to fit in at work, and Endre, her boss who takes an interest in her. Though the two are socially awkward and out of sync, they are drawn together when a company-wide counseling session reveals they have been sharing the exact same dream—but...
title_norm:心のパズル:
A drama that explores the multifaceted nature of the human psyche through the lens of Dissociative Identity Disorder (multiple personality disorder). Former stage actor Kimihiko Yuasa, unable to control a violent "other self" within him, once struck the director he admired, Kiyoshi Yanagimoto, during a rehearsal. Now, while grappling with his own inner turmoil, Yuasa works as a private investigator. One day, he is approached by Takayama—who, like Yuasa, was a victim of Yanagimoto’s abuse of power—with a request: "He must have multiple personalities; find the evidence." As Yuasa begins his investigation, he encounters a version of Yanagimoto who seems like a completely different person.

The film marks the directorial debut of Shigeharu Kadowaki. Coming from the food and beverage industry, Kadowaki turned to filmmaking
title_norm:心をつないで 思いを紡いで: Screening at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:心平、: A brother who cannot fit into society, a father who has given up on the future, and a sister bound to the home. This is a story of the small steps the three of them take forward. One day, the Great East Japan Earthquake suddenly upends their peaceful daily lives. Not only the earthquake and tsunami, but also the nuclear accident forced many people to lose their homes and jobs, leaving Fukushima behind. This is the story of a family living in the aftermath, three years later, in a deeply scarred Fukushima.
title_norm:急に具合が悪くなる: Director Ryusuke Hamaguchi ("Drive My Car," "Evil Does Not Exist") portrays the spiritual encounter of two women with the same-sounding name in Paris. Based on the exchange of 20 letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who survived cancer metastasis, and anthropologist Maho Isono, titled "Suddenly Feeling Ill," the film depicts the connection between two women who meet by chance and their confrontation with the world. Marie-Lou Fontaine, director of the care facility "Garden of Freedom" on the outskirts of Paris, struggles with staff shortages and misunderstanding while striving for humane care. She meets Japanese stage director Mari Morisaki, who is battling cancer, and draws courage from her theater work. Guided by the coincidence of their similar-sounding names, Marie-Lou and Mari begin a friendship. But one day, Mari suddenly falls ill. As her illness progresses, their bond deepens, and their souls connect. Virginie Efira ("Benedetta") plays Marie-Lou, and Tao Okamoto, a global fashion model who has appeared in Hollywood films like "The Wolverine," plays Mari. Kyozo Nagatsuka ("Enemy") plays Goro Seimiya, an actor in Mari's play, and Koyo Kuroki ("The Generation of the Looking-Ahead") plays Tomoki Kubodera, Goro's grandson. Screened in the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto jointly won the Best Actress award. Okamoto became the first Japanese person to win the Cannes Best Actress award.
title_norm:怪物: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda, winner of the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival for "Shoplifters," this human drama is based on an original screenplay by Yuji Sakamoto, the popular screenwriter known for films like "We Made a Beautiful Bouquet" and the TV drama "The Days of Natsume." The music was composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto, who became the first Japanese to win an Academy Award for Best Original Score for "The Last Emperor" and passed away in March 2023. In a suburban town by a large lake, a single mother who loves her son, a caring schoolteacher, and innocent children live peaceful daily lives. One day, a fight breaks out at school. It seems like an ordinary scuffle between kids, but the accounts of those involved conflict, gradually escalating into a major incident that draws in society and the media. Then, on a stormy morning, the children suddenly vanish. What is the "monster"? This collaboration among leading Japanese creators—Hirokazu Kore-eda, Yuji Sakamoto, and Ryuichi Sakamoto—depicts the conclusion reached through a search for the "monster" from each character's perspective. Alongside Soya Kurokawa and Hinata Hiiragi, who play the two central boys, the film features a stellar cast including Sakura Ando, Eita Nagayama, Mitsuki Takahata, Akihiro Kakuta, Shido Nakamura, and Yuko Tanaka. It was screened in the Competition section of the 76th Cannes Film Festival in 2023, winning the Best Screenplay Award. It also received the Queer Palm, awarded to films dealing with LGBT and queer themes.
title_norm:悲しくて美しい世界 this is sparklehors: This documentary explores the enigmatic life and music of Mark Linkous, the central figure of the American act Sparklehorse, who emerged during the mid-1990s alternative rock boom and earned a devoted following for his singular musicality. Sparklehorse released their debut album, *Vivadixiesubmarinetransmissionplot*, in 1995, garnering critical acclaim across the West for its inventive sound. The band gained further prominence as the opening act for Radiohead and R.E.M., but during a European tour with Radiohead, Linkous suffered a near-fatal alcohol and drug overdose. Though he survived, the lasting effects of the incident cast a long shadow over his life, and in 2010, while working on his sixth album, he took his own life. Through interviews recorded shortly before his death and testimonies from fellow musicians and filmmaker David Lynch, this film unravels the reality of Linkous’s existence and his music.
title_norm:情事: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
title_norm:惊天大营救: A revenge action film starring Thai action star Tony Jaa, known for 'Ong-Bak' and 'Tom-Yum-Goong'. It depicts a man who lost his family confronting a massive conspiracy, packed with powerful Muay Thai-based hand-to-hand combat and high-speed, hard-hitting action. After his wife and daughter are killed by a mysterious organization, Bai An heads to the Republic of Parivina to uncover the truth and exact revenge. As he investigates on his own, he discovers a giant corporation secretly controlling the drug trade, but behind it swirls a vast conspiracy involving the military and police. The situation becomes intricately tangled with a mad drug lord, corrupt military police, and unexpected trials involving the only daughter of the corporation's owner. Bai An is tossed about but continues to battle the enemies closing in on him. Directed by Cheung Sui-yee. Co-stars include Xing Yu from 'Master Z: Ip Man Legacy', Philip Keung from 'Goldfinger', and Jason Han from 'Overheat: The Final Sanction'.
title_norm:惑星ソラリス: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
title_norm:愛の世紀: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:愛の新世界: Ray is an actress in a small theater troupe. By day, she devotes herself to rehearsals with her friends, and by night, she works as a dominatrix at an SM club in Shibuya. One evening, Ray becomes friendly with Ayumi, a hotel escort girl she occasionally sees in the elevator of the building where the club is located. Ayumi is a shrewd girl living with Kenji, a ronin studying for medical school entrance exams. The two hit it off and head out into the nightlife. After drinking, dancing, and partying, they part ways, promising to go see the sea at dawn together someday. Finally, the day of Ray's theater troupe's performance arrives. With Ayumi and Ray's client Sawatari watching, Ray's play is a success, met with thunderous applause. Ray is moved by the satisfaction of accomplishing something. Ayumi is also moved seeing Ray like this. The two head out to the coast at dawn in a car driven by a man they picked up.
title_norm:愛妻記: A film adaptation of the autobiographical novel by Ozaki, who won the Akutagawa Prize for "Norakuro Megane," with his wife as the model. This endearing film depicts the poor but happy days of a quirky writer husband (Frankie), who calls his wife by the pet name "Yoshihyoe," and his simple, charming wife (Kishi).
title_norm:我ら山人たち: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:戦国自衛隊: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
title_norm:敵:
Director Daihachi Yoshida (*The Kirishima Thing*, *Kiba: The Fangs of Fiction*) adapts Yasutaka Tsutsui’s novel of the same name into a monochrome cinematic experience. It tells the story of an elderly man living a tranquil, solitary life who is suddenly confronted by an "enemy."

Gisuke Watanabe, 77, is a retired university professor and widower living alone in the traditional Japanese house he inherited from his grandfather. He wakes at the same hour every morning, prepares his own meals, and treats every item he owns—from his clothing to his stationery—with meticulous care. Occasionally, he shares drinks with a few close friends or hosts dinner for a former student. His days pass in peace as he calculates how many more years his savings will sustain this lifestyle. However, into this quiet existence comes a disturbing message, flashing across his computer screen: "The enemy is coming."

Kyozo Nagatsuka takes on his first leading film role in 12 years as Gisuke. He is joined by Kumi Takiuchi as his former student, Asuka Kurosawa as his late wife, and Yuumi Kawai as a university student he meets at a bar, with Satoru Matsuo, Takashi Matsuo, Shinsuke Kato, and Ayumu Nakajima rounding out the supporting cast. The film competed at the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival in 2024, where it achieved a triple crown: the Tokyo Grand Prix / The Governor of Tokyo Award, Best Director (Daihachi Yoshida), and Best Actor (Kyozo Nagatsuka).
title_norm:新作歌舞伎 風の谷のナウシカ 前編: The first part of "New Kabuki: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind," a kabuki adaptation of all seven volumes of Hayao Miyazaki's manga version of "Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind." The story is set in a world where industrial civilization was destroyed by a war known as the "Seven Days of Fire," and most of the land is covered by the "Sea of Corruption," a forest that emits giant insects and toxic miasma. Nausicaä, the daughter of the chieftain of the small "Valley of the Wind," where people who control the wind live, is not afraid of the feared Sea of Corruption or its insects and seeks to unravel the mystery of its origin. One day, a stone containing the power to revive the "God Warrior," which burned the world in the Seven Days of Fire, is discovered in the small kingdom of Pejite, and the powerful empire of Tolmekia moves to seize it. This first part includes three of the seven acts: Act I "The One in Blue Garments Stands in a Golden Field," Act II "The Revival of the Devil's Law," and Act III "The White Witch Marches on the Bloody Path." This is a recorded video of the stage performance held at Shinbashi Enbujo Theatre from December 6 to 25, 2019, screened as a delayed viewing in February 2020 at Togeki, Shinjuku Piccadilly, and other venues (Part 1: February 14–20, 2020 / Part 2: February 28–March 5, 2020, each for a limited one-week run).
title_norm:新劇場版☆ケロロ軍曹 復活して速攻地球滅亡の危機であります: As part of the 20th-anniversary project for the TV anime "Sergeant Keroro," based on the manga by Mine Yoshizaki serialized in "Monthly Shonen Ace" since 1999, this theatrical anime is the first in 16 years since "Keroro Gunso the Super Movie: Creation! Ultimate Keroro, Wonderous Time-Space Island!!" in 2010. It depicts the Keroro Platoon, who were supposed to invade Earth, fighting to protect the planet from a new invader. Sergeant Keroro and his platoon members, who came to Earth to invade but now spend their days idly at their host family's home, encounter mysterious phenomena occurring across the country. Feeling a sense of crisis, the Keroro Platoon rises to the challenge, putting their pride as invaders on the line, but they encounter mysterious letters wherever they go. The screenplay and general direction are handled by Yuichi Fukuda, known for directing the live-action "Gintama" series. The staff includes key members who have supported the series, with Satoshi Ozaki as director, Satoshi Koike as character designer, and BN Pictures handling animation production. Jesse from SixTONES voices the theatrical original characters, the brothers Aruru and Deruru, playing both roles.
title_norm:旅立ちのラストダンス: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
title_norm:旅立ちのラストダンス: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. title_norm:日泰小食: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. Located about 30 minutes southwest of Hong Kong Island by ferry, Cheung Chau is a small island known as a fishing village, where colorful boats bob in the harbor and time flows gently. The 'Yat Tai' diner on the island is always bustling with locals who gather to play cards and mahjong with a beer in hand. However, societal changes and the fervor of citizens reach this island far from Hong Kong, and the diner's regulars cannot remain indifferent. From the owner staring at the TV to young people eagerly seeking information, each person grapples with the tides of the era from their own perspective and distance. Eventually, the pandemic that engulfs the world also has a major impact on this diner. The director is Frankie Shin, for whom this is his first feature-length documentary. Shin, a native of Cheung Chau who was also a regular at the Yat Tai diner, carefully captures how the people he treated like family faced the changing times and continued their daily lives. The film won the Best Documentary Award at the 29th Busan International Film Festival in 2024.
title_norm:日泰食堂: Set in a small diner on Cheung Chau, an outlying island of Hong Kong, this documentary observes a changing world through the islanders who gather there. title_norm:映画 それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星: The key word in the film 'Anpanman: Pantan and the Star of Promise' is 'promise.' The central character in this work is a new character, a red panda traveler named Pantan. Pantan embarks on a grand adventure to find a treasure said to be on the Rainbow Star shining in the night sky, in order to keep a precious promise made long ago with a certain adventurer! Along the way, Pantan meets Anpanman, Cream Panda, and other friends, and together they join forces to face one challenge after another! What kind of adventure awaits Pantan and the others? And will they be able to obtain the treasure...? Enjoy a thrilling, suspenseful, and epic story! Long ago, the red panda Pantan was traveling to keep a precious promise made with a certain adventurer. However, during the journey, he was hit by Baikinman's baby spray and turned into a child! Helped by Anpanman and the others, he tells everyone about the reason for his journey and his regret over breaking that important promise. Jam Uncle encourages him, saying, 'Isn't the important thing the feeling of wanting to keep a promise?' Renewing his resolve to 'keep the promise this time,' Pantan sets off for the Rainbow Star with Cream Panda. Cream Panda promises Pantan, 'I will never give up!' and joins the adventure, but is nearly discouraged by many crises. Meanwhile, Baikinman and his gang, who secretly boarded the plane, also come after the treasure... Pantan and the others keep trying, determined never to give up no matter what! When the Rainbow Star shines again, what they see at the promised place is... Can Pantan keep his promise this time? A story of precious promises and friendship.
title_norm:映画 デジモンアドベンチャー: The first theatrical film in the "Digimon" series. From a midnight computer screen, a strange creature named "Botamon" is born! While Tai is uneasy, his little sister Kari is overjoyed. Botamon evolves into Agumon! Suddenly, the Digital World, home to digital monsters, appears. A bird-like monster charges at Agumon. But then, another change occurs in Agumon's body... Evolution into the giant monster "Greymon" begins! Two colossal monsters clash—what will be the outcome of this fierce battle?
title_norm:映画『それいけ！アンパンマン パンタンと約束の星』: Pantan, a red panda, is traveling to keep a precious promise made with an adventurer. However, during the journey, he gets sprayed with Baikinman's baby spray and turns into a child! Pantan had long regretted breaking a promise in the past, but Uncle Jam encourages him, saying, 'What matters is the will to keep a promise.' Determined to keep the promise this time, he sets off with Cream Panda toward the Rainbow Star. When the Rainbow Star shines once more, what do they see at the promised place?
title_norm:映画史特別編 選ばれた瞬間: A special edition of the monumental video monument 'Histoire(s) du cinéma' by Jean-Luc Godard, the master of the French New Wave, re-edited by Godard himself. 'Histoire(s) du cinéma' is an epic work completed by Godard over ten years from 1988 to 1998, spanning 8 chapters and totaling 5 hours. This video art, weaving together a rich tapestry of images and sounds while freely quoting films, music, literature, and art from around the world that Godard loved, garnered significant attention, particularly in Europe. This film is a reconstruction of the original digital video version, re-edited by Godard in 2002 with new arguments and his unique perspective, and produced on 35mm film for theatrical release. It was given a special screening at the 58th Cannes Film Festival in 2005. In Japan, it will be screened in theaters for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
title_norm:春树:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.

Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

title_norm:昭和元禄落語心中 “与太郎放浪篇”ディレクターズカット版: Haruko Kumota’s popular manga series "Showa Genroku Rakugo Shinju," which explores the true nature and deep-seated karma of storytellers set against the backdrop of the Showa-era rakugo world, receives an animated adaptation. This theatrical release compiles the two-part original animation DVD (OAD) "Yotaro Wandering Arc"—previously bundled with the special editions of the manga’s 7th and 8th volumes—into a single feature, screening ahead of the January 2016 television broadcast. For its theatrical run, the film features newly enhanced sound effects, heightening the immersive atmosphere of the rakugo performances delivered by the characters on stage.
title_norm:是枝裕和初期tvドキュメンタリー作品集: A collection of TV documentaries researched and directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda during his time at Television Man Union. This program screens the first two works that Kore-eda himself has said 'directed my path afterward.'
title_norm:時々、私は考える:
Daisy Ridley (the "Star Wars" series) stars in and produces this human drama about an awkward woman who discovers the beauty of life through a new romance and connections with her colleagues.

Set in the quiet port town of Astoria, Oregon—famously known as the setting for "The Goonies"—the story follows Fran, a socially awkward woman who leads a solitary life, simply commuting between her office and her home. With no friends or romantic partners, her sole comfort lies in indulging in surreal daydreams of her own death. Her stagnant routine begins to slowly shift following a series of small interactions with a friendly new coworker named Robert. But even as her dates with Robert progress smoothly, Fran finds herself unable to break free from the emotional barriers holding her back.

Director Rachel Lambert, who was named one of IndieWire’s "28 Rising Female Directors to Watch" in 2023, brings this feature-length adaptation of Stephanie Abel Horowitz’s 2019 short film of the same name to the screen.
title_norm:時をかける少女: The first anime adaptation of Yasutaka Tsutsui's classic novel, previously adapted into TV dramas and films. A youth sci-fi drama depicting high school girl Makoto, who gains the power of "time leap" to travel to the past by chance, and realizes the preciousness of irreplaceable moments in life as she repeatedly redoes the past. Second-year high school student Makoto Konno gains the power to "time leap" back to the past after accidentally cracking a walnut found in the school science lab. Using this power, Makoto fully enjoys her carefree daily life, singing karaoke as much as she wants with her male friends Chiaki Mamiya and Kosuke Tsuda, and making spectacular plays in baseball. No matter what happens, she can go back in time and reset as many times as she wants. But this fun everyday life was supposed to continue... Directed by Mamoru Hosoda, who had worked on theatrical versions of "Digimon Adventure" and "ONE PIECE" and later became a leading Japanese animation director with films like "Summer Wars," "The Boy and the Beast," and "Mirai." Character design by Yoshiyuki Sadamoto ("Neon Genesis Evangelion"), animation production by Madhouse. Riisa Naka voices the protagonist Makoto, and Sachie Hara made her voice acting debut as Makoto's aunt, Kazuko Yoshiyama. Initially released in only 6 theaters in 2006, it gained popularity through word-of-mouth and achieved a long run exceeding 8 months. In 2021, it was re-released with the immersive 4DX system as part of a project commemorating the 10th anniversary of Hosoda's production company, Studio Chizu.

title_norm:曦曦: This documentary, the feature debut of Taiwanese director Wu Fan, captures the bond she forms with the unique Chinese dancer XiXi, whom she met by chance in Berlin, portraying the vibrant lives of two women. While studying in Europe from Taiwan, director Wu Fan meets XiXi, a Chinese contemporary dancer, in Berlin. Deeply drawn to XiXi, who dances like a free bird, Wu Fan begins filming her daily life. XiXi's journey, wandering Europe as a dancer in search of a free soul, appears beautiful to Wu Fan's eyes, like a wild bird unafraid to take flight. At the same time, XiXi lavishes love on her daughter Nina, whom she is allowed to see occasionally while staying in touch with her ex-husband Mederic. Eventually, Wu Fan's camera begins to capture the deep wounds hidden in XiXi's past. This becomes a catalyst for Wu Fan herself to confront her own family trauma. The film won the Emerging International Filmmaker Award at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival 2024.
title_norm:書を捨てよ町へ出よう: A grandmother who is a habitual shoplifter, a father who is a war criminal, and a sister with an obsessive love for rabbits. Raised in a dysfunctional family, "I" am always thinking of running away from home, while "he" is placed in a privileged environment. Burdened by a restless, pent-up passion with nowhere to go, "I" encounters strange people and wanders through a city where fantasy and memory blend together.
title_norm:最後通告: A 1998 fantasy film by Swiss filmmaker Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' and 'We, the Mountain People,' which allegorically depicts the mass disappearance of children. Through the form of fantasy, it portrays social issues still relevant today, such as the runaway collective psychology fueled by uncertain information and miscommunication within families. One morning after a full moon, ten-year-old children vanish across Switzerland: six boys and six girls, evenly selected from the four language regions. With police and media unable to find solid leads, the incident develops into an inexplicable situation. Reflecting the contradictions and anxieties lurking in society, the story moves toward the next full moon. Directed and written by Murer, with cinematography by Pio Corradi ('Höhenfeuer') and music by Mario Beretta. Starring Hanspeter Müller, Lilo Bauer, and Benedikt Freitag. It won the Grand Prix at the 1998 Montreal World Film Festival. Released in Japan in 2000, it will receive a special 35mm film screening in 2026 to coincide with the final Japanese screenings of Murer's documentary trilogy, the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
title_norm:月の犬:
Starring Masato Hagiwara, this noir drama depicts the existential despair of two men who would never have met if not for one woman taking an interest in them. Having failed to notice his long-time wife’s illness and living in regret after her death, Higashijima leaves the yakuza underworld behind. He drifts into an unfamiliar town and meets a woman named Saori at a bar. Intrigued by him, Saori begins to entrust him with work. Meanwhile, Minami, a member of a criminal organization, finds himself unable to endure the monotony of his daily life. Upon learning of Higashijima’s existence through Saori, Minami hopes the man will change the scenery of his world and assigns him to look after a young boy named Shogo. Higashijima carries out his duties in silence, but after discovering Shogo’s secret, he defies his orders and takes the boy outside...

Masato Hagiwara plays Higashijima, Tomoka Kurotani plays Saori, and Motoki Fukami plays Minami, supported by a cast including Soraji Shibuya, Kyosuke Yabe, Eriko Nakamura, Suzuka Ohgo, Hideko Hara, and Susumu Terajima. The film is directed by Kenji Yokoi, who won the
title_norm:月老: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
title_norm:月老〜また会う日まで〜: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. title_norm:未来: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
title_norm:東京物語: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic. Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
title_norm:栄光のバックホーム: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
title_norm:根本敬の映像夜間中学＜同窓会＞: Principal Nemoto continues to be active and well in the fields of manga, art, music, education, and others even after the school's closure. On the day, we plan to gather nostalgic footage along with new works, and spend a pleasant time watching them together with everyone. Of course, there will also be plenty of updates on Principal Nemoto's unusual current situation, as only a special manga artist can provide.
title_norm:欲望の翼: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."

title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第1巻「若鮎の巻」:
This is the first volume of an epic six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, that chronicles the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII from age 84 to 90. Nizaemon was a mainstay of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras. In 1987, as the "Wakaayu-no-kai"—a study group for young Kamigata Kabuki actors—prepared for its eighth independent performance, the camera follows Nizaemon XIII as he provides supervision and acting instruction. The featured plays are "Ichijo Okura Monogatari" from *Kiichi Hogen Sanryaku no Maki* and "Domomata" from *Keisei Hangonko*, with the film tracking the process from the rehearsal room to the final stage performance. The rehearsal footage captures Nizaemon meticulously instructing on every detail, from pronunciation to physical movement, conveying the raw intensity of the practice space. 

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The Ode to Hayachine*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第2巻「人と芸の巻 上巻」:
The second volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, recording the life of the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who supported the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This is the first half of the "The Man and His Art" segment, following Nizaemon over a four-year period from age 84 to 88, capturing his occasional discourses on his craft, his stage performances, and his daily life.

The film includes footage of rehearsals and performances from 1987, featuring "Numazu" from *Iga-goe Dochu Sugoroku* (Nakaza, Osaka), "Daimonjiya" from *Kamiko Jitate Ryomen Kagami* (National Theatre, Tokyo), and *Kotobuki Soga no Taimen* (Minamiza, Kyoto). The latter was a milestone performance marking his 35th consecutive appearance at the Minamiza’s *Kaomise* festival, and the camera captures Nizaemon as he receives commendations and interviews. Furthermore, it depicts his daily routine
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第3巻「人と芸の巻 中巻」:
The third volume of a monumental six-part documentary series totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, capturing the legendary actor Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—between the ages of 84 and 90. This is the middle installment of the "Man and Art" section, which turns the camera toward Nizaemon’s artistic discourse, stage performances, and personal life over a four-year period from age 84 to 88.

The film features his 1988 performances at Tokyo’s Kabuki-za, including the "Gakumonjo" and "Domyoji" scenes from *Sugawara Denju Tenarai Kagami* and the "Hanawatashi" scene from *Imoseyama Onna Teikin*. It further captures a "Gathering to Hear Artistic Talks" with his patrons; rehearsal footage for his role as Okina in *Kotobuki Shiki Sanbaso* for the opening of Omiya Sonic City; a gathering of supporters in Matsumoto, Nagano; reflections on a short story he wrote at age 23; his passion for trains; a scene of him plucking a shamisen at a Gion teahouse; and the Kataoka family’s Obon traditions.

The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, theatrical screenings have been rare, and because it has never been released on home video or streaming platforms, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will receive their first Japanese theatrical screening in 17 years.
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第4巻「人と芸の巻 下巻」: The fourth volume of a monumental six-part documentary totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, this film chronicles the life of the legendary actor Nizaemon Kataoka XIII—a pillar of the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. This installment serves as the second half of the "Man and His Art
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第5巻「孫右衛門の巻」: The fifth volume of a monumental six-part documentary, totaling 10 hours and 46 minutes, which captures the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—the legendary actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. The camera focuses on the rehearsals and stage performances of the "Fuin-giri" and "Ninokuchi-mura" scenes from *Koi Bikyaku Yamato Orai* (The Love Messenger on the Yamato Highway) held at the Kabukiza Theatre in Tokyo in 1989. During dress rehearsals, a red lamp was placed at the edge of the *hanamichi* runway to serve as a marker for Nizaemon, whose eyesight had weakened, yet he could no longer see even that guide. On stage, Nizaemon performed the role of Magoemon, with Kataoka Takao as Chubei and Nakamura Jakuemon as Umekawa. The beginning of this volume also includes interview footage from the 1988 publication of Nizaemon’s photo book *Fushi*, featuring the master himself alongside his sons Gato, Hidetaro, and Takao. The film is directed by Sumiko Haneda, a documentary filmmaker renowned for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer* and *The
title_norm:歌舞伎役者 片岡仁左衛門 第6巻「登仙の巻」:
The sixth volume of a comprehensive six-part, 10-hour and 46-minute documentary following the life of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII—a master actor who sustained the Kabuki world from the late Showa to early Heisei eras—from the age of 84 to 90. Capturing Nizaemon’s final years from age 88 to 90, the film records performances including "Sanmon" from *The Golden Gate and the Paulownia Crest* (1991, Minamiza, Kyoto), "Arakawa no Sakichi" from *Eight Views of Ryogoku* (1992, Minamiza), "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" from *The Treasury of Loyal Retainers of the Genroku Era* (1992, Misonoza, Nagoya), "The Carriage Pull" from *Sugawara and the Secrets of Calligraphy* (1992, Minamiza), *The Auspicious Sanbaso* (1993, Meijiza reopening, Tokyo), *The Felicitous Soga Confrontation* (1993, Meijiza), "The Inner Garden" from *Kiichi Hogen’s Book of Strategy* (1993, Minamiza), and his final stage appearance in "The State Barge on the Lake" from *The Eight-Array Guardian Castle* (1993, Minamiza), portraying a man dedicated to his craft until the very end. 

In the "Artistic Discussion" segment, he reflects on "Lord Tsunatoyo at the Mihama Pavilion" and recalls seeing Matsumoto Koshiro in "The Inner Garden" at the Imperial Theatre 70 years earlier. The film also features their 62nd wedding anniversary celebration and interviews with his wife, Kiyoko, his second daughter, Yuko, and his fifth daughter, Shizuka. Directed by Sumiko Haneda, known for works such as *Akiko: Portrait of a Dancer*. Due to its immense length, opportunities for theatrical screenings have been limited, and with no home video release or online streaming available, the film has long been difficult to view. However, in 2026, to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of Kataoka Nizaemon XIII’s passing and the centenary of director Sumiko Haneda’s birth, all six volumes will be screened in Japanese theaters for the first time in 17 years.
title_norm:歩いても 歩いても: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
title_norm:死ねばいいのに: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
title_norm:死亡遊戯で飯を食う。 44 cloudy beach: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
title_norm:死神バーバー: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
title_norm:残されたヘッドライン:
A documentary film compiling Japanese newsreel footage that has been lost to history. Behind the evolution of news from newspapers and radio into visual media were the "newsreels" once screened in cinemas. This work features a careful selection of footage across various fields filmed from the Meiji era to the early 1950s, with a primary focus on the early Showa period. Produced with the cooperation of Chunichi Eigasha—a company that created theatrical newsreels during the Showa era—the film weaves together culture, politics, entertainment, social customs, and incidents that have faded with time. 

Categorized into "War," "Disasters and Accidents," "Infrastructure," and "Culture and Customs," the film presents rare footage, including some being shown for the first time in Japan. Highlights include the threat of the dictator Hitler, a legendary snake-handling nude dancer, the enforcement of the Prostitution Prevention Act, and the personal effects, final letters, and hidden stories of the Kamikaze Special Attack Units. The narration is provided by Yuichi Mayama, the Nippon TV news anchor who brought the news into living rooms across the nation throughout the Showa and Heisei eras.
title_norm:殺しの分け前 ポイント・ブランク: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
title_norm:殺し屋1: A violent action film based on the popular manga of the same name by Hideo Yamamoto, directed by Takashi Miike. Set in a yakuza apartment building in Shinjuku's Kabukicho district, it depicts a surreal battle between insane men with thorough violence. The boss of the Anjo-gumi yakuza group, based in Kabukicho, suddenly disappears. Kakihara, a masochist who loved the violence given by the boss, persistently searches the city. Eventually, he learns of a hitman named Ichi, and upon witnessing his deranged killing style, feels an excitement akin to love. Tadanobu Asano plays Kakihara, with bleached hair and a face full of scars, and Nao Omori plays Ichi, a weak-willed man who turns into a crying killing machine. The cast includes Shinya Tsukamoto, Suzuki Matsuo, SABU, and Jun Kunimura. The screenplay is by Sakichi Sato, known for 'The Golden Grasslands.' A 4K remastered version will be re-released in May 2026.
title_norm:殺し屋のプロット: Directed by, starring, and produced by Michael Keaton, this crime noir follows an aging hitman losing his memory as he attempts one final perfect crime. John Knox is a contract killer with an unconventional past, holding two PhDs and having served as a former Army reconnaissance officer. Upon being diagnosed with a rapidly progressing form of dementia that will erase his memory within weeks, he resolves to retire from the trade. But just as he prepares to walk away, his estranged son, Miles, appears on his doorstep. Miles tearfully confesses to murdering the man who raped his daughter and begs his father to help cover up the crime. Racing against his own fading mind, Knox sets out to pull off one last perfect crime for the sake of his son. Alongside Keaton as Knox, the film stars Al Pacino as his confidant Xavier, Academy Award winner Marcia Gay Harden (Pollock) as his ex-wife Ruby, and James Marsden (X-Men series) as Miles.
title_norm:殺し屋１ ４k:
The boss of the Anjo-gumi has suddenly vanished, along with 300 million yen of the gang's funds. Kakihara (Tadanobu Asano), an ultimate masochist who lived for the violence inflicted upon him by his boss, believes the man has been abducted but is still alive, and begins a relentless search through Kabukicho. Eventually, he learns of the existence of a killer named Ichi (Nao Omori) and feels a thrill akin to love at the sight of his brutal handiwork. "I want to meet Ichi soon." "I want to taste the despair before I'm killed." Despite their paths crossing without meeting time and again, Kakihara’s heart races at the prospect of their encounter. Now, the moment of their meeting draws closer with every passing second...

*Screening in 2K at this theater.
title_norm:水俣一揆 一生を問う人々: Director Noriaki Tsuchimoto, who brought global attention to Minamata disease with *Minamata: The Victims and Their World*, returns to the subject in this feature-length documentary. On March 20, 1973, the Kumamoto District Court ruled in favor of the patients, ordering Chisso Corporation to pay damages and establishing its legal liability for the disaster. Following the verdict, direct negotiations unfolded at Chisso’s headquarters as patients sought compensation for lifelong medical care and living expenses. This film closely follows the actions of the patients involved in these talks. Utilizing synchronized sound recording, the film captures the raw intensity of the negotiations, providing a meticulous record of the patients' struggle.
title_norm:氷血: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area. The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
title_norm:汚れた英雄: The International A-Class 500cc final (All-Japan Road Race Championship, Round 8) is held at the UGO Circuit. The fateful showdown between bike racers Akio Kitano and Keishi Oki ends just before the finish line when Oki overtakes Kitano, pushing the decisive battle to the final round. Kitano uses his handsome looks and sexual prowess to secure funding from multiple patrons to maintain his team. When Christine Adams, heir to a billion-dollar fortune and owner of an international conglomerate, arrives in Japan, Kitano quickly approaches her and successfully secures funding. Finally, Kitano faces the final race, but...
title_norm:決断するとき: Starring Cillian Murphy of "Oppenheimer," this film adapts the bestselling novel "Small Things Like These" by Irish author Claire Keegan. Set against the backdrop of the real-life human rights abuses at Ireland's Magdalene laundries, it depicts the inner conflict and decision of a man who discovers a truth society has long ignored. In 1985, in a small Irish town, coal merchant Bill Furlong lives modestly with his family. One day before Christmas, while delivering coal to a local convent, a girl confined there begs him, "Please get me out of here." Confronted with the reality of young women suffering with no way out, Bill understands it would be wise to look the other way, but his conscience torments him, leading him to make a fateful decision. Emily Watson of "Breaking the Waves" plays the convent's Mother Superior, Sister Mary, winning the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival in 2024. Eileen Walsh of "The Magdalene Sisters" plays Bill's wife, Eileen. Murphy, who fell in love with the original novel, personally pushed for the film adaptation and served as a producer for the first time. Directed by Tim Mielants of "Peaky Blinders," the film also features Matt Damon as a producer and Ben Affleck as an executive producer.
title_norm:沓掛時次郎 遊侠一匹: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
title_norm:沖縄狂想曲: A documentary that spotlights various issues occurring in Okinawa, delving into the reality of Okinawa and Japan. Directed by Takafumi Ota, known for social issue works such as "The House of the Rising Sun" and "Documentary: The Battle of Okinawa - Unknown Memories of Sorrow," the film investigates numerous problems facing Okinawa, including the Henoko base issue, the International University helicopter crash, Osprey noise and crash incidents, as well as historical events like the Koza riot and the Yumiko-chan incident. Experts including former major newspaper editorial board members, prominent university professors, a former mayor, and former prefectural government executives thoroughly explain realities that major media cannot report. Furthermore, the film introduces the challenges of former Okinawa Governor Masahide Ota, the true intent behind former Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama's statement "at least outside the prefecture," and a parliamentary question by Taro Yamamoto of Reiwa Shinsengumi.
title_norm:沢田美由紀のガマランドにお邪魔します:
Set in the mysterious amusement park "Gamaland," this medium-length horror film employs a found-footage format to depict an inexplicable story surrounding Miyuki Sawada. Gamaland was a real-life location once symbolized by its iconic, giant toad statue. A VHS tape recorded there, steeped in the atmosphere of the early Heisei era, captures a date between a couple, Kohei Shimizu and Miyuki Sawada—but the footage gradually transforms into something deeply unsettling.

The film is directed by Koki Nishii, the filmmaker behind the YouTube channel "Filmest TV," which specializes in recreating modern subjects with a 1980s and 90s aesthetic. Nishii, who also made waves with the September 2024 YouTube drama *Tomochika Suspense Theater: Sotoyu Meguri Mystery - Dogo Striptease Girl Serial Murders*, served as screenwriter and editor, and appears in the film under the name "Nishii." The cast features Tsubasa Nakahara (Masashi Yamamoto’s *DUDE*) as Miyuki Sawada and Takeo Gozu (Netflix’s *Tokyo Swindlers*). The film is produced by NOTHING NEW, a label garnering attention for horror works such as *Chilled* (winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival), the short film anthology *NN4444*, and the medium-length horror *Shiki*.
title_norm:河内山宗俊: To save the daughter of an amazake shop owner from a dire situation, two rogues throw themselves into the fray. A masterpiece showcasing perfect chemistry between the renowned actors of Zenshinza and director Yamanaka. The beauty of a 15-year-old Setsuko Hara is captivating.
title_norm:河童のクゥと夏休み: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
title_norm:海よりもまだ深く: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together.
