Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
title_norm:海灘的一天: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title_norm:海街diary: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
title_norm:海辺のポーリーヌ: The third film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. It depicts the romantic entanglements of six men and women at a seaside villa, seen through the eyes of adolescent girl Pauline. Fifteen-year-old Pauline comes to Normandy for a vacation with her older cousin Marion. When they go to the beach, they meet Marion's ex-boyfriend Pierre. Pierre still harbors feelings for Marion, but Marion falls for Henri, a playboy acquaintance of Pierre's. Meanwhile, Pauline grows close to Sylvain, a boy windsurfing at the beach... The film won the Silver Bear and the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival.
title_norm:海辺の一日: Edward Yang × Christopher Doyle! A masterpiece heralding the dawn of Taiwanese New Cinema by these two guiding lights of world cinema!
title_norm:海辺の恋:
The 1963 feature debut of Guy Gilles—a director currently being rediscovered as a "forgotten master of the Nouvelle Vague"—is an autobiographical work that captures the fleeting love of youth. On a summer shore, Geneviève and Daniel, a sailor, find love in each other's arms. But when the vacation ends, he returns to the port city of Brest while she goes back to Paris. Hoping for a reunion, they continue to write to one another. Their story expands with the arrival of Guy, another sailor returning from the Algerian War, as the paths and emotions of the three quietly interweave. 

Starring Daniel Moosmann and Geneviève Thénier, the film also features director Guy Gilles himself as the sailor Guy, with a supporting cast of legendary actors including Jean-Pierre Léaud, Jean-Claude Brialy, Alain Delon, and Juliette Gréco. Impressed by Gilles’ 1959 short *Au biseau des baisers*, the master Jean-Pierre Melville provided partial funding for the film. A winner of the Critics’ Prize at the Locarno Film Festival, it will be released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
title_norm:消えない光: Screening at the "Finland Film Festival 2025" (November 8–14, 2025 / Eurospace, Tokyo). Screening at "EU Film Days 2026" (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Kinema Noi; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:済州島四・三事件 ハラン: Based on the 'Jeju April 3 Incident,' a massacre in which nearly 30,000 people are said to have been killed but which was covered up for a long time, this drama depicts the flight of a mother and daughter desperately trying to survive while being driven into a corner by unreasonable violence. On April 3, 1948, the 'Jeju April 3 Incident' began when some islanders on Jeju Island, opposed to interference by foreign forces, staged an armed uprising. From October of the same year, the government designated areas more than 5 kilometers from the coastline as 'hostile zones' and issued a proclamation stating, 'Anyone entering or leaving will be shot without condition.' To escape disaster, the villagers head for Hallasan Mountain, which rises in the center of Jeju Island. A-jin, a woman who has to leave the village temporarily, is extremely worried about her 6-year-old daughter Hye-sen, whom she left behind. Meanwhile, in the village, the South Korean army is mercilessly shooting the elderly. Surviving, Hye-sen heads into the mountains alone to find her mother. After miraculously reuniting, the mother and daughter embark on a life-or-death escape to survive. Directed and written by Ha Myeong-mi, who built her career as a screenwriter for commercial films, it vividly portrays the nameless people tossed about by state power. Kim Hyang-gi, known for 'Along with the Gods' and 'Innocent Witness,' stars as A-jin.
title_norm:火葬人: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title_norm:災 劇場版: A psychological suspense film directed, written, and edited by Yutaro Seki and Kentaro Hirase of the filmmaking collective "May," who gained domestic and international attention for their 2022 feature debut "Miyamatsu to Yamashita." It stars Kōji Yakusho, who also collaborated with them on that previous film. This is the theatrical version of the WOWOW drama series "Wazawai" (Disaster), broadcast from April to May 2025. It boldly restructures the six-episode series into a single film, depicting the calamity brought by a single man who infiltrates the everyday lives of six unrelated people. A high school girl troubled by family and her future, a deliveryman with a past, a shopping mall cleaner and a barber, the manager of a debt-ridden inn, and an ordinary housewife. The modest daily lives of these six people are suddenly struck by inexplicable disasters. The police dismiss them all as suicides or accidents, but Detective Dōmoto senses something strange and pursues the truth. Lurking around the edges of these six disasters is a single man. Changing his personality and appearance, he appears before the six as completely different people, bringing calamity upon them. Detective Dōmoto is played by Anne Nakamura, his colleague by Pistol Takehara and Kaito Miyakuni, and the people struck by disaster by Sena Nakajima, Ryuhei Matsuda, Megumi Uchida, Shunki Fujiwara, Jiro (Shisonne), and Maki Sakai.
title_norm:炎のごとく: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
title_norm:炎上: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
title_norm:無こその存在 あるいは鮎子の人生:
A social drama depicting the darkness of a crumbling Japan through the story of a young woman living at the bottom of a stratified society who dreams of terrorism, and the mysterious Italian man who helps her. 

Ayuko Amami, a woman in her 20s, commits repeated acts of fraud and theft using matching apps. Her accomplice is Otoya Yamaguchi, whom she met on an app a year ago; they are "comrades in terrorism," a bond that is neither friendship nor romance. The two plan a large-scale terrorist attack targeting the Ministry of Finance, but unable to even find a route to acquire firearms, they continue their fraudulent activities. One day, they are caught in an undercover sting operation led by Detective Sasaki. While Otoya is arrested on the spot, Ayuko manages to escape. During her flight, she is rescued by Leo, a foreign tour guide who happens to be passing by. Upon learning of Ayuko’s terrorist plot, Leo introduces her to Manjiro Haruki, a high-profile wanted terrorist, but...

Ayumi Sakuma (Fast Break) stars as Ayuko, with Diego Martina—a multi-talented scholar of Japanese literature, translator, poet, and illustrator—playing Leo, and Naoya Serizawa (NHK’s Hanbun, Aoi) as Otoya. The film is written and directed by Gen Takahashi, known for works such as Confessions of a Dog and GOTH.
title_norm:焼け石と雨粒: The debut feature film by Director Yuya Kushida, a graduate of the Japan Institute of the Moving Image, completed in 2022. This coming-of-age drama draws on the director's own experiences of heartbreak to depict young people struggling to navigate unconventional relationships. Akira Ujita, a part-time worker, develops feelings for a clerk at a local supermarket, but unsure of how to handle his emotions, he begins stalking them. He reaches out to Satsuki, a high school classmate and art student, for advice, but finds himself gradually drawn to her instead. As Akira and Satsuki confront their pasts and their current realities, they grow closer, until a pivotal event occurs between them. The film stars Hiroki Sano, who gained recognition for his role in Kohei Igarashi's "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," which screened at the Venice International Film Festival. Although it received only a single theatrical screening following its completion in 2022, the film finally sees a full theatrical release in 2026, four years later.
title_norm:熊蟲萬壽無彊クマムシばんじゅ・きわみなし the spac: A documentary focusing on the theme of "life strategies," examining how life forms adapt by changing themselves in response to their environment. Tardigrades survive extreme environments. The Okinawa ruby goby changes sex within its society. Ginkgo biloba creates a "sea" within its seeds to nurture swimming sperm. These life forms have persisted by employing strategies of self-transformation in tune with their surroundings. This feature-length film weaves together three subjects into a single narrative, revealing their quiet wisdom. It integrates the short documentary "The Space Bears 4 Ever: Life Strategies"—which records the daily lives, feeding, molting, reproduction, and cryptobiosis of three species of tardigrades living in moss on roadsides in Tokyo and Chiba—with two other short documentaries produced by the same team (cinematography by Tsuneya Taniguchi, directed by Yuki Suzuki, produced by Kazuo Okada): "Sex Change: Society and Sex Reversal in the Okinawa Ruby Goby" and "The Sea Within the Seed: Ginkgo Sperm and the Reproductive Evolution of Plants."
title_norm:熱狂をこえて: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
title_norm:牛乳屋フランキー: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
title_norm:特急にっぽん: Aboard an express train from Tokyo to Osaka, waitress Sayoko (Dan) pressures kitchen assistant Kiichi (Frankie) to marry her. An adaptation of a popular novel by Bunroku Shishi, this ensemble comedy depicts the chaos stirred up by a group of eccentric passengers sharing the dining car.
title_norm:犬王: A feature-length musical anime directed by Masaaki Yuasa (*Lu Over the Wall*), adapting Hideo Furukawa’s novel *Tales of the Heike: Inu-Oh*, which was modeled after the real-life Noh performer Inu-Oh who flourished during the Nanboku-cho and Muromachi periods. In the capital of Kyoto, a child is born into the Hiei-za family of Omi Sarugaku. This child would grow up to be the Noh performer Inu-Oh, who would later drive the masses into a frenzy, but his physical form is so bizarre that the adults cover his body in clothing and hide his face behind a mask. One day, Inu-Oh meets Tomona, a blind boy and biwa priest. Bound by a firm friendship as business partners to survive the world, the two unleash their respective talents and produce a string of hits. As Inu-Oh captivates audiences on stage, he transforms a part of his body with every performance, gradually attaining a singular beauty. The film features character designs by Taiyo Matsumoto, the manga artist of *Ping Pong* (which Yuasa previously adapted), and a screenplay by Akiko Nogi (*I Am a Hero*).
title_norm:犬神家の一族: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
title_norm:猫を放つ: A love story that interweaves past and present, depicting the current state of a drifting married couple and a reunion with a friend that stirs up past memories. This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:田園に死す: An autobiographical work written and directed by Shuji Terayama, adapting his own poetry collection of the same name. In a village at the foot of Mount Osore in Aomori Prefecture, a young boy, 'I', lives with his mother in an old house after losing his father. The boy's only solace is having an itako (a spirit medium) summon his father's spirit to talk to him. A beautiful woman who marries into the neighboring house and a circus troupe that comes to the village tempt the boy to run away from home. Later, 'I' grows up, moves to Tokyo, becomes middle-aged, and makes a film. Before this 'I' appears the boy he once was... Kantaro Suga, known for 'Thirteen Assassins' and others, plays the lead, and Kaoru Yachigusa plays the neighbor's wife.
title_norm:白い車に乗った女:
A suspense thriller marking the first collaboration between Jung Ryeo-won (*My Lovely Sam Soon*) and Lee Jung-eun (*Parasite*). The film depicts the course of a mysterious murder case in a snow-covered rural town through an unpredictable and original narrative.

At dawn, a writer named Do-gyeong arrives at a hospital with an unconscious woman in her car. When police officer Hyeon-ju questions the distraught Do-gyeong, she claims the woman is her sister and that they were fleeing from her sister's violent fiancé. However, it is soon revealed that the two are complete strangers, and the man alleged to be the fiancé is found dead in the snow. As the credibility of Do-gyeong's testimony is called into question, Hyeon-ju struggles to uncover the truth behind the incident, but...

Jung Ryeo-won plays the writer Do-gyeong, who holds the key to the case, winning the Korean Fantastic Actor Award at the 26th Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival in 2022 for her performance. Lee Jung-eun plays Hyeon-ju, a police officer who must confront her own trauma while conducting the investigation. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Ko Hye-jin.
title_norm:白夜: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
title_norm:白夜（1971）:
Following his 1969 film "A Gentle Woman," French master Robert Bresson directed this drama, adapting a short story by the literary giant Dostoevsky. Jacques, a lonely young painter, spends his days fantasizing about meeting his ideal woman and recording his thoughts into a tape recorder. One night, on the Pont Neuf bridge over the Seine, he encounters Marthe, a beautiful woman with a look of despair. Marthe explains that her lover left to study in America a year ago, promising to meet her in a year's time once he was in a position to marry; however, a year has passed, and he has failed to appear. Harboring passionate feelings for Marthe, Jacques does everything he can to help her reunite with her promised lover, yet the man does not show. Before long, Marthe’s heart also begins to be drawn toward Jacques.

The setting has been moved from the 19th-century Petersburg of the original story to the Paris of the time of filming. In Japan, the film was first released in theaters in 1978, followed by a 35mm new print release in 2012. A 4K restored version will receive a revival release in 2025, with another revival scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpieces Selection."
title_norm:白衣の男: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
title_norm:看我今天怎麼說: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:真実: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
title_norm:真田風雲録: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
title_norm:真空地帯: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
title_norm:眩暈 vertigo: January 2020, just before the coronavirus envelops New York. Poet Gozo Yoshimasu traces the traces of his ally Jonas Mekas (1922–2019), the father of avant-garde cinema, in Manhattan and Brooklyn on the first anniversary of his death, a friendship that had continued since 1985. Wartime study notes left in the studio, a 1945 passport, personal effects arranged by his son Sebastian. In a corner of the bedroom, Yoshimasu becomes dizzy and collapses. Early in the morning of January 23rd, the anniversary of his death, a memorial poem is completed in an instant. Crossing the bridge to the office. Yoshimasu reads it aloud to the waiting Sebastian. Then, a long silence falls.
title_norm:石井ふく子 100歳 心のドラマの軌跡:
A documentary focusing on producer and director Fukuko Ishii, the visionary behind legendary TV dramas such as *Onna to Misoshiru*, *Kimottama Kaasan*, and *Wataru Seken wa Oni Bakari*, who will celebrate her 100th birthday in September 2026. By partnering with screenwriters like Sugako Hashida and Yumie Hiraiwa, Ishii produced a string of masterpieces and established the "home drama" genre in Japan.

As the world’s oldest active producer, Ishii continues to create new works to this day. In her own words, she shares the origins of her creativity, the untold stories behind her classic hits, and her life in the present as she remains at the forefront of the industry. Through an extensive interview and rare archival footage, the film explores her creative philosophy.

Directed by Daiki Sai (*Hinomaru: 40 Years After Shuji Terayama’s Provocation*, *Ride the Ark: The Truth of Jesus’ Ark 45 Years Later*). The film will be screened as part of the "3rd TBS Retrospective Film Festival: Fukuko Ishii Special" (starting May 22, 2026, at Morc Asagaya and other venues), a festival dedicated to the digital restoration and theatrical release of precious films from the TBS archives.
title_norm:砂丘: Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, who won top prizes at all three major film festivals (Berlin, Venice, Cannes) in the 1960s, made this film after moving to America in 1970. Set in Los Angeles and Death Valley, it depicts the psychological landscape of love between a man and a woman. In the late 1960s, amidst the peak of counterculture, with university protests raging and students clashing with armed police, Mark grows tired of futile debates at student gatherings. He grabs a gun and confronts the police officers cracking down on campus, but misses his chance to fire and flees. He then steals a Cessna at an airfield and takes to the sky. Meanwhile, Daria, a secretary at a Los Angeles real estate company, is driving across the vast desert to attend a meeting. The two meet by chance and arrive at Zabriskie Point, overlooking Death Valley... The leads are newcomers Mark Frechette and Daria Halprin, whom Antonioni scouted on the streets. The soundtrack effectively features music by Pink Floyd, Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, Kaleidoscope, John Fahey, The Rolling Stones, and The Youngbloods. Released in Japan in 1970, it also had a late-show release in 1996. A revival release is scheduled for 2026, the first in 30 years.
title_norm:破·地獄: A human drama reuniting Hong Kong comedy king Michael Hui, popular in Japan for the 'Mr. Boo!' series, and Dayo Wong, a top Hong Kong comedian and actor ('A Witness Out of the Blue'), after 32 years. It became a massive hit, breaking Hong Kong's all-time box office record. Set in Hong Kong's funeral industry, it carefully explores universal themes of family, tradition, and views on life and death. Wedding planner To-sang, burdened with debt from the pandemic, reluctantly switches to the funeral business but faces difficulties as weddings and funerals are vastly different. To-sang, focused on profit, constantly clashes with the strict Taoist priest Master Man, who values tradition. However, as To-sang interacts with Master Man and his daughter Man-yuet, his resentment gradually fades. He begins to understand the true meaning of the traditional Taoist ritual 'Breaking Hell' that Master Man performs at funerals. Dayo Wong plays funeral director To-sang, and Michael Hui plays Taoist Master Man. Director Anselm Chan, a screenwriter making his third feature, helmed the film. It won five awards at the 43rd Hong Kong Film Awards in 2025, including Best Actress (Michelle Wai). At the 37th Tokyo International Film Festival's World Focus section, a 126-minute version was screened under the title 'The Last Dance'. The theatrical release is a 140-minute director's cut.
title_norm:祝山: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
title_norm:祝（ほうり）の島: Iwaishima, located in Kaminoseki, Yamaguchi Prefecture, is a beautiful island in the Seto Inland Sea with a population of approximately 500. In 1982, a plan emerged to build a nuclear power plant just four kilometers across from the island, sparking an opposition movement that the residents have maintained for 28 years. This documentary explores the fundamental nature of humanity and society through the daily lives of the islanders. Produced by Seiichi Motohashi, director of *Alexei and the Spring*, the film marks the theatrical debut of director Aya Hanabusa.
title_norm:神と恩送り、:
Starring former AKB48 and HKT48 member Chiyori Nakanishi alongside Saeri Umehara, known for her work in stage plays such as *Assault Lily* and *Towatsugai*, this hopeful drama is set in Tokyo’s Adachi Ward and the town of Kyonan in Chiba Prefecture. It depicts the way people forge connections even amidst misunderstandings and heartache.

Saori, a 26-year-old temporary worker in Tokyo, feels increasingly suffocated by the pressures of her job and personal relationships. One day, while preparing a surprise gift for a loved one’s birthday, she is confronted by their betrayal. On the verge of an emotional breakdown, she stops by an izakaya and meets Miumi, a young woman working there part-time. This chance encounter begins to spark a gradual change in Saori’s life. Having been estranged from her family for years, Saori must confront deep-seated tensions; spurred by her mother’s illness, she begins to face her past and herself with Miumi by her side.

The film was created by actor and director Hayato Otoki, in collaboration with actor and choreographer Keiko Matsumoto and musician Yosuke Saigo. Conceived as a sequel to their short drama *Around 30 Woman, God, and a Roommate*, the work blends dance, drama, and music to weave a story that speaks to the pain and hope inherent in modern life.
title_norm:神龍小虎闖江湖: In the late Qing dynasty, the villainous Im Kun-ho rules over Gold Sand Village, a place rife with all kinds of crime and violence, including drugs and human trafficking. The Dragon group, traveling while punishing evil, and at the same time, the legendary female martial artist Eagle, arrive in this village. They are both searching for a treasure called the 'Silver Pearl', said to have been stolen from a Tibetan temple. Then, the ruthless killer karate practitioner Black Jaguar also appears, and fierce battles unfold among the powerful fighters over the Silver Pearl. This is the Japan comeback film for Yasuaki Kurata, who was active primarily in Hong Kong.
title_norm:私たちの一日: The 30th feature film by Korean master Hong Sang-soo, who continues to release works in his unique style, distanced from large-scale commercial cinema. It depicts a day in the lives of a resting actor and an elderly poet living in seclusion, whose paths almost cross but never quite do. Sang-won, an actor on hiatus staying at a friend's house, and Hong Ui-ju, an elderly poet living alone in a small apartment, receive visits from young guests burdened with anxiety about the future, who ask various questions: What is necessary for acting? How does one become an actor or poet? Why did you start writing poetry? The topics the young people raise gradually develop into important conversations about life. Meanwhile, a friend's cat suddenly goes missing... Through two alternating locations and times, and the comedic dialogue that unfolds, the film discovers dramatic moments hidden in everyday life. Kim Min-hee, an indispensable presence in Hong Sang-soo's works, plays the actor Sang-won, and Ki Joo-bong, who won the Best Actor award at the Locarno International Film Festival for "Hotel by the River," plays the poet Hong Ui-ju. The film will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fourth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:私たちの話し方: A Hong Kong youth film vividly depicting the changes and growth of three young people with hearing impairments. Sophie, in her 20s, lost her hearing at age 3 and uses a cochlear implant to live a "normal" life as a "hearing person." Jason, born deaf, lives proudly as a sign language user. Alan, also a cochlear implant user, is bilingual in sign and spoken language. Jason and Alan met at a deaf school that banned sign language and promoted oral education; despite recognizing their different circumstances, they remained close friends into adulthood. When Alan and Sophie meet as ambassadors promoting cochlear implants, Jason becomes furious at Sophie's statement at a promotion event: "If science advances, there will be no deaf people in this world." John Shiuin, known for "Aspiring Lyricist" and "Kill the Twilight," plays Sophie and also wrote the lyrics for Panther Chan's theme song "What If." Directed by Adam Wong, highly acclaimed for "The Way We Dance" and "The Way We Keep Dancing." Won Best Leading Actress (John Shiuin) at the 61st Golden Horse Awards in 2024, and received a Special Mention at the 20th Osaka Asian Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:私は貝になりたい: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
title_norm:秘密の森の、その向こう: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
title_norm:空気人形: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
title_norm:立てば転ぶ: Set in a supermarket after closing, this film depicts complex human relationships through a continuous stream of idle chatter. Actor Jun Hosoi planned, directed, and starred in the project, with Nanami Hidaka also serving as planner and co-star. They are joined by a talented supporting cast including An Ogawa, Ryohei Higashino, and Seiichi Kohinata. The film won the Audience Award in the Japanese Short Film Competition at the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2024. Following a double Acting Award win (Jun Hosoi and Nanami Hidaka) and a positive reception at MOOSIC LAB 2025, the film has now been set for a one-week solo theatrical release.
title_norm:竜宮の誘い: A crime suspense film depicting a man consumed by a desire for cannibalism as he descends into the abyss of ruin. It won the Grand Prize at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, a first for a suspense film in the festival's history. Satō, a young man working as a host at a cabaret club, harbors a secret desire to eat people. One day, he finds a smartphone at work, which leads to him being threatened by a mysterious duo and forced into a dark side job as a courier. After making a large sum of money from the illegal but lucrative work, Satō begins to use his earnings to satisfy his hidden desires. Shun Tohari stars in his film debut as Satō. The film will be screened theatrically as part of the 'Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026.'
title_norm:第6回ジーンシアタースタジアム: GeneHeart Co., Ltd. operates "GeneTheater," a Japanese subscription service specializing in short films, and the mini-theater and independent film information site "Japanese Cinema Online," in addition to its theatrical distribution business. Launched in October 2025, "GeneTheater Stadium" screens three independent short films as a single program for a limited one-week run. Under the banner "Movies aren't just for watching. It's time to nurture them!", the project implements a new form of film screening centered on three keywords: "Audience Participation," "Discovering Your Favorites," and "Short Films."
title_norm:第五の騎士は恐怖: Set in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, this drama portrays the terror of an informant society during wartime. Dr. Braun, a Jew living in Nazi-occupied Czechoslovakia, is forbidden from practicing medicine. The elderly man seems to have already accepted the fate of the Jews. Then one day, a neighbor asks him to treat a wounded political fugitive, and he reluctantly provides care. Eventually confronting his inner self, Dr. Braun decides to continue illegal treatment for the resistance to reclaim his identity. He wanders the streets of Prague in search of the morphine needed for this, but... Through the various people Dr. Braun meets and the wartime cityscape, the film depicts a society decaying and collapsing under war with hallucinatory visual beauty. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
title_norm:箱の中の羊: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:約束の土地ziemia obiecana the prom: A masterpiece by the legendary Andrzej Wajda, this epic portrays the shifting of eras and generations through a portrait of ambitious youth. Based on the novel by Władysław Reymont, Wajda depicts the rise and fall of three young men in a film that was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and is considered one of the greatest landmarks in Polish cinema history. In the 19th-century industrial city of Łódź, Karol, Moryc, and Maks come from different backgrounds but share a common dream: to establish their own textile factory and seize control from the older generation. After a turbulent journey, they finally achieve success—only to find that the time has come to pay the price for their dreams...
title_norm:絞首台からの生還: On November 22, 1975, the South Korean government arrested Zainichi Koreans studying in the country on "suspicion of spying." 160 people were detained, and nine were sentenced to "death." Half a century has passed since then.
title_norm:給阿マ的情書 おばあちゃんへのラブレター: Ye, living a quiet old age in the southern Chinese town of Chaozhou, receives an unexpected visit. One day, her grandson Xiaowei, burdened with debt, secretly heads to Thailand without telling his grandmother. His goal is to find his grandfather, known as a 'legendary billionaire' who hasn't returned to his homeland in over 50 years, and borrow money from him. However, upon finally arriving, he learns that his grandfather has already passed away. Furthermore, the person with whom his grandmother had been exchanging love letters for decades turns out to be someone completely different. As Xiaowei pursues the truth, the family secrets sealed away for half a century gradually come to light.
title_norm:緋牡丹博徒 花札勝負: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
title_norm:緑の光線: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
title_norm:緑の山: A documentary by Swiss master director Fredi M. Murer, known for "Mountain Fire," investigating a planned radioactive waste disposal facility in the Alps. It follows both opponents and supporters among the residents trying to protect their roots and land. Murer dedicated this film "to the children and the children's children," posing questions to adults who should bear responsibility for the next generation. Along with "We Mountain People" and "Mountain Fire," it is considered part of the "Mountain Trilogy."
title_norm:總輯版 天兵童子: Based on the children's novel by Eiji Yoshikawa, this grand and magnificent adventure spectacle depicts the life of Tenpei Doji (So), a boy who boasts of having descended from the heavens, as he survives a turbulent era through training imposed by Bodaiji (Hara) and battles against rampant villains. Although this version has had its "lines glorifying feudalistic Emperor-centrism" removed post-war, traces of the wartime Imperial View of History remain visible. Director Shozo Kumita made his directorial debut under the name Kyoji Kumita with *Hungry Bushido* (1932). Following works such as the three-part serial action film *Maboroshi-jo* (1940) starring Kensaku Hara, he went on to work on television period dramas after the war.
title_norm:罗目的黄昏:
Winner of the Best Film Award in the Competition Section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival.

The traces of a lost lover, and a path that recedes the more you search—another time flowing through Luomu, an ancient town in Sichuan Province.

A postcard arrives from Wang, a lover who vanished without a trace three years ago, bearing only the words "Twilight in Luomu." Bai, who worked as a dancer in a theater troupe, follows this single clue to an inn in the ancient town of Luomu, Sichuan. There she meets Liu, the inn's proprietress; Huang, who has harbored feelings for Liu for twenty years; and a stream of passing travelers. In this town, once prosperous from trade and now flowing with quiet time, what she encounters is not Wang himself, but the traces of the time he left behind. The faint sound of a distant whistle echoes, and before Bai, who wanders the ancient town, Wang appears and disappears like a phantom. One day, Bai learns that a man resembling Wang was reportedly seen at a mountain temple—

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Chunshu," shot with the same cast prior to this work.
title_norm:罠 ドナウ川の守り人: Screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29, 2026 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at National Film Archive; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neue; also held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:罪の棘: A human drama depicting the conflicts and redemption of people burdened by past sins. It portrays the intersecting fates of individuals living in harsh realities as they confront their own transgressions. Directed by Hisashi Ueda, known for 'The Last Theatrical Version of Tokumei Kakarichō Tadano Hitoshi.' Erika, a former female inmate who lost her father at a young age and grew up without love, struggles to form relationships, trapped in a cycle of dependency and loneliness. She tends to cacti, believing their thorns are a survival mechanism for the dry, harsh desert, reflecting her view that human society is equally dry and brutal. Her parole officer is Iwanaga, a man who served time for a robbery 25 years ago and carries regret for someone he once failed to protect. He tries to support Erika. Meanwhile, Detective Tōdō, who lost his father in that same incident 25 years ago, suspects a link between the old case and a new series of robberies, relentlessly pursuing Iwanaga. Their three fates become intricately intertwined. Model Yabin stars in her film debut as Erika, with Tomohiro Waki as Iwanaga and Katsuya as Tōdō. Mami Yamazaki and Koichi Miura round out the supporting cast.
title_norm:罪人たち: A survival thriller directed by Ryan Coogler ('Black Panther,' 'Creed'), starring Michael B. Jordan, with whom Coogler has frequently collaborated on feature films. In the 1930s, in a devout small town in the American South, twin brothers Smoke and Stack open a dance hall in their former hometown, serving illegal alcohol and music in pursuit of a fortune. On opening night, the crowd revels in a night of swirling desires, but the arrival of uninvited guests changes everything. The dance hall is consumed by senseless despair, and a night of chaos beyond human comprehension begins. Jordan plays the dual role of the twin brothers. The cast includes Hailee Steinfeld ('Bumblebee'), Jack O'Connell ('Ferrari'), and Delroy Lindo ('Da 5 Bloods'). Coogler also wrote and produced the film, reuniting the 'Black Panther' team including production designer Hannah Beachler, composer Ludwig Göransson, and costume designer Ruth E. Carter. At the 98th Academy Awards, it received a record-tying 16 nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, winning four awards: Best Actor (Michael B. Jordan), Best Original Screenplay, Best Cinematography, and Best Original Score.
title_norm:羽織の大将: A new rakugo performer who jumps from his university comedy club into the world of rakugo and becomes an instant hit... This delightful and bittersweet film gently chronicles the hardships of training in the world of performance, unexpected success, and setbacks. The naturally gifted entertainer Frankie gives a superb and convincing portrayal of a storyteller.
title_norm:聴く隣人のいるところ: A documentary recording one year at a boarding high school. Christian Aishin High School, with a total student body of 34, is situated halfway up Mt. Asari Fuji in Gotsu City, Shimane Prefecture. In this secluded location, students live away from their parents, sharing their daily lives with their peers. While smartphones and the internet are absent from school life, they are surrounded by
title_norm:脛擦りの森:
An original work from the creative duo behind the *Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan* series, director Kazutaka Watanabe and star Issey Takahashi. Inspired by the "Sunekosuri" (shin-rubber) folklore of Okayama Prefecture, this film is set deep within a forest to tell a mysterious, beautiful, and cruel tale of love.

Deep in a forest far from civilization, a young man with an injured leg is led by a woman’s sweet singing voice to an ancient shrine. Living there are a mysterious man and his young, beautiful wife, Sayuri. Nursed back to health, the young man spends a dreamlike time where it feels as though time itself has stopped. These peaceful, repeating days seem as if they might last forever, but...

Director Watanabe personally visited the forests of Okayama, drawing inspiration from local legends to pen this original screenplay. Filming took place in the cities of Takahashi and Niimi in Okayama Prefecture. Issey Takahashi stars as the mysterious man, while rising star Nijiko Aoto, in her second film role, plays Sayuri, the mysterious woman living deep in the woods. Koudai Kurosaki, who garnered attention for his lead role in *The Miharashi Generation* (selected for the 78th Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight), portrays the injured young man who wanders into the forest.
title_norm:臨時増発 ミルキー☆サブウェイ 各駅停車劇場行き: A version of the theatrical film "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway: Local Train to the Theater" with new scenes added. "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway: Local Train to the Theater" is the theatrical adaptation of the short anime "Galaxy Express Milky☆Subway," which gained popularity for its surreal and lively developments featuring unique characters aboard a runaway galaxy express. It was released in theaters in February 2026, re-editing all 12 episodes broadcast and streamed from July 2025 with new scenes added. In "Special Extra Edition: Milky☆Subway Local Train to the Theater," a new post-credits scene is added after the ending. In addition to the standard 2D version, a 4D version was also produced.
title_norm:自然は君に何を語るのか: Korean master Hong Sang-soo, a multiple award-winner at the Berlin and Cannes film festivals, humorously and realistically depicts the irreparable failures caused by alcohol in this home drama centered on a young poet who ends up spending a day with his girlfriend's family. When poet Dong-ha escorts his girlfriend Juni home, he runs into her father at the front door and unexpectedly spends the day with her family. Initially awkward, Dong-ha gradually grows closer to Juni's family as they show him around their home and neighborhood and engage in conversation. Eventually, at dinner with the family, he drinks as urged, becomes intoxicated, and an uncomfortable atmosphere settles over the table. Ha Seong-guk, who previously played poets in Hong Sang-soo's "The Woman Who Ran" and "In Front of Your Face," takes on the role of Dong-ha, marking his first lead role in a Hong Sang-soo film. The parents welcoming their daughter's boyfriend are played by Hong Sang-soo regulars and real-life couple Kwon Hae-hyo and Cho Yun-hee. Kang So-yi ("In Front of Your Face," "By the Stream") plays Juni, and Park Mi-so ("Introduction") plays Juni's older sister. The film was selected for the competition section of the 75th Berlin International Film Festival in 2025. It will be released in theaters in 2026 as the fifth installment of "Monthly Hong Sang-soo," a project screening new works for five consecutive months to commemorate the director's 30th debut anniversary.
title_norm:花よりもなほ: In the 15th year of the Genroku era. A young samurai (Okada) burdened by the duty to avenge his father travels from Shinshu to Edo and hides out in a tenement slum. The film depicts how his resolve begins to waver as he interacts with the residents of the tenement. While weaving the story of the Ako Ronin's raid into the background, director Kore-eda turns it on its head, aiming for 'a story where the weak are affirmed as they are.' This ambitious work marks Kore-eda's first deep dive into a narrative world, having previously been conscious of the distance between fiction and nonfiction in his live-action films.
title_norm:花様年華: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
title_norm:花様年華 25周年特別版:
Wong Kar-wai’s masterpiece *In the Mood for Love* (2000) earned Tony Leung the Best Actor award at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival and became a massive hit upon its Japanese theatrical release in 2001. This year, as the film celebrates its 25th anniversary on March 31st, *In the Mood for Love* will be screened alongside the legendary short film *In the Mood for Love 2001*—previously shown only at a masterclass during the 2001 Cannes Film Festival—as the "In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition."

*In the Mood for Love* was originally conceived under the title "THREE STORIES ABOUT FOOD," intended as a trilogy depicting three different eras. Within this concept, *In the Mood for Love 2001* was positioned as the "dessert." While the two stars, Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, eventually saw *In the Mood for Love* evolve into a standalone feature film, *In the Mood for Love 2001* remained dormant, much like canned or frozen food.

Now, they "re-encounter each other across time, revealing a connection through this first meeting." The newly unveiled poster visual features Maggie Cheung from both films, contrasting her vermilion coat with a modern blue striped set-up. As the tagline "Drawn to each other, again and again" suggests, *In the Mood for Love* continues to captivate not only the original generation of fans but also younger audiences with every theatrical run. By encountering *In the Mood for Love 2001*, featuring the same cast, viewers can once again savor the story of two people drawn together by fate.

The accompanying trailer begins with the iconic image of Maggie Cheung turning toward the camera. It unfolds to the sound of Nat King Cole’s "Quizás, Quizás, Quizás," and just when it seems to end, a brief glimpse of *In the Mood for Love 2001* appears.

**【Film Overviews】**

**In the Mood for Love 4K**
A classical depiction of the emotional turmoil between a man and a woman, both married to others. 
Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, an editor for a local newspaper, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. Eventually, they realize their respective spouses are having an affair...
2000 / Hong Kong / Original Title: 花樣年華 / 98 min / 1.66:1 / Cantonese / 5.1ch / Japanese Subtitles: Sohei Okada

**In the Mood for Love 2001**
A postmodern tale capturing the moment love blossoms between a man and a woman. 
A convenience store owner finds himself drawn to a regular customer who often comes to buy cake to satisfy her hunger. A series of strange coincidences follow...
2001 / Hong Kong / Original Title: 花様年華2001 / 9 min / 1.66:1 / Cantonese / 5.1ch / Japanese Subtitles: Sohei Okada

Cast: Tony Leung, Maggie Cheung
Director, Writer, Producer: Wong Kar-wai
Cinematography: Christopher Doyle, Mark Lee Ping-bing

title_norm:花樣年華: A romantic drama directed by Wong Kar-wai of 'Days of Being Wild' and 'Happy Together,' starring Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, depicting the adulterous love between a married man and woman. Hong Kong, 1962. Chow, a newspaper editor, and Chan, a secretary at a trading company, move into the same apartment building on the same day and become neighbors. They soon discover their respective spouses are having an affair and begin spending time together. Hesitant yet strongly drawn to each other, Chow and Chan... Some settings and the worldview are carried over from 'Days of Being Wild,' and the story connects to the 2004 film '2046.' It won the Best Actor award and the Technical Grand Prize at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival. Released in Japanese theaters in 2001. In February 2018, it had a special screening at Bunkamura Le Cinéma alongside the digital remastered release of Wong Kar-wai's 'Days of Being Wild.' In August 2022, the 4K restored version was screened as part of 'WKW4K: Wong Kar-wai 4K.' In May 2026, a revival release titled 'In the Mood for Love 25th Anniversary Special Edition' is scheduled, screened simultaneously with the short film 'In the Mood for Love 2021.'
title_norm:花緑青が明ける日に: This animated film marks the feature directorial and screenwriting debut of Yoshitoshi Shinomiya, who has worked across genres primarily as a Nihonga (Japanese-style) painter. It is a Japan-France co-production with the cutting-edge French studio Miyu Productions. The 330-year-old Tategami Fireworks Factory, nestled in the woods, is facing eviction due to town redevelopment. Keitaro Tategami, who grew up there, has barricaded himself in the factory for four years, striving to complete the legendary "Shuhari" firework in place of his missing father, Eitaro. Meanwhile, Keitaro's childhood friend Kaoru Shikimori left their hometown for Tokyo after a past incident. Contacted by Keitaro's older brother Sentaro, who works at the city office, Kaoru visits the Tategami family on the last day of summer, the day before the eviction deadline, reuniting with Keitaro for the first time in four years. As they clash, trying to reclaim lost time and broken bonds, they hatch a surprising plan to uncover the secret of the phantom firework. The key lies in a beautiful blue pigment called "hanaryokusei" (copper acetoarsenite). Actors Rihito Noda and Kotone Furukawa make their voice acting debuts as Keitaro and Kaoru respectively, with voice actor Miyu Irino as Keitaro's brother Sentaro and actor Takashi Okabe as their father Eitaro. The film was selected for the Competition section of the 78th Berlin International Film Festival in 2026.
title_norm:芸術家、ただいま迷走中: Screened at EU Film Days 2026 (Tokyo: May 16–29 at Theater Image Forum, May 19–24 at the National Film Archive of Japan; Nagoya: June 6–19 at Nagoya Cinema Neu; also to be held in Hiroshima, Kyoto, and Fukuoka).
title_norm:華麗な関係: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
title_norm:落下音: Four girls from different eras, spanning from the 1910s to the present day, experience inexplicable events on a farm in northern Germany. A century-spanning visual epic where their anxieties resonate with one another.
title_norm:蒸発: A documentary co-directed by German filmmaker Andreas Hartmann and Berlin/Tokyo-based video artist Arata Mori, exploring the Japanese phenomenon of "evaporation" (disappearance). In Japan, approximately 80,000 people go missing each year, with thousands vanishing completely. Known as "evaporated people," their reasons range from relationship troubles and debt to yakuza threats. Some, with the help of so-called "night escape artists," abandon all ties and start new lives elsewhere. "Evaporation," intersecting deep loss and the hope of starting over, has been a motif in literature and film. This work uses immersive imagery to delve into the unknown work of "night escape artists" and the emotional conflicts and paths to reconciliation for both the disappeared and those left behind. It garnered attention at film festivals worldwide, winning Best Documentary at the 39th Munich International Documentary Film Festival.
title_norm:蘇える金狼: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
title_norm:蘇える金狼（1979）: A hard-boiled action film reuniting actor Yusaku Matsuda and director Toru Murakawa—the duo behind *The Most Dangerous Game* and *The Execution Game*—to adapt Haruhiko Oyabu’s novel of the same name. Tetsuya Asakura is a 29-year-old ordinary salaryman, but by night, he hones his physique at a boxing gym, driven by a burning ambition to seize control of Towa Yushi, the conglomerate where he is employed. After successfully robbing an armored car of 90 million yen, Asakura uses narcotics obtained during the money-laundering process to manipulate Kyoko, his boss’s mistress. Armed with Kyoko’s insider information on the company’s corrupt inner workings, Asakura begins eliminating his rivals one by one, but...
title_norm:街の灯（1931）: A timeless masterpiece written, directed by, and starring the King of Comedy, Charles Chaplin, depicting the struggles of a man who falls in love with a blind flower girl through a blend of humor and pathos. Defying the rising tide of "talkies," the film was intentionally produced as a sound film without dialogue. Charlie, a homeless and jobless tramp, falls for a blind girl selling flowers on a street corner. Mistaken for a wealthy gentleman, he attempts to earn money for her by working as a street sweeper and competing in boxing matches, but success is hard to come by. In the midst of his efforts, Charlie befriends a drunken millionaire and receives a large sum of money from him, but...
title_norm:裸の拍車: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
title_norm:西游记·女儿国: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
title_norm:西遊記 女人国の戦い: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. title_norm:西遊記 孫悟空 vs 白骨夫人: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.

title_norm:見はらし世代: Set in rapidly redeveloping Tokyo's Shibuya, this drama portrays the relationship between a father and son left behind after the mother's death. It marks the film debut of Koyo Kurozaki, who gained attention for his acting debut in the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie." This is the feature debut of Yuiga Dansuka, based on his original script; he previously directed the short "I Want to Go Far Away" as part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs' young filmmaker development project "ndjc (New Directions in Japanese Cinema)." Ren, a young man working as a Phalaenopsis orchid delivery driver in Shibuya, became estranged from his father, Hajime, a landscape designer, after losing his mother, Yumiko, as a child. One day, Ren coincidentally meets his father during a delivery and tells his sister Emi, but she remains indifferent, quietly preparing for her own wedding. Amidst this, Ren tries to reassess his distance from his family. Kurozaki plays the protagonist Ren, Kenichi Endo (an indispensable supporting actor in Japanese cinema) plays his father Hajime, Haru Ikewaki (active as an actress and model) plays the deceased mother Yumiko, and Maso Kuryu (a talented actress from "Chrysanthemum and Guillotine" and "The Lies of the Suzuki Family") plays his sister Emi. The film was selected for the Directors' Fortnight at the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
title_norm:親切なクムジャさん: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
title_norm:親密さ: Spanning approximately four hours, this feature-length work originated as a project for the acting course graduation at ENBU Seminar, a vocational school for film, theater, and actor training. It is composed of two parts: a narrative film depicting the process of creating a play titled "Intimacies," and a recording of the actual stage performance, with fiction and reality intertwining in each. With the premiere of their new production drawing near, directors Reiko and Ryohei find the limits of their collaborative partnership beginning to show...
title_norm:記憶の解凍: A film by director Anju Niwata from Hiroshima Prefecture, expressing her nine-year project "Memory Thawing" through documentary and animation. "Memory Thawing" recreates the "colors of memory" by colorizing black-and-white photos capturing daily life before and after the atomic bombing, combining dialogue with war survivors and AI technology. Through conversations based on the colorized photos, frozen sad memories transform into memories of happy pre-war daily life. The film conveys precious "narratives" from records of dialogues with over 30 people in Japan and abroad, including former residents of Nakajima-honmachi, a once-thriving entertainment district in the area now home to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park. The animation part depicts the protagonist Anji, who travels through time in a time machine to restore the colors of a lost everyday life. Director Niwata drew the illustrations for the animation part, which was produced under the supervision of Sunao Katabuchi, director of the animated film "In This Corner of the World," with participation from video artist Kenta Nomura and others. Composer and pianist Kanako Hara handled the music, composing the theme song "Heiwa Iro no Shashin" after visiting the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park and speaking with atomic bomb survivors. Director Niwata wrote the lyrics, and HIPPY, a singer-songwriter active in passing down the atomic bomb experience, performed the song.
title_norm:許されざる者: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.

title_norm:詩人iidabii ある宗教2世の記録: A documentary capturing the spoken-word poet iidabii, a so-called 'second-generation religious believer' raised under a specific faith, as he bares his past, wounds, and inner conflicts. iidabii unleashes the power of words and the cry of his soul with his entire being. Growing up in a religion practiced by his parents, he spent a childhood where even questioning was forbidden, until he encountered 'poetry.' For him, burdened with a complex background and a stutter, poetry became a weapon to shout his emotions in silence and a means to redefine himself. His poetry resonates deeply with those living on the fringes of society. This film records iidabii's life journey and creative process over three years, weaving a story about faith, family, language, and freedom. Directed by Matsui Shuhiro and Tsuda Tomomi, who have worked on numerous television documentary programs.
title_norm:誓い 建築家 b・v・ドーシ: A documentary about the world-renowned Indian architect Balkrishna Doshi. Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, who in 2018 became the first Indian to win the Pritzker Prize, considered the Nobel Prize of architecture, passed away in 2023 at the age of 95. Beginning his career under Le Corbusier in Paris in the 1950s, he oversaw the implementation of Corbusier's projects in Ahmedabad, western India, and later collaborated with Louis Kahn after India's independence. Influenced by Corbusier and Kahn, Doshi incorporated sustainable and ecological ideas into his architecture early on, establishing a unique style that fused modernism with Indian tradition, climate, and spirituality. He aimed for architecture that contributes to society and the environment, a 'people's architecture' rooted in daily life. This film delves into Doshi's inner world in his final years, visiting the buildings he collaborated on with Corbusier and Kahn, as well as his own works, as he discusses his architectural philosophy, creative process, and career spanning 70 years. Screened as part of the special program 'Le Corbusier and Doshi: Indian Modernism' (starting May 1, 2026, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other theaters nationwide).
