This is the feature-length directorial debut of Daisuke Shigayuki, who gained attention for short films like "Haru Mitai da" and "Madotachi," completed after a seven-year production period. Mori, a musician, is troubled by the distance he feels from his wife Maiko, a photographer. One day, Mori unexpectedly reunites with a former friend, Asako, rekindling old feelings for her. Asako also remembers being attracted to Mori in the past. However, their memories, tinged with expectations and desires, appear blurry, distorted, and conveniently rewritten in each of their minds. After a long walk, Mori and Asako reexamine their two lives that have already gone off track and the present moment they each stand in. Actor Soma Fujii, who also works as singer-songwriter "soma," stars as Mori and also handles the music. Ran Taniguchi (from "Hold Your Breath") plays Mori's wife Maiko, and Yukiho Murakami (from "August My Heaven") plays Mori's former friend Asako. The film was selected for the competition section of the 30th Busan International Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:1536538: A documentary tracing the final three and a half years of world-renowned musician Ryuichi Sakamoto, who passed away in March 2023. Based on the 2024 NHK documentary "Last Days: Ryuichi Sakamoto's Final Days," which garnered a significant public response, this film version incorporates new elements such as unfinished music and footage. Throughout his career, Sakamoto was a multifaceted artist who transcended boundaries between music, art, film, and literature. Centered on his personal diaries—where he meticulously recorded the sights and sounds of his life—and featuring rare private footage and portraits provided with the full cooperation of his family, the film reflects on his battle with cancer and the creative activities he pursued until the very end. Through casual daily musings, his struggles with mortality, and profound words on the nature of music, the film explores how this peerless musician faced the end of his life and what he sought to leave behind. It captures Sakamoto’s final days and his unwavering passion for creating the ideal sound he sought throughout his life, set against the beautiful natural sounds and landscapes that captivated him in his later years. Dancer and actor Min Tanaka, a close friend of Sakamoto, performs the readings of the diary entries.
tmdb:1537112:
A documentary by journalist Yasunori Kawakami, covering Palestine and Israel following the events of October 7, 2023. On that day, the militant group Hamas launched a cross-border attack from the Gaza Strip—a Palestinian territory blockaded by Israel’s "separation wall"—prompting the Israeli military to launch a devastating retaliatory offensive "beyond the wall." With the death toll exceeding 50,000, including more than 18,000 children, the situation is catastrophic, and as there are still no signs of a ceasefire, the number of victims continues to rise. 

Amidst conditions making it difficult for foreign journalists to enter Gaza, Director Kawakami traveled to the Palestinian West Bank—also separated by a wall—in July 2024 to conduct field reporting. Traveling from Bethlehem to Hebron and on to Masafer Yatta—the setting of the film *No Other Land*—he witnesses firsthand the destruction caused by Israeli military operations and the violence perpetrated by Jewish settlers. Meanwhile, on the Israeli side, while much of the public remains unaware of the devastation beyond the wall, three young people stand firm in their refusal to perform military service. By vividly capturing the realities on both sides of the wall, the film brings the complex background of the Israel-Palestine conflict into sharp focus.
tmdb:1537860: A feature film directed, planned, and starring Korean-born filmmaker Shin Chae-rin, created as her graduation project from the Kyoto University of Arts Film Department. Shot with a minimal production setup and incorporating documentary elements, it was screened at various film festivals, including being an invited work at the 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival and selected for the 47th Pia Film Festival. Rin, who came to Kyoto from Seoul, and Sora, who came to Kyoto from Okinawa, meet at university and aspire to make films. They give form to the impulses and desires that arise in their daily lives through the act of 'making a film.' Their relationship, which seeks to know each other through actions like sending jam sandwiches flying into the sky or tracing roots in Okinawa, continues to change. Shin Chae-rin plays Rin, and Sora Itami from Okinawa plays Sora, both also participating in the production. The film was made by a small team of five staff members, including the two actresses.
tmdb:1542261:
The 45th feature film in the beloved national anime series "Doraemon." This film is a remake of the fourth entry in the series, "Nobita and the Castle of the Undersea Devil," originally released in 1983.

During summer vacation, Nobita and his friends find themselves divided over where to go camping. At Doraemon's suggestion, they decide to set up camp in the middle of the ocean. Using secret gadgets like the "Underwater Buggy" and the "Adaptation Ray," they enjoy their time on the seabed. However, after discovering a sunken ship, they encounter a mysterious young man named El, who is revealed to be an undersea dweller from the "Mu Federation" that spans the ocean floor. The undersea people, who harbor a deep distrust of surface dwellers, are hesitant to trust Nobita and his friends. Meanwhile, news arrives that the "Castle of the Undersea Devil"—a place feared by all undersea people—has begun to move.

The film is directed by Tetsuo Yajima, known for his work on storyboards and direction for the "Doraemon" TV series and films, as well as "Pokémon the Movie: Secrets of the Jungle." Actress Airi Taira and the comedy duo "Alco & Peace" serve as promotional ambassadors and make guest voice appearances in the film. This installment also marks the first time a film in the series will be screened in 4D.
tmdb:1543797:
A mystery period drama based on the award-winning novel by Sayako Nagai—recipient of both the Naoki Prize and the Yamamoto Shugoro Prize—marking the first screen collaboration between Tasuku Emoto and Ken Watanabe.

Set in the Edo period, the story begins on a snowy night near the Morita-za theater in Kobikicho, where a beautiful youth named Kikunosuke successfully carries out a revenge killing to avenge his father. Witnessed by many, the event is hailed as a noble tale of justice. A year and a half later, a country samurai named Soichiro Kase, claiming to be a relative of Kikunosuke, arrives at the Morita-za seeking the full story of the incident. As he interviews those connected to Kikunosuke, the facts slowly unravel, eventually exposing a "secret" hidden beneath the surface of the revenge.

Tasuku Emoto stars as Soichiro Kase, the samurai pursuing the truth, while Ken Watanabe delivers a commanding performance as Kinji Shinoda, the head playwright at Morita-za who orchestrates the schemes within the theater. The ensemble cast features Kento Nagao (Naniwa Danshi) as Kikunosuke Ino, the young man who achieved his revenge; Kazuki Kitamura as Sakubee, the outlaw who killed Kikunosuke’s father; Koji Seto as Ippachi, a theater barker; Kenichi Takito as Yosaburo Sagara, the fight choreographer; Kazuya Takahashi as Hotaru Yoshizawa, an *onnagata* actor and costume manager; and Bokuzo Masana as Kyuzo, the prop master. The film is written and directed by Takashi Minamoto, known for the period drama *Chushingura Rhapsody No. 5: Nakamura Nakazo’s Rise to Fame* and the film *Until the Lights Come Back*.
tmdb:1544878: A film adaptation of the masterpiece novel "Slave of the Flesh" by the unconventional author Hideo Shirasaki. Adapted by Shinobu Hashimoto and directed by Yoshitaro Nomura, this ambitious and provocative work depicts the actions and ruin of a man who lives by cold calculation. Keiji Sada delivers a rare performance as a villain.
tmdb:1545621: The 29th theatrical film in the nationally hit series "Detective Conan", based on the manga by Gosho Aoyama. Conan, Ran, Sonoko, and Kogoro, along with motorcycle enthusiast Sera Masumi, encounter a mysterious black motorcycle speeding out of control while on their way to the "Kanagawa Motorcycle Festival" in Yokohama's Minato Mirai district. Kanagawa Prefectural Police traffic officer Hagiwara Chiharu chases the black bike but narrowly misses catching it. Conan and the others arrive at the festival venue, where a new white motorcycle called "Angel" equipped with cutting-edge technology is being unveiled. News then arrives that the runaway black bike has appeared in Tokyo. After evading the Metropolitan Police Department's pursuit, the black bike, whose body closely resembles the "Angel", is dubbed the "Black Angel" or "Lucifer", and the chase continues. In Chiharu's mind, memories of her younger brother Hagiwara Kenji and his colleague Matsuda Jinpei flash by. Hagiwara Chiharu, praised by Ran as the "Goddess of the Wind" for her driving skills, makes her first appearance in a theatrical film, engaging in intense motorcycle action against the mysterious black bike "Lucifer". Chiharu is voiced by Miyuki Sawashiro, who took over the role from Atsuko Tanaka, who passed away in August 2024. Guest voice actors Ryusei Yokohama and Mei Hata make their voice acting debuts. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, who handled direction for "Detective Conan: Black Iron Submarine".
tmdb:1548366: A documentary observing a 99-year-old woman and her son and daughter-in-law, who were affected by the Great East Japan Earthquake and the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster and live in disaster recovery public housing, over a three-year period from 2018 to 2021. Seven years after the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, a family forced to evacuate from Namie Town, Fukushima, wavers between returning to their hometown and choosing a new life. Having closed their long-running printing business due to the disaster and living in disaster recovery public housing in Iwaki City, the roles and relationships within the family quietly change. Tetsu, the 99-year-old mother, clings to memories of her birthplace, Okuma Town, even as her memory fades. Her taciturn son Takemasa respects his mother but leaves most of her care to his wife Shigeko. Shigeko, who has continued to bear this role, begins to reexamine her taken-for-granted position within the family and her own way of living. Through the family's daily life in flux, the film questions what "home" is and what "I" is. Directed by Toru Yamada, who has continued making films in Fukushima since the Great East Japan Earthquake.
tmdb:1548370: A documentary that observes people's lives and the present state of Fukushima through the dining tables of those living along National Route 6, commonly known as "Rokkoku," where areas still remain designated as difficult-to-return zones.
tmdb:1548626: This film traces the life of former professional baseball player Shintaro Yokota, who was drafted second by the Hanshin Tigers and expected to have a bright future, but was forced to retire at age 21 after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. It stars Taya Matsutani and Kyoka Suzuki. In the 2013 draft, 18-year-old Shintaro Yokota was selected second by the Hanshin Tigers. In the opening game of 2016, he was chosen as a starter for the first team and recorded his first hit, with everyone holding great expectations for his future. However, soon after, Shintaro began experiencing double vision. The doctor's diagnosis was a brain tumor, a harsh reality for a 21-year-old. Nevertheless, supported by his family, mentors, and teammates, Shintaro fought against his illness. At his retirement game in September 2019, he performed a miraculous throw home, moving the stadium to tears. But Shintaro's story didn't end there. Matsutani, a former high school baseball player, plays Yokota, and Suzuki plays his mother, Manami. The director is Jun Akiyama of "20 Years Old Soul."
tmdb:1548708: A live-action film adaptation of the hit comic by Yuto Suzuki, serialized in Shueisha's "Weekly Shonen Jump", starring Ren Meguro of "Snow Man". It comically depicts a legendary retired hitman running a small shop who throws himself into battle to protect his beloved family and peaceful daily life. Sakamoto Taro, once feared as the "strongest ever," falls in love at first sight with a woman named Aoi who works at a convenience store, and promptly retires from being a hitman. After marrying and having a daughter, he becomes the manager of a small shop called "Sakamoto Store" and enjoys a happy family life, having grown so fat that he no longer resembles his former self. One day, a 10 billion yen bounty is suddenly placed on Sakamoto, and assassins from all over the world attack him. With his former subordinate, the esper Shin, as his partner, Sakamoto rises to protect his peaceful daily life. Meguro uses special makeup to portray two contrasting versions of Sakamoto: a plump one weighing an estimated 140 kg and a sleek one who rapidly loses weight when he gets serious, and also takes on full-fledged action scenes. Takahashi Fumiya plays Sakamoto's partner Asakura Shin; Ueto Aya plays Sakamoto's wife Aoi; Yokota Mayuu plays Lu Shaotang, a tai chi expert working at Sakamoto Store with Shin; Tozuki Junki plays Masumo Heisuke, a skilled sniper; Kitamura Takumi plays Nagumo, a member of the hitman world's highest force "ORDER"; Yagi Yusei plays Kamigami; and Nemu Yumemi plays Daibutsu. Directed and written by Yuichi Fukuda of the "Gintama" series.
tmdb:1553969: A feature film directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda ("Monster", "Shoplifters"), starring Haruka Ayase and Daigo (from the comedy duo "Chidori"), based on an original script about a couple who welcome a humanoid in the form of their deceased son. Set in the near future. Architect Kōmoto Oto and her husband Kensuke, the second-generation president of a construction company, take in a humanoid resembling their son Sho, who died two years ago. On the day the humanoid arrives, Oto joyfully welcomes him with Sho's same smile and voice, while Kensuke hides his bewilderment behind a stiff expression. Family time gradually begins, but an unexpected event occurs, revealing the couple's hidden feelings about their son's death. Meanwhile, the humanoid Sho secretly starts connecting with other humanoids. The role of the deceased son Sho and his humanoid counterpart is played by Kuwaki Rito, chosen from over 200 auditionees. Kiyono Yasho plays Oto's younger sister Kotaki Arisu; Kanichiro plays Nikawa Gen, an employee at Kensuke's construction company Tamaken; Yo Kimiko plays Oto's mother Nishimura Nobuyo; and Tanaka Min plays Yamagata Akio, a skilled worker at Tamaken. The title "The Sheep in the Box" is derived from a passage in Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's classic novel "The Little Prince". The film was selected for the Competition section of the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
tmdb:155509: In Ueno just after Japan's defeat in the war. One day, a young man named Tetsu unexpectedly runs into Joshu Tora, who once taught him how to gamble. Led by Tora into the Chinchiro slums, Tetsu bets his last bit of money on a game run by Dosa Ken, a professional gambler. He wins a considerable amount, but most of it is taken by Dosa Ken as a coaching fee.
tmdb:1555229:
Winner of the Best Director Award and Best Actor Award in the Competition Section of the 38th Tokyo International Film Festival.

A woman who has lost her mother tongue returns home. Dreams, love, memories, and the time of cinema gently unravel—

Chunshu, 37, has lost her way as an aspiring actress and is stuck in her love life. Returning to Chengdu, her former hometown she left twenty years ago, she visits her old acting instructor, Zhang Mei. But Zhang Mei has dementia and is gradually losing her speech. Unable to find a place anywhere, Chunshu is quietly accompanied by Dongdong, Zhang Mei's son who has returned from Shanghai to care for his mother. Like the decaying national film studio that remains in ruins, past glories, teachings, and lessons are gradually forgotten in the flow of time, and days pass quietly beside people stuck in stagnation.

Released simultaneously with its sister film "Twilight in Luomu," shot consecutively with the same cast.
tmdb:1555231: A comedy about a prideful feud between a deaf Japanese family and a Kurdish family, told through Japanese Sign Language and Kurdish. Natsumi Koga lives with her deaf father and younger brother, who run an electronics shop. One day, their family gets into a minor conflict with a Kurdish family living in the same town. Natsumi, who can hear, and Hiwa, the only member of the Kurdish family who speaks Japanese, are drafted as interpreters for their respective families. As they interpret for each other, a bond of trust grows between Natsumi and Hiwa, but the conflict between the two families only deepens. Then one day, a mysterious drawing by Natsumi's younger brother Shun escalates into an incident that engulfs the entire town. Nagisa Nagashima of "The End of Love" plays the protagonist Natsumi. Kazuyoshi Kezuka, a deaf ramen shop owner in Tokyo's Nishi-Nippori, makes his acting debut as Natsumi's father. Hideaki Nasu of the TV drama "Deaf Voice: Court Sign Language Interpreter" and Akito Imai of "The Two Worlds of My Life" play the father's friends. Shunya Itabashi of "Laughing Kaibutsu" plays a community organizer planning a town revitalization project, and Karin Ono of "Animation x Paralympic: Who Is the Hero?" plays a teacher at a school for the deaf. The film is directed by Ken Kawai, known for works like "Nanno-chan's Second World War" and who is himself a CODA (Child of Deaf Adults).
tmdb:1556442: High school senior Misaki (Runa Nakashima) has no clear goals for her future. Living in a single-mother household and wanting to avoid burdening her parent, she decides against pursuing higher education, spending her final year of high school working part-time while planning to find a local job. Her best friend Satsuki (Maikichi) is aiming for university to satisfy her parents' wishes, but spends her days obsessed with social media. One day, a ghost-like figure is accidentally captured in a vlog Misaki filmed, and the video goes viral instantly. Seeing an opportunity, the two begin posting a series of fake paranormal videos. As the buzz grows, they start raking in ad revenue. Carried away, their filming escalates as they seek even greater thrills by sneaking into a local ruin rumored to be haunted. There, they finally capture something "real" that can never be undone. Furthermore, after praying to a Jizo statue on the way to the ruins, Misaki finds herself haunted by a "God" in traditional Japanese attire with a mask-like face—.
tmdb:1557893:
The second part of a two-part film project that serves as the culmination of the TV drama series "Kyojo" starring Takuya Kimura. While the first part, "Kyojo: Reunion," was released exclusively on Netflix, this sequel will be released in theaters. Set in "Kyojo," the academy for training future police officers, the film depicts instructor Kimichika Kazama (played by Kimura) confronting students burdened with various circumstances, as well as graduates who assemble to counter an ominous shadow closing in on Kazama.

The 205th class has been relentlessly put through the wringer by Kazama. As the darkness and secrets harbored by the students are exposed, some are forced to withdraw, yet Kazama’s scrutiny of the remaining students continues. Various dramas
tmdb:1559123: Based on the bestselling novel of the same name by Amone Nagatsuki, winner of the Shogakukan Bunko Novel Award Grand Prize, starring Minami Hamabe and Ren Meguro, directed by Takahiro Miki ("Ao Haru Ride," "Tomorrow I Will Date Yesterday's You"). It depicts a heroine who joins a funeral company and, together with her supervising funeral planner, aims to create the "best possible funeral." Misu Shimizu, struggling with job hunting, has a secret she can't tell anyone: she can hear the voices of the deceased. A fateful encounter changes her life when Reiji Urushibara, a funeral planner who notices her ability, invites her into the world of funeral planning. Guided by something, Misu becomes an intern at the funeral company "Bando Kaikan." Teaming up with Urushibara, she confronts the question "What is a funeral that satisfies not only the surviving family but also the deceased?" through various families' funerals, including a husband who lost his pregnant wife and a couple who lost their young daughter. Eventually, Misu comes to admire Urushibara's sincere dedication to the deceased and their families, and decides to pursue a career as a funeral planner herself. Hamabe plays Misu, Meguro plays Urushibara, with a stellar cast including Mochika Yamada, Ken Mitsuishi, Mirai Shida, Keisuke Watanabe, Kotone Furukawa, and Takumi Kitamura. The script is by Takuro Honda (drama "Lion's Snack"), supervised by Yoshikazu Okada, known for various hit works.
tmdb:1559125:
Director Eisuke Naito, who has sharply depicted the harsh realities and struggles of teenagers in films such as *Liverleaf* and *Forgiven Children*, presents a monster panic adventure set in the unique situation of young people caught in illegal "dark labor" facing off against a ferocious brown bear.

On the very day 18-year-old Osanai receives his university acceptance letter, his father commits suicide after falling victim to a specialized fraud scheme that left him with massive debt, forcing Osanai to abandon his plans for higher education. In his desperate search for money, Osanai finds himself stepping into the world of "dark labor"—the very underworld that drove his father to the brink. One day, Osanai participates in a kidnapping operation promising a high reward, only to find that the job has escalated to include the murder of the abducted woman and the disposal of her body. Just as they carry the woman into the forest and are about to commit the deed, an unprecedented situation occurs.

Fuku Suzuki stars as the protagonist Osanai, while Wan Marui (*Backfire*, *The Unknown Girl*) takes on her first action role as his highly skilled combat partner, Sakurako Wakabayashi. Additionally, Takashi Ukaji plays the key role of Hunter Kanzaki, and special effects/makeup artist Tomo Hyotake, who also worked on *Golden Kamuy*, handled the design of the brown bear.
tmdb:1559185:
Shunsuke Michieda (Naniwa Danshi) and director Takahiro Miki, who previously collaborated on "Even If This Love Disappears from the World Tonight," reunite for this love story based on the novel of the same name by Misaki Ichijo, the author of the original work. The film depicts a 10-year romance between a man and a woman who are drawn to each other through their time spent creating music together, even as they are buffeted by the whims of fate.

Haruto Mizushima is a high school student living an unremarkable life with a secret hobby of writing poetry. His secret is discovered by his classmate, Ayane Tosaka. While Ayane possesses a singing voice that captivates all who hear it, she struggles with developmental dyslexia, making it difficult for her to read and write. When Ayane asks Haruto to write lyrics for her, the two begin to grow closer while spending time alone in a clubroom after school making songs together, but...

Meru Nukumi, appearing alongside Michieda for the first time, plays the heroine. She makes her debut performance as a singer and guitarist after nearly a year of vocal training and guitar lessons. The screenplay is penned by Tomoko Yoshida ("Let Me Eat Your Pancreas"), with music production by Seiji Kameda ("Even If This Love Disappears from the World Tonight," "Threads - Our Tapestry of Love").
tmdb:1559189: Director Makoto Nagahisa, known for "We Are Little Zombies" and "And So We Put Goldfish in the Pool," casts Nana Mori in a drama set in Shinjuku's Kabukicho, depicting a "flame war" incident started by a girl. Born into a family of cult followers, Kobayashi Kurie is raised under strict discipline alongside her younger sister. The sisters pray to God daily for their painful days to end and for their education-obsessed father to disappear. Years later, their prayers are answered when their father dies, but their mother continues the harsh upbringing. Unable to bear it any longer, Kurie runs away from home, leaving her sister behind. Following a message on social media, she arrives at a square in Kabukicho where young people gather. There, she is given the name "Juju," a place to sleep, food, a smartphone, and a job. Experiencing the world for the first time and meeting various people, she finally begins to develop her own will. She dreams of taking her sister away from their mother and living together, but... Nagahisa wrote the original script and filmed on location in Kabukicho, capturing the raw reality of the neighborhood and the young people living there. Mori plays the protagonist Kurie, with Aoi Yamada ("Perfect Days"), Ryosuke Soda ("The Liar and His Lover"), and Wataru Ichinose (Netflix's "Sanctuary") co-starring.
tmdb:1561: Master filmmaker Robert Bresson's eighth feature, made right after his masterpiece "Au Hasard Balthazar." Based on a novel by French author Georges Bernanos, it starkly and realistically depicts the tragic fate of a young girl through rigorous framing and the actors' minimally restrained performances. 14-year-old Mouchette lives in the French countryside, forced to run the household for her alcoholic father and ill mother, while being cruelly treated by classmates and teachers at school. The unfortunate girl's fate takes a turn for the worse when, one rainy night, she encounters a poacher in the forest, sending her spiraling into further misery and ruin. Nadine Nortier, discovered for this role, plays the protagonist Mouchette, a girl standing on the brink of despair yet harboring a rebellious spirit. Produced in 1967, it was first released in Japan in 1974 by Equipe de Cinema, and again in 1995 by France Eiga Sha. A 4K restored digital remastered version had a revival release in October 2020. Another revival release is scheduled for 2026 as part of the "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
tmdb:1561767:
Masaharu Fukuyama directs his second live film, capturing the "Great Freedom" free concert held in his hometown of Nagasaki in October 2024.

On October 13, 2024, the Japanet Group presented "Great Freedom" as the grand opening performance for Nagasaki Stadium City. From over 530,000 applicants, 25,000 fans gathered at the main venue in a whirlwind of excitement. Combined with free broadcasts at adjacent sites and live viewings hosted by municipalities across Nagasaki Prefecture, more than 310,000 people witnessed the historic event.

Fukuyama himself supervised every aspect of the production, including the direction, visuals, and sound. Captured from a 360-degree perspective using 52 cameras, the performance has been reconstructed for the cinema with cutting-edge audio technology and stunning visual beauty, bringing the immersive atmosphere of the venue to the big screen. Centered on the concert footage performed under the moonlight, the film weaves an emotional narrative by interspersing scenes of Fukuyama’s childhood—a time before he had even begun to dream of his future.

Following the previous film, *FUKUYAMA MASAHARU LIVE FILM: Kotodama no Sakiwau Natsu @ NIPPON BUDOUKAN 2023*, actor Hinata Hiiragi—who played the younger version of Fukuyama’s character in the TV drama *Last Man: The Blind Investigator*—returns to portray the artist in his youth.
tmdb:1566225: An adaptation of the 2022 bestselling mystery novel "Your Quiz" by Naoki Prize-winning author Satoshi Ogawa. The stage is the grand finale of "Q-1 Grand Prix," a live quiz show with a 10-million-yen prize. As the nation watches with bated breath, Reo Mishima, the "Absolute King of Quizzes," and Kizuna Honjo, "The Man Who Saved the World in His Head," are both one step away from victory. On the final buzzer question, Honjo presses his button before a single character of the question has even been read. To the shock of the audience, he correctly identifies the answer and claims the championship. Unable to hide his bewilderment at this impossible feat, Mishima launches his own investigation to uncover how Honjo achieved a "zero-character correct answer." Tomoya Nakamura stars as the protagonist Reo Mishima, a man of vast knowledge and logical thinking; Ryunosuke Kamiki portrays the enigmatic genius player Kizuna Honjo; and Tsuyoshi Muro plays Yasuhiko Sakata, the show’s producer who will stop at nothing to create a spectacle. Directed by Kohei Yoshino (*Anime Supremacy!*, *The Silent Service*), the film utilizes stylish VFX to depict the labyrinthine thought processes unfolding within a quiz player's mind.
tmdb:1568452: Akiko joins the Hinomaru University American football team as a manager to be near her crush, Yoshioka. However, under the direction of their advisor, Sawada, the team repeatedly resorts to dangerous plays during games, resulting in a suspension. To make matters worse, Captain Hirayama informs her that Yoshioka has died in an on-field accident, driving Akiko to despair. Spurred by his death, Akiko resolves to become a player herself and throws herself into grueling training. Meanwhile, Saori, a detective from the Josai Police Station, uncovers a grave secret involving the team and a former member named Sasaki.
tmdb:1568457:
Even as an adult, she doesn't want to go to school... Even as an adult, she's in the middle of a rebellious phase... Eriko is a middle school teacher who can't gain independence from her parents. Meanwhile, Chika is a "truant for unknown reasons" who wears the mask of a mature adult—she excels at her studies, has friends, and shows no signs of delinquency. The two are teacher and student at the same school, but they share one thing in common: neither can leave their room.

One day, Eriko lists her favorite BL manga for sale online and hits it off with a girl named "Chi." That girl is Chika. Unaware of each other's true identities, they exchange messages on social media, eventually becoming close friends who can share their deepest secrets. As they try to step out of their rooms and face their parents and school together, the "truth behind Chika's truancy" and Eriko's "past wounds" corner them, and the world around them begins to shift in an unexpected direction—
tmdb:1569763: A crime suspense film depicting a man consumed by a desire for cannibalism as he descends into the abyss of ruin. It won the Grand Prize at the 19th Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival, a first for a suspense film in the festival's history. Satō, a young man working as a host at a cabaret club, harbors a secret desire to eat people. One day, he finds a smartphone at work, which leads to him being threatened by a mysterious duo and forced into a dark side job as a courier. After making a large sum of money from the illegal but lucrative work, Satō begins to use his earnings to satisfy his hidden desires. Shun Tohari stars in his film debut as Satō. The film will be screened theatrically as part of the 'Tanabe-Benkei Film Festival Selection 2026.'
tmdb:1576370: This documentary film was produced as the culmination of the anniversary year for Tohoshinki, the South Korean male vocal unit celebrating the 20th anniversary of their Japanese debut in 2025. Having debuted in Korea in 2004, Tohoshinki has continued to thrive on the global stage as representative artists of Asia. In Japan, they have enjoyed immense popularity since their debut in April 2005. Their "Tohoshinki 20th Anniversary LIVE TOUR ~ZONE~," held from November 2024 to April 2025 leading up to their milestone anniversary, drew approximately 350,000 fans across 22 performances in nine cities. Three of these shows were held at the Tokyo Dome, breaking their own record for the most performances at the venue by a foreign artist. This film captures Yunho and Changmin as they continue to venture into unprecedented territory, delving into the very heart of their identity.
tmdb:1580162: A horror film directed by Yoshizo Sakai of "Fictional" and "Counselor," planned and produced by Tokio Omori, a TV Tokyo producer who brought forth "The Missing Exhibit" and "Searching for Kikue Ishinaga." Rio Yamashita, who starred in the 2025 long-running hit "Yukiko a.k.a." primarily in mini-theaters over about a year, plays the lead role of a woman tormented by paranoid fear through caring for her mother. After her father's death, Kana returns to her childhood home and begins caring for her mother, who has dementia. She devotes herself to caregiving as if trying to reclaim time with her mother, but her mother's inexplicable behavior gradually becomes increasingly bizarre, and Kana begins to feel uneasy about strange occurrences around her. Eventually, possessed by the sensation that something has entered her mother's inner being, Kana is driven mad by the presence of an unearthly "something." In addition to Rio Yamashita as the protagonist Kana, An Ogawa, who has starred in successive films including "There Is a Stone" and "Song of the Beyond," plays Kana's younger sister Anri, who rushes to the family home after hearing Kana's pleas, and Sports Makita plays psychiatrist Kumagai, who becomes acquainted with Kana and Anri's family through a certain incident.
tmdb:1580374: A mystery drama based on the acclaimed novel by best-selling author Kanae Minato, considered her magnum opus, directed by Takahisa Zeze ('The Last 10 Years', 'Those Who Were Not Protected'). Shinomiya Mayuko fulfills her grandmother's expectations and becomes a teacher despite her complicated family background. One day, her student Saeki Akiko receives a letter from someone claiming to be 'Me, 20 years from now'. Half-doubtful, Akiko writes back, enduring the grief of losing her father and the lonely days with her withdrawn mother. But violence from her mother's boyfriend, bullying, and an unbelievable truth push her to the edge. In deep despair, Akiko and her only friend Arisa hatch a forbidden plan: 'kill the parents'. Mayuko tries to save Akiko, reaching out even as she herself is crushed by society's injustices. Yuna Kuroshima plays Mayuko, the teacher who tries to support children despite her own complicated past. Nanami Yamazaki plays Akiko, the girl struggling to survive harsh reality. Tori Matsuzaka and Kitagawa Keiko play Akiko's parents Ryota and Fumino. Ryuta Bando plays Mayuko's lover Haruki Yuki. Kanata Hosoda and Hana Kondo play Hirota Higuchi and Shinju Morimoto, who deeply influence the lives of Mayuko and Akiko.
tmdb:1584397: A film adaptation of the psycho-violent manga "Nanashi" by Sato Jiro—who is active not only as an actor but also as a screenwriter and film director—marking his first work based on a manga. Sato stars and wrote the script, with Hideo Shijo of "Bad Summer" directing. A brutal murder occurs at a family restaurant in the afternoon. Security cameras capture a bald middle-aged man who appears to be the culprit, but he holds no weapon. The footage records the bizarre sight of people spurting blood and collapsing just from the man approaching and lightly touching them. Investigating police identify the bald man as "Taro Yamada," who was questioned for shoplifting 11 years earlier. When investigators rush to Yamada's home address, they find a decomposed female corpse. Sato plays the protagonist, serial killer Yamada. Takaya Kamikawa plays Teruo, the patrol officer who becomes the namesake for the nameless orphaned young Yamada. MEGUMI plays Hanako Yamada, who grew up with Yamada in the same children's home and lives with him. Kuroudo Yashima plays Detective Kunieda, who works tirelessly to stop Yamada.
tmdb:1584762:
This documentary explores "Barefoot Gen," the manga created by Keiji Nakazawa based on his own experiences as an atomic bomb survivor, which has long been read as a powerful plea for anti-war and anti-nuclear causes. The story follows the young protagonist, Gen, who survives the bombing but loses his family, depicting his resilient struggle through poverty and prejudice.

In the half-century since its serialization began in Weekly Shonen Jump in 1973, the work has been translated into 25 languages and read across the globe. However, in recent years, it has become the subject of intense debate; some have called for restrictions on its access in school libraries, citing "extreme depictions" or the "instilling of incorrect historical perceptions," and it has even been removed from Hiroshima City’s peace education materials.

Why does "Barefoot Gen" continue to ignite such passion in people? By examining the work from its inception to the present day, this film reflects the anger, sadness, and kindness that permeate our world. A cinematic adaptation of the September 2024 BS12 Special "The Transmission of 'Barefoot Gen': Those Who Pass on the Atomic Bomb Manga," the film is directed by Masanori Komiyama, a veteran of numerous documentary programs making his feature debut. Arata Oshima (Kagawa 1st District, The Day of the State Funeral) and Aki Maeda (NO ELECTION, NO LIFE) serve as co-producers.
tmdb:1587473: A film adaptation of the bestselling novel 'A Survey About the Mouth' by author Senkin, who sparked the mockumentary horror boom with 'About a Certain Place in the Kinki Region.' Published in 2024, the palm-sized, 60-page story became a huge sensation on social media for delivering a solid scare in such a short format. Directed by Takashi Shimizu of the 'Ju-On' series, it marks Rihito Itagaki's first solo lead role in a live-action film. A group of university students hear a rumor about a 'cursed tree' in a cemetery known as a haunted spot and visit it for a test of courage. The next day, one of the group members mysteriously disappears. Since then, inexplicable phenomena begin to occur around the students who visited the cemetery, and they are gradually driven into a corner. Guided by the baffling testimonies of the five students, a terrifying truth emerges. Rihito Itagaki plays Shota Murai, one of the university students. The cast also includes Keito Tsuna as Tatsuya, Ai Yoshikawa as An, MOMONA (ME:I) as Mirei, Shuto Mori (BUDDiiS) as Horita, a student who visits the cemetery for fun, Tomoki Nishiyama (TAGRIGHT) as Kawase, who is forcibly taken to the cemetery by Horita, Shido Nakamura as Detective Kusabe, who pursues the missing student, and Tokio Emoto as journalist Nishi.
tmdb:1591447:
The popular anime series "Girls & Panzer," which depicts high school girls dedicating their youth to "Senshado" (the Way of the Tank)—a fictional martial art involving tank warfare—is receiving an anime adaptation of its official spin-off manga, "Girls & Panzer: Motto Love Love Sakusen desu!" This film marks the first act of a four-part theatrical series.

Miho Nishizumi and the members of the Oarai Girls' Academy Senshado team have been fully committed to the Way of the Tank, from their victory in the 63rd National High School Senshado Tournament to the fierce battle against the University Selection Team, where students from various schools united to save Oarai from closure. However, they are still high school girls at heart. Away from the heat of practice and matches, they fully enjoy a peaceful and fun-filled school life. Embracing the spirit of "yesterday's enemy is today's friend," they engage in lively "cross-cultural" exchanges with students from schools like Anzio High School, St. Gloriana Girls' Academy, Chi-Ha-Tan Academy, and Kuromorimine Girls' Academy. But as they are drawn to the unique cultures and charms of these other academies, one student after another begins to contemplate transferring...

The film is directed by Masami Shimoda (Zegapain series), with series composition and screenplay by Noboru Kimura (Code Geass: Rozé of the Recapture). Animation production is a joint effort between P.A.WORKS, known for hits like SHIROBAKO, and Actas, the studio behind the Girls & Panzer series.
tmdb:1598671: Yū, a high school senior, is on the verge of giving up his dreams to support his mother, who suffers from a serious illness. Torn by his inability to confess his hope of pursuing higher education... A heart-wrenching human drama about the bonds between parent and child and the journey toward independence.
tmdb:1599751:
Poet Chise Yamanaka pens her first screenplay for this medium-length film, depicting the reunion of two sisters who had lost touch after leaving their seaside hometown. Ku-chan, the elder sister, has lost her sense of purpose amidst the monotony of city life when she receives an unexpected phone call from her younger sister, Saki-chan. Choosing to meet at a beach away from their childhood home, a poem they once read together serves as a catalyst, awakening shared memories and emotions. In a world where memory and dreams blend and reality and imagination intertwine, the sisters embark on a new journey of "escape."

Based on Yamanaka’s original script titled after her poem "In the Midst of Escape" and incorporating excerpts from her "Dream Diary," the film explores the collaboration between cinema and language. It frames the sisters' reunion as a metaphor for the reconciliation of "fragmented words" and "the body," weaving a fresh perspective on the shared experience of time and space.

Yukino Murakami (*August My Heaven*) stars as Saki-chan, while Marino Kawashima (*Floating Boundary*) plays Ku-chan. The film was produced by Kinokoya, a cafe-bar and cine-club in Tama, Tokyo, and directed by Yukinori Kurokawa (*Garden Sandbox*, *Village on the Village*).
tmdb:1600737: Actor Ageha Tanaka is suddenly swept into a journey across the multiverse. Alongside Kanai, an aspiring film director, and Alien K, a traveler driven by curiosity, Ageha embarks on a strange odyssey. Amidst their travels, he finds himself reminiscing about the days spent with his late best friend, Glico.
tmdb:1600743: Into the home of Japanese sisters Kameko and Tsukiyo Hinomoto, two illegal immigrant sisters from Largo—Forte and Voce—come barging in...
tmdb:1601185: A fusion of individuality from promising young creators. Directed by Yuka Nishida, a graduate of Kyoto University of the Arts, who now belongs to STARDUST CREATORS as a screenwriter. This film is her graduation project, made when she was 22. It has been nominated for the SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival 2025, the 23rd Ueda Castle Town Film Festival Independent Film Competition, and the 28th Kyoto International Student Film Festival. Lead actor Mao Yoshino passionately plays dual roles: Ichitaro Sahara and his 'ideal self' Sahara. After this film, Yoshino was cast as a main host in 'Love and Rumors Last Seventy-Five Days' (2023, directed by Ririko Shinjo). Satoru Murayama, playing Junji Setoguchi who forms a duo 'Geki Amazu Buta' with Yoshino, portrays his partner while carrying a difficult-to-share secret, and was selected as a main cast member from about 700 applicants for the 2026 film 'Hello My Friend' (2026, directed by Masahide Ichii). Nanami Kitano, playing Sahara's neighbor Suzuka Murii, expresses a delicate distance with Sahara through a transparent performance, and has appeared in many films since. Distribution is handled by GeneHeart, which operates 'GeneTheater,' a streaming service curating only high-quality Japanese short films that stir emotions.
tmdb:1601204: This drama depicts a chef with communication difficulties and a free-spirited Korean woman who comes to learn Japanese cuisine. As they repeatedly try to revitalize the restaurant, they gradually break free from their rigid values. It is the feature-length debut of director Harumi Ikemoto, whose short film 'The Hunt' won the Excellence Award in the short film category at the 2023 SKIP City International D-Cinema Festival. Three years after losing his father, George Uehara took over the restaurant 'Yurie.' Although his cooking skills are solid, he is forced to accept the reality that the restaurant has recently seen fewer customers. Then Kim Juri, who came to Japan from Korea to learn Japanese cuisine, appears and starts working part-time at the restaurant. Despite clashing due to their differing values, they gradually grow closer and try various ideas to boost the restaurant's business. Sho Aoyagi, a member of 'Gekidan EXILE' active in films and dramas, plays George, a chef who struggles to express his thoughts and feelings and has some communication difficulties. Yeon-su Ha, who moved her base of operations from Korea to Japan and appeared in the NHK morning drama 'The Tiger's Wing,' plays Kim Juri, the part-time worker who initially keeps her distance from George due to her free-spirited nature. Yusuke Mikawa, known for 'Cloud,' co-stars as Iwakura, another part-time employee who watches over the two.
tmdb:1605972: A heartwarming comedy that became a massive hit in France, depicting the chaos that ensues when a father-and-son jewel thief duo hide out at a summer camp for people with disabilities. Paulo and his father rob a jewelry store, but when their getaway car is towed, they are left with no means of escape. Stranded on the street, they are mistaken for new arrivals by staff from a care facility about to depart for a summer camp. Taking advantage of the confusion, they pose as a resident and his caregiver to sneak into the camp. The lively days spent with the vibrant residents gradually begin to soften the hearts of the father and son. Popular French comedian, actor, and writer Artus serves as director and screenwriter while starring as Paulo, joined by veteran actor Clovis Cornillac (Paris 36) as the father. The fellow campers are played by 11 amateur actors who actually have disabilities.
tmdb:1607600:
A youth music film reuniting director Tomorowo Taguchi and screenwriter Kankuro Kudo of *Iden & Tity*. Based on the autobiographical essay *Street Kingdom* by photographer Yuichi Jibiki—who served as the group's photographer and manager—the film depicts the "Tokyo Rockers," a movement of young people who forged Japan's first homegrown punk rock scene.

In 1978, Yuichi, a young photographer who moved to Tokyo driven by the sounds of the Sex Pistols on the radio, visits a live house after discovering a small rock zine called *Rockin' Doll*. There, he finds a space overflowing with raw energy where music, bands, and audiences are free from all restraint. Blown away by a performance from the band TOKAGE, led by vocalist Momo, Yuichi captures the moment in a frenzy of shutter clicks.

Officially hired as their photographer, Yuichi grows closer to the band. Their music soon ignites a fire among the youth, evolving into the "Tokyo Rockers" movement that would redefine the landscape of Japanese rock.

Kazunobu Mineta stars as Yuichi alongside Ryuya Wakaba as Momo. The ensemble cast includes Riho Yoshioka, Taiga Nakano, Shotaro Mamiya, Nao Omori, Shido Nakamura, and Sena Nakajima. Yoshihide Otomo (*Iden & Tity*) provides the film's music.
tmdb:1608471: Satoshi Kimura, director of 'Strange Lovers from Another Planet' and 'The Melancholic After-School of Yoyogi Johnny', takes on the classic French genre of 'vacation film' with this dialogue-driven drama. At the start of summer, Yuka, freshly divorced from Haruki after three years together, visits a seaside town on vacation with her best friend Shina and Shina's boyfriend Dazai. Yuka and Dazai were once in love, and reuniting with him rekindles her feelings. Meanwhile, Shina finds herself drawn to Tenma, a poet living in the seaside town. The film creates '1:1' scenes where characters enter the frame in pairs, unfolding the story through a chain of different combinations. The emotion of 'liking' determines each character's formation, shifting relationships as they cross paths. Yu Imari ('Soirée', 'A Janitor') plays Yuka, Ei Adachi ('If Tokugawa Ieyasu Became Prime Minister') plays Dazai, Yuki Shinho ('YOUNG&FINE') plays Shina, Takeo Yamaguchi ('BADBOYS THE MOVIE') plays Tenma, and Ryo Igarashi ('Before Dawn') plays Haruki.
tmdb:1613385:
The classic drama series "Oretachi no Tabi," a quintessential symbol of youth in the Showa era, receives its first-ever film adaptation. Since its debut as a serial drama on the Nippon TV network in 1975, the series has continued through special episodes produced at various milestones in the protagonists' lives. This sequel, arriving 20 years after the last installment, marks the directorial debut of lead actor Masatoshi Nakamura.

Kosuke Tsumura (nicknamed "Kasuke"), his college classmate Takao Kanzaki ("Omeda"), and his elementary school senior Shinroku Kumazawa ("Guzu-roku") have now reached their 70s, their friendship spanning over 50 years. Kasuke runs a small local factory, Omeda serves as the mayor of Yonago City in Tottori Prefecture, and Guzu-roku is the chairman of a nursing care facility—each living out their peaceful daily lives.

One day, Omeda visits Kasuke's factory, but he appears deeply troubled
tmdb:1620313: Acclaimed director Kiyoshi Kurosawa ("Wife of a Spy," "Creepy") takes on his first period film, adapting the mystery novel of the same name by Honobu Yonezawa, which won both the 166th Naoki Prize and the 12th Yamaneko Prize. Murashige Araki rebels against Nobunaga Oda's tyrannical methods and holes up in Arioka Castle. Surrounded by the Oda army and isolated, Murashige struggles to control his hot-blooded retainers while relying on his wife, Chiyo, for emotional support, striving to protect the castle and its people. Amidst this, a boy is murdered inside the castle, followed by a series of strange incidents. With the suspects being the retainers and family members trapped inside the sealed-off castle, and the enemy outside, everyone falls into suspicion and paranoia. Cornered, Murashige seeks help from the genius military strategist Kanbei Kuroda, who was imprisoned after being sent as Nobunaga's envoy to persuade him, and sets out to solve the case. Starring Masahiro Motoki as Lord Murashige Araki, Masaki Suda as the genius strategist Kanbei Kuroda, Yuriko Yoshitaka as Murashige's wife Chiyo, Takao Aoki as Murashige's trusted retainer Kyusaemon Araki, Ryota Miyate (Snow Man) as the young retainer Saburo Inui, Tasuku Emoto as the skilled sniper Sagari Saika who witnesses the events, and Joe Odagiri as Juemon Kori, who operates in the shadows as Murashige's hidden blade. The film was selected for the Cannes Premiere section at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in 2026.
tmdb:1621777: A psycho-horror film self-remade by director Taro Miyaoka, known for "The Fallen" and "Last Summer Wars," based on his own independent film "Chain"—which won the Special Jury Prize at the 21st Tokyo Student Film Festival—after more than 15 years. Exploring the boundary between love and obsession, it thrillingly depicts human madness. Tatsuki, a 23-year-old who has never had a girlfriend, meets Erica, a beautiful woman working at a café, and is captivated by her kindness. Their relationship deepens, but Erica's suggestive words and actions, along with inexplicable events around Tatsuki, gradually cast an unsettling shadow over his daily life. Eventually, Erica's abnormal obsession and madness are revealed, dragging Tatsuki into an inescapable fate. Starring Ayumu Mochizuki, who rose to fame with the two-part film "Solomon's Perjury." The heroine Erica is played by Mei Hayashi, who has worked as a model since elementary school and made her acting debut in the 2024 drama "Goodbye, Teacher." The cast also includes Hayato Takao, Kurea Hatsuki, Moeka Koizumi, and Itsuki Fujiwara. The screenplay was written by Tete Inoue of "Initiation Love."
tmdb:1623075:
This cinematic experience fuses footage from large-scale music live events with animation, following the expansive worldview of LDH JAPAN’s next-generation comprehensive entertainment project, "BATTLE OF TOKYO." Set in the fictional future city of "Super Tokyo," the project reimagines real-life LDH artists as fictional characters, depicting a narrative that traverses both real and virtual worlds. Between 2019 and 2024, massive live events featuring GENERATIONS, THE RAMPAGE, FANTASTICS, BALLISTIK BOYZ, and PSYCHIC FEVER (2023/2024 only) were held, drawing a cumulative audience of 500,000 people. 

This film features a re-edited mix of carefully selected live performance footage and music videos, with audio remastered in 5.1ch surround sound. The animated segments vividly and dramatically portray the final chapter of the story—originally depicted in the novel "BATTLE OF TOKYO" by Soki Tsukishima—revolving around the battles and bonds of five teams of youths possessing special skills. The film features voice acting by Yuki Kaji, Yuma Uchida, and Tomokazu Sugita. EXILE HIRO serves as the project producer, with Norihisa Hiranuma ("HiGH&LOW THE WORST X") directing and Dai Sato ("Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex") writing the screenplay.
tmdb:1624755:
**Introduction**
Fifteen years after the Great East Japan Earthquake. A Self-Defense Force member who lost his wife and child, and a boy who lost his parents. This is a story of rebirth for two individuals as they begin to walk forward alongside their experiences of loss.

Director Yuji Kakizaki, who earned high acclaim for his previous work *The Sun Falls*—a profound human drama focusing on the resolve of a samurai’s wife and the bond of a married couple—now takes on a new challenge: a story of "loss" and "rebirth."

The film stars Yasuyuki Maekawa, who left an unforgettable impression in the director's previous work. He breathes life into Third Lieutenant Kasuga, a JSDF member who continues his duties despite losing his wife and young daughter in the tsunami, through a performance imbued with quiet strength. Set in the disaster-stricken areas of the Great East Japan Earthquake, Kasuga spends his days providing support at evacuation centers, facing people head-on while carrying his own deep pain. It is there that he meets Kazuki Yoshimura, a boy who has
tmdb:1624812: A crime drama about three women who have drifted through life, who deepen their bond through gold smuggling and reclaim their respective lives. Director Chihiro Amano ("Mrs. Noisy") was inspired by a real 2017 incident in which housewives were arrested for gold smuggling at Chubu Centrair International Airport. She co-wrote the original script with Madoka Kumagai, with whom she also worked on "Sato-san and Sato-san." Large-scale location shooting was conducted in Singapore, depicting the glamorous yet perilous journey of gold smuggling. Wakako, a mother of two living a peaceful life, learns that her husband has been fired from his company for embezzlement. To pay off her husband's debts, she becomes involved in gold smuggling in Singapore, where she meets Kiyoe, a non-regular researcher struggling with student loan repayments, and Mayu, an unmarried pregnant woman with zero savings. After successfully smuggling gold and getting a taste for it, the three decide to start smuggling on their own. For the first time, they gain money, freedom, and the joy of living authentically, spending a magical time together—but... Kasumi Arimura plays Wakako, the mother of two who learns of her husband's embezzlement; Haru Kuroki plays Kiyoe, the indebted researcher; Sara Minami plays Mayu, the unmarried pregnant woman; Akihisa Shiono plays Wakako's husband Takashi; Yuzu Aoki plays Kiyoe's colleague Shiina; and Takumi Saito plays Takashi's boss Tanoue.
tmdb:1630435: Based on the debut novel by physician-author Yo Hisakabe published in 2003, this human suspense film stars Shota Sometani. At the daycare facility 'Ijinzaka Clinic,' an innovative treatment devised by director Kuranosuke Urushibara spreads quietly among the elderly. Aiming for cost-effective care, the treatment involves 'useless limbs' (paralyzed body parts with no hope of recovery), and unexpected 'favorable side effects' have appeared, such as 'feeling lighter in body and mind' and 'a harsh personality softening.' Hearing rumors, editor Yagura senses potential for a revolution in geriatric medicine and proposes publishing a book to Urushibara. However, everything takes a dark turn when an internal whistleblowing about the daycare leaks to a weekly magazine, and a shocking incident occurs at a patient's home. Sometani delivers a haunting performance as Urushibara, a doctor who, in pursuit of his ideals, steps into the gap between rationality and madness. The cast includes Yuki Kitamura as editor Yagura, Naomasa Rokudaira as elderly patient Iwagami who reclaims his life through Urushibara's treatment, and Kumi Takiuchi as Urushibara's wife Kikuko. The film is directed and written by Mitsuki Yoshida, who has gained international attention for works such as 'Family X' and 'Three Lights.'
tmdb:16306: A singular fantasy masterpiece, this film adapts the novel by French sci-fi author Stefan Wul through the distinct visual artistry of illustrator Roland Topor. Set on the wild planet Ygam, it depicts the conflict and eventual cooperation between the humanoid Oms and the giant Draags, who treat them like slaves. The film’s staggering sci-fi imagination and unique animation style are truly a sight to behold.
tmdb:1631314: A youth comedy directed by Makoto Ueda, head of the theater group "Europe Kikaku," known for writing screenplays for numerous hit films like "Summer Time Machine Blues" and "River, Don't Flow On." This is his feature directorial debut, set in the real-life building "Shelbo Shimokitazawa" in Shimokitazawa, employing innovative gimmicks. At the cinema Tollywood on the second floor of "Shelbo Shimokitazawa," Madoka, a playwright from Shimokitazawa, and Kazuma, a band musician from Sangenjaya, each go to see a movie. An impossible structure emerges where each other's events are projected onto the screen as a film. Meanwhile, problems arise at the shops adjacent to the cinema, "Good Heavens" and "Mikazuki Rock." Madoka and Kazuma try to solve the problems using this structure, but their films influence each other, and the situation spirals in unexpected directions. Starring Maria Ito ("Summer Film ni Notte") as Madoka the playwright and Kai Inowaki ("Musicophilia") as Kazuma the band musician. The cast also includes Oshiro Maeda and Hinako Kikuchi as members of Madoka's theater troupe, Suzuyuki Kaneko and Yusuke Mikawa as members of Kazuma's band, Takafumi Imai as a semi-delinquent who frequents "Mikazuki Rock," and the comedy duo "The Geese" as a pair of detectives. Additionally, members of Europe Kikaku, including Gota Ishida, Shintaro Kanamaru, and Riko Fujitani, play unique characters.
tmdb:1633438: This documentary captures the life of Shigeru Endo, who, despite being confined to his bed by cerebral palsy, interacts with young caregivers and composes numerous tanka poems from his bedside. The film is directed by Shinichi Ise, a friend of Endo since their student days, who previously helmed the 1999 documentary *Entoko*, which also followed Endo’s daily life. Despite his physical limitations, Endo organized his own caregiver network called "Entoko" (meaning both "where Endo is" and "a place of connections"). As his disability progressed over more than 35 years in bed, Endo began writing tanka in his late 50s, using poetry to give voice to the cries of his soul. Through the deep emotional connection between Endo and his caregivers, the film portrays people living in a way that honors and sustains life exactly as it is.
tmdb:1634021:
The fourth installment of the "Our Recipe Book Series," a youth film project centered on the themes of community, food, and high school life. Set in Kiyose City, Tokyo, the film humorously depicts a summer spent by high school film club members with an alien they encounter by chance.

Hayate, a high school sophomore living in Kiyose, is a massive sci-fi fan. He secretly dreamed of filming an alien movie with his club, but had lost his nerve after his previous work was panned by critics. However, one day just before summer break, something crashes into the woods of Kiyose, and Hayate and his fellow film club members encounter a real alien there. Alongside this extraterrestrial visitor and a group of unique friends—including his handsome, movie-loving childhood friend Hinata; the cheerful and brainy "Bon-chan"; and the easygoing, music-loving Wakamizu—Hayate sets out to make his movie.

The film is directed by Masahide Ichii, known for "Haruchika: Bring on the Melody," "The Family of Typhoon," and "What to Do with My Husband: Oh My Charlie."
tmdb:1637456: Starring Tasuku Emoto, this drama explores themes of family memory and records. Yuta, who lives with his wife and daughter in Tokyo, travels to a rural town in Kyushu to care for his father-in-law Makoto, who has broken his leg, until he recovers. While helping out at Makoto's old-fashioned photo studio, Yuta exchanges videos taken on his smartphone with his wife and daughter back in Tokyo. Even without major events, the accumulation of daily trivial records and memories quietly and vividly reveals the long span of a family's life. Moka Kamishiraishi ("Shōgun," "Girl Encounters") plays Yuta's wife Yuki, who continues working and raising their child in Tokyo. Issey Ogata plays Makoto, the taciturn father-in-law, and Yū Kashii plays a character symbolizing precious family memories. Director Miu Sakanishi, who gained attention for short films while at Kyoto University of Art and Design and later worked as an assistant director for Yūya Ishii and a making-of cameraman for Yūichirō Doi, makes her feature-length directorial debut.
tmdb:1637635: Directed by Keisuke Yoshida of "Himeanole" and "Missing," this drama portrays boys who cannot understand pain or common sense, and the adults who continue to confront them head-on. Yoshida wrote the original script based on the juvenile delinquents he encountered during his own sensitive adolescence and the community surrounding them. Nishiken Go, a former half-gray area gangster and ex-convict, runs a full-time residential rehabilitation facility called "Mirai no Sato" in a coastal provincial town. Drawing on his own experiences, Nishiken tackles troubled children with all his might, but his rehabilitation methods, which do not shy away from corporal punishment, are criticized by educators. One day, a middle school teacher named Fuyuko consults him about an uncontrollable student, Kaito, and Yu, who has just been released from a juvenile detention center. Meeting the two, Nishiken instantly sees through Kaito's madness. Kaito's mother, exhausted by his severe domestic violence, decides to entrust her son to "Mirai no Sato." However, Kaito causes trouble with the other residents, escapes, and is arrested for assault. Wataru Ichinose of the Netflix drama "Sanctuary" stars as Nishiken, while the newcomer Hayato Uesaka is cast as the delinquent boy Kaito. Kaho plays middle school teacher Fuyuko, Atsushi Shinohara and Fusako Urabe play Kaito's parents, Iori Wada plays Kaito's delinquent friend Yu, and Nanami Yamazaki and Mansaku Takada play the facility's residents.
tmdb:1639386: A documentary depicting the life of activist Teishiro Minami, who organized Japan's first Pride Parade in 1994. Today, Pride Parades are held in over 40 locations in Japan, and partnership systems are spreading nationwide. At the starting point of this progress were the grassroots activities of pioneers who forged a path from "zero" to "one." Born in Karafuto (Sakhalin) in 1931 and raised in Akita Prefecture, Teishiro Minami moved to Tokyo at age 22, constantly searching for a way to live authentically. In 1984, he began the gay liberation movement, immersing himself in activism and following his passion. Then, in 1994, he launched Japan's first Pride Parade. The activities Minami spearheaded became the foundation of the pride movement in Japan, but he gradually became fixated on his own beliefs, deepening the rift with those around him. By the third parade, he faced significant backlash and was forced to step back from the front lines of the movement. What did Minami, driven by justice and swept along by the times, find in the end of his fervor? Tracing his tumultuous path through his own testimony, interviews with people involved at the time, news reports, photos, and videos, the film depicts the origins of the pride movement in Japan. Directed by Hiroaki Matsuoka ("Okinawa Coming Out Story").
tmdb:1642802:
An original work from the creative duo behind the *Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan* series, director Kazutaka Watanabe and star Issey Takahashi. Inspired by the "Sunekosuri" (shin-rubber) folklore of Okayama Prefecture, this film is set deep within a forest to tell a mysterious, beautiful, and cruel tale of love.

Deep in a forest far from civilization, a young man with an injured leg is led by a woman’s sweet singing voice to an ancient shrine. Living there are a mysterious man and his young, beautiful wife, Sayuri. Nursed back to health, the young man spends a dreamlike time where it feels as though time itself has stopped. These peaceful, repeating days seem as if they might last forever, but...

Director Watanabe personally visited the forests of Okayama, drawing inspiration from local legends to pen this original screenplay. Filming took place in the cities of Takahashi and Niimi in Okayama Prefecture. Issey Takahashi stars as the mysterious man, while rising star Nijiko Aoto, in her second film role, plays Sayuri, the mysterious woman living deep in the woods. Koudai Kurosaki, who garnered attention for his lead role in *The Miharashi Generation* (selected for the 78th Cannes Film Festival Directors' Fortnight), portrays the injured young man who wanders into the forest.
tmdb:1645545:
Twenty-two-year-old Iroha lives at home, dissatisfied with her current self and facing an uncertain future. One day, her older sister Karen returns for the first time in five years. Karen is free-spirited and lives for romance—a woman who, unlike Iroha, has always made bold choices in life. But the reality she carries with her is this: "I'm pregnant. But I don't know who the father is."

There are three possibilities: a wealthy heir, an older man with a violent streak, and an ex-boyfriend burdened by debt. In each relationship, there remains an ambiguity that falls short of being called "love." Why does Karen keep repeating romances she knows will only end in pain? Dragged along on the search for the father, Iroha travels across Nagasaki Prefecture with her sister, witnessing the loneliness and the desperate need for validation that lie beneath the surface of romance.

The sister who seemed so strong was, in truth, longing to be loved more than anyone else. Contrary to her glamorous exterior, she had been constantly entrusting her self-worth to others. At the same time, Iroha realizes that she herself had been running away from being hurt by avoiding love altogether.

More important than being chosen by someone else is acknowledging yourself. Before being loved by another, you must accept yourself. Clashing and baring their true feelings, the sisters finally come to understand each other's weaknesses. Carrying their love without answers and their own imperfect selves... the sisters' journey continues.
tmdb:1647782: A bold, original film adaptation of Junichiro Tanizaki's novel 'The Key', which explores the depths of sexuality through the alternating diaries of a married couple. Starring Mitsuru Fukikoshi, it lays bare a dying man's obsessive attachment and pure love for his younger wife. Kenzo Kenmochi, who runs a construction company, is told by his doctor he has only six months to live. Worried about his much younger wife Ikuko, he schemes to push her into an affair with his subordinate Kimura. As Kimura and Ikuko grow closer, things go according to plan, but Kenzo cannot let go of his feelings for Ikuko. Despite his physical decline, his jealousy intensifies. When he secretly reads Ikuko's diary, he finds her feelings of strong attraction to Kimura's body. Mitsuru Fukikoshi humorously plays the clumsy, jealousy-consumed Kenzo. Kei Kanno plays his wife Ikuko, and Keisuke Koide plays Kimura. The film is directed and written by Shinji Imaoka, known for scripting 'The Zombie Child' and directing 'Reiko and the Dolphin', with Minoru Matsumoto co-writing the screenplay.
tmdb:1649900: A documentary following Namiko Kawamura, an 84-year-old expressive artist who continues to work as a dancer and performer. Directed by Toshiko Rin, known for documentary works such as "Jibun, Maru! Ippo no Hanashi," "Nishi Tenka Chaya Ooishi So," and "Blessed." Kawamura has been familiar with dance since childhood, and from the 1970s onward, she explored a unique form of expression incorporating perception and walking in nature. After participating in a workshop by American dancer Anna Halprin in the 1980s, she established a performance of "slow walking"—a forward-moving gait. This act, both a dance and a way of life, has continued for many years. Set in Okinawa, a place Kawamura had long wished to visit, the film explores the thoughts and memories behind her expression through beach performances and interviews. It records her walking and dancing while confronting the time embedded in a land marked by war memories, observing the journey of a woman who has dedicated her life to dance.
tmdb:1651162: A film adaptation of the novel "Iwaiyama" by Nanami Kamon, an author known for works on folklore and the occult, based on her own experiences, starring Ai Hashimoto. Directed and written by Shingo Takeda, a filmmaker who has won awards at film festivals for his horror works, marking his feature-length theatrical debut. Horror novelist Minami Kano, suffering from writer's block, receives a letter from her middle school classmate Asako Yaguchi. The letter describes unexplainable phenomena that have been occurring ever since she went on a dare to visit a ruin known as a haunted spot. Seeking material for her new work, Minami reunites with Asako and their old friends, and becomes entangled in mysterious events. As the investigation progresses, it emerges that behind the series of strange occurrences lies the forbidden mountain "Iwaiyama" they once set foot on. Ai Hashimoto plays the protagonist Minami Kano, marking her first horror film role in ten years since "Zan: The Haunted Room." The cast also includes Ren Ishikawa, Sayu Kubota, Takuya Kusakawa, Yuya Matsuura, and Go Riju.
tmdb:1651166: A live-action film adaptation of novelist Kyogoku Natsuhiko's unique mystery novel of the same name set in modern times, starring Nao. A woman named Asami Kashima is murdered. With no clue as to the culprit's identity or motive, a mysterious woman named Eiko Watarai visits those who knew Asami in life, claiming she wants to ask about her. As she follows various testimonies, the outline of Asami's character and her relationship with Eiko gradually emerge. Nao plays Eiko, who goes around asking about Asami. Aoi Ito plays Asami, whose impression changes depending on who is asked; Ko Maehara plays Asami's boss and lover, Hiroyuki Yamazaki; Hikaru Takahashi plays Asami's senior, Kaori Shinomiya; Takuya Kusakawa (from the group Shinkansen) plays Asami's boyfriend, Yuya Sakuma; Tomoko Tabata plays Asami's mother, Naoko Kashima; and Tetsu Hirahara plays the lawyer involved in Asami's case, Riku Gojo. Directed by Junichi Kanai, who previously worked with Nao on "My Daddy," with a screenplay by Kohei Kiyasu (known for "The Kirishima Thing"). The rock band "This is LAST" performs the theme song.
tmdb:1651171: A youth story based on the manga 'Zakken!' (published by Shogakukan), which was developed from a real club activity, the 'Weed Research Club,' at Tokyo Metropolitan Hibiya High School, by screenwriter and film director Naho Uemura and the scenario creation team 'Monogatari Lab,' with Uemura herself writing and directing the film adaptation. It delicately and freshly depicts a teenage girl lost and unsure of herself, who discovers her own identity through the weeds growing at her feet, which she had never paid attention to before. Spring of her first year of high school. Sugano Yukari, an ordinary girl who isn't passionate about anything and just goes through the motions, meets her classmate Tokuda Mimi, nicknamed 'Dokudami-chan,' who loves weeds and is fascinated by their vitality. Slightly eccentric but with a straightforward and pure heart, Yukari gradually opens up to her. Dokudami-chan dreams of reviving the 'Zakken,' or 'Weed Research Club,' and Yukari, while hesitant about her enthusiasm, begins activities with her aimed at reviving the club, but... Luna Nakajima, who has starred in films like 'A Town of Old Houses' and 'Tore!' and won the Japan Academy Prize for Newcomer for 'Tokyo Taxi,' plays Sugano Yukari, and Miyu Oshima, known for the NHK morning drama 'Omusubi' and the drama 'Bokutachi nchi,' plays Tokuda Mimi, taking on the lead roles.
tmdb:1653724:
Set in Shinjuku’s Kabukicho district following the closure of the "Toyoko" area, this suspenseful drama follows four displaced youths over the course of a single night as their fates collide in a desperate escape. Marking the feature film debut of 24-year-old rising talent Ren Akiba, the film is a feature-length adaptation of his own short film which won the Grand Prix at the 2nd Tokyo Independent Film Festival. Akiba penned the original screenplay based on his own personal experiences in Kabukicho.

Asuka, a high school student who feels she has no place at home or school, travels to Kabukicho drawn by "Tokyo Escape," an autobiographical web novel written by a girl living in Toyoko. There, she happens to meet the author, Hiyori, and the two form an immediate bond. Asuka is introduced to Edo, a protector of the drifters in Toyoko, and Merio, a leader among the local youth. However, after attending a meeting led by Merio and witnessing a shocking reality, Asuka grabs Hiyori’s hand and flees. Their escape earns them the ire of a "han-gure" criminal group, leaving them hunted. Meanwhile, Edo fights to preserve the youths' sanctuary, while Merio makes increasingly dangerous choices in his pursuit of the girls. As the police become involved, the situation spirals toward a rapid climax.

The film stars Rio Teramoto as Asuka, Akana Ikeda as Hiyori, Keito Tsuna as Edo, and Nao Takahashi as Merio, supported by Yuya Matsuura, Motoki Fukami, and Honami Sato. Michihito Fujii, director of *The Strangers* and *The Journalist*, serves as executive producer.
tmdb:1654870: A comedy starring Hiroshi Tachi, depicting a 70-year-old movie star caught up in a major uproar over surrendering his driver's license. Nanjo Hiroshi, who has enjoyed a smooth acting career and recently won numerous film awards for art films, secretly longs to appear in action movies. When his longtime actor friend Ozaki Makoto gets into a motorcycle accident, Nanjo is asked by the media for comment as a fellow actor of the same generation. His remarks admonishing Ozaki unexpectedly attract public attention, and the narrative takes on a life of its own, involving his manager and family, and being interpreted in ways far from his original intent. Although Nanjo wants to continue performing action scenes with cars and motorcycles, those around him expect him to surrender his license, plunging him into the biggest crisis of his life. Hiroshi Tachi comically plays actor Nanjo Hiroshi, the same name as the character he played in the 1994 film "License!". Nishino Nanase plays his manager Kawauna Mai, who is thrown into chaos by Nanjo; Kurokawa Sooya plays young man Kugami Ryo, whose life changes dramatically after meeting Nanjo; Yoshida Kotaro plays Mita Atsushi, the president of Nanjo's talent agency; and Uzaki Ryudo plays Ozaki Makoto, an actor friend who built an era alongside Nanjo. Directed by Kawai Yuji of "Kaguya-sama: Love Is War" fame, with screenplay by Hayashi Tamio of "From the Land of Love to the Land of Sorrow".
tmdb:1656442:
Set in the mysterious amusement park "Gamaland," this medium-length horror film employs a found-footage format to depict an inexplicable story surrounding Miyuki Sawada. Gamaland was a real-life location once symbolized by its iconic, giant toad statue. A VHS tape recorded there, steeped in the atmosphere of the early Heisei era, captures a date between a couple, Kohei Shimizu and Miyuki Sawada—but the footage gradually transforms into something deeply unsettling.

The film is directed by Koki Nishii, the filmmaker behind the YouTube channel "Filmest TV," which specializes in recreating modern subjects with a 1980s and 90s aesthetic. Nishii, who also made waves with the September 2024 YouTube drama *Tomochika Suspense Theater: Sotoyu Meguri Mystery - Dogo Striptease Girl Serial Murders*, served as screenwriter and editor, and appears in the film under the name "Nishii." The cast features Tsubasa Nakahara (Masashi Yamamoto’s *DUDE*) as Miyuki Sawada and Takeo Gozu (Netflix’s *Tokyo Swindlers*). The film is produced by NOTHING NEW, a label garnering attention for horror works such as *Chilled* (winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival), the short film anthology *NN4444*, and the medium-length horror *Shiki*.
tmdb:1657017: The protagonist is Sohui, a 14-year-old Zainichi Korean girl. She attends a Korean school and devotes herself to Korean dance in her club activities. One day, at an exchange event with a Japanese school, she becomes friends with a Japanese girl named Mirai over their shared love of K-Pop, and Sohui gradually connects with the outside world. To earn money for tickets to their favorite K-Pop idol's concert, the two decide to sell unused items from Sohui's house on a flea market app. Surprisingly, the item that sells for a high price is a North Korean CD owned by Sohui's father, Sanju, who is the principal of the Korean school. Emboldened, Sohui and her friend even sell a "medal" awarded to Sanju by his homeland, North Korea.
tmdb:1657504: Actor Tsuyoshi Rishu, who has directed films such as 'Chloe' and 'Goodbye Debussy', takes the director's chair for a feature film for the first time in 13 years, with Issei Takahashi in the lead role. This human drama humorously depicts a man who has avoided social interactions, whose life takes an unexpected turn when he discovers he has been unknowingly registered as married to a woman he doesn't know. Mikio Natsuno, a slightly naive man who never gets angry, goes to get a copy of his family register to renew his passport and is shocked to find the words 'Relationship: Wife' for a woman he has absolutely no memory of. Learning that a woman named 'Shigeko' has registered herself as his wife without his knowledge, Mikio begins searching for this mysterious woman. He eventually finds Shigeko at a small flower shop on a street corner, but she is an unconventional woman who destroys everything she touches. Though Mikio is tossed around by Shigeko, this strange encounter gradually brings unexpected changes to both their lives. Issei Takahashi plays the kind-hearted and sensitive protagonist Mikio, and Kumi Goshima (NHK morning drama 'Manpuku') plays the enigmatic heroine Shigeko who bewilders everyone around her. Okihiko Serizawa and Chizuru Ikewaki co-star, and director Rishu also appears as a key character. World-renowned jazz pianist Junko Onishi provides the music.
tmdb:1658268: Minoru (Hiromitsu Kitayama) and Yuki (Chihiro Kato) move with their young son Akira to Minoru's family home in a heavy snowfall area.
