The couple wishes for a peaceful life, but Minoru's father Shigeru, who has dementia, is inexplicably terrified of Yuki and calls out his deceased wife's name. One morning, Shigeru dies grotesquely in an abnormal state. From that moment on, the family is plagued by suspicion and fear. Soon, eerie 'white women' begin appearing in the house one after another, encroaching on their daily lives. Minoru, as if losing his mind, keeps drawing pictures of the 'white woman,' while young Akira's view of his mother gradually begins to reflect 'something else.' One by one, the family members break down. Minoru, captivated by snowflakes and losing his reason; Yuki, being eroded; and Akira, placed in danger. Is this a curse, an illusion, or reality? When the snowy plains are stained with fresh blood, an unknown 'white terror' appears and runs amok with brutality.
tmdb:1659338: A sequel to the 2026 TV anime 'Death Game de Meshi o Kū,' based on the popular light novel by Yūshi Ukai, this theatrical anime adapts the original 'Cloudy Beach' arc. A deadly murder game where survival earns you prize money. Allies you encouraged yesterday can become enemies today, and even with full preparation, you can lose your life. The girl Yūki aims to clear this life-or-death game 99 times, making a living from the prize money she wins. Overcoming the 'Wall of Thirty'—a jinx where player survival rates drop drastically—she continues forward and takes on her 44th game, 'Cloudy Beach.' Among the eight players gathered on a remote island, Yūki spots a familiar veteran. Continuing from the TV anime, Sōda Ueno of 'Stepsister Life' directs, with animation production by Studio Deen.
tmdb:1662803: A rare directorial effort from Isamu Kosugi—the star actor of Nikkatsu’s contemporary dramas—produced during his time at Toyoko Eiga. Ryosuke (Haida) and Kinuko (Hidaka) are engaged but unable to take the plunge into marriage due to the post-war housing shortage. When they finally secure a new home through a housing lottery, Ryosuke’s benefactor Kawakami (Furukawa), a repatriate from Manchuria, moves in unannounced, throwing their new life into unexpected chaos. The film vibrantly depicts the couple as they navigate Kawakami’s inconsiderate behavior, striving to overcome their troubles with songs and laughter.
tmdb:1663038: The third installment in the human comedy series that explores family dynamics and second chances through the theme of "shukatsu" (end-of-life planning), following "Oshukatsu: Jukushun! Jinsei, Hyakunen Jidai no Sugoshikata" and "Oshukatsu: Saishun! Jinsei Rhapsody." Aya, the eldest daughter of Shinichi and Chikako Ohara, finally decides to marry her fiancé Ryota. However, just before the wedding, a casual remark from Aya causes a rift in their relationship, escalating into a major commotion involving both families. Meanwhile, Shinichi's junior colleague Kato struggles to accept his mother Toyoko's progressing dementia, speaking harshly to her. Chikako gently tells Kato, "Even with dementia, the heart doesn't forget." Continuing from the previous two films, director Hideyuki Kazuki helms this installment, incorporating the latest end-of-life planning trends and knowledge while depicting family bonds with light humor and a warm perspective. The cast reunites familiar faces from the series, including Tsurube Shofukutei as Shinichi Ohara, Junko Takahata as his wife Chikako, Ayame Goriki as their daughter Aya, along with Yuki Matsushita, Masahiko Nishimura, Norika Fujiwara, Renji Ishibashi, Kumiko Fujiyoshi, LiLiCo, Kunikazu Katsumata, and Yoshihiko Hakamada. Guest stars include Keiko Mita as Toyoko, who has dementia, and Fumiyo Kohinata as her son Kato, who supports her despite his own inner conflict.
tmdb:1663041: Director Taichi Kazama, known for the TV drama "Silent," adapts manga artist Akari Tamura's comic into a live-action film, a love story about the first crushes of "supporting characters" who have quietly lived on the fringes of society. Shy and reserved college student Nobuko Tanaka identifies with the term "mob," meaning crowd, extra, or non-major character, and has lived her life watching from afar as other protagonists shine. Then, she notices Hiroki Irie, a young man working part-time at the same supermarket. Touched by Irie's natural thoughtfulness, Nobuko gradually becomes drawn to him. Through her encounter with Irie, she begins to struggle to break free from the shell that has bound her, and while sometimes confronted with harsh realities, she perseveres with the support of her coworkers. Meanwhile, Irie also notices Nobuko's quiet kindness and looks straight at her. The accumulation of small, everyday moments eventually gives them both the strength to take a step forward. Hiyori Sakurada ("The Diary of a Substitute Lie") plays Nobuko, aka Mobuko, and Taisei Kido ("Yukite Kaeranu") plays Hiroki Irie, the object of her first love. The cast also includes Ikoi Hayase as Nobuko's junior coworker Abe, Erika Karata as senior coworker Shinozaki, Takuya Kusakawa as fellow part-timer and Irie's friend Kaneko, Tsubasa Araki as new part-timer Ono, and Kanji Furutachi as store manager Orihara.
tmdb:1663504: A film version serving as a sequel to the TV dramas 'Chaser Game W: My Ex-Girlfriend is My Harassing Boss' and 'Chaser Game W2: The Beautiful Celestial Maidens,' which delicately portrayed the realities of the game industry and a romance between women. Set seven years after the drama, it depicts the relationship evolving over time and the two women confronting life choices. Itsuki and Fuyu live in Ito City, Shizuoka Prefecture, with their daughter Tsuki, now a middle school student. As they become consumed by housework, childcare, and work, their time together becomes routine. Over the seven years, their relationship shifts from lovers to family, and they gradually begin to drift apart. Though they maintain a peaceful home while being disturbed by each other's casual words and attitudes, their daughter Tsuki senses the unease between her parents. One day, Tsuki gets into trouble and is helped by a taxi driver named Kozue. This encounter prompts Itsuki and Fuyu to confront each other's true feelings for the first time and re-examine the form of love they have lost sight of. Continuing from the drama series, Sugai Yuka stars as Itsuki, Nakamura Yurika as Fuyu, Okamoto Mirai as their middle-school-aged daughter Tsuki, Ito Ayumi as taxi driver Kozue, and Kurotani Tomoka as Department Chief Ro. Directed by Ota Isamu, who also worked on the drama series, with a screenplay by Asada Atsushi.
tmdb:1671640: The second installment of the omnibus film 'The Bastard and the Beautiful World,' released in 2018 and starring Goro Inagaki, Tsuyoshi Kusanagi, and Shingo Katori of 'New Map.' Directed and written by Kenji Yamauchi, who also participated in the previous film and is known for his work in theater and commercials, as well as directing films like 'I Like My Friend's Dad' and 'Unique Countries of Asia.' In an age where information and answers are instantly available and people try to find meaning in everything, this film invites Inagaki, Kusanagi, and Katori into a story that runs counter to 'meaning,' with the concept of enjoying not knowing things as they are. The cast includes First Summer Uika, who is active not only in variety shows but also in films and taiga dramas; Shuri, who starred in the NHK morning drama 'Boogie Woogie'; and veteran actors such as Kanji Furutachi, Seiyo Uchino, and Mitsuru Fukikoshi.
tmdb:1677118: A documentary produced to commemorate the 60th anniversary of the landmark special-effects drama series 'Ultraman.' The special-effects TV drama 'Ultraman,' which first aired in 1966, achieved a peak viewership rating of 42.8% and sparked a social phenomenon. Even over 60 years since its birth, Tsuburaya Productions continues to release new Ultraman series works, beloved across generations and borders. This film is planned by filmmaker Kore-eda Hirokazu, known for 'Monsters' and 'Shoplifters,' and features numerous leading creators from film, special effects, and design. Filmmakers Guillermo del Toro, Kore-eda Hirokazu, and Nicolas Winding Refn, game creator Kojima Hideo, anime director Anno Hideaki, and special effects/film director Higuchi Shinji, among others active at the forefront of their fields both in Japan and abroad, offer their unique perspectives to unravel the question, 'What is Ultraman?' The film explores the worldview where the protagonist is a hero yet carefully depicts the background of the kaiju, and the strong appeal of the designs of both Ultraman and the monsters, while also shedding light on the ideas and work of Tsuburaya Eiji and the staff of that era, tracing the journey of how Ultraman spread across the world.
tmdb:1677894: A youth suspense film depicting the struggles and growth of a university student working on a documentary about an incident that occurred in a certain local city. University student Mayu Kuroda is tasked with creating a documentary for a class project based on her own high school experience. Back then, rumors spread that a male teacher, Nitta, had engaged in inappropriate sexual acts with her senior in the broadcasting club, Nojima, whom she admired. Articles in weekly magazines and social media posts drastically changed Nojima's life. Feeling this situation was unjust, Mayu intended to create a work that would serve as a warning about the information society by reflecting on that time. However, as she proceeds with research and filming alongside her university classmates, she is confronted with the reality that the local community is not welcoming the reopening of the case. Furthermore, facts she didn't know at the time and the various intentions of those involved and related parties come to light. Director Hiroki Inoue, highly acclaimed domestically and internationally for the short film 'Aza' and the VR live-action film 'Nagisa ni te', depicts social issues such as bullying, reputational damage via social media, and the insularity of local communities through an original script. Luna Toyota, in her first lead film role, naturally and delicately portrays the protagonist Mayu. Co-stars include Koshu Hirano from the special effects drama 'Ultraman Z', Kohei Yamashita from 'Toritsukushima', Yu Takaoka from the short film 'Tsunagaru', and Yuri Some no from 'Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!'.
tmdb:168040: After his cheesemaker father passes away, 18-year-old Totone is left to shoulder the family business and care for his seven-year-old sister. This film vividly depicts his daily life as he clumsily yet earnestly strives to carve out a path for himself.
tmdb:1680559: Novelist Jotaro Izumi (Sojiro Yoshimura) made a spectacular debut after winning the Bungei Prize. However, his success was short-lived; now, he spends his days in depravity, borrowing money from his editor, Eiji Matsumura (Kohshu Hirano), on the condition that he write. Pursued relentlessly by photographer Ranko Kijima (Aika Yukihira), he drifts into a relationship and moves into her home, yet the twisted desires writhing within him remain unfulfilled. It is then that Matsumura introduces him to a research subject: Anna Unabara (Suika Yamasaki), a woman once dubbed the "Beautiful Criminal" for swindling 30 million yen through sugar dating. Beneath her quiet and submissive facade lurks an inexplicable strangeness—and Jotaro begins to feel that she may be the one who can finally satisfy his desires.
tmdb:1694409: A human fantasy set in a mysterious beauty salon run by Death, where a woman who must spend her final days there reexamines her life through various encounters and farewells. Based on a proposal by Yoichi Umeki submitted for a Nihon University College of Art class assignment, with a screenplay by Kohei Taniguchi ('This Video Cannot Be Played THE MOVIE') and directed by Shinji Imaoka ('Reiko Iruka'). Hairdresser Miho Saeki, frustrated by troubles at work and in her private life, slips on stairs. Waking up, she is led by rookie Death Sakuma to a suspicious salon 'Meikup' (Makeup), where Death hairdressers touch up the deceased to connect them with loved ones for one last day. However, Miho's actual death is days away, and Sakuma jumped the gun. She stays at the salon until her death. Hinako Sakurai plays Miho, KANON from dance & vocal group STARGLOW plays Sakuma. Okabe Dai (comedy trio Hanako) plays the salon owner, Hirai Amon plays Miho's boyfriend, Inuzuka Kenta plays her salon manager, and Miho Jun plays her mother.
tmdb:1694487: A woman armed with a knife breaks into the office of a paranormal documentary production company. After injuring an employee, she reveals her motive: to "save humanity." She is apparently obsessed with a conspiracy theory claiming that "unless a certain videotape is returned to its rightful place, the human race will perish." The production crew tracks down the man spreading these theories online. He reveals that the video was once submitted to the "Shi-gazo" series and is a clip so terrifying it surpasses even the legendary "Kuniko." The crew unearths the tape and sets out to uncover the true identity of what is captured on screen. However, this was merely the entrance to a labyrinth with no exit, where countless horrors writhe in the shadows...
tmdb:1694504: A youth ensemble drama set on Wakasa Wada Beach in Takahama Town, Fukui Prefecture, the first beach in Asia to receive the international environmental certification "Blue Flag," depicting a young man lost and without dreams who meets lifeguards and grows through challenging trials. Yuki Otomo, a university junior, has no motivation for job hunting and is lost in life. Plagued by loneliness at being left behind by those around him and a sense of futility about the future, he is invited by his uncle to spend summer vacation in Fukui. One day, Yuki tries to save a drowning person but ends up drowning himself, and is rescued by members of the "Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club." Witnessing their love for the sea and their courage to act for others, a passionate feeling begins to stir in the apathetic Yuki's heart. Deciding to become a lifeguard, Yuki trains hard alongside his peers, but... Model and actor Nose Rin, who made his screen debut in "About a Place in the Kinki Region," makes his film lead debut as Yuki. Satoshi Tokushige plays the leader of the Wakasa Wada Lifesaving Club, Hina Irei plays a club member, Toru Kazama plays Yuki's uncle, and Tokuma Nishioka plays the chairman of the Takahama Town Water Rescue Association. Directed and written by Yoshihisa Kodama, known for "Oshorin," with the ending theme performed by singer-songwriter Hana Sekitori.
tmdb:1696868: An unconventional home drama depicting the daily life of a new father (Frankie), who works from home and is run ragged by his mischievous toddler yet raises him with abundant love. His chemistry with his on-screen wife Ikeuchi is excellent, and Bando and Miki are amusing as hopeless fathers.
tmdb:1719557: Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Jet Li, Donnie Yen... Yasuaki Kurata is the one and only active action actor who has engaged in fierce battles with countless legends. Now 80 years old and celebrating 60 years as an action actor, this legend takes on a new challenge! Directors Koichi Sakamoto, Kenji Tanigaki, and Yuji Shimomura—three currently active talents who are graduates of the Kurata Action Club—have taken the helm. Filming also took place in Hong Kong, resulting in a historic reunion on screen with Sammo Hung! The miraculous film 'Dream Story' follows a man who has dedicated his life to action. Be sure to see its full scope on the big screen!
tmdb:17234: Elementary school student Kōichi Uehara finds a large stone buried on a riverbank on his way home. Driven by curiosity, he cracks it open and discovers a dried-up, fossil-like creature inside. It is a baby kappa that has been in a state of suspended animation underground for a long time. Kōichi names it 'Kū' and begins living with it.
tmdb:173: In the 1860s, a series of shipwrecks caused by a mysterious sea monster occur across the globe. Marine biologist Professor Aronnax and his companions are dispatched by the U.S. government to investigate. One night, their vessel collides with a mysterious object: the Nautilus, a versatile submarine commanded by Captain Nemo, a brilliant scientist who harbors a deep hatred for authority and war. Invited by the captain, the professor and his group embark on an extraordinary journey to the depths of the ocean.
tmdb:1730:
Film director David Lynch passed away on January 15, 2025, at the age of 78. Since his 1976 debut *Eraserhead*, the master filmmaker captivated creators and audiences worldwide as the "King of Cult." He left behind only ten feature films, the final of which—2006’s *Inland Empire*—has been 4K remastered under Lynch’s own supervision. This is his most concentrated work, with Lynch himself handling everything from directing and screenwriting to cinematography, music, and editing. Starring Laura Dern as an actress who lands a lead role, the film depicts a nightmarish, absurdist drama where the boundaries between reality and cinema gradually blur. Regarding its alluringly inscrutable content, the director left only one explanation: "about a woman in trouble." This mystery-laden tale sparked polarized reactions upon its release and continues to be spoken of as a legend today.

【STORY】
Hollywood actress Nikki Grace (Laura Dern) is cast in *On High in Blue Tomorrows*, a remake of an unfinished Polish film titled *47*. Before long, she falls into an affair with her co-star Devon Berk (Justin Theroux)—mirroring the film's plot—and the movie's narrative begins to intertwine with her own life. As the boundary between reality and fiction dissolves, Nikki’s psyche is driven toward a total collapse.
tmdb:175: Jacques (Jean-Marc Barr) and Enzo (Jean Reno) grew up together as childhood friends on a Greek island. Years later, when they reunite on the Côte d'Azur for the first time in twenty years, Enzo invites Jacques to compete in a free-diving world championship held in Sicily, Italy. Meanwhile, Johanna (Rosanna Arquette), who had a chance encounter with Jacques in the Andes, travels from New York to Sicily under the pretext of a business trip.
tmdb:17729: Young trombonist Glenn Miller was always in search of a new sound. He joined a prestigious orchestra but left to focus on arranging. The turning point in his music came from his beloved wife Helen. Following her advice, he formed his own band and eventually achieved unprecedented popularity and fame. However, when World War II began, he volunteered for the Air Force. In late 1944, the plane carrying Glenn Miller disappeared over the English Channel... An emotional musical film, with numerous hit songs coloring the love and bond between the couple played by James Stewart and June Allyson!
tmdb:177945: Ryota (Fukuyama) is a company employee who has carved out his own life and enjoys smooth sailing. One day, a call from the hospital informs him that the son he has raised with love for six years is actually another couple's child, switched at birth. Through interactions with the family who raised his biological son, his values gradually begin to waver, and he grapples with what family and blood ties truly mean. Winner of the Jury Prize at the 66th Cannes Film Festival.
tmdb:17962: A fantasy drama by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Maborosi" fame, depicting the seven days between death and reaching heaven. Twenty-two deceased people arrive at a facility shrouded in mist. The staff waiting for them instruct them to choose the single most important memory from their lives within the seven days before they go to heaven. Some choose a memory immediately, while others struggle to decide. But the final day, when a screening will be held, steadily approaches. Starring ARATA in his film debut.
tmdb:18148: A timeless masterpiece by the master Yasujiro Ozu, this film depicts the changing family relationships in post-war Japan through the story of an elderly couple visiting their children in Tokyo. Using his signature "Ozu style"—characterized by low camera angles and static shots—he meticulously portrays the parent-child dynamic. Shukishi and Tomi, an elderly couple living in Onomichi, travel to Tokyo for the first time in a while to visit their children. However, their eldest son, Koichi, a doctor, and their eldest daughter, Shige, who runs a beauty salon, are both too busy with their own lives to pay much attention to their parents. Only Noriko, the widow of their second son who died in the war, shows them genuine kindness and consideration.
tmdb:18311: Director Wong Kar-wai's second feature film from 1990, this youth ensemble drama depicts the romantic entanglements of young people in 1960s Hong Kong with a sense of rushing visual beauty, catapulting Wong Kar-wai to international fame. Yuddy approaches Su, who works as a vendor at a soccer stadium, and they fall in love. However, Yuddy is troubled by not knowing his biological mother. After breaking up with Su, Yuddy spends a night with Mimi, a dancer at a nightclub. Leaving the room, Mimi encounters Yuddy's best friend Zeb, who falls in love with her at first sight. Tide, a policeman on night patrol, has feelings for Su, but she cannot forget Yuddy. The cast features Hong Kong cinema's biggest stars, including Leslie Cheung, Maggie Cheung, Carina Lau, Tony Leung, Andy Lau, and Jacky Cheung. First released in Japan in 1992. A digital remastered version was released in February 2018 at Bunkamura Le Cinema and other venues. A 4K restored version was released in December 2023 as part of the special screening "Wong Kar-wai: The Beginning."
tmdb:18352: Set in Prague, Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II, this dark comedy depicts how an ordinary citizen working at a funeral home is influenced by his pro-Nazi friend and the social climate, driving him toward a disastrous solution. Karel Kopfrkingl, who works as a cremator at a small Prague funeral home, is an ordinary man who loves his family. One day, he reunites with a war buddy from World War I, who has become a member of the Nazi Party. Persuaded by his friend to monitor the local Jewish community, Karel gradually becomes influenced by his friend and the social situation... The film portrays how an utterly ordinary person becomes a perpetrator, using beautiful yet eerie expressionistic imagery. This work, which exposes the terror of totalitarian ideology, was banned in its home country of Czechoslovakia and could not be shown until the fall of the communist regime in 1990. It won the Grand Prize at the 5th Sitges - Catalonian International Film Festival. In Japan, it will have its theatrical premiere in April 2026 as part of "Czech Film Masterpieces," a series featuring classics of the Czech New Wave.
tmdb:18872: Having witnessed grief work in his TV documentary 'However... In an Age of Welfare Cuts,' Kore-eda tackles this theme head-on in his first theatrical feature, based on the novel of the same name by Teru Miyamoto. Yumiko (Esumi), who carries childhood trauma, loses her husband to suicide in the midst of a happy marriage. Years later, she lives a peaceful life with a new family, but a lingering unease never fully fades. Against the backdrop of Noto's nature captured in long shots, the quiet rebirth of a woman's heart is depicted with a serene gaze.
tmdb:18910: The directorial debut of William Peter Blatty, known as the author of 'The Exorcist,' who adapted his own novel. Blatty wrote, directed, produced, and scripted this unique human drama set in an old castle used as a psychiatric hospital. In a remote mountain castle serving as a sanatorium, soldiers driven insane by the Vietnam War are gathered and treated. Among them is astronaut Billy Cutshaw, who was committed after going mad just before a rocket launch. One day, Navy psychiatrist Hudson Kane arrives at the facility. Kane listens sympathetically to the patients, but Cutshaw is defiant, and Kane soon begins to be plagued by nightmares. Won the Golden Globe for Best Screenplay. Stars Stacy Keach of 'Roadgames' and 'Escape from L.A.' Although never theatrically released in Japan, it will have its first theatrical screening in 2026 as part of the 'Shinjuku Hardcore Masterpiece Selection 2' special screening (April 17 - May 21, 2026, at CineMart Shinjuku).
tmdb:190060: Mekas established his unique "diary film" method with his first feature, *Walden* (1968). This work serves as a sequel of sorts, woven from 124 film sketches of friends he socialized with in New York between 1969 and 1984—the period surrounding the founding of Anthology Film Archives. It also stands as a precious record of the figures behind "Fluxus," the art movement that shaped the SoHo district. A deeper understanding of this context can be gained by referring to the book *Mekas no Yujin Nikki* (Mekas’s Diary of Friends), compiled by Mekas himself following the film's completion (published in 1989 by Shobunsha).
tmdb:19105: Iron Maiden is the definitive band of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal (NWOBHM) movement that emerged in the UK in the early 1980s. They made their debut in 1980 with the self-titled album *Iron Maiden*. Following the release of *Killers* the next year, Bruce Dickinson joined as the band's second lead singer. Their 1982 release, *The Number of the Beast*, became a massive global hit, selling over two million copies. They continued their ascent to the pinnacle of the heavy metal world with a succession of iconic albums, including *Piece of Mind* (1983) and *Powerslave* (1984). After several lineup changes, the band’s roster stabilized in the late 1990s. In 2008, they embarked on the "Somewhere Back in Time Tour," an unprecedented world tour that sent metalheads across the globe into a frenzy.
tmdb:1923: FBI Special Agent Chet Desmond vanishes mysteriously while investigating the murder of local waitress Teresa Banks. One year later, the evil entities lurking throughout the town begin to target the high school queen, Laura Palmer. At the same time, Special Agent Dale Cooper, who has taken over the investigation into the Teresa Banks case, resolves to unravel the profound mystery by drawing upon his unique gift—a sharp sixth sense.
tmdb:196929: Two years after the worldwide acclaim of "Freeze Die Come to Life," protagonist Valerka is now fifteen. As he prepares to bid farewell to his boyhood, the adult world has taken on an even more tragic aspect. His only emotional refuge is Valya, Galya’s younger sister. When Valerka is expelled from school and leaves town alone, Valya continues to send him letters, but...
tmdb:20108: The 7th feature film by master director Robert Bresson, known for "L'Argent," "Pickpocket," and "The Trial of Joan of Arc," released in 1966. Inspired by an episode from Dostoevsky's novel "The Idiot," it portrays the strange fate of a donkey and a young girl. In a small Pyrenean village, little Marie names a newborn donkey Balthazar and cherishes him. Ten years later, Balthazar is used for hard labor by a blacksmith but escapes the suffering and returns to Marie. The grown Marie rejoices at their reunion and takes Balthazar with her, but Gérard, who has feelings for her, becomes jealous and torments the donkey. Through the silent perspective of the donkey, the film calmly depicts human folly and ugliness, winning the Special Jury Prize at the Venice International Film Festival and earning acclaim as a masterpiece. Starring Anne Wiazemsky, who later appeared in many Godard films including "La Chinoise," in her film debut. First theatrically released in Japan in 1970, and again in 1995 distributed by France Eigasha. Revived in October 2020 in a 4K restored digital remaster. Also revived in 2026 as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
tmdb:203612: A documentary about the Sagrada Família, the century-spanning architectural project conceived by Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí, under construction since 1882 for over 130 years. Registered as a World Heritage Site in 2005, the Sagrada Família continues to captivate over three million visitors annually from around the world. As construction continues towards a projected completion in 2026, computers have been introduced on site, and staff repeatedly experiment to determine how to best reproduce Gaudí's vision with current technology. Incorporating footage from inside the site, inaccessible to outsiders, and interviews with architectural staff, the film unravels the project surrounding the Sagrada Família, including how the construction period, once said to require '300 years until completion,' has been shortened to a projected completion in 2026.
tmdb:20442: Like 'The Naked Spur,' this is a Technicolor Western directed by Anthony Mann and starring James Stewart, produced by William H. Wright of 'Violent Behavior' in 1953. The screenplay was written by up-and-coming radio and TV writing team Sam Rolfe and Harold Jack Bloom, cinematography by William C. Mellor of 'Cross Missouri,' and music by Bronisław Kaper of 'The Wolf of the North.' Co-stars include Janet Leigh of 'Blood Fight,' Robert Ryan of 'The Three Bad Men of the Wilderness,' newcomer Ralph Meeker of 'The Four Jeeps,' and Millard Mitchell of 'Singin' in the Rain.'
tmdb:20525: In the 15th year of the Genroku era. A young samurai (Okada) burdened by the duty to avenge his father travels from Shinshu to Edo and hides out in a tenement slum. The film depicts how his resolve begins to waver as he interacts with the residents of the tenement. While weaving the story of the Ako Ronin's raid into the background, director Kore-eda turns it on its head, aiming for 'a story where the weak are affirmed as they are.' This ambitious work marks Kore-eda's first deep dive into a narrative world, having previously been conscious of the distance between fiction and nonfiction in his live-action films.
tmdb:2061: Frank, a highly skilled drug pusher, makes money with his partner Tony by carrying out jobs for drug kingpin Milo. After taking a huge loan from Milo for a large deal, a police raid causes the deal to fail, and Frank loses the money, facing relentless pressure from his boss to repay the debt. A crime action drama that depicts a man spiraling into a hellish debt trap in the underworld of rampant drug trafficking, pushed to his absolute limits, all rendered in dark, stylish visuals. This is Nicolas Winding Refn's landmark debut film, hailed as the Danish film that first achieved worldwide success as a gangster movie.
tmdb:20874: A deadpan sci-fi comedy made in Soviet-era Georgia in 1986, which became a huge hit in the USSR at the time. One day, a student named Gedevan asks construction engineer Mashkov for help, looking troubled, saying, 'There are some men over there who claim to be aliens.' Mashkov, who doesn't believe in aliens, presses a button on a space travel device the men were holding, and in the next instant, Mashkov and Gedevan are warped to the planet Pluke in the Kin-Dza-Dza Nebula, far from Earth. There, for some reason, Earth matches are extremely valuable, and the two try to use the value of matches to somehow return to Earth... Culturally popular in Japan as well, it was first introduced at the 'Soviet SF Film Festival' held in Tokyo in 1989, later released in a new print in 2001 and a digital remaster in August 2016. In May 2021, to coincide with the release of the animated version 'Ku! Kin-Dza-Dza,' the live-action film had its fourth theatrical release.
tmdb:238937: Tokijiro sets out on a journey with the wife and child of a man he killed out of obligation to the underworld. This eighth film adaptation of a classic play, directed by Tai Kato, crystallizes supreme lyricism into a poignant love story, resulting in a masterpiece.
tmdb:24128: A live documentary of the rock band Talking Heads. Capturing their 1983 stage performance at the Pantages Theatre with various camera angles, it conveys the raw energy and excitement directly.
tmdb:25050: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Maborosi" quietly captures the scene of a family gathering at their elderly parents' home for the first time in a while, bringing out the joys and sorrows of life in this home drama. One summer day, the second son, Ryota, and the eldest daughter, Chinami, bring their respective families to the home where former doctor Kyohei Yokoyama and his wife Toshiko live alone. The Yokoyama family spends a casual time together, but this day happens to be the anniversary of the death of their eldest son, Junpei, who passed away 15 years ago.
tmdb:25051: Four men and women, all family members of the perpetrators of a murder case committed by a cult three years earlier, meet once a year to pay their respects at the lake where the ashes were scattered. That year, their car goes missing as they try to return from the lake. Stranded, they end up spending the night at a lodge where the cult members once lived, along with a former cult member who also lost his motorcycle. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "After Life" fame. Starring ARATA, Yusuke Iseya, Susumu Terajima, Tadanobu Asano, and others.
tmdb:25053: Based on a short manga by Yoshiie Gouda, this allegorical work uses the love story of a sentient love doll to lead viewers into philosophical contemplation about the emptiness and life of modern people. With cinematographer Mark Lee Ping-bing and art director Yohei Taneda on board, the fictional setting is brilliantly visualized using analog special effects.
tmdb:2517: Keiko (YOU) and four children, including Akira (Yagira), live in a single apartment room under false pretenses. When Keiko eventually stops coming home, the children are left to fend for themselves, but their financial situation gradually becomes dire. Inspired by a real-life child abandonment case, the film delicately portrays modern social issues such as neglect, young carers, and those who fall through the cracks of the welfare system, earning high international acclaim.
tmdb:25657: A drama depicting the peaceful daily lives of three Japanese women set in a small restaurant in Helsinki, the capital of Finland. Based on the novel of the same name by author Yōko Mure, adapted and directed by Naoko Ogigami, who gained attention with her feature directorial debut "Barber Yoshino." Japanese woman Sachie opens a small restaurant called "Kamome Diner" on a street corner in Helsinki, but no customers come. One day, Sachie happens to meet a Japanese tourist named Midori and asks her to help out at the restaurant. Soon, a variety of colorful characters start coming to Sachie's shop one after another... Satomi Kobayashi, Hairi Katagiri, and Masako Motai play the three Japanese women, with Markku Peltola from "The Man Without a Past" co-starring.
tmdb:26039: A hard-boiled action film directed by British master John Boorman in 1967, early in his career, starring Hollywood legend Lee Marvin ('The Dirty Dozen,' 'The Professionals'). Based on Richard Stark's crime novel 'The Hunter' (featuring the character Parker), it depicts a man's revenge against his betrayers, blending avant-garde New Wave techniques with the psychedelic culture of the American West Coast. Walker, at the request of his friend Reese, robs a criminal organization's deal at the abandoned Alcatraz prison and steals a large sum of money. However, Reese betrays Walker, shooting him and fleeing with his $93,000 share and Walker's wife, Lyn. As his consciousness fades, memories and fantasies swirl through Walker's mind. Surviving, Walker sets out to recover his share and exact revenge, tracking Reese down. Marvin delivers a powerful performance as the ruthless avenger Walker, with Angie Dickinson ('Rio Bravo') and John Vernon ('Dirty Harry') co-starring.
tmdb:261558: After serving two years in the army prison for stealing an officer's wallet, Kitani returns to his unit. Inside the unit, the squad leader and senior soldiers bully the new recruits. In particular, Private First Class Aita, a university graduate, is subjected to daily violence. Kitani, however, refuses to take part in the bullying. Aita grows fond of Kitani and they become close, but he learns that Kitani has been selected for frontline deployment. Both Kitani's imprisonment and his selection for the front lines were the result of factional infighting.
tmdb:263232: An erotic film directed by Roger Vadim, based on the sensual novel 'Les Liaisons Dangereuses'. Set in 19th-century France, it depicts the affair between a playboy count and a married woman. The bewitching performances of two charismatic actresses are captivating.
tmdb:26347: A feature film by French master Jean-Luc Godard, shot in the war-torn city of Sarajevo as a prayer for world peace. Based on Dante's epic poem 'The Divine Comedy,' it is structured in three parts: 'Hell,' 'Purgatory,' and 'Paradise.' Visiting Sarajevo for a lecture, Godard finds a historical crossroads in the rebuilding city, which is also a history of human conflict and massacre. Using the asymmetry between Israel and Palestine, and Judaism and Islam as examples, Godard discusses the dominant structures of conflict in the world. 'Hell' is composed of montages of war footage; 'Purgatory' depicts the interaction between Godard, invited to Sarajevo for a lecture, and a female student named Olga; and 'Paradise' shows the peaceful world Olga reaches after her death. Godard appears as himself, along with Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish and Spanish novelist Juan Goytisolo, who appear under their real names. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
tmdb:266598: A puppy named Rock rises up with stray dogs to defeat Killer the tiger, who killed his mother. Drawing on 'Chushingura' and Sazanami Iwaya's children's literature 'Koganemaru,' this film more consciously adopts Disney's style compared to earlier feature-length works. The stateless urban depictions and the action in a snow-covered amusement park, inspired by an idea from Osamu Tezuka, exude a chic and modern sensibility.
tmdb:26868: A massacre occurs deep in the Tohoku mountains, killing most of a village's residents. A self-defense force special unit member, Misawa, who was training in the mountains, happens upon the scene, kills the perpetrator, and rescues the sole survivor—a village girl named Yoriko. Later, after retiring, Misawa adopts Yoriko and works as an insurance salesperson. One day, he rescues a female journalist named Tomoko from an attacker, but she is being targeted because she tried to expose the corruption of a local businessman, Oba. Meanwhile, Detective Kitano, who suspects Misawa of being the massacre killer, continues to shadow him.
tmdb:27432: The feature debut of Charles Burnett, a filmmaker who quietly revolutionized American cinema by depicting the daily lives and humanity of African Americans, released in 1977. It portrays the everyday existence of African American workers living on the fringes of Los Angeles with a realistic gaze and poetic visual beauty. Set in the Watts district of Los Angeles in the early 1970s, still bearing the scars of the Watts riots. Stan works at a sheep slaughterhouse to support his wife and two children, living an empty daily life. Exhausted physically and mentally by labor and poverty, he withdraws into himself, while his wife grows increasingly lonely. Directed by Burnett as his graduate thesis film while a student at UCLA Film School, it was shot in Watts using a mostly amateur cast of people he knew. Long unreleased due to music copyright issues, it finally had a theatrical release in the US in 2007. The 4K restoration completed in 2025 replaces the music in the final scene with Dinah Washington's "Unforgettable," as Burnett originally intended. It won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Forum section of the 31st Berlin International Film Festival in 1981. In Japan, it will have its first theatrical release in the 4K restored version as part of the special screening series "Charles Burnett: Everyday Blues" (starting February 7, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:275: An unconventional crime suspense film by the Coen Brothers, laced with black humor. In snow-covered Fargo, Minnesota, car salesman Jerry, drowning in debt, plots to have his wife Jean kidnapped to extort a ransom from her wealthy father. But when the two hired kidnappers shoot a police officer and a witness, the case spirals out of control. Winner of multiple film awards, including the Academy Awards for Best Original Screenplay and Best Actress.
tmdb:2767:
A love story from French visionary Leos Carax, following *Boy Meets Girl* and *Bad Blood*, this film serves as the final chapter of his trilogy centered on a young man named Alex. On the Pont-Neuf, the oldest and most beautiful bridge in Paris, a street performer named Alex encounters Michèle, an art student wandering the streets while suffering from the pain of a broken heart and a seemingly incurable eye disease. Before long, the two begin living together on the bridge, deepening their bond amidst their shared loneliness. Michèle struggles with lingering feelings for a cellist named Julien and the fear of losing her sight as an artist, while Alex has lived his life without ever knowing a true connection to others. Gradually, a profound love blossoms between them. However, Michèle eventually learns that her parents are searching for her and that a cure for her eye disease has been found...

Denis Lavant returns to play the protagonist Alex, following his roles in *Boy Meets Girl* and *Bad Blood*, while Juliette Binoche portrays Michèle. Produced in 1991 and released in Japan in 199
tmdb:27958: A crime suspense film directed by William Friedkin, who won an Academy Award for "The French Connection" and had a worldwide hit with "The Exorcist," released in 1980, set against the backdrop of New York City's underground gay culture at the time. A series of murders targeting only gay men occurs in New York at night. Police detective Burns, given a secret mission, goes undercover in S&M clubs frequented by gay men, pretending to be homosexual. Wandering the depths of male sexuality night after night, Burns wears himself down both physically and mentally, finally finding a clue to the killer... Based on actual murders of gay men that occurred between 1973 and 1979, Friedkin wrote the script after experiences including meeting with a suspect who had also appeared in "The Exorcist." Considered the first Hollywood film to openly depict male same-sex S&M sex, it faced protests from the time of its announcement through its release for allegedly promoting homophobia, and was not a commercial success. However, since the 2000s, it has been re-evaluated as a valuable record of gay culture before the global spread of HIV.
tmdb:28436: The directorial debut of Robert Wise, the master behind "West Side Story" and "The Sound of Music," made in 1944. This is a sequel to the cult horror film "Cat People" directed by Jacques Tourneur. A lonely, imaginative girl named Amy finds a beautiful ring in a dilapidated old house in her neighborhood. When she returns home and makes a wish on the ring, a beautiful woman named Irena appears before her. Amy becomes friends with Irena, whom only she can see, but...
tmdb:287765: A black man is murdered in an elevator at a luxury hotel in Tokyo, leaving behind the word 'Stoha' and a poetry collection by Saijo Yaso. Fashion designer Kyoko Yasugi and her son appear and disappear along the investigative trail. Detective Muneyori travels to the United States to trace the black man's past. The unexpected relationship between Kyoko and the black man, as well as the connection between the American detective and Detective Muneyori, comes to light.
tmdb:290098: Directed by Park Chan-wook of 'Oldboy' fame, this suspense drama is based on Sarah Waters' novel 'Fingersmith' but transposed to 1930s Japanese-occupied Korea. Sook-hee, a girl raised by a gang of swindlers in a slum, is approached by a con man known as Count Fujiwara with a plan: seduce Lady Hideko, an heiress to a vast fortune, marry her, then commit her to an asylum and steal her wealth. Agreeing to take part, Sook-hee begins working as a maid named Ok-ju at a remote mansion where Hideko lives with her domineering, Japanophile uncle Kouzuki. But as devoted Sook-hee gradually opens Hideko's heart, Sook-hee herself finds herself drawn to the woman she is supposed to betray. Kim Min-hee plays Hideko, while newcomer Kim Tae-ri was cast as Sook-hee through auditions. Ha Jung-woo plays the Count, and Cho Jin-woong plays Uncle Kouzuki.
tmdb:29269: A love story adapted from Haruki Murakami's short story of the same name, directed by Jun Ichikawa of 'Tokiwa: The Manga Apartment' and 'Tsugumi,' starring Issey Ogata and Rie Miyazawa. Tony Takitani, born as the son of a trombonist, loses his mother shortly after birth and grows up carrying loneliness. After working at a design company, he becomes an independent illustrator, falls in love with a woman, and marries her. But their happy days are short-lived; his wife dies in an accident. Feeling his loneliness, he hires a woman who closely resembles his late wife as an assistant and tries to get used to her death by having the assistant wear the vast collection of clothes his shopaholic wife left behind... Issey Ogata plays the protagonist Tony Takitani and his father, Rie Miyazawa plays Tony's wife and the woman who resembles her, with Hidetoshi Nishijima providing narration. The music is composed by Ryuichi Sakamoto. The film won the Special Jury Prize, the FIPRESCI Prize, and the Youth Jury Award at the 57th Locarno International Film Festival in 2004. A 4K remastered version was re-released in 2026.
tmdb:293:
Robert Redford’s third directorial feature is an adaptation of the autobiographical debut novel by former professor Norman Maclean, written at the age of 74 (and nominated for the 1977 Pulitzer Prize). Set amidst the natural splendor of Montana, the film portrays the enduring bonds of family through luminous cinematography (winner of the Best Cinematography Oscar at the 65th Academy Awards), a lyrical score, and a superb ensemble cast.

In the 1910s, in the small town of Missoula, Montana, brothers Norman and Paul are the sons of a Presbyterian minister. Though their personalities are polar opposites—Norman is serious and studious while Paul is free-spirited and reckless—they are united by their shared devotion to fly fishing. After leaving home for university, Norman returns years later as a young man. He finds that Paul has become a newspaper reporter and an even more skilled fisherman, but has also become dangerously entangled in high-stakes poker. Norman watches over his brother with growing concern, but...
tmdb:298467: The pinnacle of Japanese musicals, depicting a salaryman struggling in the battle for foreign tourists in Tokyo just before the Olympics. Throughout the film, talented performers sing and dance, and Frankie's astonishing physical abilities leave you in awe. The grand group dance in 'Man Alone' is especially breathtaking.
tmdb:298621: The second feature film by Guy Gilles, a director re-evaluated since the 2000s as a 'forgotten master of the French New Wave,' depicting a woman living with the memory of her lover who chose death. The present is shown in black-and-white, and fragments of recollection in color, delicately and melancholically portraying the memory of love and the pain of absence. Jeanne lives with the memory of her deceased lover Jean. Jean rejected social order and the bourgeois world, found no place in the Beat generation, and chose death. Unaware of his death, Jeanne feels him always by her side, existing like a ghost. Masha Meril, known for 'A Time for Loving' and 'Belle de Jour,' plays the protagonist Jeanne, and Patrick Jouané, an actor who met Guy Gilles during the filming of 'Le Rempart des Béguines' and became an irreplaceable presence in his life and work, plays the deceased lover Jean. The film was released in Japanese theaters in April 2026.
tmdb:2998: Italian master Michelangelo Antonioni, who won top prizes at all three major film festivals (Berlin, Venice, Cannes) in the 1960s, made this film after moving to America in 1970. Set in Los Angeles and Death Valley, it depicts the psychological landscape of love between a man and a woman. In the late 1960s, amidst the peak of counterculture, with university protests raging and students clashing with armed police, Mark grows tired of futile debates at student gatherings. He grabs a gun and confronts the police officers cracking down on campus, but misses his chance to fire and flees. He then steals a Cessna at an airfield and takes to the sky. Meanwhile, Daria, a secretary at a Los Angeles real estate company, is driving across the vast desert to attend a meeting. The two meet by chance and arrive at Zabriskie Point, overlooking Death Valley... The leads are newcomers Mark Frechette and Daria Halprin, whom Antonioni scouted on the streets. The soundtrack effectively features music by Pink Floyd, Jerry Garcia of the Grateful Dead, Kaleidoscope, John Fahey, The Rolling Stones, and The Youngbloods. Released in Japan in 1970, it also had a late-show release in 1996. A revival release is scheduled for 2026, the first in 30 years.
tmdb:300590: Ginji, driven from his hometown, returns after ten years... This is a representative work marking the starting point of Tai Kato's unique style, with actors wearing no makeup, low-angle cameras, and simultaneous sound recording.
tmdb:303629: The turbulent life of gambler Senkichi, who continues to love one woman. Set in Kyoto at the end of the Edo period, this powerful portrayal of unadorned love between a man and a woman stands as Tai Kato's final, crowning live-action film.
tmdb:30497: A giant man wearing human skin wanders with a chainsaw in hand... Just how much human blood has soaked into his filthy apron? A horror film inspired by a real-life killer from Wisconsin. In rural Texas, five young people are on a road trip. When they run out of gas and stop at a farmhouse to rest, they are swept into a gruesome “festival.” Facing the masked man “Leatherface” and his sinister family—amidst inescapable despair, a night of terror begins.
tmdb:305588: A cheerful young man moves to Tokyo to help at a relative's milk shop and struggles to outdo his business rivals. A film adaptation of a popular radio drama, this is an early representative work of Frankie Sakai, known as a hidden gem of slapstick comedy.
tmdb:30617: Kamen Rider Decade, aka Kadoya Tsukasa, arrives in a "certain world." In this world, for some reason, the photos Tsukasa takes do not distort the image. Suddenly, a certain Western-style mansion comes to mind. Following faint memories, Tsukasa reaches the mansion, where he meets a girl who calls herself his sister, Kadoya Sayo. Tsukasa becomes convinced this is his own world. However, even in this world, the "collapse of worlds" is progressing. Sayo's servant, Tsukikage Nobuhiko, claims that the cause of the world's collapse lies in the Riders born in each world, and declares that to stop it, they must decide on a single "strongest Rider."
tmdb:313297: Long ago in Japan. A boy named Kubo, who lost his left eye, lives with his ailing mother. Playing a magical shamisen inherited from his mother, he earns a living by telling the story of a samurai named Hanzo in the village. On the night of the Bon festival, two 'Sisters of the Dark' who claim to be his mother's sisters appear and attack Kubo, but his mother tells him to gather his father's 'sword, armor, and helmet' and magically sends Kubo far away. Beginning his journey, Kubo makes allies of a female monkey and a male stag beetle while searching for the 'sword, armor, and helmet'.
tmdb:314186: During the early days of TV anime, orders were unstable, so to secure steady theatrical commissions, a medium-length film series called "B Works" was planned (conventional feature-length films were called "A Works"). Based on Shotaro Ishinomori's popular sci-fi manga, the film employed TV anime staff such as Keiichiro Kimura, the animation director of "Rainbow Sentai Robin," and utilized TV production efficiency techniques. While there were changes from the original manga, such as turning one of the characters into a child, the battles unfold across land, sea, and air, offering high entertainment value, and the composition shows awareness of widescreen framing.
tmdb:314223: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's words, 'My life is a fairy tale,' this musical drama weaves together tales like 'The Red Shoes' and 'Thumbelina' while depicting Andersen's boyhood. The night sky sparkles with colorful stars, and the orchestra's melodies envelop the story. The art by Reiji Koyama and the music by Seiichiro Uno sweetly bring this fairy-tale world to life.
tmdb:315846: A story spanning one year in the lives of three sisters (Ayase, Nagasawa, Kaho) who, after the death of their father who left home 15 years ago and with whom they had lost touch, come to live with their half-sister Suzu (Hirose), who has lost her own family. Based on the best-selling manga by Yoshida Akimi, it carefully depicts the town of Kamakura, where the story is set, and the changing seasons, while bringing to light the love and sorrows of women of different generations.
tmdb:32568: A social satire comedy that depicts the fate of a scientist obsessed with developing a 'miracle fiber' that never gets dirty, delving into the fundamental contradictions of capitalism. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Alexander Mackendrick, known for 'The Ladykillers.' Sidney, a scientist working in the British textile industry, spends his days experimenting to develop a fiber that never gets dirty and never frays, no matter how much it's washed. He builds strange contraptions in a corner of the factory, remaining expressionless and unfazed by the lack of understanding around him. With the backing of the company president and his daughter Daphne, Sidney finally completes the 'miracle fiber,' but... The lead role of the scientist Sidney is played by the renowned actor Alec Guinness, known for 'Star Wars' and 'The Bridge on the River Kwai.' This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
tmdb:326598: Shizuka Mita is a 20-year-old woman who works hard to become an actress as a trainee at the theater troupe "Sea." Moriguchi, a 26-year-old former troupe member now working at a real estate agency, first notices sincere Shizuka in a park. Shizuka prepares for the lead role audition in the troupe's next production, "The Tragedy of W," but her peer Kaori lands the part, and Shizuka is assigned a minor role with only a single line at the beginning of the story. Downcast after failing the audition, Moriguchi confides in her about his own psychological struggles as an actor. He then proposes marriage on the condition that she never becomes a star, and conversely promises to send a large bouquet to her dressing room as a farewell if she succeeds as an actress.
tmdb:32961: A crime comedy that depicts, with ironic humor, how two men's gold bullion heist plan takes an unexpected turn. One of the 'Ealing Comedies,' a series of comedy films produced at Ealing Studios in the UK from the late 1930s to the mid-1950s, directed by Charles Crichton, who was later nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director for 'A Fish Called Wanda.' Henry, a serious man who has worked as a bank security guard for 20 years, conspires with his friend Pendlebury, a souvenir shop owner, to steal a shipment of gold bullion. After successfully pulling off the heist, they process the gold into miniature Eiffel Towers to smuggle it abroad, but in a lounge at the Eiffel Tower in Paris, they accidentally sell them to a group of schoolchildren on a trip from England... Alec Guinness of 'Star Wars' fame plays Henry, and Stanley Holloway of 'My Fair Lady' plays Pendlebury. A young Audrey Hepburn appears in a single scene. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay at the 25th Academy Awards in 1953. This film is part of the special screening series 'The Golden Age of British Ealing Comedies' (June 20–July 17, 2026, at Shinjuku K's Cinema).
tmdb:331322: An entertainment film based on Arima Yorichika's original work "Kisaburo Ichidai," adapted by Kikushima Ryuzo and directed by Masumura Yasuzo. Its success led to a series of nine films. The dynamic duo of the outrageous protagonist played by Katsu Shintaro and the intellectual officer played by Tamura Takahiro are the highlight.
tmdb:338371: Mitsu's birthday. Natsuko buys matching Virgo necklaces and a rose. However, a white handkerchief is hanging in the apartment window. It's the signal that Mitsu's lover, Hideo, is there. Natsuko, who has secretly fallen in love with Mitsu, approaches Hideo in order to have Mitsu all to herself... On a midsummer afternoon, a shocking ending that will shake the world.
tmdb:339: On the planet Earth, in five cities—Los Angeles, New York, Paris, Rome, and Helsinki—five taxi drivers pick up passengers. Five stories unfolding simultaneously on the same night. This film features the strange humor and brilliantly sharp dialogue common to Jarmusch’s work, and the underlying sense of desolate emptiness remains as potent as ever. While his films often polarize audiences due to their unique atmosphere, this entry is relatively accessible and crafted to be enjoyed by a wide range of people. The New York segment and the Paris segment starring Roberto Benigni are particularly recommended.
tmdb:342737: From director Mike Mills, who drew on his own gay father for "Beginners," comes a story now centered on his mother. Set in Santa Barbara in 1979, it depicts a special summer for 15-year-old Jamie, his single mother Dorothea, and the people around them. Dorothea, a single mother struggling with how to raise her adolescent son Jamie, asks her roommate, photographer Abbie, and Jamie's childhood friend Julie, who lives nearby, to help him out. Starring as the mother Dorothea, Annette Bening was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy. Elle Fanning ("Maleficent") plays Julie, and Greta Gerwig ("Frances Ha") plays Abbie.
tmdb:354433: It's Laura's birthday. Hamtaro has prepared a present, but Laura ignores him, and in frustration he runs away from home. Seeing this, the Ham-Hams are about to help Hamtaro run away when a mysterious fairy hamster appears and takes everyone to Ham-Ham Land, a dream world where only hamsters live. But Hamtaro can't stop thinking about Laura. Hearing from the fairy hamster about 'magic sunflower seeds' that allow hamsters to talk to humans, Hamtaro sets out on an adventure to find them. But what awaits?
tmdb:354570: A small-town barber who has returned from the war unexpectedly finds himself put on trial as a war criminal. This film version, directed by screenwriter Hashimoto himself, is based on a television drama that won an Art Festival Award. A legendary work that portrays the absurdity and cruelty of war, with Frankie's heartfelt performance that shakes the soul.
tmdb:354759: Starring four women with no acting experience, this film portrays the anxieties and worries of ordinary women in their late 30s through a tense 317-minute drama. Directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi, known for challenging works like the 4-hour-plus epic "Intimacies" (using film school students) and the Tohoku documentary trilogy ("The Sound of the Waves," "Voices from the Waves," "Singing in the Dark"), the film won the Best Actress award for its four leads at the 68th Locarno International Film Festival in Switzerland. Akari, Sakurako, Fumi, and Jun, all in their late 30s, thought they were best friends who could tell each other anything. However, it is revealed that Jun had been hiding her year-long divorce negotiations. Shaken by this, the four women take a trip to Arima Onsen for a brief escape and enjoy a fun time together, but...
tmdb:3549:
Academy Award nominee for Best Foreign Language Film. An emotional human drama that inspired a Hollywood remake.

Jacob, a Danish man dedicated to helping orphans in India, receives an offer for a massive donation from Jørgen, a businessman back in his home country. Returning home, Jacob finalizes the deal with Jørgen, only to be invited to his daughter's wedding. There, an unexpected reunion leads him to a shocking discovery...

Mads plays this role:
Jacob, a naive idealist with a secret who runs an orphanage in India. Beloved by the children, he is a gentle soul who evokes a sense of tenderness, yet he harbors a hidden past...
tmdb:355135: Hamtaro had a dream. It was a dream of a beautiful hamster princess... 'Help me... Please... Come here quickly...' The princess was trapped inside a soap bubble, tears in her eyes. Even after waking up, Hamtaro can't stop worrying about the princess from his dream. So, he and the Ham-Hams decide to go rescue her. They arrive at the 'Hamja Kingdom,' the homeland of hamsters with a history of 8686 in the Ham Calendar, surrounded by desert. The sky is dark, and the hamsters living there seem downcast. No wonder—Princess Shera of the Hamja Kingdom, who was engaged to Prince Hamuha of the neighboring country, has been kidnapped by a mysterious cat that suddenly appeared and trapped her just like in Hamtaro's dream. That cat wants to marry Princess Shera and take over the kingdom! At this rate, the princess and the kingdom are in danger! Can Hamtaro and the Ham-Hams save the princess and protect the hamsters' homeland? An adventure of love and courage begins now.
tmdb:355345: Based on 'Nobody's Boy.' Even after being sold by his stepfather to traveling performers, young Remi never loses heart. The background art incorporates elements from diverse European masterpieces by Millet and Monet, while Yugo Serikawa's masterful use of dramatic pauses heightens the arduous journey. Frankie Sakai's voice performance as Remi's sidekick Capi, with his playful demeanor, offers a refreshing respite amid the relentless tragedy.
tmdb:35717: The fourth feature film by French wunderkind Leos Carax, released eight years after 'The Lovers on the Bridge.' An adaptation of the novel 'Pierre' by 19th-century American author Herman Melville, written the year after his masterpiece 'Moby-Dick.' Shifting the setting to modern-day Paris, it uses emotional imagery and sound to depict the intense, racing love of a man and woman swept up by fate and drawn into despair. Pierre, a young novelist living in a Norman castle, enjoys a wealthy, contented rural life with his mother Marie and fiancée Lucie. One day, Isabelle, a Bosnian refugee claiming to be Pierre's half-sister, appears. Drawn to Isabelle's charm, Pierre abandons everything and heads to Paris with her. Guillaume Depardieu, son of Gérard Depardieu, passionately plays Pierre, and Katerina Golubeva, known for 'Paris at Night,' plays Isabelle. Catherine Deneuve co-stars as Pierre's mother Marie. Cinematography is by Éric Gautier, known for 'My King,' and music is by singer-songwriter Scott Walker. A 4K restored version will be re-released in February 2026.
tmdb:36095: A masterpiece of psychological suspense in Japanese film history, directed by the brilliant Kiyoshi Kurosawa and starring Kōji Yakusho. A series of bizarre murders occur one after another. While the perpetrators of each case have no connection, the victims all have an X-shaped cut from their neck to their chest, all the assailants are arrested near the crime scene immediately after the incident, and none of the killers had a clear intent to murder just before the act. Detective Takabe, whose wife suffers from a mental illness, is assigned to the investigation but struggles to find a common thread among the perpetrators. Around the same time, a murder with the same modus operandi occurs on a beach near Tokyo, and a young man named Mamiya, who has no memory of being near the scene, is taken into custody. Takabe discovers that Mamiya is a former medical student and realizes he has been using hypnosis to trigger the series of events, but...
tmdb:366331:
<Director’s Statement>

I felt a desire to record this event. I am a historian and a sociologist. I believed that what I must do now is to document this and preserve it for future generations.

I had never made a film before. I had never even been interested in filmmaking. However, gathering fragments of historical records and weaving them into a single world is exactly what I have done in my previous writings. Whether the medium I handled was text or video was of no consequence in this instance.

It goes without saying that this is not a work I created alone. The people who filmed on-site at the time and those who sat for interviews all cooperated without compensation.

Above all, the protagonists of this film are every single person who appears in it. they are diverse in gender, generation, social status, nationality, origin, and ideology. I found the sight of such varied people gathering in a single place to be both a rare occurrence and something profoundly powerful and beautiful.

Such miraculous moments rarely visit a nation or a society. As a historian, I know this to be true. What I have done—what I set out to do—is simply to record such a moment, and nothing more.

I believe this is a film that can be interpreted in many ways. After viewing it, I hope you will share your honest thoughts with the person sitting next to you. It is the audience, and society as a collective, that gives meaning to a film. From that dialogue, I believe something new will be born, both for you and for society.
tmdb:36832: A science fiction film set in a near-future New York ten years after a social-democratic liberation revolution. Now hailed as a classic of feminist cinema, the film uses a documentary-style approach to depict women uniting across lines of gender, race, and class to confront the oppression that persists even in the post-revolutionary era.
tmdb:369557: A semi-autobiographical work by director John Carney of "Begin Again" and "Once," this youth drama depicts the love and friendship of a boy who forms a band to impress a girl he likes, set to 1980s British sounds. In 1985 Dublin, Ireland, struggling through a severe recession, 14-year-old Conor is forced to transfer to a rough public school after his father loses his job. At home, his parents constantly fight, pushing the family to the brink of collapse. Conor's only solace in his miserable days is watching music videos from neighboring London on TV with his music-obsessed older brother. One day, captivated by the mature charm of a girl named Raphina he sees on the street, Conor invites her to appear in a music video for his band. Hurriedly forming a band, Conor begins intense training to create a video that will amaze the London music scene...
tmdb:374671: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Our Little Sister" and "Like Father, Like Son" teams up with Atsushi Abe for the third time, following "Still Walking" and "I Wish," in this human drama centered on a man who can't grow up and his aging mother, portraying a family living a present different from the future they once dreamed of. Ryota is a middle-aged man who won a literary prize 15 years ago but hasn't been successful since, still chasing his dream of becoming a writer. He currently works at a detective agency to make ends meet, but makes excuses to himself and others that it's "research for his novel." Still hung up on his ex-wife, Kyoko, he is shocked to discover she has a new boyfriend while "staking out" her apartment. One day, Ryota, Kyoko, and their 11-year-old son Shingo gather at the apartment of his mother, Toshiko, who lives alone in a housing complex. Stranded by a typhoon, they end up spending the night together. Kirin Kiki delivers a wonderful performance as the protagonist's mother, with a stellar supporting cast including Yoko Maki, Satomi Kobayashi, and Lily Franky.
tmdb:37959: High school senior Sugihara has South Korean nationality, but usually doesn't think about it. He starts dating a girl named Sakurai and thinks he must confess his nationality to her someday, when a tragedy befalls a close friend of the same nationality. Based on the Naoki Prize-winning novel "GO" by Kinichi Kaneshiro. Directed by Isao Yukisada, who won the International Critics' Award at the previous year's Busan Film Festival for "Himawari." Screenplay by Kankuro Kudo of the TV series "Ikebukuro West Gate Park." Co-starring popular young actors including Yosuke Kubozuka from that show and Ko Shibasaki from "Battle Royale."
tmdb:38047: Directed by Kiyoshi Aoyama of 'Helpless,' this human drama depicts the journey of recovery for people traumatized by a bus-jacking incident. It won the FIPRESCI Prize and the Ecumenical Jury Prize at the 53rd Cannes International Film Festival in 2000. A bus-jacking occurs in a regional city in Kyushu, and many passengers are killed. The only survivors are the driver, Sawai, and two siblings: junior high school student Naoki and elementary school student Kozue. All three are deeply scarred. Two years later, Sawai, who had disappeared leaving his family behind, returns to town. Around the same time, a series of murders occur in the area, and suspicion falls on Sawai. Learning that the siblings are living alone, Sawai visits their home and begins living with them. Joined by the siblings' cousin, Akihiko, the four set out on a journey in a bus driven by Sawai... Kōji Yakusho plays Sawai, while real-life siblings Shō Miyazaki and Aoi Miyazaki play Naoki and Kozue. Following director Kiyoshi Aoyama's death in March 2022, a digital master complete version was released in theaters that May as a memorial screening.
tmdb:381902: Five hundred years after the violent Son Goku was imprisoned under Five Elements Mountain, he is freed from his seal by the monk Sanzo, who is heading to India, and joins the journey as Sanzo's bodyguard. Along the way, the group gains new companions, but they are confronted by the demoness Hakukotsu-fujin, who seeks to kill Sanzo in order to maintain her own eternal beauty. Using various schemes, Hakukotsu-fujin finally captures Sanzo.
tmdb:384024: The debut feature film by Lizzie Borden (b. 1958) examines a New York feminist collective. After being screened only a few times following its production, the film remained shelved for nearly 40 years due to the dissatisfaction of its cast members. Permission was finally granted in 2016, leading to a 4K restoration by Anthology Film Archives in 2022. Utilizing a documentary style, the film explores the dynamics of female collectivity that would later be further developed in *Born in Flames* (1983) and *Working Girls* (1986).
tmdb:393091: Kyoko, a nun at St. Saffron Church on Mount Rokko, plays hymns on the organ. Haruhiko Tenryu, the second-generation head of the Tenryu-gumi yakuza clan, is deeply in love with Kyoko because of her refined beauty, and has even forced his underlings to be baptized as Christians. Also harboring feelings for Kyoko is Detective Jindai, whose family runs a Tendai sect temple, presenting another formidable obstacle. However, Kyoko herself secretly harbors feelings for Eiji, whom she met fatefully one stormy day. As the feelings of those around her intertwine, Kyoko's destiny begins to move in an unexpected direction.
tmdb:39951: Toei Animation's first sci-fi feature. It is also the first feature-length film solely directed by Kuroda Yoshiro, whose highly designed compositions and musical style highlight the allegorical world. Ambitious meta-cinematic structures are employed, marking a breakthrough for a new generation at Toei Animation. The princess's secret revealed at the end carries a critique of civilization, an idea proposed by then-animator Hayao Miyazaki.
tmdb:400033:
"I want to film a documentary on Ryuichi Sakamoto for a French television program." In 1983, director Elizabeth Lennard visited Sakamoto in Berlin—where he was attending a David Sylvian recording session—to make this proposal. In May 1984, just as Sakamoto began work on his fourth solo album, *Ongaku Zukan*, filming took place in Tokyo over a brief span of only one week. The five-member French crew, led by Lennard, captured a vivid record of Japan, the city of Tokyo, and the musician Ryuichi Sakamoto.

Following its 1985 completion and French TV broadcast, the film screened at international festivals in Rotterdam, Locarno, and São Paulo. In Japan, it premiered at the inaugural Tokyo International Film Festival on June 9th of that year. While the subsequent VHS and DVD releases were long out of print and difficult to obtain, the original 16mm film was recently discovered in a warehouse and has been digitally restored.

Within its 60-minute runtime, the film captures a 30-something Sakamoto in the studio and in interviews, discussing his upbringing, values, musical philosophy, and culture. It also features footage from Nagisa Oshima’s *Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence* (1983), YMO’s "scatter" concerts, and music videos, while projecting the vibrant energy of 1980s Tokyo—from the Shibuya Scramble to Shinjuku Alta—onto the screen. This legendary documentary, an immersion into the "Sounds of Tokyo" as seen through Sakamoto’s eyes and portrait, finally makes its theatrical debut after nearly 40 years.
tmdb:400579: Marlo, a mother of three including a newborn, is given a night nanny by her brother. Initially hesitant, she soon bonds deeply with Tully, a nanny who is thoughtful, surprising, and at times challenging.
tmdb:404:
73-year-old Alvin Straight (Richard Farnsworth) lives with his daughter Rose (Sissy Spacek) in Laurens, Iowa. One day, he suffers a fall and is forced to go to the hospital. The doctor advises him to undergo treatment and use a walker, but he refuses. Accepting only the use of two canes, he promptly returns home. He is a stubborn man. On a stormy night, news arrives that his 76-year-old brother Lyle (Harry Dean Stanton), from whom he has been long estranged, has collapsed from a heart attack. It is 560 kilometers to Mount Zion, Wisconsin, where Lyle lives. By car, it would be a day’s journey, but Alvin does not have a driver’s license. Determined to see his brother on his own terms, Alvin ignores the opposition of those around him and sets out alone on a tractor traveling at just 8 km/h. All for the chance to gaze at the starry sky with his brother once more.

*Note: This theater will be screening a 2K converted version.
tmdb:415379:
Depicting a world of female passion filled with deep-seated grudges and a blood-stained drama of love and hate, Mio Saito’s novel—winner of the inaugural Yokomizo Seishi Prize—was brought to the screen by master director Yasuzo Masumura (*Black Express*, *Nakano Spy School*, *Idiot’s Love*, *The Wife of Seishu Hanaoka*, *Artery of the Archipelago*). Boasting a magnificent cast including Shima Iwashita, Jinpachi Nezu, and Kyoko Kishida, the film is a visual masterpiece defined by a unique color palette rich in shadows; it would ultimately serve as Masumura’s final directorial work. The musical score by Yuji Ohno, renowned for the *Lupin III* series, is another standout feature.

The brutally murdered body of Ryoko Ikehata (Yoko Hatanaka) is discovered. She had been a frequent visitor to the home of Kazuki Hata (Kunio Murai), a secretary to a cabinet minister with ambitions for the premiership. Koichi Moda (Naoki Sugiura), a reportage writer who had been in contact with Ryoko to expose political corruption, begins investigating Seiga (Mari Henmi), a fortune teller and Hata’s common-law wife. Moda enlists the help of his junior colleague, Sudo (Jinpachi Nezu). During the investigation, Moda finds himself drawn to a bar hostess named Yukiko (Shima Iwashita), and the two begin a series of secret trysts. However, just as Moda uncovers Seiga’s true identity, he meets a mysterious death. Taking Moda’s place to uncover the truth, Sudo heads to Aizu, where he witnesses...
tmdb:41948: The Soviet Union, shortly after World War II. In Suchan, a small coal-mining town turned labor camp zone, 12-year-old Valerka constantly acts out in rebellion against his single mother. Galya, a girl of the same age, is always looking out for him, appearing like a guardian angel to rescue him whenever he is in trouble. One day, after a prank goes too far and causes a locomotive to derail, Valerka flees the town alone, fearing arrest.
tmdb:41972: In 1982, the deadly virus MM-88 is stolen from a research institute in East Germany. However, the plane carrying the spy who stole it crashes in the Alps, and the virus spreads across the Earth, wiping out humanity except for a small group of survivors in Antarctica. One of these survivors, earthquake researcher Yoshizumi, realizes an even greater danger is approaching: a massive earthquake could strike the eastern United States, potentially triggering the launch of nuclear missiles.
tmdb:42112: The 13th feature film by French master director Robert Bresson, who left behind masterpieces such as "Resistance: From the Prisoner's Diary" and "Mouchette." Bresson, already over 80 at the time of filming, passed away in 1999, making this his final work. Based on the novella "The Forged Coupon" by Russian literary giant Leo Tolstoy, it depicts the life of Yvon, a young fuel delivery man who, after unknowingly using a counterfeit bill that falls into his hands, triggers a family massacre and spirals downward. The title "L'argent" means "money" in French. First released in Japan in 1986. Revived in 2011 as part of "Cinema Masterpiece Selection III: The Art of Robert Bresson" with new prints. In 2026, it will be revived again in a 2K restored version as part of "Robert Bresson Masterpiece Selection."
tmdb:429845: Director Takashi Kato presents an unconventional period action film depicting the story of the Sanada Ten Braves, who fought in the Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka, with fantastical fun and excitement! Affected by the radiation of a meteorite that fell from space, the Warring States street urchin Sasuke gains mysterious abilities. Growing up, he calls himself Sarutobi Sasuke and, along with the flying squirrel Okiri, becomes a subordinate of the cool commander Sanada Yukimura, rampaging through the rigged Winter and Summer Sieges of Osaka!
tmdb:42994: An epic theatrical omnibus animation consisting of three stories, with Katsuhiro Otomo serving as executive producer and general director. "Magnetic Rose" is a sci-fi drama set aboard a distressed spacecraft, adapted by Satoshi Kon from Otomo’s manga of the same name. "Stink Bomb" is a black comedy depicting the massive panic triggered by a man who accidentally swallows an experimental drug. "Cannon Fodder," directed by Otomo himself, chronicles the daily life of a boy living in a city built entirely for the purpose of firing cannons. Each segment is characterized by a unique, strange flavor imbued with a profound sense of wonder.
tmdb:431339: The world's oceans are overflowing with massive amounts of plastic waste. This documentary investigates the hidden impacts of marine pollution on animals, the environment, and humanity.
tmdb:433702: In present-day Japan, the giant demonic monster Orochi appears on a coast. Hibiki and Asumu rush to fight it, but Hibiki is defeated by Orochi and falls into a coma.
