Asumu seeks clues to save Hibiki in the Takeshi's ancient documents describing Orochi, but there he finds the name "Asumu," the same as his own, along with the stories of Oni... The ancient document tells of a village in the Sengoku period. There, Orochi demanded a human sacrifice every year. When Asumu's acquaintance Hitoe is chosen as the sacrifice, Asumu consults Tobei Tachibana to find a way to save her. Following the idea of asking an Oni for help, Asumu and the others set out to search for an Oni.
tmdb:434775: Lawyer Shigemori (Fukuyama) takes on the defense of Misumi (Yakusho), who has been arrested on suspicion of murdering the president of the company where he worked. Misumi had previously been sentenced to life imprisonment for a robbery-murder committed 30 years ago and was on parole. Misumi's testimony shifts back and forth repeatedly. Eventually, an unexpected connection emerges between the victim's daughter, Sakie (Hirose), and Misumi... This film, framed as a courtroom suspense, questions ethical issues that lie outside legal judgment.
tmdb:435421: The 23rd work in Stan Brakhage’s (1933–2003) 8mm silent “Song” series, this film was created as a direct response to the Vietnam War. Interweaving historical footage of war, death, violence, and mobilization with psalms and scenes of everyday life, Brakhage employs his signature mythopoetic structure to deliver a clear message to his contemporaries.
tmdb:437543: Continuing their westward journey to India, Sanzo and his companions Son Goku, Cho Hakkai, and Sha Gojyo are attacked by a giant fish while traveling by boat on a river. The four are swept through a mysterious hole in the sky and land in a strange land—the "Land of Women," where only women live. The queen and Sanzo develop mutual affection. Soon, the four are sentenced to execution under the land's laws, but they manage to escape thanks to the queen's intervention. However, they have no idea how to return from the Land of Women to their original world...
tmdb:43963: Legendary popular actor Yusaku Matsuda stars as a lone wolf with two faces—a salaryman and an outlaw—in this hit Kadokawa action film based on the novel of the same name by Haruhiko Oyabu, which was a huge success upon its release. Following his explosive popularity in the pioneering TV drama 'Taiyo ni Hoero!', Matsuda teams up again with director Tohru Murakawa and cinematographer Seizo Sengen—who also worked with him on the 'Game' film series and the drama 'Daitokai PARTII'—to break new ground in domestic hard-action cinema. A must-see film, Matsuda enhanced his wild charisma by experiencing live-fire shooting abroad for his role. Murakawa's signature long-take cinematography brings unique intensity to the gunfight scenes, and the final line is said to be an ad-lib by Matsuda himself, not in the script. Tetsuya Asakura appears to be an ordinary salaryman by day, but by night he trains his body and plots to take over a massive corporation. One day, he uses drugs he obtained to seduce his boss's mistress, Kyoko Nagai. Soon after, he discovers that a man named Sakurai is blackmailing company executives over an embezzlement scandal. Asakura skillfully manipulates Sakurai and the company to successfully become engaged to the president's daughter, Eriko. Meanwhile, burning with jealousy, Kyoko makes a fateful decision.
tmdb:44012: A masterpiece drama by Belgian female director Chantal Akerman, who left many works earnestly examining women's lives in society and daily life, carefully capturing a housewife's frustrations and details while tracing how cracks emerge in ordinary routine. Jeanne lives alone with her adolescent son in a Brussels apartment. Boiling water, peeling potatoes, going shopping—she leads an "ordinary" life, but... Starring Delphine Seyrig, known for "Last Year at Marienbad" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." Screened at the "Chantal Akerman Film Festival" (April 29 - May 12, 2022, Human Trust Cinema Shibuya).
tmdb:44018: A film by renowned French filmmaker Agnès Varda, tracing the steps of a young girl who freezes to death after wandering, which won the Golden Lion, the top prize, at the 42nd Venice International Film Festival in 1985. In winter in southern France, the body of an 18-year-old girl, Mona, is found frozen to death in a roadside ditch in the countryside. The film traces Mona's journey over the final weeks of her life as she hitchhikes aimlessly and continues a solitary journey, through the testimonies of the people she met on the road. Starring Sandrine Bonnaire (from "The Hairdresser's Husband"), with co-stars Macha Méril (from "Belle de Jour"), Stéphane Freiss (from "The Five Senses"), and Yolande Moreau (from "Séraphine"). It recorded over one million admissions in France at the time, becoming Varda's biggest hit.
tmdb:441660: Sengoku once took the world by storm with performances using his ability to read residual thoughts, but the mental toll eventually drove him to retire from show business and seek a quiet life. One day, a high school pianist named Ami approaches him with a request for the "Mighties" to find her missing music teacher, Yukie. Though initially reluctant, Sengoku eventually teams up with his former partner, Mighty Maruyama, to pursue the mystery of the case.
tmdb:44686: Sean Boyd, a former police officer turned truck driver, lives with his only daughter, Cassie, following a divorce from his wife. It was supposed to be the start of another peaceful, ordinary day for the two of them; after celebrating Cassie’s 15th birthday, Boyd drops her off at Central Park on her way to school. However, without warning, Cassie is suddenly dragged into a mysterious car. Having witnessed his daughter’s kidnapping right before his eyes, a desperate Boyd gives chase, but he is rushed to the hospital after his vehicle flips in a violent accident...
tmdb:454639: A new live-action film adaptation of the popular "Masters of the Universe" series, based on the action figures created by Mattel in 1981, which have been expanded across comics, animation, and other media, and previously adapted into the 1987 live-action film "Masters of the Universe" starring Dolph Lundgren. Prince Adam of the planet Eternia is sent to Earth as a child to protect him from war, and grows up hiding his identity. Fifteen years later, guided by the legendary Power Sword he accidentally discovers, he returns to his homeworld and learns that Eternia is under the control of his archenemy Skeletor. To save Eternia and its people, Adam transforms into the warrior He-Man and plunges into a deadly battle against the forces of evil. Directed by Travis Knight ("Bumblebee", "Kubo and the Two Strings"), with a screenplay by Chris Butler ("Missing Link"). Nicholas Galitzine, who has gained attention for roles in "Red, White & Royal Blue" and "The Idea of You", plays the lead role of Adam/He-Man. Camila Mendes ("The Revenge Swap", "Upgraded") plays the warrior Teela, who fights alongside He-Man; Jared Leto ("Tron: Ares") plays the villain Skeletor; and Idris Elba plays Man-At-Arms, a father figure to He-Man, in a star-studded cast.
tmdb:4550: Director Park Chan-wook's final installment of his "Revenge Trilogy," following "Sympathy for Mr. Vengeance" and "Oldboy," is a suspense drama about a woman wrongfully imprisoned who exacts revenge. Lee Geum-ja is imprisoned after a man takes her daughter hostage and forces her to take the blame for his child kidnapping and murder. During her sentence, she never loses her gentle smile, earning the nickname "Kind Geum-ja." After serving 13 years, she is released and begins her revenge against the true culprit who framed her. She retrieves her daughter, who was adopted abroad, and with the help of former inmates who have already been released, corners the man. Starring Lee Young-ae ("JSA," "Last Present") and co-starring Choi Min-sik ("Oldboy"), with cameos by Kang Hye-jung, Yoo Ji-tae, Song Kang-ho, and Shin Ha-kyun.
tmdb:46919: A landmark film of the 1960s Czech New Wave, this work portrays the wild antics of two uninhibited girls, both named "Marie," using a boldly experimental array of techniques including color shifts, coloring, optical effects, innovative sound design, and abrupt scene transitions. The older sister, with a blonde bob and a daisy wreath, and the younger sister, with dark brown hair in two pigtails, both call themselves "Marie" and pretend to be siblings. They live freely, tricking men into buying them meals only to fake-cry and run away. At home, they do whatever they please—bathing in milk, burning paper, cutting out magazine photos, slicing up bed sheets, and eventually cutting each other's bodies, until the screen itself fragments. Directed and written by Věra Chytilová, a pioneering Czech filmmaker and the most prominent female director of the Czech New Wave. The two leads were played by non-professional actresses selected through auditions: Jitka Cerhová and Ivana Karbanová. Other roles were also filled by non-actors, such as composers and designers. The film had its first official theatrical release in Japan in 1991 at Kichijoji Baus Theater, where it ran for an extended period through word of mouth. It has since gained a cult following, and in March 2026, a 4K restored version will be re-released to commemorate the 60th anniversary of its production and the 35th anniversary of its Japanese release.
tmdb:473702: A documentary by the renowned Swiss master Fredi M. Murer, known for 'Höhenfeuer' (Alpine Fire), capturing the mountainous region of his native Canton of Uri. Exploring the lives and spiritual world of mountain people in a changing alpine landscape, the film contains many elements that would later connect to 'Höhenfeuer,' such as folkloric themes and the insularity of communities. It won the International Critics' Prize at the 1974 Locarno International Film Festival. This film, along with 'Höhenfeuer' and 'Green Mountain,' forms the 'Mountain Trilogy.'
tmdb:47578: Kinji Fukasaku directs this adaptation of Toshio Kamata's legendary novel "Shin Satomi Hakkenden," a fresh take on Bakin Takizawa's classic "Nanso Satomi Hakkenden." Starring the glamorous duo Hiroko Yakushimaru and Hiroyuki Sanada, it became a massive hit characteristic of Kadokawa Films, which dominated the era and breathed new life into Japanese cinema. Tamazusa, who once married into the Hikita domain and indulged in debauchery and tyranny before being destroyed by the Satomi clan, returns as a demon queen to exact revenge. She orders her son Motofuji Hikita and his retainers to attack the Satomi's Tateyama Castle. The Satomi clan is annihilated, but Princess Shizu and a few retainers escape, pursued by Tamazusa's forces. The eight warriors, each possessing a jewel inscribed with one of the virtues—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, loyalty, faith, filial piety, and brotherly love—scattered from Princess Fuse's body, live their separate lives. Guided by fate, they gather around Princess Shizu and rise to battle, aiming to crush Tamazusa's ambitions.
tmdb:48153: A crime suspense film co-produced by France, Italy, and the United States, starring the renowned French actor Jean-Louis Trintignant, known for "A Man and a Woman" and "The Conformist." Lucien, a French hitman, arrives at Los Angeles International Airport. Checking into a Beverly Hills hotel and concealing a pistol, Lucien drives to the upscale residential area where his target, a crime boss, lives. After efficiently eliminating the target, Lucien returns to the hotel only to find that someone has checked him out and his passport and plane ticket are gone. As Lucien becomes paranoid, a hail of bullets suddenly rains down on him from an unknown assassin. Alongside Trintignant as Lucien, the film features a cast of distinctive French, Italian, and American actors including Ann-Margret from "The Hunter" and Roy Scheider from "The French Connection." Directed by Jacques Deray, known for the two "Borsalino" films and "Flic Story." The screenplay is by Jean-Claude Carrière, who worked on numerous masterpieces such as "The Unbearable Lightness of Being" and "The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie." After more than half a century since its production in 1972, it receives its first Japanese release in 2026 in a 4K remastered version.
tmdb:487850: The commercial film debut of director Ryusuke Hamaguchi, who gained attention for "Happy Hour," a film that meticulously depicted the daily lives and friendships of four women over more than five hours and won major awards at numerous international film festivals including Locarno and Nantes. This film was entered into the Competition section of the 71st Cannes International Film Festival. It is an adaptation of the award-winning love novel of the same name by Akutagawa Prize-winning author Tomoka Shibasaki, starring Masahiro Higashide and Erika Karata. Asako, a 21-year-old living in Osaka, meets Baku and falls into a fateful love, but one day, Baku suddenly disappears from her life. Two years later, having moved from Osaka to Tokyo, Asako meets Ryohei, who has a face identical to Baku's. Unable to forget Baku, Asako tries to avoid Ryohei, but he develops feelings for her. Despite her hesitation, Asako finds herself drawn to Ryohei. Higashide plays the dual roles of Baku and Ryohei, while Karata plays Asako.
tmdb:490067: A small city on the outskirts of Osaka. The Teramitsu-gumi, backed by the Kansai crime syndicate Josei-kai, proposes a merger to their rivals, the Ishida-gumi, but is rejected by the lieutenant, Ibuki. In retaliation, the Teramitsu-gumi begins a campaign of harassment. Around that time, Prosecutor Nakagami is assigned to the city. Although Nakagami was Ibuki’s university classmate and had married the daughter of the Ishida boss, Tatsunosuke, he remains cold toward them. Meanwhile, Teramitsu summons Tatsunosuke, and when he refuses the deal once more, Teramitsu murders him...
tmdb:493514: The Yangtze River Delta region extends across the lower reaches of the great Yangtze River, with Shanghai at its heart. This massive economic hub alone boasts a GDP that far surpasses that of all Japan. Yet, this film depicts neither the giant corporations nor the massive factories of the region. Instead, it focuses on the labor and daily lives of a younger generation—those in their late teens and twenties—working in the garment factories of Zhili, a town within the Delta. Most are migrant workers who have traveled from rural villages. Few acknowledge that these youths are the very backbone supporting the Yangtze River Delta’s economy; the world pays them no mind. And yet, here lies a surprisingly vibrant and raw sense of youth. This film represents the true essence of director Wang Bing—who defines his mission as "recording the lives of those invisible to the world"—and marks his first foray into the genre of youth cinema.
tmdb:4972: Popular Danish actor Mads Mikkelsen stars in this Danish black comedy about the struggles of two men who find themselves serving human meat to their customers. After opening their own butcher shop, Sven and Bjarne discover the body of an electrician who had been accidentally locked in their freezer. Through a bizarre turn of events, Sven prepares a marinade using the corpse’s meat and serves it to a customer, only for the dish to become an unexpected sensation. Desperate to maintain the shop’s reputation, he begins killing people one after another to procure more "ingredients." Mikkelsen delivers an eccentric performance as the town outcast Sven, sporting a unique hairstyle, while Nikolaj Lie Kaas of the "Department Q" series plays his partner, Bjarne. The film is written and directed by Anders Thomas Jensen, who has collaborated with Mikkelsen on numerous works, including "Adam's Apples." In Japan, the film will receive its first theatrical release in November 2025 as part of the special screening project "The Treasure of Scandinavia: Mads Mikkelsen's 60th Anniversary Festival."
tmdb:499: Cleo (Corinne Marchand) is a beautiful blonde woman. Lately, however, Cleo is troubled. She feels unwell. The thought that it might be cancer makes her restless. Recently, she underwent a thorough examination at the hospital. The results are due this evening. Cleo is terrified of that moment. Five o'clock. Cleo sits down before a female fortune teller. The fortune teller sees through her illness.
tmdb:49964: An Iranian film that vividly captures a boy's journey to find his friend's house to return a precious notebook he accidentally took home, bringing director Abbas Kiarostami international fame. At a primary school in the village of Koker in northern Iran, Mohammad is severely scolded by his teacher for doing his homework on a piece of paper instead of a notebook and is told he will be expelled if it happens again. However, his best friend Ahmad, who sits next to him, accidentally takes Mohammad's notebook home. Panicked that Mohammad will be expelled without his notebook, Ahmad searches for his friend's house in a distant neighboring village to return it, but struggles to find it... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
tmdb:500914: In a large rundown house overlooking the Tsutenkaku Tower in Osaka, a group of eccentric lodgers live... Frankie, in his famous partnership with Kawashima, plays a laid-back jack-of-all-trades who works as a ghostwriter and konnyaku maker. With unique supporting actors like Naniwa and Ozawa, this is a brilliant ensemble comedy that leaves a lasting impression.
tmdb:504234: In the late Meiji period, a poor farmer's daughter is sold as a prostitute to the Suzaki pleasure quarters. A fierce masterpiece of women's cinema by Tai Kato, depicting the sorrow and resilience of women exploited to the bone.
tmdb:504437: A youth music film about a young man's struggle to become a player of the mridangam, a traditional Indian percussion instrument. Peter, the son of a mridangam craftsman living in Chennai, India, is inspired to become a player himself after seeing a master perform on a mridangam his father made. Apprenticing under the master and training diligently, Peter faces various challenges including caste discrimination, conflicts over preserving traditional arts, and generational differences, but confronts them with passion and respect. The music is composed by A. R. Rahman, who won an Academy Award for 'Slumdog Millionaire.' G. V. Prakash Kumar, Rahman's nephew and a renowned film music composer, plays the protagonist Peter. Screened under the title 'The World Is Full of Rhythms' in the World Focus section of the 31st Tokyo International Film Festival in 2018. For its theatrical release in October 2022, the film was distributed by 'Nandori,' a South Indian restaurant in Tokyo's Arakawa Ward that fell in love with the film.
tmdb:505192: Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda of "The Third Murder" and "Our Little Sister," this human drama portrays human connections through the lens of a family that engages in petty crimes together. At the 71st Cannes Film Festival in 2018, it won the Palme d'Or, the top prize, for the first time for a Japanese film since "The Eel" in 1997. It also earned high praise overseas, including a nomination for Best Foreign Language Film at the 91st Academy Awards, the first for a Japanese film in a decade. At the 42nd Japan Academy Film Prize, it won eight awards, including Best Picture. In a working-class district of Tokyo, in an old one-story house seemingly left behind among high-rise apartments, live the homeowner Hatsue, the couple Osamu and Nobuyo, their son Shota, and Nobuyo's younger sister Aki, all dependent on Hatsue's pension. They make ends meet by shoplifting, living on the fringes of society, yet their days are filled with laughter. One winter day, Osamu brings home a little girl shivering on the balcony of a nearby apartment complex, and Nobuyo decides to raise her as a daughter. Triggered by an incident, the close-knit family begins to fall apart, revealing the secrets and desires each of them harbors. Alongside regular Kore-eda collaborators Lily Franky as the father Osamu, who repeatedly shoplifts with his son, and Kirin Kiki as Hatsue, the film marks the first Kore-eda works for Sakura Ando as Nobuyo and Mayu Matsuoka as Aki, Nobuyo's sister.
tmdb:5165: Sandro, his lover Anna, and her friend Claudia go sailing on a yacht. When they land on a certain island, Anna suddenly disappears. Sandro and Claudia search for her, but gradually find themselves drawn to each other, giving in to their desires despite their guilt.
tmdb:516543: A theatrical release version re-edited from a special 70th post-war anniversary program broadcast on Hiroshima TV in August 2015. It reveals the portraits of 321 first-year students of the former Hiroshima Prefectural Hiroshima Second Middle School, who lost their lives in the atomic bombing and for whom a memorial stone was erected along the Motokawa River, based on the writings of their bereaved families. While building on a reading drama broadcast on the same station in 1969, composed by Matsuyama Zenzo, it adds original elements such as projection performances using wooden boxes and interview footage by Ikezawa Akira.
tmdb:517468: Kore-eda's first international co-production. On the occasion of the publication of the memoir 'The Truth' by Fabienne (Deneuve), a grande dame of French cinema, her screenwriter daughter Lumir (Binoche) returns home with her actor husband and daughter. However, mother and daughter clash fiercely over the book's embellished contents. As they hurl their long-held feelings at each other, the differences in the 'truth' they each hold come to light. The film portrays a family where the memories and emotions of mother and daughter intertwine, eventually moving toward a new bond.
tmdb:52717: A drama by Jean-Luc Godard, the master who led the French New Wave, centered on the theme of 'love.' Edgar, a young artist in Paris, conceives a new work depicting four moments related to love—'encounter, passion, separation, reconciliation'—using three couples. The heroine Edgar considers ideal for this project is a woman he met two years ago. She is the granddaughter of an elderly couple who were once involved in the Resistance, whom Edgar met while researching the history of the Resistance in Brittany. Searching for her, Edgar revives his memories of Brittany two years ago. The first half depicts present events in richly shaded black-and-white 35mm film, while the second half shows protagonist Edgar's flashbacks in vivid color using digital video. The 4K restored version will be screened in Japan for the first time as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
tmdb:53016:
The third installment of the "War Trilogy" by Roberto Rossellini—the standard-bearer of Neorealism who profoundly influenced the directors of the New Wave—this drama depicts the cruelty of war through the lives of a young boy and his family in the ruins of post-WWII Berlin. Utilizing Neorealist techniques such as extensive location shooting and the use of non-professional actors, the film portrays the tragedy that befalls the boy with a documentary-like touch.

Berlin after the fall of Nazi Germany. Young Edmund lives in a cramped, rented room with his frail, bedridden father; his brother, a former Nazi Party member who hides indoors for fear of the police; and his sister, who supports the household while nursing their father. To earn money in place of his father and brother, Edmund wanders the devastated city instead of attending school. One day, he reunites with Enning, his former primary school teacher. Having been expelled from the school system and now involved in the black market, Enning preaches Nazi ideology, by which the innocent Edmund gradually becomes influenced.
tmdb:53023: One of the representative works of Agnès Varda, a leading female director of the French New Wave, this human drama depicts the ironic fate that befalls an ordinary couple in search of happiness. François lives a peaceful and happy life surrounded by his beautiful wife Thérèse and their adorable children. One day, while visiting a nearby town, François meets Émilie, a woman who works at the post office, and falls in love with her. At the same time, François truly loves his wife Thérèse. One day, while on a picnic with his family, François confesses his infidelity to Thérèse... The film won the Silver Bear at the 1965 Berlin International Film Festival.
tmdb:533444: The International News Department of Czechoslovak State Radio, led by Director Milan Weiner, operates in defiance of government censorship, striving for the freedom of the press. Tomáš, who looks after his younger brother Pája following the death of their parents, is transferred from the Central Communications Bureau to the news department on his superior's orders. The move is a calculated one: in exchange for the authorities overlooking his brother’s involvement in student activism, Tomáš is forced to collaborate with the State Security (StB) to monitor Weiner and his team. However, as he witnesses the journalists' sincere dedication to the truth and begins to earn their trust, Tomáš finds himself increasingly conflicted, caught between his brother’s safety and the pangs of his own conscience. Then, the "Prague Spring" arrives. Amidst the nation’s jubilation, Tomáš is summoned back to the Central Communications Bureau and ordered to broadcast a shocking announcement—
tmdb:54001: The feature-length debut of Iranian master Abbas Kiarostami, made in 1974, this human drama freshly depicts the funny yet poignant adventures of a boy struggling desperately to watch a soccer match. Gassem, a 10-year-old boy attending elementary school, is obsessed with soccer, often neglecting his homework and classes, earning constant scolding from his teacher and mother. Determined to go see an important match held in the capital, Tehran, he tries every trick to get money for transportation and a ticket, including stealing from home and deceiving his friends... A digital remastered version was screened as part of the special program "And Kiarostami Continues" (from October 16, 2021, at Eurospace in Tokyo and other venues).
tmdb:54083: A visual poem by French master Jean-Luc Godard, depicting modern Europe with overwhelming visual beauty and masterful editing. It is Godard's first feature film shot entirely in digital, his first in six years since 'Our Music.' Set on a luxury cruise ship touring the Mediterranean, it consists of three movements: the first movement 'Such Things' depicts human drama over gold lost during the Spanish Civil War; the second movement 'Where to, Europe' is a political comedy about a family living in the French countryside; and the third movement 'We Humans' explores history and culture across six locations related to human history, using countless quotations and collages. Utilizing various video formats and freely incorporating images, words, sounds, and even digital noise, it is depicted with overwhelming density and speed, full of rebellious spirit. Musician Patti Smith, guitarist Lenny Kaye, and philosopher Alain Badiou appear as themselves. Screened as part of the special screening series 'Jean-Luc Godard in the 21st Century: Our Films 2001-2010' (starting June 20, 2026, at Theater Image Forum Shibuya and other locations nationwide).
tmdb:54160: A bandwagon film made by Kinji Fukasaku during the Star Wars boom. Though the story is simplistic, borrowing from the Tale of the Eight Dog Warriors, it generated buzz with the casting of Vic Morrow and the construction of a full-scale replica of the Riave ship. While the special effects fall short compared to Star Wars, the chase scenes created without compositing were highly praised overseas. The planet Jirusia in the Andromeda Galaxy has been transformed into a "Planet Fortress" by the invading Gabanas Empire, led by Emperor Roxeia XII. Jirusia's Great Chief Kido seeks a hero of miraculous salvation, releasing eight "Sacred Riave Fruits" into space and instructing his granddaughter Emeralida and two warriors, Urokko, to pursue the fruits and retrieve the hero. However, Roxeia launches pursuit warships without delay. The Riave fruits reach five individuals on the Earth Federation colony planet Miraseria: Galda, a former general who resigned in disillusionment; Shiro and Aron, young space bikers; Jack, a thug; and Meia, a wealthy heiress. The youths find Emeralida's damaged ship while collecting "Space Fireflies" and rescue her and Urokko, but are bewildered by their mission. Galda returns the fruit and declines to join. Shiro and the others, keeping Meia in the dark, lie about introducing other heroes and sell Emeralida to an old woman seeking a bride for her son. The old woman and Emeralida are later captured by Gabanas pursuit forces. Meia, furious upon learning of their actions, inspires the repentant youths to prepare for Jirusia's rescue. They modify Meia's space boat to carry Shiro and Aron's small craft and head for Jirusia. Along the way, they are joined by Hans, a Gabanas man who holds a Riave fruit and is the rightful heir to the Gabanas throne, usurped by Roxeia. Meanwhile, Gabanas, captivated by Earth's beauty, demands unconditional surrender from the Earth Federation. Amid the chaos, Shiro and his six companions, now reunited with Galda, infiltrate the Gabanas fortress to destroy the planet fortress and rescue Emeralida. Gathering the remaining two allies, the eight confront Roxeia.
tmdb:547151: The International A-Class 500cc final (All-Japan Road Race Championship, Round 8) is held at the UGO Circuit. The fateful showdown between bike racers Akio Kitano and Keishi Oki ends just before the finish line when Oki overtakes Kitano, pushing the decisive battle to the final round. Kitano uses his handsome looks and sexual prowess to secure funding from multiple patrons to maintain his team. When Christine Adams, heir to a billion-dollar fortune and owner of an international conglomerate, arrives in Japan, Kitano quickly approaches her and successfully secures funding. Finally, Kitano faces the final race, but...
tmdb:54898: The fifth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Through lively dialogue and beautiful imagery, it depicts the journey of a lonely woman seeking love and happiness on vacation, winning the Golden Lion at the Venice International Film Festival. Delphine, who works as a secretary, is looking forward to a vacation in Greece, but her female friend who was supposed to go with her cancels at the last minute. She goes to the South of France with other friends but can't fit in and returns to Paris alone. Later, visiting the beach at Biarritz alone, Delphine hears about the "green ray" from a Jules Verne novel—a flash of light visible only for an instant just before sunset. Starring Marie Rivière of "The Aviator's Wife" and "Autumn Tale."
tmdb:5544: An actress, once condemned for having an affair with an enemy soldier in a French village under German occupation, visits Hiroshima for a film shoot and indulges in a one-day affair with a Japanese architect. Through this, she learns of Hiroshima's tragedy. The date is August 6th. Against the backdrop of the anti-nuclear movement, their lonely conversation continues. The city, miraculously rebuilt from the ashes, can never forget the shadow of death.
tmdb:554967: The final work of the late French master Agnès Varda, who passed away in March 2019. From her debut feature film 'La Pointe Courte' (1955) to her award-winning previous work 'Faces Places', this comprehensive self-portrait sees Varda passionately and humorously recounting her creative career spanning over half a century, looking back with precious footage. It unravels the secrets of her creativity, which was sustained by an insatiable curiosity and passion that kept her active throughout her life.
tmdb:55645: The third film in the "Red Peony Gambler" series. In the mid-Meiji period, Oryu (Sumiko Fujiwara), traveling to learn the ways of the world, joins the Nishinomiya family, Nagoya's top gambling clan, ahead of the Atsuta Shrine Festival's charity gambling. However, she gets caught in a merciless conflict between the gambler Hanooka (Ken Takakura), who owes a debt to the Kimbara family aiming for the position of gambling boss, and both sides.
tmdb:558: THE RIVER, one of Japan's largest overseas pop culture media outlets, celebrates its 10th anniversary in 2026. "REVIVAL by THE RIVER" is a new project expanding the community of online film fans into the real-world space of movie theaters. THE RIVER brings the films we once longed for back to the big screen. THE RIVER reunites films with their audiences! The commemorative first screening is 'Spider-Man 2'! Two years after the fierce battle with the Green Goblin, college student Peter Parker struggles with part-time jobs and classes while fighting for justice, leading a hectic life. Torn between his love for MJ and his friendship with Harry due to his identity as Spider-Man, Peter accepts his fate. A new enemy, Doctor Octopus, stands in his way. The most powerful action entertainment ever, surpassing its predecessor and achieving historic box office records. Flat rate of 1,600 yen (free tickets, invitation tickets, and various discount services not applicable). Online/TCG members: June 23 (Tue) 18:00~. General sale: June 23 (Tue) 21:00~. Box office sales begin June 24 (Wed). Screenings: July 3 (Fri) ~ July 9 (Thu), one screening per day at 18:10.
tmdb:55847: Jacques, an aspiring painter, saves a young woman named Marthe from throwing herself into the Seine one night. She had a lover who left for America a year ago, and that very night was when they had promised to reunite. Jacques finds her, sunk in anguish, beautiful. Driven by a fierce impulse of love, he forces himself to remain calm, hoping her heart will drift away from her lover, while feeling guilt over this. Like the 1957 version, this is a modern adaptation of Dostoevsky's famous tragic love story, a poignant work revealing Bresson's awakened worldview. Visconti's romanticism is absent here; the young man's blind love is brutally exposed as he pours out his feelings into a mini tape recorder, a habit of his, making it painful to watch.
tmdb:572979: A poetic and humorous road movie depicting a young girl’s journey to Bosnia to visit her estranged father and the two young men who become her traveling companions. Alma is a Bosnian girl living in the Netherlands. Her parents fled their war-torn homeland to raise her there, but her father eventually left Alma and her mother to return to Bosnia, leading to years of estrangement. When news arrives that her father has been hospitalized, Alma follows her mother’s wishes and sets off for Bosnia alone. At the airport, she is met by her cousin Emir, who is surly and unhelpful; only Denis, Emir’s self-proclaimed “intern,” is willing to listen to her. Alma boards a bus for the town where her father is staying, but during a rest stop, the bus leaves her behind, driving off with only her luggage. Bosnian-born, Dutch-raised Ena Sendijarević makes her feature directorial debut, projecting her own roots onto the protagonist while drawing significant influence from Jim Jarmusch’s *Stranger Than Paradise*. The title is derived from a song by the Scottish rock band Mogwai. The film won the Special Jury Award in the Tiger Competition at the 48th International Film Festival Rotterdam in 2019.
tmdb:57389: Italian filmmaker Michelangelo Frammartino tells the story of four lives that are born and die. Based on the Pythagorean concept of "four transmigrations," the film presents humans, animals, plants, and minerals with equal weight from a fundamentally egalitarian perspective that does not center the human world. After an elderly shepherd quietly dies in a mountain village in Calabria, southern Italy, his young goat dies beside a large fir tree. The tree is cut down for a village festival and eventually becomes charcoal. With no dialogue and long takes, the film captures nature as it is. In Japan, it screened in the natural TIFF section of the 23rd Tokyo International Film Festival in 2010 and was released theatrically in 2011. It will be released in 2026 as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
tmdb:58229: A samurai yet not a samurai! A shogunate spy who sniffs out darkness and delivers death—he is the Wind Samurai. This suspenseful ninja romance by Ryotaro Shiba weaves together the strange fate and love of Shinzo and Miki, caught in a conspiracy surrounding the phantom land of "Arai" in the Kumano mountains. Sleeping gold, a princess's love, and approaching evil swords! Director Takashi Kato, with ace star Hashizo Okawa, crafts a thrilling ninja suspense epic, connecting Edo and the wilderness with swords and romance.
tmdb:589068: Synopsis: Fuyuko (Ashikawa) supports her household by working at an insurance company. She asks her father, a painter, to paint her portrait, but... This literary masterpiece depicts the profound bond between a struggling artist and the daughter who devotedly supports him. Ashikawa is breathtakingly beautiful, portraying a strong-willed woman with poise and dignity.
tmdb:593: When communication is lost with the space station Prometheus, which is exploring the ocean-and-cloud-covered planet Solaris, psychologist Kris is sent to investigate. Upon arriving at the Prometheus, Kris witnesses the suicide of a friend, traces of people who shouldn't be there, and a series of inexplicable phenomena caused by the sentient organic ocean.
tmdb:601556:
A noir romance inspired by Junichiro Tanizaki's 1915 novel *The Murder of Otsuya*. Produced as part of the "TANIZAKI Reimagined" film project commemorating the 140th anniversary of Tanizaki’s birth, the film depicts the warping of love and obsession into violence as a man’s weakness and a woman’s presence become inextricably entwined. 

After serving time for copper wire theft, Shinsuke Abe is released from prison and begins working as a live-in employee at a surveying company. Soon, he is confronted by Santa Tokui, the childhood friend who instigated the crime, and Tsuya Yanagida, Shinsuke’s former lover. Though the theft had been Santa’s idea, Shinsuke had shouldered the full blame and served the sentence alone. While Shinsuke still harbors feelings for Tsuya, she is now involved with Santa. However, their reunion rekindles their mutual attraction, leading them to begin a secret affair behind Santa’s back. Amidst this tension, an irreversible tragedy unfolds.

The film stars Yugo Mikawa (*Cloud*, *Dish Up*), Remi Naoki (TV drama *Sayonara, Teacher*), and Jun Matsuo (*Red Bridge*, *Six Loners*). It is directed by Yoshihiro Tokijo, who previously wrote the screenplay for Toshiki Sato’s *Wandering Bonbon Candy*.
tmdb:604079: The first-ever film adaptation of Stephen King's first novel, "The Long Walk," written while he was in college in the 1960s and published under the pseudonym Richard Bachman in 1979. In a near-future America divided by war, a national competition called "The Long Walk" is held as a beacon of hope for a struggling society. Fifty selected teenage boys challenge this contest, where the only requirement is to keep walking. The prize is a staggering sum of money and the fulfillment of one wish. The rules are simple: maintain a pace of 4.8 km/h, receive a warning if you slow down, be executed after three warnings, and keep walking until only one person remains. Surrounded by armored vehicles and under the threat of guns, the boys desperately continue walking in extreme conditions with no rest or sleep allowed... Starring Cooper Hoffman ("Licorice Pizza") and David Johnson ("Alien: Romulus") as the young participants, and Mark Hamill ("Star Wars" series) as the Major who oversees the competition. Directed by Francis Lawrence ("The Hunger Games" series) with a screenplay by J.T. Molner ("Strange Darling").
tmdb:620824: The theatrical film of the TV anime 'Aikatsu Stars!', which began airing in April 2016 as a new series following the popular idol anime 'Aikatsu!'. It depicts the struggles of girls, including the protagonist Yume Nijino, who enrolls at Yotsusei Gakuen aiming to become the top idol. In this first theatrical film of 'Aikatsu Stars!', the story is set on a southern island where the characters come for an event. It revolves around the rumored 'Legendary Dress' said to be sleeping on the island, and depicts the friendship between Yume and Laura Sakuraba, as well as the school's top four-idol unit 'S4' taking the stage together. The short film 'Aikatsu! The Targeted Magical Aikatsu! Card' is shown simultaneously.
tmdb:627: A youth film that portrays the cheerful yet miserable lives of young people addicted to drugs, becoming an iconic work of 1990s British pop culture. Renton, a heroin addict living in Edinburgh, Scotland, spends his aimless days hanging out with fellow heroin addicts Sick Boy and Spud, and the violent, alcoholic Begbie. One day, after being arrested for shoplifting, Renton decides to reform, moves to London, and gets a job. However, Begbie and Sick Boy, on the run after a robbery, show up one after another, and Renton gets fired. When they return home, they attend the funeral of their friend Tommy, who turned to drugs after a breakup. Amid overwhelming despair, Renton and the others take a big gamble to change their lives... This is Danny Boyle's second directorial work and the breakout film for Ewan McGregor and Robert Carlyle.
tmdb:628742: Set in Lithuania just after its independence, this drama quietly observes memories, conflicts, and the lives of people caught between shifting eras through the eyes of an American-born boy visiting the country with his Lithuanian mother. Director Tomas Vengris, making his feature-length debut, draws on his own experience growing up as the son of Lithuanian immigrants in Washington, D.C., to delicately portray the reality of people tossed about by changes in territory and political systems. In 1992, mother and son Victoria and Kovas arrive from America to Lithuania, which has just gained independence from the Soviet Union. As a child, Victoria was separated from her family under Soviet occupation and lost her home and land. In Lithuania, where control shifted from Nazi Germany to the Soviet Union, people's freedom continued to waver under different regimes. Returning to her homeland after 20 years, Victoria seeks to reclaim her lost family land and start a new life with her son, but finds a Russian family already living there. Faced with the harsh reality that reclaiming the land is not easy, her ideal of a fresh start in Lithuania begins to quietly unravel. Martas Metlevskis, an American-born actor of Lithuanian descent, plays the boy Kovas, and renowned Lithuanian actress Sevilija Janušauskaitė plays his mother Victoria.
tmdb:632617: Johnny, a radio journalist living alone in New York, is asked by his sister to look after his nine-year-old nephew, Jesse, for a few days. Their sudden life together at his sister's home in LA is a constant series of bewilderments. The highly inquisitive Jesse flusters Johnny by asking blunt questions about his strained relationship with his sister, why he is still single, and his own father's illness. Yet, as Jesse shows an interest in Johnny’s work and recording equipment, the two gradually grow closer. When Johnny must return to New York for work, he decides to take Jesse with him, but...
tmdb:63418: The feature debut of French maverick Leos Carax, released in 1983. It depicts the encounter of two lonely souls wandering through the Paris night in beautiful black-and-white imagery, winning the Youth Prize at the 37th Cannes Film Festival and generating buzz at festivals worldwide. Alex, a young man whose best friend stole his girlfriend, has a fateful encounter with Mireille, a woman who just fought with her lover. Alex falls in love with Mireille at first sight, but they soon meet with an unexpected tragedy. The roles of Alex and Mireille were played by then-newcomers Denis Lavant and Mireille Perrier. The protagonist Alex, played by Lavant, later reappeared in transformed forms in 'Bad Blood' and 'The Lovers on the Bridge', forming what is known as the 'Alex Trilogy' along with this film. Jean-Yves Escoffier handled the cinematography and continued as cinematographer for the subsequent two films. In Japan, it was first theatrically released in July 1988, following the release of 'Bad Blood' in February of the same year. A 4K restored version was re-released in January 2026.
tmdb:63659: French writer Marguerite Duras, known for 'The Lover,' adapts her own book 'The Malady of Death / Agatha' into a film. Set in a dilapidated seaside hotel, this experimental work depicts the forbidden love between a brother and sister through lyrical imagery and Duras's own narration. Agatha, reuniting with her brother after eight months at the winter seaside villa Villa Agatha, decides to leave the next morning and part from him forever. The two reminisce about their forbidden love. The brother is played by Yann Andréa, Duras's lover who was 38 years her junior. In Japan, the film had its first theatrical release in 2003, 23 years after its 1981 release. It was re-released in 2012.
tmdb:63768: A road movie written and directed by Shin Adachi, known for scripting the NHK morning drama "Boogie Woogie" and films like "Zako-domo yo, Taishi o Idake" and "Theater Version: Still, I Want to Be with My Wife," set in Bungo-Ono, Oita Prefecture, depicting a small journey of a man and woman lost in life. Taro Oyama, approaching 30, calls himself a film director but is actually supported by the woman he lives with. He is selected for a film festival in Oita Prefecture but receives harsh criticism from the female organizer. The next day, heartbroken, Taro heads to neighboring Chikugo-Ono and meets a mysterious woman named Miki Sunahara. Miki, who says she saw Taro's film at the festival, and Taro embark on a small one-night, two-day trip. Miki is of unknown identity but has a frank personality. Taro, baring his lack of confidence in filmmaking to her, gradually develops a faint romantic feeling... Taro, the struggling film director protagonist, is played by Hiroki Sano from "SUPER HAPPY FOREVER," and Miki, the mysterious woman he meets on his journey, is played by Hana Amano from "Chime." The supporting cast includes Saki Kato, Ryo Shinoda, Ayame Gouriki, and Yuka Itaya.
tmdb:638905: Synopsis: An ordinary couple is drawn into a terrifying ordeal after witnessing a murderer. A hidden masterpiece from noir master Hideo Suzuki.
tmdb:639988: Korean master filmmaker Park Chan-wook, winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes for "Oldboy" and Best Director for "Decision to Leave," directs this suspense drama laced with irony and black humor about a salaryman whose life is turned upside down by a sudden layoff. Park reunites with Lee Byung-hun, who starred in his breakthrough film "Joint Security Area," for the first time in 21 years. Man-su, an ordinary salaryman at a paper company, lives with his wife, two children, and two dogs, believing he has everything he could want. But his life changes drastically when he is suddenly fired from the company he has worked for for 25 years. His job search drags on for over a year, and he is forced to sell his beloved home. Desperate, Man-su walks into a rapidly growing paper company with his resume, only to be flatly rejected. Convinced he is the most qualified person for the company, he makes a decision: if there's no opening, he'll have to create one himself. The film is based on the novel "The Ax" by Donald E. Westlake, which was also adapted into a film by Costa-Gavras. Lee Byung-hun plays the increasingly cornered Man-su, and Son Ye-jin of "Crash Landing on You" plays his wife Mi-ri, who grows stronger as the crisis deepens. The film was selected for the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and won the newly established International Audience Award (for non-North American films) at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival.
tmdb:640192: A moving drama based on the true story of a young woman who suddenly becomes paralyzed. Izumi delivers a powerful, soul-stirring performance as the heroine wandering the depths of despair, leaving viewers unable to hold back their tears.
tmdb:64131: In a Paris plagued by STBO—a mysterious disease contracted through loveless sex—Alex is a young man who has lived with a sense of nihilism and isolation since childhood. Even in the company of his lover, Lise, the emptiness remains. Stricken by unexplained abdominal pains and weary of his existence, he is consumed by the need to change his life. It is then that his estranged father is killed by a train. Marc, an old friend of his father, finds himself saddled with the dead man's massive debts and devises a plan to steal and traffic the STBO serum. He seeks out Alex as the essential recruit for the job. Alex joins the heist, but when he meets Marc’s lover, Anna, he feels a profound sense of destiny, and the story begins to unfold.
tmdb:64544: The sixth film in Éric Rohmer's "Comedies and Proverbs" series. Set in a new town on the outskirts of Paris, it lightly depicts the romantic affairs of four men and women. Blanche, a shy woman working at city hall, and Léa, a pragmatic female student, hit it off and become friends. Léa lives with her boyfriend Fabien, but their relationship isn't going well. Meanwhile, Blanche develops feelings for Alexandre, a playboy and friend of Fabien's, but her timid nature prevents her from confessing. Eventually, Fabien finds himself drawn to Blanche... The colorful 1980s fashion is also a highlight.
tmdb:648878: From Ari Aster, director of 'Midsommar', and following 'Beau Is Afraid', this thriller stars Joaquin Phoenix and depicts how a local election in a small town locked down during the COVID-19 pandemic escalates into a nationwide crisis. In 2020, the small town of Eddington, New Mexico, USA. Forced into a suffocating quarantine due to the pandemic lockdown, residents' frustration and anxiety are about to explode. Amidst this, town sheriff Joe clashes with ambitious Mayor Ted, who wants to save the town by attracting an IT company, over a minor dispute about wearing masks, and suddenly declares his candidacy for mayor. The fire of Joe and Ted's quarrel spreads, and social media erupts with fake news and hatred. Meanwhile, Joe's wife Louise becomes captivated by the inciting videos of cult leader Vernon, sinking into conspiracy theories. As suspicion, controversy, and rage swirl, violence begets violence, and criticism and conspiracy shroud the truth, the town of Eddington hurtles toward the brink of destruction. Joaquin Phoenix plays Sheriff Joe, Pedro Pascal plays Mayor Ted, Emma Stone plays Joe's wife Louise, and Austin Butler plays cult leader Vernon. Screened in the Competition section of the 78th Cannes Film Festival in 2025.
tmdb:660708: Director Michelangelo Frammartino, whose "Four Lives" depicting the cycle of life earned high praise at the Cannes Film Festival, questions the meaning of humanity's venture into the unknown against the historical context of Italy's economic boom. This film won the Special Jury Prize in the Competition section of the 78th Venice International Film Festival in 2021. Young explorers descend 683 meters underground without maps, using acetylene lamps to measure and map the cave structure. Above ground, an elderly shepherd on the Pollino Plateau prepares for a quiet death amidst vast nature, suffering from illness. The shepherd's death coincides with the explorers reaching the deepest abyss, creating a grand cycle of life and death, time and space. The cinematographer is the renowned Renato Berta, known for collaborations with masters like Jean-Luc Godard, Éric Rohmer, Daniel Schmid, and Manoel de Oliveira. In Japan, it screened under the title "Cave" in the World Focus section of the 34th Tokyo International Film Festival. It will have its theatrical premiere in Japan in 2026 under the title "Journey to the Depths of the Earth" as part of the special screening series "The Amazing World of Michelangelo Frammartino."
tmdb:662286:
1989, Cold War Switzerland. A police officer is assigned a mission: to surveil a theater troupe.

A political romantic comedy depicting the greatest scandal in Swiss history!

1989. Fear of Soviet communism is rampant in Cold War Switzerland. Police officer Viktor Schuler is ordered to go undercover at the Schauspielhaus theater, a site of active protest, to gather intelligence and monitor dissidents.

However, as he falls in love with the lead actress Odile Jolla—the very person he is supposed to be watching—and builds bonds with the troupe, he begins to question his own mission.

Should he follow his duty, or his heart?
tmdb:6643: The Zachary family runs a ranch on the Texas plains. Rumors spread that their adopted daughter, Rachel, is a Kiowa girl. Ben, the eldest son who manages the ranch, tries to uncover the truth. The facts eventually come to light through the mother, but the Zacharys become isolated, and the Kiowa attack to reclaim Rachel. Ben and his family fight back. This is Audrey Hepburn's first and only Western film.
tmdb:66788: The boss of a small yakuza gang called Medaka-gumi, who has only four underlings, dies leaving a will stating that his successor must be a blood relative. Around the same time, high school girl Izumi Hoshi is saying her final goodbye at the crematorium to her father Takashi, who died after being hit by a car in front of Narita Airport. Izumi's mother passed away long ago, leaving her truly alone. When Izumi returns to her apartment, a woman named Mayumi is there, carrying a letter from her father that says, 'If I die, please take care of Izumi.' The next day, a crowd of men in black suits lines up in front of her school. Ignoring her friends Tomoki, Tetsuo, and Shuhei, who try to stop her, Izumi heads toward the school gate. The man from the crematorium steps forward and says, 'You're Izumi Hoshi, right?' This man, named Sakuma, takes her to a shabby office and asks her to succeed as the fourth-generation boss of the Medaka-gumi.
tmdb:670: Oh Dae-su, a man living an ordinary life, regains consciousness to find himself locked in a small, confined room. After 15 years of imprisonment without knowing why, he is suddenly released. Who did this?! For what purpose?! With the help of a young woman named Mi-do, Dae-su vows revenge. A mysterious man named Woo-jin appears before him and proposes a deadly "game": Dae-su must uncover the reason for his imprisonment within five days, with both their lives at stake. An unimaginable and terrifying scheme lies behind it all...
tmdb:67263: A 1985 film by the master Fredi M. Murer, known as a pioneer of New Swiss Cinema, which won the Golden Leopard, the top prize at the Locarno International Film Festival. A family of four lives a nearly self-sufficient life surrounded by the majestic Alps. The teenage younger brother, who is deaf-mute, grows up healthily, sometimes frustrated by his disability but loved by his parents and older sister. One day, angered by a broken lawnmower, he throws it away, incurring his father's wrath. Running away from home, he begins living alone in a mountain hut. His worried sister brings him food, and they spend happy times together around a campfire on the mountain peak. Eventually, the sister's pregnancy is discovered... The film was first released in Japanese theaters in 1986. A digitally remastered version was revived in February 2020.
tmdb:682012: An animated film set in 1960s Kobe, depicting the growth of Amélie, a Belgian girl born in Japan. Based on the autobiographical novel "Tube Metaphysics" by Belgian writer Amélie Nothomb, it portrays a world rich in emotion, seen through the eyes of the two-year-old protagonist Amélie, woven with life, color, and her witty words. In 1960s Kobe, Amélie, a Belgian girl born into a diplomat's family, is unresponsive until age two and a half, but then enters an invincible childhood, believing herself to be a god and living in a magical world. Her days with her beloved housekeeper Nishio and her family are adventures full of new discoveries. One day, she learns the kanji for "rain," which suits her perfectly. Then, on her third birthday, an event occurs that changes everything. Directed by Myriam Ballard and Liang-Cho Han, who worked on "Long Way North," with music by Japanese composer Mari Fukuhara. It won the Audience Award at the 2025 Annecy International Animated Film Festival and was nominated for Best Animated Feature at the 98th Academy Awards.
tmdb:685550: Synopsis: Early Taisho era. This film depicts the growth of a boy raised by an elderly woman in a mountain village on the Izu Peninsula. A masterpiece of literary drama, it was adapted and filmed by master director Keisuke Kinoshita from the autobiographical novel by the literary giant Yasushi Inoue. Incidentally, "Shirobamba" refers to the snow bug. Ashikawa plays the role of the boy’s fleeting "Madonna."
tmdb:687163: A film adaptation of the bestselling science fiction novel by Andy Weir, author of "The Martian" (the basis for the Oscar-nominated "The Martian"). It depicts a middle school science teacher entrusted with the fate of Earth on the brink of extinction, who encounters an unknown life form with the same purpose at the edge of the universe, and together they risk their lives to save their home planets. An unexplained anomaly occurs where the sun's energy is being drained. If this continues, Earth will freeze and humanity will perish. It is discovered that the same phenomenon is happening not only to the sun but to countless stars scattered across the universe, and a single intact star is found 11.9 light-years away. Humanity's only remaining option is to travel to that star in a spaceship and solve the mystery to save the sun and humanity. Sent into space for this "Hail Mary" project is Grace, a brilliant scientist who left academia and now works as a humble middle school teacher. Alone in the vastness of space far from Earth, he relies on his scientific knowledge to tackle the mission, where he meets Rocky, an alien also struggling to save his home planet. Despite their different forms and languages, the two use science as a common language to face challenges, developing a friendship along the way. Ryan Gosling of "La La Land" and "Barbie" plays the protagonist middle school teacher Grace, with Sandra Hüller of "Anatomy of a Fall" and "The Zone of Interest" co-starring. Drew Goddard, who also worked on "The Martian," wrote the screenplay, and Phil Lord & Christopher Miller, known for producing and writing the "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse" series, directed.
tmdb:690: Michel, a poor university student, discovers by chance that he has a talent for pickpocketing. Though once caught by a detective, he is released due to lack of evidence and soon targets others' wallets again. Eventually, his methods become organized as he brings in accomplices. In 'A Man Escaped,' Bresson realistically and thrillingly depicted a prison break; here, he turns his focus to pickpocketing, introducing actual techniques while portraying a lonely young man distrustful of others. A gripping masterpiece where the realism born from amateur actors and the suspense created by various pickpocketing scenes blend seamlessly.
tmdb:701387: The eccentric genius Yorgos Lanthimos, known for 'Poor Things' and 'The Favourite', directs this kidnapping suspense film starring Emma Stone in their fifth collaboration. Ari Aster, director of 'Welcome to Eddington' and 'Midsommar', serves as producer. It is a remake of the 2003 Korean film 'Save the Green Planet!'. Michelle, the charismatic CEO of a globally renowned pharmaceutical company, is kidnapped by Teddy, a conspiracy theorist who firmly believes she is an alien set on invading Earth, and his devoted cousin Don. They imprison her in a basement and demand she abandon her plans for Earth. Michelle dismisses their absurd demands and tries to talk her way out, but the tug-of-war takes unexpected turns. As Teddy's hidden past comes to light, the absurd kidnapping plot veers in unforeseen directions. Emma Stone appears with a shaved head, passionately playing Michelle. Jesse Plemons and newcomer Aiden Delvis, cast through auditions, play the two kidnappers. The film was presented in the competition section of the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025 and was nominated for four Academy Awards at the 98th ceremony, including Best Picture and Best Actress.
tmdb:70520: Alibaba XXXIII, descendant of the original Alibaba and now king, indulges in pleasure and uses the lamp's genie to oppress his people. The descendant of a thief, Al-Hack, teams up with one mouse and 38 cats, riding a flying carpet into the castle. Akira Daikuhara's challenge is evident in the round, deformed characters. Hack is voiced by Nobuyo Oyama, and the shadow-puppet flashback scenes were handled by the theater troupe Kakashiza. This was the last film credited to Toei president Hiroshi Okawa, who passed away suddenly that year.
tmdb:705996: From Park Chan-wook, director of 'Oldboy' and 'The Handmaiden', comes a suspense drama about a detective investigating a murder and the victim's wife, a suspect to whom he finds himself drawn. When a man falls to his death from a mountain peak, Detective Hae-joon suspects it may be murder rather than an accident. He focuses on the victim's mysterious wife, Sore, but she has an alibi. As the investigation proceeds, Hae-joon finds himself attracted to Sore, and she develops special feelings for him too. Just when a lead emerges and the case seems solved... Park Hae-il plays Hae-joon, Tang Wei plays Sore, with Lee Jung-hyun and Go Kyung-pyo in supporting roles. The film won the Best Director award at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022.
tmdb:71933: One of four dark sci-fi works by Piotr Szulkin, a pioneer of dystopian science fiction in Poland, created under the socialist regime in the late 1970s and 1980s. With a style blending fierce satire and extreme surrealism, the film explores the theme of "escape from totalitarianism." In a world devastated by nuclear war, the planet is frozen, and radiation kills anyone who ventures outside the dome. A man who controls the last surviving humans walks among the crowds, preventing morale from collapsing, seducing prostitutes, suppressing rebellions, and occasionally feeding the hungry. But as the true evil nature of the dome becomes clear, he begins to question whether humanity is worth saving. The film had its Japanese theatrical premiere in 2026 as part of the special screening series "Polish Dark Sci-Fi: The End of Civilization Tetralogy" (starting February 21, 2026, at Theater Image Forum).
tmdb:736732: A road movie that won two awards at the 75th Cannes Film Festival, featuring a Korean production team and cast. Two male brokers who kidnap an infant from a 'baby hatch' and the mother who once abandoned her child. Bound by a strange sense of solidarity, they journey to find adoptive parents, quietly pursued by two female detectives. This film returns to Kore-eda's signature theme of 'quasi-family,' depicting certain hope beyond the moral dilemmas surrounding the salvation of unwanted lives.
tmdb:73990: Led by Lieutenant Yoshiaki Iba, 21 members of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force, armed with modern weapons, suddenly time-slip along with their supply depot to the Sengoku period while en route to an exercise. As they stand bewildered, Nagao Heizo Kagetora arrives with his retainers to meet them. Upon first seeing Iba, Kagetora takes an instant liking to him, calling him "a kindred spirit," and is drawn to their unfamiliar clothing and weapons, hoping to recruit them. Iba and his soldiers struggle to accept the reality of their time slip. However, after encountering Kagetora and being attacked by guerrilla forces of a rival feudal lord—resulting in a comrade's death—and witnessing Kagetora's battle firsthand, they are forced to come to terms with having arrived in the Sengoku period.
tmdb:74617: A theatrical version of the TV anime "Mazinger Z," featuring a piloted giant robot as the protagonist. Director Nobutaka Nishizawa heightened the drama by entrusting the robot with the protagonist's worries and pain, depicting the invincible Mazinger Z fighting while battered and broken. The surprise appearance of the successor Great Mazinger, ahead of the TV series, astonished children. "Mazinger Z" achieved strong revenue from merchandise licensing, sparking a trend of incorporating merchandising into projects from the planning stage onward.
tmdb:746257: A historical ensemble drama starring Haruma Miura, depicting the life of Tomoatsu Godai, a visionary who built the foundations of modern Japan's economy and was hailed as a 'Tengaramon' (a person of extraordinary talent). Written by Eriko Komatsu and directed by Mitsutoshi Tanaka, the film presents an original story. In the late Edo period, Japan is shocked by Perry's arrival. Young samurai Saisuke Godai (later Tomoatsu), sensing the dawn of a new era, ignores internal conflicts over expulsion or opening of the country and looks to the world. After meeting the courtesan Haru, he is driven by the desire for 'free dreams' and joins forces with Ryoma Sakamoto, Yataro Iwasaki, Hirobumi Ito, and others to build a nation where everyone can dream. Shohei Miura plays Ryoma Sakamoto, Godai's ally; Takanori Nishikawa plays Yataro Iwasaki, who later founded the Mitsubishi conglomerate; Yuki Morinaga plays a young Hirobumi Ito, who becomes the first Prime Minister; and Mei Nagano plays the courtesan Haru.
tmdb:749004: Directed and written by Céline Sciamma of "Portrait of a Lady on Fire," this film weaves a story of loss and healing connecting three generations: daughter, mother, and grandmother. Eight-year-old Nelly, grieving her beloved grandmother, is taken by her parents to clean out the forest house where her grandmother lived. But her mother, who spent her own childhood there, is overwhelmed by memories at every turn and eventually leaves. Left behind, Nelly wanders the woods and meets another eight-year-old girl who calls herself Marion—the same name as Nelly's mother. The girl invites Nelly to her home, which turns out to be "grandma's house." Sisters Joséphine and Gabrielle Sanz, making their film debut, play Nelly and Marion. Nina Meurisse ("A Woman's Life") and Margot Abascal ("Sagan") co-star. The film was presented in the competition section of the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in 2021.
tmdb:75233: The second feature film by director Joachim Trier (known for "The Worst Person in the World"), released in 2011. A bold adaptation of Pierre Drieu La Rochelle's novel "Le Feu Follet" (also the basis for Louis Malle's film "The Fire Within"), it sensitively portrays the pain and despair of a young man addicted to drugs, set in modern-day Oslo. Anders, undergoing a drug addiction treatment program at a facility in the suburbs, is plagued by suicidal thoughts. As his rehabilitation nears its end, he receives a leave pass and returns to his hometown of Oslo to reunite with friends. However, conversations are strained, and a job interview goes poorly. Eventually, he goes to a party but fails to fit in, and after a long period of abstinence, he starts drinking alcohol and then turns to drugs. This is the second film in what is called the "Oslo Trilogy," which includes Trier's 2006 debut "Reprise" and his 2021 film "The Worst Person in the World." Anders Danielsen Lie, who also starred in "Reprise," plays the protagonist Anders. The film was screened in the Un Certain Regard section at the 64th Cannes Film Festival in 2011. It received its first Japanese theatrical release as part of the special program "Joachim Trier: The Oslo Trilogy" (from February 13, 2026, at Bunkamura Le Cinéma Shibuya Miyashita in Tokyo and other venues).
tmdb:752867: A found footage horror film that uses avant-garde visuals and storytelling to depict four men and women visiting a desert who encounter unimaginable terror. Three memory cards are discovered in the Mojave Desert, containing horrifying footage. One day, Robbie, Angela, Scott, and Michelle come to the Mojave Desert in California to shoot a music video. But when night falls, strange sounds, lights, and inexplicable phenomena begin to occur. Soon, the four are swallowed by a rift in reality, and the camera captures the nightmare that befalls them. Robbie Banfitch, a multi-talented filmmaker, screenwriter, actor, and musician from New Jersey, makes his feature-length directorial and screenwriting debut, also starring in the lead role.
tmdb:758866: Inheriting the original story of a man's loss and hope after losing his wife, this is a remarkable narrative where the story and the play within the film resonate contrapuntally, boldly incorporating theatrical elements from timeless works like 'Uncle Vanya' and 'Waiting for Godot.' It won four awards including Best Screenplay at the 74th Cannes Film Festival and won the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film at the 94th Academy Awards.
tmdb:760329: The untold story of mixed martial artist Mark Kerr, who rose to fame during the early days of the "PRIDE" tournament that captivated all of Japan, is brought to film by Dwayne Johnson—also known as the wrestler The Rock—who stars and produces. Making his MMA debut in 1997, Mark Kerr rose undefeated to the top. After consecutive wins in the UFC, he also made a stunning run in Japan's PRIDE, becoming feared as "the strongest man in the hominidae family," but the pressure quietly eroded his mind. Kerr gradually became dependent on painkillers, and his relationship with his girlfriend Dawn deteriorated. After experiencing his first defeat, he finally confronts his own weakness and decides to step back into the ring to rebuild his life. Dwayne Johnson, inspired by the 2002 documentary of the same name, personally secured the film rights and carefully portrays the vulnerable side of a tough man. Emily Blunt plays Kerr's girlfriend Dawn, and Japanese actors including Tadanobu Asano, Satoshi Ishii, Yasuko Mitsuura, and Tomoyasu Hotei also appear. Benny Safdie, highly acclaimed for his co-directed works with his brother Josh such as "Uncut Gems," makes his solo directorial debut with this film, winning the Silver Lion for Best Director at the 82nd Venice International Film Festival in 2025. A team led by Japanese makeup artist Kazuhiro Tsuji handled the special effects makeup, earning a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards.
tmdb:76715: The will of the old family patriarch Saibee Inugami is made public, but it states that the heir to the vast fortune is the one who marries Tamayo Nonomiya, the granddaughter of Saibee's mentor. Saibee's three grandsons each scheme to claim Tamayo for themselves, but this soon escalates into a series of murders...
tmdb:77056: Three stories about love and chance, all centered around a date in Paris.
tmdb:783111: The 1979 presidential assassination trial. Told through the perspectives of those who defend, those on trial, and those pulling the strings from the shadows, this shocking suspense thriller reveals the truth behind the worst political trial in South Korean history.
tmdb:783263: High school student Momoko (Ashikawa) nurtures a tender romance while dreaming of her future at university. Set against a backdrop of breathtaking lakeside scenery, this impactful film vividly portrays the sometimes cruel reality of youth. Experience Ashikawa’s legendary appearance in a sailor uniform on the big screen.
tmdb:783740: From Giddens Ko, director of "Mon Mon Mon Monsters!" and "You Are the Apple of My Eye," comes a pure love fantasy inspired by the Taiwanese folk deity "Yue Lao" (the God of Matchmaking) and the concept of reincarnation. After being struck by lightning and brought to the underworld, Xiao Lun, along with Pinky who also arrives there, returns to the mortal world as the Taiwanese matchmaking god "Yue Lao" to tie the fates of people together. One day, a dog appears before them, triggering Xiao Lun to recover his lost memories of his past life. He remembers a promise he made to his first love, Xiao Mi, which he was unable to fulfill due to his sudden death. Starring popular Taiwanese actors: Ku Chen-dong ("You Are the Apple of My Eye") as Xiao Lun, Vivian Sung ("Our Times") as Xiao Mi, and Wang Jing ("The Soul of the Banquet," "My Ghost Friend") as Pinky.
tmdb:784524:
From Briarcliff Entertainment, the bold distributor of *The Apprentice*, and the production team behind *Nightcrawler* comes a descent into madness. Featuring brutal workout scenes and a performance brimming with a chilling intensity that overwhelms the viewer, this film set social media ablaze and sparked a massive sensation across the U.S. immediately upon the trailer's release. Its imagery—at once beautiful and destructively ominous—and its relentless psychological depth have earned rave reviews from major international media, with *The Guardian* praising its "Joker-like sharpness" and *IndieWire* declaring that it "surpasses Travis Bickle from Taxi Driver."

The film is written and directed by Elijah Bynum, one of Hollywood’s most watched young talents, who made a striking debut with *Hot Summer Nights* starring Timothée Chalamet and Maika Monroe. It is produced by Jennifer Fox (*Nightcrawler*, *We Need to Talk About Kevin*) and Dan Gilroy (*Nightcrawler*). These masters of thrilling human drama, known for pushing the boundaries of morality, have teamed up to take the audience beyond a new kind of "extreme." In the lead role, Jonathan Majors underwent a grueling physical transformation to showcase a physique that rivals professional bodybuilders. He pours his heart and soul into portraying a protagonist who possesses both a titan’s strength and a fragile, dangerous psyche—a character that evokes both terror and profound empathy.

"I will become the world's best bodybuilder—"
A lonely man dreaming of glory pushes his body and mind to their absolute limits. With brutal workout scenes and a performance of overwhelming intensity, this film ignited social media and created a whirlwind of excitement across America the moment the trailer was unveiled. Its beautiful yet ruinous atmosphere and its merciless dive into the depths of the human heart have been hailed by major critics, earning comparisons to the sharpness of *Joker* and the legendary Travis Bickle of *Taxi Driver*.

Writer-director Elijah Bynum, who burst onto the scene with *Hot Summer Nights*, has solidified his status with this, his second feature—a film he describes as the moment he "realized what I truly wanted to film." Produced by the powerhouse duo of Jennifer Fox and Dan Gilroy, these experts in provocative, boundary-pushing drama have formed a formidable tag team to show audiences what lies beyond the edge. Jonathan Majors delivers a tour-de-force performance, embodying a man of immense physical power and haunting vulnerability.

The Japanese subtitles were supervised by Hidetada Yamagishi, an IFBB (International Federation of Bodybuilding and Fitness) Pro bodybuilder. Through the cooperation of Yamagishi—a world-renowned athlete who has achieved immense success in numerous competitions and remains active primarily in the U.S.—this film offers a "strongest-tier" cinematic experience that captures the raw reality of the American bodybuilding world.

Killian Maddox lives in rural America, caring for his ailing grandfather. Living a life of isolation with a low income and no friends or lovers, he holds onto one unwavering dream: to become a world-class bodybuilder and grace the cover of a magazine with his sculpted physique. He sacrifices everything to a regime of grueling training and strict dieting, but as his body screams in pain, the injustices of society and his own isolation begin to erode his sanity. Following a specific incident, his pure dream begins to transform into total madness.
tmdb:785542: Twenty-nine-year-old Rona (Saoirse Ronan) returns to her childhood home in Scotland’s Orkney Islands for the first time in a decade. Having lost herself in the chaos of London while studying biology, she spent years escaping into addiction, but has finally managed to break the cycle. Now sober and seeking a fresh start, Rona finds herself still haunted by fragments of memory—the rift she caused with her lover and the many troubles she left in her wake. Amidst the freezing seas and wild winds, she learns to embrace the past she tried to escape and reaches out for a vibrant tomorrow. A song of beginnings; a journey back to herself.
tmdb:790999: Produced for PBS as a tribute to Chuck Berry (1926–2017)—the founder of rock and roll who transcended barriers of race and generation to exert a profound influence on future artists, culture, and society. This documentary brings together rare footage of Berry’s signature songs performed by the man himself and the rock legends he inspired, including The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, Jimi Hendrix, Keith Richards, Paul McCartney, and Bruce Springsteen. These performances were collected with the permission of the artists and their estates, with many of them digitally remastered. The film is narrated by Danny Glover, star of *The Color Purple* and the *Lethal Weapon* series.
tmdb:79382: Director Hirokazu Kore-eda of "Nobody Knows" and "Air Doll" depicts a family drama set in Kyushu, which is buzzing with excitement over the full opening of the Kyushu Shinkansen line in March 2010. Starring the comedy brother duo Maeda Maeda's Koki Maeda and Koshiro Maeda. The story follows two brothers, separated by their parents' divorce to live in Kagoshima and Fukuoka respectively, who strive to reunite their broken family, spurred on by the full opening of the bullet train line. Co-stars include regulars from Kore-eda's films such as Yui Natsukawa, Atsushi Abe, Yoshio Harada, and Kirin Kiki.
tmdb:795052: Starring the "Grand Prix actress" Machiko Kyo. On a Christmas night filled with the sound of hymns, a woman surrenders her purity to a man who is little more than a passing stranger, leading her down a sorrowful path into a world of betrayal and sin. Throwing away her irreplaceable youth into a quagmire and crying out in anguish, the film depicts the heartbreaking poignancy of a love that unexpectedly blossomed in a woman’s heart.
tmdb:795811: Trivial love talk between best friends, a student seeking guidance from a professor, female friends reuniting after 20 years... A first 'short story collection' woven from three tales themed around 'coincidence.' With a small production system ensuring ample rehearsal and shooting time, it carefully captures the actors' light yet delicate expressions. Won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival.
tmdb:800513: Legendary Broadway icon Lillian Hall is struck by a sudden illness. Struggling against memory loss, she stakes everything on what may be her final stage performance. Will the play successfully reach its opening night? A moving masterpiece and an ode to life that powerfully conveys the joy of living.
